suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file modifications to C:\Windows\System32\inetsrv\config\applicationHost.config, urlRewrite.config, or web.config outside change-control windows. Track filesystem operations and timestamp anomalies on IIS config directories.

suggestion.title: IIS Module Registration and DLL Injection
suggestion.rationale: IIS malware persistence commonly uses native module registration. No detection suggested for DLL loading into IIS process space despite 'hijacks' language implying code injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned DLLs loaded into w3wp.exe, especially from user-writable paths or IIS directories. Track new module entries in HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\Microsoft\InetStp\Components. Watch for requests to non-existent modules in IIS logs.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Outbound HTTP Connections from w3wp.exe
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'redirect users to illicit sites'—implies C2 communication or redirect infrastructure. No detection for command-and-control or external beaconing from IIS process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate outbound connections from w3wp.exe (typically none or limited to app backends). Alert on new external IPs/domains, non-standard ports, or high-frequency requests from IIS worker processes. Correlate with IIS access logs.

suggestion.title: HTTP Response Header Manipulation and URL Rewriting
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: 'redirect users to illicit sites.' Pipeline missed detection for HTTP header injection or IIS URL Rewrite rules insertion without authorization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect IIS access logs and HTTP response headers for injected Location, Refresh, or X-Redirect headers not matching domain allowlist. Monitor URL Rewrite rule additions via IIS Manager audit logs or registry. Baseline expected redirect patterns by site.

suggestion.title: IIS Service Account Privilege Escalation and Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Hijacking requires compromising or escalating IIS service account context. No detection for account manipulation, lateral movement from IIS host, or SAM/LSASS access attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on IIS service account (typically IUSR, ApplicationPoolIdentity, or custom accounts) performing privilege escalation, accessing SAM/LSASS, or initiating lateral movement via SMB. Monitor for unexpected domain enumeration queries from IIS host.

suggestion.title: DLL Sideloading via fltMC.exe and FLTLIB.dll
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'it starts with the execution of a batch script that drops payloads to stage a DLL-sideloading procedure (fltMC.exe + FLTLIB.dll)'. This is the Windows execution vector that precedes JFMBackdoor payload loading and is a critical detection point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for fltMC.exe process creation with parent process being batch script execution (cmd.exe, powershell.exe). Correlate with unusual FLTLIB.dll file writes to system directories. Flag if fltMC.exe loads FLTLIB.dll from non-standard paths or recently-created DLL files.

suggestion.title: Service Creation for Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'establish persistence via a new service'. Showboat explicitly uses service registration as persistence mechanism but no specifics are provided in article.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sc.exe or PowerShell service creation commands on Linux/Windows systems (particularly telecom-adjacent networks). Alert on service registration pointing to unusual paths, especially /tmp or world-writable directories.

suggestion.title: SOCKS5 Proxy and Port Forwarding Establishment
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes: 'Its most notable function is acting as a SOCKS5 proxy and port-forwarding pivot point, serving as a foothold on compromised endpoints and enabling the attackers to move to other systems on the internal network.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SOCKS5 proxy traffic patterns (SOCKS protocol handshake bytes 0x05) from single-purpose hosts toward multiple internal IP ranges. Flag unusual port-forwarding activity or netstat entries showing listening SOCKS5 ports on compromised systems with no legitimate business justification.

suggestion.title: External Code Retrieval from Pastebin for Process Hiding
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'the hide command, which enables a process to conceal itself on a host machine by retrieving code stored on external websites such as Pastebin or online forums for use as a dead drop'. Direct evasion technique using web-hosted payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS requests to Pastebin and similar paste sites (raw.githubusercontent.com, dpaste, etc.) originating from unexpected systems, particularly servers. Correlate with process hiding or code injection signals. Flag DNS queries to pastebin.com or related services followed by file writes to /tmp or process descriptor manipulation.

suggestion.title: Batch Script Execution Dropping JFMBackdoor Payloads
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Windows attack chain: 'it starts with the execution of a batch script that drops payloads to stage a DLL-sideloading procedure'. This is initial execution vector for Windows variant.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for cmd.exe or batch script execution with suspicious child processes (powershell, certutil, bitsadmin). Alert on batch scripts dropping files to temp directories or system paths, especially multiple sequential file writes within short timeframe.

suggestion.title: Screenshot Capture with Encryption for Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: JFMBackdoor capability: 'Screenshot capture — Take screenshots of the victim's desktop and encrypt them for exfiltration'. Collection and exfiltration of sensitive visual data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for screenshot-capture APIs (BitBlt, GetDC) invoked by non-graphical processes or unusual process parents. Flag processes accessing graphics subsystems from system service contexts or unusual accounts. Correlate with file creation in temp directories followed by encryption key material usage.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Cisco Secure Workload API Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Unauthorized API Access'—pipeline should detect authentication bypass or credential abuse against Secure Workload API endpoints. No use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for API authentication failures followed by successful requests without credential re-entry, or authentication from non-whitelisted IP ranges. Flag Bearer token reuse across geographically disparate locations within short time windows.

suggestion.title: Enumeration of Secure Workload Policies and Workgroups via API
suggestion.rationale: Unauthorized API access would immediately enable discovery—attacker enumerates microsegmentation policies, workgroups, and network topology. Title establishes access but pipeline missed discovery phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on high-volume API queries to /policies, /workgroups, /agents endpoints in short time window. Threshold: >50 enumeration calls per API token per 5-minute window.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised Secure Workload API Token
suggestion.rationale: Once attacker gains API access ('Unauthorized API Access'), they pivot within the environment using valid tokens to modify policies, onboard rogue agents, or create exfiltration paths. No lateral movement UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track API calls that modify policy enforcement (PUT /policies), add agents (POST /agents), or change workgroup membership. Flag calls originating from untrusted networks. Correlate with subsequent suspicious intra-network traffic.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Secure Workload Configuration Changes via API
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Unauthorized API Access' without boundary; attacker can modify policies, bypass segmentation, disable monitoring. Pipeline generated zero impact-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on API calls that delete policies (DELETE /policies), disable agent reporting, or modify enforcement levels. Cross-reference with absence of change-request tickets in ITSM system.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via Secure Workload API Metadata Access
suggestion.rationale: Unauthorized API access includes access to workload metadata, traffic telemetry, and policy rules—all usable for targeting. Pipeline missed exfiltration-phase detection entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk API exports (GET /analytics/traffic, GET /workloads/manifest) with large response payloads. Flag data export via API to external IPs or S3 URLs embedded in API responses.

suggestion.title: Suspicious API Client User-Agent or SDK Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability exploits an API authentication flaw—attacker likely uses malformed or non-standard client headers, or scripted API abuse. Pipeline missed execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on API requests from non-standard User-Agents (custom scripts, curl, Postman, Burp), API requests missing expected SDK signatures, or requests with malformed Authorization headers (missing 'Bearer', expired tokens, invalid encodings).

suggestion.title: Drupal Web Application Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Critical Drupal Core Security Vulnerability Exposes Websites to Cyberattack'—establishes web exploitation vector. Pipeline must detect reconnaissance and exploitation of Drupal admin/REST endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Drupal-specific paths (/admin, /rest, /user, /sites/default) with suspicious payloads—SQL keywords, encoded PHP, or GET parameter counts exceeding baselines. Flag non-browser User-Agents targeting Drupal endpoints.

suggestion.title: Drupal Remote Code Execution via Unsafe Handler Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates 'cyberattack exposure' from critical vulnerability; Drupal Core RCE is standard attack pattern. Pipeline should have generated code-execution detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual child processes spawned by web server daemon (apache, nginx, php-fpm). Alert on execution of shells, compilers, or interpreters from Drupal theme/module directories. Monitor for eval() or system() calls in application context.

suggestion.title: Drupal SQL Injection Query Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Drupal Core vulnerabilities manifest as SQL injection (observation 1305: CVE-2026-9082 Drupal SQL Injection). Pipeline should have flagged SQL injection detection given Drupal software context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor database query logs for UNION-based injection syntax (UNION SELECT), time-based delays (SLEEP()), or comment obfuscation (/*!, --, #) originating from web application user. Alert on queries to information_schema or system tables from Drupal context.

suggestion.title: Drupal Authentication Bypass or Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Critical vulnerability may bypass authentication or elevate privileges. Title signals 'cyberattack exposure'; pipeline must detect unauthorized admin access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for successful logins to Drupal /admin without valid credentials, rapid user role elevation (user → admin), session token creation anomalies, or admin actions from non-whitelisted IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Malicious VS Code Extension Installation
suggestion.rationale: Title directly states 'Malicious Nx Console VS Code Extension' as attack vector. Should detect extension installation with suspicious network/credential access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VS Code extension marketplace installations and post-install behavior. Flag extensions with suspicious process spawning, credential/SSH key access, or outbound connections to non-standard hosts within 60s of activation.

suggestion.title: GitHub Credential Access from Development Tool Context
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates breach of GitHub 'internal repositories,' implying credential/token theft. Extension execution should precede credential enumeration (git config, SSH keys, environment variables).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect VS Code process or child processes reading ~/.ssh, .git/config, or environment variables containing GITHUB_TOKEN, GIT_SSH_KEY. Alert on bulk reads of credential stores within extension execution context.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Git Operations from IDE Extension Context
suggestion.rationale: Breach of internal repos suggests attacker-driven git commands (clone, push, credential enumeration). Extension should not spawn git with unusual argument patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor git child processes spawned by VS Code/extension with non-standard arguments: git credential fill, git config --list (especially credential.helper enumeration), or git clone/push to unfamiliar remotes.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of GitHub SSH Keys / PATs
suggestion.rationale: Title states breach of GitHub repos; typical follow-on is outbound exfil of credentials to C2. Extension code should not initiate unexpected network connections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag VS Code or extension child processes making outbound connections to non-development-tool domains, especially with subsequent HTTP POST payloads containing base64-encoded keys or token patterns.

suggestion.title: Environment Variable Credential Theft from VS Code
suggestion.rationale: GitHub repos breach implies theft of CI/CD tokens, SSH keys stored as env vars. Extension has access to parent process env and can exfil via DNS/HTTP.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VS Code extension child processes for env var enumeration (printenv, env command) or process memory reads targeting strings matching GITHUB, SSH, TOKEN, KEY patterns.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Marketplace Distribution of Nx Console Extension
suggestion.rationale: Attack depends on users downloading poisoned Nx Console from VS Code marketplace. Should detect version anomalies, rapid version churn, or marketplace availability gaps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VS Code extension marketplace requests and installation events. Flag installations of Nx Console v18.95.0 or versions with unusual hash mismatches, rapid re-releases, or withdrawn-then-republished packages.

suggestion.title: Lucifer Phishing Site Hosting Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Affiliates provide traffic through phishing links, fake websites' and 'website-cloning feature that allowed affiliates to clone phishing pages and receive ZIP files preloaded with the latest Lucifer code.' No UC generated for detecting phishing infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for newly registered domains with crypto/NFT/DeFi keywords matching legitimate platforms (uniswap, opensea, airdrop) deployed under known affiliate hosting providers. Correlate high-velocity subdomain creation and SSL certificate issuance. Alert on phishing-kit ZIP file downloads from C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Wallet ERC20 Approve & Permit2 Transaction Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'ERC20 support, Permit2 abuse, off-chain signatures' as Lucifer features enabling execution. 'Once permission is granted, the drainer can automatically transfer tokens...often within seconds.' No UC for malicious wallet approvals.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ERC20 approve()/Permit() transactions to unknown spender contracts from victim wallets. Flag rapid approve → transfer() patterns within 60 seconds. Correlate approval events with phishing domain access logs. Monitor Permit2 contract interactions from unverified dApp origins.

suggestion.title: Lucifer Zero Config Affiliate Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Zero Config deployment workflows, allowing affiliates to upload static files, automatically generate phishing-ready packages, and deploy infrastructure with minimal manual work.' Pipeline missed automated deployment infrastructure UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ZIP downloads containing drainer payload templates from C2. Identify automated deployment signatures: static file uploads followed by rapid site generation, certificate provisioning, and DNS propagation cycles. Flag command-line patterns for Lucifer build/deploy tooling.

suggestion.title: Lucifer Telegram C2 Coordination & Hit Notifications
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Telegram notifications' and 'Telegram-browser support' are Lucifer product features. 'The operators announced bug fixes, wallet compatibility updates, Telegram-browser support...' Telegram is core C2 channel for operator-affiliate coordination; no UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for persistent HTTPS/WebSocket connections to Telegram API endpoints and bot subscriptions. Correlate Telegram notifications with wallet-approval events (indicating successful 'hits'). Flag high-volume bot activity indicating affiliate coordination channels.

suggestion.title: Multichain Asset Exfiltration & Wallet Security Bypasses
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'wallet-security bypasses, multichain functionality' and 'transfer cryptocurrency assets...often within seconds and across multiple blockchains.' Pipeline missed cross-chain asset-movement detection UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid sequential cross-chain bridge transactions from victim wallet within 60 seconds of approval event. Monitor for transfers to attacker wallet clusters across Ethereum, Polygon, Arbitrum, BSC. Flag patterns bypassing hardware wallet enforcement via off-chain signatures.

suggestion.title: Affiliate Commission Tracking & Hit Validation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The DaaS operator...takes a 20% commission from successful hits' and describes Lucifer's internal metrics on affiliate performance. Pipeline missed UC for detecting commission settlement patterns and affiliate infrastructure coordination.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for regular cryptocurrency payouts from attacker-controlled wallets to multiple affiliate wallets (20% fee patterns). Correlate payout events with preceding victim drains. Track wallet cluster relationships indicating operator-affiliate financial ties via on-chain analytics.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Cisco Secure Workload REST API Access Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'enables unauthenticated attackers to access resources' and 'An attacker could exploit this vulnerability if they are able to send a crafted API request to an affected endpoint.' Pipeline generated no detection for this critical initial-access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco Secure Workload REST API endpoints for requests lacking valid Authorization headers or authentication tokens. Flag crafted/malformed requests reaching /api/* endpoints with HTTP 200/201 responses, especially against sensitive configuration paths. Correlate with asset inventory to identify unpatched 3.9 and earlier or 4.0–4.0.3.16 instances.

suggestion.title: Cisco Secure Workload Unauthorized Site Admin Privilege Escalation via API
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'gain Site Admin privileges' through API exploitation due to 'insufficient validation and authentication.' This is the core privilege escalation mechanism; no UC was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco Secure Workload audit logs for unexpected Site Admin role assignments originating from REST API calls rather than the administrative UI. Flag role escalations without corresponding approval workflows or authorization context. Track source IP, authentication chain, and API endpoint involved.

suggestion.title: Cross-Tenant Resource Access in Cisco Secure Workload
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attackers can 'make configuration changes across tenant boundaries with the privileges of the Site Admin user.' No lateral-movement or cross-tenant enumeration detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor API request logs for single sessions or authentication contexts accessing resources from multiple distinct tenant IDs within short timeframes. Flag anomalous patterns where a single source (especially unauthenticated or spoofed Admin context) enumerates or modifies configurations across organizational boundaries.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Configuration Exfiltration via Cisco Secure Workload REST API
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'could allow the attacker to read sensitive information and make configuration changes.' No collection or exfiltration detection hypothesis was provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor REST API request patterns for bulk GET operations against sensitive endpoints (/api/policies, /api/credentials, /api/tenants, /api/workloads). Detect unusually high request volumes or large response payloads from single sources or sessions, especially when followed by outbound data transfer anomalies or external API calls.

suggestion.title: Microsoft Malware Protection Engine Privilege Escalation via Symlink Abuse (CVE-2026-41091)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states CVE-2026-41091 stems from 'improper link resolution before file access ( link following ) weakness, which allows attackers to gain SYSTEM privileges.' This is the primary attack vector and pipeline did not surface a detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious symlink or hardlink creation and traversal during Malware Protection Engine execution (MpCmdRun.exe, MsSense.exe). Detect when a lower-privileged process attempts to establish symlinks to SYSTEM-critical paths (Registry, System32, Drivers) followed by child process spawning with SYSTEM privilege. Alert on failed link resolution attempts before elevation.

suggestion.title: Microsoft Defender Antimalware Platform Denial-of-Service Exploitation (CVE-2026-45498)
suggestion.rationale: Article states CVE-2026-45498 'enables threat actors to trigger denial-of-service (DoS) states on unpatched Windows devices.' No detection hypothesis generated despite explicit DoS impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid restart cycles or crashes of Microsoft Defender Antimalware Platform (MsSense.exe, WinDefend service) within short time windows (< 5 min). Detect abnormal service state transitions (Stop → Start → Stop). Alert on Windows Security service failure events (Event IDs 7041, 7043) correlated with suspicious parent process or arguments.

suggestion.title: Malware Protection Engine Out-of-Date Version Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies vulnerable versions (1.1.26030.3008 and earlier) and patched versions (1.1.26040.8 and later). Pipeline did not generate compliance-based detection despite CISA mandate to patch by June 3.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query endpoints for Malware Protection Engine versions < 1.1.26040.8 and Antimalware Platform versions < 4.18.26040.7 (from Registry HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\Software\Microsoft\Windows Defender or WMI Win32_QuickFixEngineering). Flag as non-compliant with CISA BOD 22-01 patching requirement. Cross-reference with failed Windows Update logs to identify deployment blockers.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Malware Protection Engine Process Behavior Preceding Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes CVE-2026-41091 as a privilege escalation within the engine; detection should monitor for behavioral precursors. No use case generated for suspicious MPE process activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Malware Protection Engine process (MpCmdRun.exe, WmiPrvSE.exe hosting mpengine.dll) performing unusual file system operations: direct Registry modification, device driver installation, or file operations outside %ProgramFiles%\Windows Defender. Correlate with subsequent child process creation with elevated (SYSTEM) privilege, which should not occur during normal scanning.

suggestion.title: Defender Service Stop or Failure During Active Scanning
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-45498 DoS allows attackers to disable Defender; article notes CISA's warning of 'significant risks to the federal enterprise.' Detection should surface unexpected Defender termination.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected WinDefend service stop (Event ID 7036) or MsSense.exe process termination while scheduled scans are active. Detect if service termination is initiated by non-System account or non-expected administrative tools. Cross-correlate with suspicious process launch immediately before or after service failure.

suggestion.title: Microsoft Malware Protection Engine Elevation-of-Privilege Indicator Hypothesis
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes vulnerability allows 'attackers to gain SYSTEM privileges' but does not describe the exploitation trigger; pipeline should infer early-stage indicators (file handles, Registry access patterns) that precede successful exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for MpCmdRun.exe or WmiPrvSE.exe processes accessing or modifying SYSTEM-owned Registry keys (HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM, HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SAM) or sensitive files (%WINDIR%\System32\drivers, %WINDIR%\System32\config). Alert on handle creation to system objects from Defender engine processes with intent to escalate.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Dependency Injection via Malicious Packages
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly addresses '5 Supply Chain Attacks in 48 Hours'—supply chain compromise is the primary threat. Title signals dependency poisoning but pipeline returned no use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for package installations with source URLs pointing to non-standard registries, newly-registered authors, or packages with typosquatting names. Alert on dependency tree additions without corresponding code review or unusual commit patterns. Correlate npm/pip install calls with zero-day package names (< 7 days old, no GitHub repository).

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Environment Variable Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article covers GitHub Actions tag-spoofing attacks and CI/CD credential theft. Pipeline missed detection for secrets exported through workflow logs or external webhooks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GitHub Actions workflows that echo, log, or export environment variables matching *_TOKEN, *_KEY, *_SECRET, *_PASSWORD patterns. Detect Actions jobs that send output to external URLs (Discord, Slack, public paste services) or exfiltrate secrets via HTTP POST requests. Flag workflows run by newly-created bot accounts.

suggestion.title: Malicious npm Package Installation Spike Detection
suggestion.rationale: Shai-Hulud npm worm and TeamPCP campaigns exploit package installation vectors. Article describes 48-hour attack window suggesting rapid package proliferation; pipeline missed detection for installation anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual npm package installation velocity in build pipelines—especially packages with < 30 days age, zero GitHub links, or suspicious names resembling popular libraries. Alert on packages installed outside normal CI/CD build windows or by unexpected service accounts. Correlate with deployment logs to detect post-install command execution.

suggestion.title: Git Commit and Tag Spoofing via Object Replacement
suggestion.rationale: Article references attacks injecting fake commits and tags into GitHub repositories. Pipeline did not surface detection for repository integrity violations or imposter commits.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub audit logs for commits with impossible timestamps, mismatched author/committer fields, or tags pointing to non-existent SHAs. Alert on mass tag creation events, commits from newly-created bot accounts, or repositories receiving commits from unexpected GitHub Actions runs. Flag any git gc or git repack operations followed by push events.

suggestion.title: Unusual Package Registry Reconnaissance Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks often perform reconnaissance on dependency ecosystems before compromise injection. Article describes multi-stage attacks; pipeline missed detection for abnormal registry queries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk sequential queries to npm/PyPI/Maven registries for package metadata without corresponding install attempts. Detect queries from CI/CD runners resolving 50+ new package names from a single branch or PR. Flag requests with non-standard user-agents, unusual geographic source IPs, or rapid retry patterns against 404 responses.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration via Poisoned Build Artifacts and Published Packages
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain compromises exfiltrate data through artifacts. Article describes attacks across 48 hours implying post-compromise data theft; pipeline missed detection for abnormal artifact generation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor published packages and build artifacts for embedded sensitive data (base64-encoded credentials, API keys, environment variables, SSH keys). Alert on artifact uploads to unexpected repositories, unusual file sizes for distribution packages, or build processes that read .env, credentials.json, or ~/.ssh before packaging. Correlate with GitHub Actions jobs exfiltrating environment variable contents.

suggestion.title: Linux Kernel Privilege Escalation via CVE (Local Exploit)
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'root command execution' as outcome. No UC generated for detecting privilege escalation from unprivileged user context — core attack vector for kernel exploits.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process privilege escalation via kernel exploit: unprivileged process spawning shell/command with elevated capability bits, setuid/setgid abuse, or direct root UID acquisition without credential submission. Correlate process creation with kernel module loading or memory access patterns.

suggestion.title: Kernel Module Loading and Exploit Staging
suggestion.rationale: Kernel vulnerabilities typically require kernel module manipulation or direct memory access. Pipeline missed detection for exploit staging phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on insmod/modprobe execution from unprivileged or unusual context, or kernel module loading with suspicious parameters. Monitor for fork/execve syscalls immediately followed by ptrace, mmap on /dev/mem, or CAP_SYS_MODULE capability abuse.

suggestion.title: Exploitation PoC / Proof-of-Concept Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article should specify whether PoC is public. If yes, need detection for known exploit tooling (gcc compilation of PoC, specific binary signatures, hardcoded ROP gadgets). Pipeline did not extract this critical context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for compilation of C/assembly code in /tmp or suspicious directories immediately before privilege escalation attempts. Flag gcc/clang with output .o/.elf targeting kernel-related headers. Correlate with network downloads of public PoC repositories.

suggestion.title: Affected Kernel Version Matching
suggestion.rationale: Article title says '9-year-old flaw' affecting 'major distros' — should enumerate specific kernel versions. Pipeline did not extract CVE, version range, or distro list despite these being primary IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference running kernel version against published vulnerable range (missing from extraction). Alert on systems running affected versions with internet exposure or user login activity. Inventory kernel versions across fleet for patch readiness.

suggestion.title: Root Command Execution from Unprivileged Context (Anomalous UID Switch)
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly describes 'root command execution' outcome — core impact. No UC for detecting successful exploitation (command spawned with UID 0 from unprivileged process parent).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes with UID 0 spawned from parent process with non-zero UID, especially for shell/command interpreters (/bin/bash, /bin/sh, /usr/bin/python). Baseline legitimate setuid binaries and exclude from alerts; flag unexpected parent->root process chains.

suggestion.title: VPN Service Abuse for Ransomware C2
suggestion.rationale: Title establishes 'First VPN Used in Ransomware Attacks'—indicates commercial VPN services are primary C2 obfuscation vector. Pipeline should detect anomalous C2 patterns masked by VPN encryption.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ransomware operators mask C2 traffic through commercial VPN endpoints to evade network detection. Detect encrypted outbound connections to known VPN infrastructure followed by lateral movement, encryption activity, or file exfiltration; flag unexpected VPN client installation on business hosts.

suggestion.title: Infrastructure Takedown Evasion—Fallback Channel Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states authorities 'Taken Down' First VPN, creating operational pressure on ransomware operators to pivot. Pipeline should detect sudden C2 channel failures followed by enumeration/connection attempts to alternate VPN/proxy services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After law enforcement infrastructure takedown, compromised hosts lose C2 contact and operators initiate rapid fallback: enumerate alternative VPN providers, install replacement clients, or establish new anonymization channels. Monitor for failed connection patterns to known-down infrastructure followed by discovery of alternate VPN endpoints.

suggestion.title: Ransomware-Staged VPN Client Installation
suggestion.rationale: Title implies VPN installation is part of ransomware attack preparation or post-compromise C2 staging. Technique T1133 (External Remote Services) maps to commercial VPN as external remote access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected commercial VPN client installation (First VPN, NordVPN, ProtonVPN, ExpressVPN, etc.) on business endpoints, especially on non-standard user accounts, service accounts, or followed by encryption/exfiltration activity. VPN installation immediately preceding lateral movement or data exfiltration is high-fidelity ransomware staging.

suggestion.title: IIS Worker Process Module Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title 'Hijacks IIS Servers' implies code execution in w3wp.exe context. Expect malicious DLL injection into IIS worker processes via IIS module API or AppInitDLL. Pipeline captured no execution-layer UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when w3wp.exe loads unsigned or unusual DLLs from non-System32 directories, especially from temp folders, Appdata, or application writeable paths. Correlate with modifications to applicationhost.config or IIS registry handler configuration. Baseline legitimate IIS modules in your environment.

suggestion.title: IIS Configuration Persistence via web.config Modification
suggestion.rationale: Server hijacking requires persistent code injection. IIS attack surface is web.config (URL rewrite rules, handler mappings, custom modules). Pipeline provided no file-integrity or config-tampering UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web.config file modifications outside deployment windows. Flag creation of new rewrite rules, custom handlers, or application extensions pointing to unknown DLLs. Inspect for executable references in `<handlers>`, `<modules>`, or `<rewrite>` sections. Alert on web.config reads/writes from non-IIS-administrative processes.

suggestion.title: Registry-Based IIS Handler or Module Persistence
suggestion.rationale: IIS hijacking persists via HKLM registry paths (apppool identity, modules, handlers). Article title confirms server compromise, requiring registry-layer detection. Pipeline missed registry persistence UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on writes to HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\W3SVC, HKLM\Software\Microsoft\IIS, or HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Image File Execution Options. Monitor for AppInitDLL, custom apppool identities, or new handler/module registrations outside standard IIS maintenance.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Child Process Spawned from w3wp.exe
suggestion.rationale: Hijacked IIS server redirecting users implies malicious code execution in w3wp context. Malware likely spawns cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or rundll32 for C2 communication or credential exfil. Pipeline captured no execution-layer UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect w3wp.exe spawning child processes outside normal IIS operations. Flag spawns of cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32.exe, certutil.exe, or anything with network connection activity. Baseline legitimate children per environment; most w3wp.exe should not spawn user-mode executables.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Outbound Connections from IIS Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Redirect Users to Illicit Sites'—indicates C2 communication or redirection to attacker infrastructure. Network-layer detection for anomalous outbound traffic from IIS. Pipeline provided no network UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected outbound connections or DNS queries initiated from w3wp.exe or the IIS server IP. Alert on queries to suspicious TLDs, known malware C2 domains, or high-volume DNS activity. Detect encrypted tunneling (DoH, DoT) from IIS processes. Correlate with HTTP traffic anomalies (unusual user-agents, unexpected hosts).

suggestion.title: Malware Distribution via Compromised IIS Application
suggestion.rationale: Hijacked IIS server redirecting users to illicit sites likely serves malware payloads. Detection should capture malware staging, distribution, or C2 beaconing from web root. Pipeline provided no staging/distribution UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor IIS access logs for unusual HTTP GET/POST patterns (e.g., requests to new file extensions, executable downloads, suspicious query parameters). Detect file writes to web root from non-deployment processes. Alert on execution of recently-written web application files. Correlate web root file changes with process execution or network connections.

suggestion.title: DLL Sideloading Chain: fltMC.exe + FLTLIB.dll Payload Staging
suggestion.rationale: Article states JMFBackdoor infection 'starts with the execution of a batch script that drops payloads to stage a DLL-sideloading procedure (fltMC.exe + FLTLIB.dll)'. This is a signature attack pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor parent process creation rules for fltMC.exe when spawned by cmd.exe or PowerShell; alert on FLTLIB.dll being loaded from non-system (non-System32) paths. Correlate batch-script execution followed within 2–5 minutes by fltMC.exe + non-standard DLL load.

suggestion.title: Service-Based Persistence: Suspicious Service Creation and Delayed Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states Showboat 'establish[es] persistence via a new service'. Coupled with modular architecture and long-term post-exploitation goals (active since mid-2022).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sc.exe or PowerShell (New-Service) creating services with anomalous names (e.g., 'kworker', non-Microsoft naming), pointing to unusual image paths, or configured with delayed/auto-start type. Cross-reference service creation with batch-script execution or unexpected binaries in temp folders.

suggestion.title: Dead-Drop Code Injection: Process Hiding via External Website Retrieval
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Showboat 'hide' command: 'retrieves code stored on external websites such as Pastebin or online forums for use as a dead drop'. Attackers pull obfuscation code at runtime to evade static analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections from non-browser processes to Pastebin, GitHub Gist, paste.ee, or similar paste-bin services. Alert if followed by in-memory code injection (CreateRemoteThread, VirtualAllocEx) or process hollowing within 30 seconds. Flag any legitimate service (svchost, rundll32) initiating external web requests.

suggestion.title: SOCKS5 Proxy and Port-Forwarding Relay for Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights Showboat's 'most notable function is acting as a SOCKS5 proxy and port-forwarding pivot point, serving as a foothold on compromised endpoints and enabling the attackers to move to other systems on the internal network'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected network services listening on loopback or internal IPs offering SOCKS5 proxying (TCP 1080 or variants). Monitor for anomalous port-forwarding configurations via iptables (Linux) or netsh (Windows). Correlate with suspicious process creation and internal host scanning patterns.

suggestion.title: Screenshot Capture and Encrypted Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: JMFBackdoor includes 'Screenshot capture — Take screenshots of the victim's desktop and encrypt them for exfiltration'. Collection and command-and-control signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Windows.Graphics.Capture, gdiplus.dll, or screenshot-related API calls (BitBlt, GetDIBits) from non-standard processes. Alert on encryption library imports (AES, RSA) shortly after screenshot attempts. Correlate with C2 domain connections or suspicious file write patterns.

suggestion.title: Registry Manipulation for Configuration Persistence and Anti-Forensics
suggestion.rationale: JMFBackdoor includes 'Registry manipulation — Modify Windows registry keys and values' and 'Self-removal and anti-forensics — Hide activity, remove persistence, and delete traces'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on non-system processes (or unexpected service accounts) modifying HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet, HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\Run, or sensitive audit/logging keys. Flag deletion of event logs, Windows Defender registry entries, or sysmon configuration. Correlate registry changes with unexpected service creation or process injection.

suggestion.title: API Authentication Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title claims 'Unauthorized API Access' via 'Critical Cisco Secure Workload Vulnerability'—this is an authentication mechanism compromise. No use case generated despite the headline explicitly describing auth bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect API requests to Cisco Secure Workload endpoints that succeed without valid credentials or with malformed authentication headers. Flag requests that bypass normal OAuth/session validation or succeed immediately after failed auth attempts from the same source.

suggestion.title: Anomalous API Call Patterns Post-Authentication Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Title signals 'Unauthorized API Access'—implies attacker can now invoke API operations they shouldn't. No UC for detecting suspicious API enumeration or privilege escalation via API abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequences of API calls to multiple endpoints, unusual parameter combinations, or calls requesting sensitive operations (user enumeration, config retrieval, token generation) immediately after successful auth-bypass exploitation. Baseline normal API call patterns and flag deviation.

suggestion.title: Cisco Secure Workload API Token Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability enables 'unauthorized API access'—attackers will obtain and cache valid tokens. No UC for detecting token harvesting or re-use patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for API calls using tokens issued to different users/service accounts being used from unexpected IPs or at unusual times. Flag bulk token requests or tokens being forwarded to external destinations.

suggestion.title: Affected Cisco Secure Workload Version Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article title and severity (CRIT) imply specific affected versions exist. No UC for detecting Cisco Secure Workload deployments running vulnerable software versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate Cisco Secure Workload version telemetry (from asset inventory, vulnerability scans, or config management) against known affected version ranges. Alert on deployments still running versions confirmed vulnerable to this API bypass.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via Cisco Secure Workload API Calls
suggestion.rationale: Unauthorized API access inevitably enables privilege escalation or lateral movement. No UC for detecting API calls that invoke high-risk operations (role elevation, policy modification, infrastructure enumeration).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor API calls for operations that modify RBAC roles, create service accounts, grant API credentials, or enumerate infrastructure. Flag calls that succeed despite the requester lacking IAM permissions for those operations.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Nx Console VS Code Extension Installation or Version Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector is the poisoned Nx Console v18.95.0 VS Code extension—'Malicious Nx Console VS Code Extension' in title. Detection must surface installations from non-marketplace sources, unsigned extensions, or version mismatches against official registry baseline (extension install path anomalies, timestamp clustering).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VS Code extensions directory (%APPDATA%\.vscode\extensions\ or ~/.vscode/extensions/) for Nx Console v18.95.0 or unexpected version numbers outside official marketplace. Alert on extension installation timestamps coinciding with GitHub developer environment setup. Cross-reference installation manifests against marketplace metadata to detect signature anomalies.

suggestion.title: Credential Access: Git SSH Keys and GitHub Token Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article title 'GitHub Internal Repositories Breached' directly indicates git credential theft. Detection must identify access to ~/.ssh/id_rsa, ~/.git-credentials, ~/.gitconfig, and GITHUB_TOKEN environment variables by non-git processes launched from Nx Console context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on non-standard processes (Nx Console child processes, VS Code extensions) reading ~/.ssh/*, ~/.git-credentials, ~/.aws/*, or environment variables containing GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, or AZURE credentials. Flag rapid enumeration of git config folders across multiple repos.

suggestion.title: Collection: Rapid Git Repository Object Access and Staging
suggestion.rationale: Breach of 'GitHub Internal Repositories' requires bulk harvesting of git objects. Detection must identify high-frequency reads of .git/objects/, .git/refs/, rapid git archive operations, or repository cloning initiated from Nx Console.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk sequential access to .git/ subdirectories (objects, refs, heads, tags) within short time windows. Flag git archive, git bundle, or git clone operations spawned from Nx Console parent process. Alert on creation of large tar.gz or zip archives containing .git metadata.

suggestion.title: Execution Anomaly: Nx Console or VS Code Spawning Shells with Suspicious Arguments
suggestion.rationale: VS Code extension malware typically achieves execution by spawning bash/PowerShell from the extension runtime. Detection must capture Nx Console or Code.exe parent process launching shells with credential exfiltration or command-and-control arguments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Nx Console.exe, Code.exe, or node.exe child processes launching cmd.exe, powershell.exe, bash, or sh with arguments containing curl, wget, python -c, base64, or POST/request patterns. Baseline legitimate Nx build commands and flag deviations involving external network I/O.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration: Dead-Drop C2 Communication and Credential Staging in Temp
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline output references 'TeamPCP C2 exfiltration infrastructure' and 'dead-drop C2.' Detection must identify outbound connections to known/suspected C2 endpoints and staging of credentials in temporary directories before transmission.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file writes to /tmp, %TEMP%, or %APPDATA%\Local\Temp containing credential patterns (ssh-rsa, RSA PRIVATE KEY, github.com tokens, aws_access_key). Correlate with DNS queries and network connections to TeamPCP C2 infrastructure (MISP/AlienVault indicators). Flag non-standard ports (>10000) from developer machines.

suggestion.title: Threat Actor Infrastructure: TeamPCP Command-and-Control Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline should enumerate TeamPCP C2 domains, IPs, and dead-drop endpoints referenced in threat intelligence. 'GitHub Internal Repositories Breached via...TeamPCP' directly links actor to campaign. Detection infrastructure requires IOC ingestion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest TeamPCP IOC list (C2 domains, IP ranges, ASNs, dead-drop service endpoints) from threat intelligence feeds (MISP, AlienVault, Wiz, CrowdStrike). Alert on DNS lookups or HTTP/HTTPS connections from developer machines to these indicators. Cross-correlate with Nx Console process context and GitHub employee machine identity.

suggestion.title: Detect Malicious Wallet Approval & Token Transfer Spike
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes: 'Once a malicious transaction or wallet signature is approved, the drainer can transfer cryptocurrency assets directly from the victim's wallet, often within seconds and across multiple blockchains.' This is the core impact mechanism and primary detection lever.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for ERC20 approve() or Permit2 permit() function calls followed within 60 seconds by unexpected transfer() calls to attacker-controlled addresses. Correlate wallet connection events with subsequent bulk token/NFT movements. Flag accounts with high approval-to-transfer ratios or transfers to addresses with no prior interaction history.

suggestion.title: Identify Fake DeFi/NFT/Airdrop Landing Page Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Victims are lured to fake crypto, NFT, airdrop, or DeFi websites and asked to connect their wallets.' The pipeline should detect cloned landing pages: 'a website-cloning feature that allowed affiliates to clone phishing pages and receive ZIP files preloaded with the latest Lucifer code.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect domains or pages mimicking legitimate DeFi/NFT platforms by comparing SSL certificates, page layout hashes, and JavaScript wallet-connector libraries against known legitimate services. Alert on recently registered or bulletproof-hosted domains advertising fake airdrops or NFT mints. Monitor for Zero-config phishing deployment patterns (rapid ZIP extraction and web server startup).

suggestion.title: Detect Permit2 Protocol Abuse & Off-Chain Signature Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies technical bypass mechanisms: 'ERC20 support, Permit2 abuse, off-chain signatures... wallet-security bypasses.' These are explicit indicators of token draining infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Permit2 contract (0x000000000022D473030F116dFC393057C2CcfAA0) interactions from non-whitelisted callers. Flag off-chain signatures (EIP-191, EIP-712) used to approve token transfers without on-chain transaction initiation. Correlate signature generation events from phishing domains with approval messages sent to drainer infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Monitor Drainer-as-a-Service Affiliate Recruitment & Management
suggestion.rationale: Article describes operational model: 'DaaS platforms like Lucifer recruit affiliates through underground forums and Telegram channels.' Lucifer specifically runs a 20% commission model, indicating structured affiliate network requiring command-and-control infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Telegram channels and dark web forums for recruitment posts mentioning '20% commission,' 'per hit,' 'DaaS,' or specific platform names like 'Lucifer.' Track affiliate management dashboards for bulk phishing deployment instructions, hit reporting, and commission payouts. Correlate Telegram account activity with phishing domain registrations and hosting provisioning.

suggestion.title: Detect Automated Phishing Deployment via Zero-Config Workflows
suggestion.rationale: Article notes operational scaling: 'Zero Config deployment workflows, allowing affiliates to upload static files, automatically generate phishing-ready packages, and deploy infrastructure with minimal manual work. This significantly lowered the technical barrier for affiliates.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk ZIP file extractions on web servers followed by rapid Apache/Nginx configuration updates. Monitor hosting provider APIs for automated domain provisioning and SSL certificate generation in bulk. Flag FTP/SFTP uploads of pre-built phishing packages. Alert on deployment automation frameworks (GitHub Actions, GitLab CI) pushing malicious code to web hosts.

suggestion.title: Identify Suspicious Web3 Connector Library Integration in Landing Pages
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack mechanism: 'Victims are lured to fake crypto... websites and asked to connect their wallets.' Detection must focus on injected or malicious wallet-connector JavaScript: article specifies Lucifer provides 'wallet-security bypasses' and management of 'wallet interaction, transaction logic, alerts.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Web3 wallet-connector libraries (ethers.js, web3.js) injected into phishing pages with custom RPC endpoints pointing to attacker infrastructure. Detect signMessage() and approve() calls with unusual parameters or approval amounts. Flag pages serving modified wallet-connector libraries with exfiltration hooks for signature data.

suggestion.title: Unpatched Malware Protection Engine Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Microsoft has released Malware Protection Engine versions 1.1.26040.8 and 4.18.26040.7, respectively, to address the two security flaws' — systems running 1.1.26030.3008 or earlier are vulnerable to CVE-2026-41091.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query Windows Security logs or Defender telemetry for Malware Protection Engine version < 1.1.26040.8. Cross-reference with device inventory to flag unpatched endpoints. Alert on any version reporting 1.1.26030.3008 or earlier as actively exploited.

suggestion.title: Suspicious SYSTEM Privilege Escalation via Defender Link Resolution
suggestion.rationale: CVE-2026-41091 exploits 'improper link resolution before file access (link following) weakness, which allows attackers to gain SYSTEM privileges' — detection must capture privilege escalation from security service context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for elevated token creation or process spawning where parent is MsMpEng.exe, MalwareProtectionService, or related Defender processes and child process runs with SYSTEM integrity. Flag any symlink/hardlink manipulation in C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows Defender or engine paths.

suggestion.title: Windows Defender Denial-of-Service Attack Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies CVE-2026-45498 'enables threat actors to trigger denial-of-service (DoS) states on unpatched Windows devices' affecting Defender Antimalware Platform versions ≤ 4.18.26030.3011.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on rapid service restarts, crashes, or hangs of WinDefend, MsMpEng.exe, or MalwareProtectionService processes. Correlate with DoS indicators: missing Defender logs, failure to scan, inability to update definitions. Monitor for unpatched Platform versions 4.18.26030.3011 or earlier.

suggestion.title: Defender Antimalware Platform Update Bypass or Failure
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes automatic updates via 'default configuration' but notes users must verify updates are enabled — detection gap exists for environments where updates are disabled, failing, or being blocked.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag devices where Antimalware Platform version has not changed in >7 days despite security updates being available. Detect Group Policy changes disabling automatic updates. Monitor for Windows Update failures specific to malware definitions or platform components.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-41091 Exploitation Attempt via File Access Interception
suggestion.rationale: The 'link following' weakness in CVE-2026-41091 is exploited to intercept file access — detection must identify attempts to create symlinks or hardlinks in security tool directories before access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for symlink/hardlink creation in C:\Program Files\Windows Defender, C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows Defender, and related engine binary paths. Alert on parent process attempting file operations on Defender binaries via link redirection. Correlate with MsMpEng.exe or MalwareProtectionService process context.

suggestion.title: CISA KEV Active Exploitation Indicator
suggestion.rationale: Article confirms 'actively exploited in the wild' and CISA added vulnerabilities to Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog with federal patch mandate by June 3 — presence of unpatched systems is a direct exploitation indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all Windows endpoints for Malware Protection Engine < 1.1.26040.8 OR Antimalware Platform < 4.18.26040.7. Cross-reference with threat feed for active exploitation signals. Treat unpatched systems as compromised until verified patched; prioritize federal/critical infrastructure assets per BOD 22-01 timeline.

suggestion.title: Kernel Exploitation via Unsafe Syscall Sequence
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Linux Kernel Flaw Enables Root Command Execution' — the flaw is a kernel-level memory safety bug requiring crafted syscall sequences to exploit. Core attack vector must be detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious mmap/mprotect/ioctl sequences targeting kernel memory regions, particularly attempts to write to kernel address space from userland processes. Flag processes making unexpected ioctl calls to device drivers or kernel subsystems before privilege escalation.

suggestion.title: Non-Root Process Spawning Root Shell
suggestion.rationale: Successful kernel exploit grants root privileges. Article title emphasizes 'Root Command Execution' as the impact — detect privilege escalation manifestation when unprivileged process spawns shell with UID 0.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when process with UID > 0 spawns bash/sh/zsh with effective UID 0. Exclude legitimate setuid binaries (sudo, doas). Correlate with preceding kernel exploitation indicators and syscall anomalies within same process tree.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Memory Mapping of Kernel Ranges
suggestion.rationale: Kernel vulnerabilities (especially 9-year-old flaws) are typically use-after-free, race conditions, or buffer overflows requiring direct kernel memory manipulation. Detect mmap of /dev/mem, /proc/kcore, or kernel virtual address ranges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor opens and mmaps of /dev/mem, /dev/kmem, /proc/kcore by non-kernel processes. Flag mprotect calls adding PROT_EXEC to kernel address space (0xffffffff80000000+ on 64-bit Linux). Baseline kernel memory access and alert on anomalies.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Kernel Module Insertion
suggestion.rationale: After gaining root via kernel flaw, attackers commonly persist via unsigned/malicious kernel modules. Article scope ('Major Distros') suggests multi-platform exploitation; module persistence is standard follow-on.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor insmod/modprobe execution by processes other than init/systemd, especially unsigned modules. Correlate with kernel exploitation + privilege escalation events. Alert on kernel module loads from /tmp or world-writable directories.

suggestion.title: Seized VPN Infrastructure Takedown Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states authorities took down 'First VPN' service used in ransomware attacks. Pipeline must surface detection for law enforcement seizure events: domain/IP status changes, cert revocation, 503/404 patterns, and C2 migration indicators post-seizure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for infrastructure availability collapse of First VPN service. Detect sudden DNS resolution failures, HTTP error responses from known C2 endpoints, certificate revocation, and confirm takedown via WHOIS/registrar status. Correlate with internal connection attempts to seized infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Operator C2 Pivot Post-Takedown
suggestion.rationale: Article documents VPN infrastructure was 'used in ransomware attacks'—pipeline must generate detection for threat actor migration to secondary/tertiary C2 infrastructure following seizure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track known ransomware operator C2 endpoint patterns pre-takedown; establish baseline of VPN connection geography, timing, and payload characteristics. Post-takedown, hunt for geographic/temporal anomalies, new VPN providers, alternative proxy chains, or direct IP-based C2 fallback indicating operator pivot.

suggestion.title: VPN Provider RaaS Infrastructure Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Service name 'First VPN' appears to be commercial VPN provider weaponized for RaaS—requires proactive monitoring of legitimate VPN providers for abuse signatures, bulletproof infrastructure indicators, and payment infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate high-volume connections from legitimate VPN providers to known ransomware C2 IPs. Monitor for VPN provider address space acquired/resold to bulletproof hosters. Cross-reference seized VPN infrastructure with open-source threat feeds for RaaS prevalence metrics and payment processor abuse.

suggestion.title: IIS ISAPI Filter or HTTP Module Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'BadIIS Malware Turns Hijacks IIS Servers' — persistence on IIS leverages native module registration in applicationHost.config. Pipeline extracted zero persistence indicators despite obvious attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor applicationHost.config, web.config, and IIS metabase for new ISAPI filter or HTTP module registration. Alert on unusual DLL loading by w3wp.exe matching malware signatures. Flag IIS service restart events (EventID 1077) with new module names in registry paths.

suggestion.title: IIS Web Configuration (web.config) Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Redirect Users to Illicit Sites' — requires URL rewrite rules, handler mappings, or custom HTTP modules in web.config. Pipeline missed configuration-layer defense evasion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthorized modifications to web.config files in IIS root and application directories. Alert on new rewrite rules, custom HTTP handlers, or response headers. Cross-reference file timestamps with process creation events (w3wp.exe or iisexpress.exe admin context).

suggestion.title: Suspicious IIS Worker Process (w3wp.exe) Child Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Malware Turns Hijacks' — implies persistence and command-and-control; requires w3wp.exe spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or rundll32.exe for payload execution or exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on w3wp.exe or iisexpress.exe spawning child processes outside normal IIS operations (cmd.exe, powershell.exe, rundll32.exe). Monitor outbound network connections from worker processes to non-standard ports and malicious IP ranges.

suggestion.title: IIS Application Pool Identity Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Hijacks IIS Servers' — implies sustained administrative control; malware typically escalates from network service or application pool identity to LocalSystem or Administrator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for privilege escalation attempts originating from w3wp.exe context (token impersonation, ROP gadgets, kernel exploits). Alert on IIS application pool identity changes to higher-privileged accounts. Detect new local account creation during IIS service operation (EventID 4720).

suggestion.title: HTTP Response Redirection Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Redirect Users to Illicit Sites' — requires response-layer manipulation: 301/302 Location headers, custom redirects, or DNS poisoning. Pipeline extracted zero response-tampering detection rules.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Analyze IIS HTTP logs for abnormal response codes and Location headers pointing to external/malicious domains. Alert on suspicious HTTP 301/302 responses with redirect destinations outside organization scope. Cross-reference with DNS query logs and firewall block lists.

suggestion.title: IIS Registry Persistence and WMI Event Subscription
suggestion.rationale: Article: High severity implies sustained persistence; malware requires registry modifications (HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\W3SVC) and scheduled tasks or WMI subscriptions for survival across service restart.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\W3SVC and HKLM\Software\Classes for unauthorized modifications. Alert on WMI event subscription creation (T1547.010) and scheduled tasks running in IIS application pool or LocalSystem context during abnormal hours.

suggestion.title: DLL Side-Loading via fltMC.exe Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes Windows attack chain: 'execution of a batch script that drops payloads to stage a DLL-sideloading procedure (fltMC.exe + FLTLIB.dll).' Named, reproducible attack primitive.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for batch/PowerShell script execution followed by fltMC.exe launches paired with FLTLIB.dll loads from non-System32 paths. Correlate temp/appdata script drops with subsequent process execution.

suggestion.title: SOCKS5 Proxy Listener Activation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'most notable function is acting as a SOCKS5 proxy and port-forwarding pivot point.' Post-compromise lateral movement indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes binding to SOCKS5 port (1080) or establishing inbound socket listeners on non-standard ports. Detect traffic relaying patterns where compromised host forwards connections to internal systems.

suggestion.title: Persistence Service Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'establish persistence via a new service.' JFMBackdoor explicitly includes 'Process/service management — Start, stop, create, or kill processes and services.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for service creation via sc.exe or registry modifications under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services. Flag services pointing to temp directories or randomly named executables.

suggestion.title: External Code Injection from Pastebin Dead-Drop
suggestion.rationale: Article details 'hide' command which enables 'retrieving code stored on external websites such as Pastebin or online forums for use as a dead drop.' Explicit code injection behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for system processes making outbound HTTP(S) to Pastebin, GitHub raw, or code-hosting platforms. Correlate with process memory operations, child spawning, or suspicious file writes.

suggestion.title: Encrypted Screenshot Exfiltration to C2
suggestion.rationale: JFMBackdoor includes 'Screenshot capture — Take screenshots of the victim's desktop and encrypt them for exfiltration.' Explicit collection-to-exfiltration pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for screenshot-capturing APIs (BitBlt, screencap) executed in unusual contexts. Correlate large binary writes with encrypted C2 traffic patterns.

suggestion.title: Registry Manipulation for Anti-Forensics
suggestion.rationale: JFMBackdoor specifies 'Registry manipulation — Modify Windows registry keys' and 'Self-removal and anti-forensics — Hide activity, remove persistence, and delete traces.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious registry modifications under autorun/service keys and event log policy disabling. Detect security tool configuration deletion and audit policy modifications.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated REST API Requests to Protected Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers can 'send specially crafted API requests to affected endpoints without requiring any authentication'—core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST/GET requests to Cisco Secure Workload /api/v* and /admin REST endpoints where Authorization header is absent or malformed, especially targeting account, config, or policy management endpoints. Alert on successful responses (200-299) to unauthenticated admin API calls.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation to Site Admin Without Admin Audit Trail
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attackers can gain 'Site Admin-level privileges'—requires detection of sudden privilege elevation without matching administrative action logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect user accounts assigned Site Admin or elevated role in Cisco Secure Workload IAM logs without corresponding administrative approval events, API calls from privileged service accounts, or role-assignment audit trails. Flag accounts transitioning from unprivileged to admin in <1 minute.

suggestion.title: Cross-Tenant Data Access from Single User Session
suggestion.rationale: Article warns of 'cross-tenant access to sensitive data'—single compromised session accessing multiple isolated tenant scopes indicates lateral movement within SaaS infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when a single user session or API key accesses configurations, data, or policy objects from multiple distinct tenant IDs within a single API session or rolling 10-minute window. Baseline per-tenant access patterns and trigger on deviation.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Configuration Modification via API
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers can tamper with configurations after gaining access—detect changes to security-critical settings without administrative authorization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Cisco Secure Workload configuration audit logs for modifications to roles, API credentials, security policies, or data access controls initiated via REST API calls from non-admin accounts or missing authorization headers. Alert on changes to authentication/authorization settings from unauthenticated contexts.

suggestion.title: Repeated Unauthenticated Admin API Calls Followed by Success
suggestion.rationale: Attack pattern: repeated probing of /admin endpoints without credentials, then successful data retrieval—indicates reconnaissance and exploitation of authentication bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate sequences of 5+ 401/403 responses to internal Cisco Secure Workload /api/admin/* endpoints from the same source IP, followed by 200 responses to the same endpoints without authentication headers. Flag if subsequent requests access sensitive resources (user data, configs, tokens).

suggestion.title: Site Admin Role Assignment via Unauthenticated API
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies endpoint vulnerability grants 'Site Admin-level privileges'—role escalation via API indicates the exploit targets user/role management endpoints directly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect role or privilege-level modifications to user accounts in Cisco Secure Workload where the triggering API call originates from an unauthenticated context, lacks a valid JWT/OAuth token, or comes from an unexpected source IP/user agent. Flag any Site Admin role assignment outside normal administrative workflows.

suggestion.title: VS Code Extension Installation — Unsigned or Anomalous Publisher
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states malicious Nx Console extension used as attack vector: 'Breached via Malicious Nx Console VS Code Extension.' No detection UC for extension installation behavior despite clear supply-chain delivery mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for installation of Nx Console or similar monorepo-tool extensions from untrusted publishers, unsigned extensions, or installations from non-marketplace sources. Cross-reference extension installation timestamps with subsequent GitHub API activity and credential access patterns.

suggestion.title: GitHub Personal Access Token Creation After Extension Install
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates breach of GitHub internal repos; implies credential theft or token generation. Article states 'GitHub Internal Repositories Breached'—requires authentication bypass or stolen credentials. No UC for GitHub API credential anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation of new GitHub Personal Access Tokens or SSH keys within 24 hours of VS Code extension installation. Flag tokens with repo-level read access created from automated tools or unusual geolocations relative to user baseline.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of GitHub Repository Data to Non-GitHub IP
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'GitHub Internal Repositories Breached'; attack culminates in data loss. No detection UC for repository-data exfiltration despite explicit breach impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor developer machines for large bulk downloads or transfers of repository data (>100MB in <1hr) to IPs outside GitHub's IP space. Correlate with malicious extension execution context and GitHub API calls to enumerate repos prior to exfiltration.

suggestion.title: GitHub API Enumeration from VS Code Process
suggestion.rationale: Breach mechanism suggests automated enumeration of GitHub repositories to identify high-value targets. Title 'Internal Repositories' indicates targeted search. No UC for GitHub API reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid enumeration of GitHub API endpoints (repos, branches, issues, pull requests) from single user/token within compressed timeframe (e.g., 50+ API calls in <10min). Flag calls to list-all-repos endpoints or organization-enumeration endpoints.

suggestion.title: Credential Access — SSH Keys or .netrc from Developer Environment
suggestion.rationale: Malicious extension runs in developer's VS Code context with access to file system. Attack requires exfiltration of GitHub credentials (SSH keys, PATs, .netrc, .gitconfig). Article states 'Breached'—requires credential theft. No UC for in-context credential harvesting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for VS Code or extension child processes accessing ~/.ssh, ~/.netrc, ~/.gitconfig, or VS Code credential stores (credentials.json). Flag reads followed by network exfiltration or Base64 encoding, particularly to non-GitHub destinations.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Stolen GitHub Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Theft of GitHub credentials enables access to internal repositories. Title 'Internal Repositories Breached' indicates successful use of stolen auth to access restricted repos. No UC for anomalous GitHub authentication or access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GitHub API authentication or repo access from IPs not associated with normal developer activity, or from geographies mismatched to user baseline. Flag access to repositories the authenticated user does not normally interact with, especially internal/private repos outside their team scope.

suggestion.title: Phishing Page Detection – Crypto DeFi Lookalike Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Victims are lured to fake crypto, NFT, airdrop, or DeFi websites.' Pipeline generated zero use cases for monitoring newly registered lookalike domains or typosquatted crypto platforms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for domains with >85% string similarity to legitimate DeFi protocols, exchanges, or airdrop distributors registered in the past 7 days. Alert on sudden traffic spikes to previously-unresolved domains claiming to offer crypto airdrops, NFT mints, or token claims. Correlate new domain registration patterns with known Lucifer affiliate hosting infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Malicious Wallet Approval Abuse – ERC20 Permit2 Signatures
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Permit2 abuse, off-chain signatures, wallet-security bypasses' and describes users approving 'malicious transaction or wallet signature.' No detection logic was generated for abnormal contract approvals or rapid permit() calls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor blockchain logs for ERC20 approve() events to contracts with no prior interaction history from the user. Alert on Permit2 signature requests (EIP-2612/EIP-5267) followed by immediate token transfer within 60 seconds. Detect off-chain signatures (EIP-191/EIP-712) requested by unfamiliar domains or MetaMask injectors on phishing pages.

suggestion.title: Compromised Crypto Influencer Account – Drainer Link Promotion
suggestion.rationale: Article states affiliates generate traffic 'through compromised social media accounts.' No use case addresses detecting legitimate high-follower crypto accounts suddenly promoting unfamiliar DeFi sites or wallet-drain phishing links.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor verified crypto-finance accounts for geolocation, posting-time, and language anomalies combined with sudden promotion of unknown DeFi protocols or 'exclusive airdrop' URLs. Correlate shortened links (bit.ly, tinyurl) shared by compromised accounts against known phishing infrastructure and Lucifer hosting ranges. Alert on account takeovers indicated by posts to non-follower communities or uncharacteristic engagement with new tokens.

suggestion.title: Website Cloning and Infrastructure-as-a-Service Phishing Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'website-cloning feature that allowed affiliates to clone phishing pages and receive ZIP files preloaded with the latest Lucifer code' and 'Zero Config deployment workflows.' No use case detects rapid batch creation of nearly-identical phishing infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for batch domain registrations (≥5 domains in 48 hours) with similar naming patterns (e.g., uniswap-v3, uniswap-stake, uniswap-claim). Alert on identical SSL certificates or common issuer/subject patterns issued to multiple structurally-similar domains. Detect rapid provisioning of static content servers from the same registrant or ASN within short timeframes.

suggestion.title: Rapid Cross-Chain Cryptocurrency Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'the drainer can transfer cryptocurrency assets directly from the victim's wallet, often within seconds... across multiple blockchains.' No detection hypothesis was generated for rapid multi-chain asset sweeps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor on-chain for token transfer sequences from a single victim address to attacker-controlled addresses across Ethereum, Polygon, BSC, and Arbitrum within <60 seconds. Alert on unusual cross-chain bridge usage (Stargate, Across, Hop Protocol) by newly-compromised addresses. Correlate victim addresses with recent wallet-approval events on phishing domains and trace attacker consolidation wallets.

suggestion.title: DaaS Platform Operational Intelligence – Affiliate Recruitment and Feature Releases
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Lucifer recruiting 'affiliates through underground forums and Telegram channels,' announcing 'version 6.6.6,' and releasing new features like 'Zero Config deployment.' No use case addresses threat-intel collection on DaaS platform evolution as a leading indicator of campaign scaling.
