suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Linux process execution for: (1) suspicious parent-child chains (web server → shell), (2) base64/hex decode operations followed by execution, (3) /dev/tcp connections or curl/wget with pipe-to-shell patterns, (4) process injection or library loading from /tmp or /var/tmp.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Edge to Internal Confluence
suggestion.rationale: Article describes pivot 'from edge appliance to enterprise compromise' and 'internal Confluence server' — no UC for detecting lateral movement post-edge-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from F5/edge appliance to internal Confluence server (typical ports 8080, 8443, 443) with payloads. Correlate with successful Confluence authentication or exploitation attempt signatures. Alert on edge device making internal network scan or port-scan behavior.

suggestion.title: Identity Compromise via Credential Theft Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'credential theft and identity compromise' — no UC detecting credential access pipeline from Confluence database or memory.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Confluence user database access (confluence.cfg.xml, database files), authentication token extraction (session files, login attempts with harvested credentials), and subsequent use of stolen credentials across domain. Alert on Confluence process reading its own credential stores or config files, followed by successful logins from unexpected IPs.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email with Prometheus Malware Attachment to Government Targets
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'Ghostwriter Targets Ukraine Government Entities with Prometheus Phishing Malware'—phishing is the explicit delivery mechanism; no use case captured this initial access.

Correlate sender domains with known phishing infrastructure. Alert on low email volume to high-value government accounts with external attachment headers.

suggestion.title: Prometheus Malware Execution via User Action
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'Prometheus Phishing Malware'—execution phase is implicit in phishing+malware pattern but not mapped to detections or kill chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution with parent=explorer.exe, winword.exe, or outlook.exe spawning suspicious child processes (powershell, cmd, rundll32) with low-reputation file hashes or living-off-the-land binary usage. Correlate with recent attachment opens within 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: Prometheus Command and Control Communication
suggestion.rationale: Phishing+malware campaigns require C2; article does not specify C2 IOCs or detection rules for post-exploitation network activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from infected endpoint to non-whitelisted IPs/domains. Flag DNS queries to newly registered domains or those with Russian IP geolocation from government networks. Detect anomalous port usage (non-standard HTTP/HTTPS) for C2 beacon callback patterns.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Initial Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Government entity compromises typically involve credential theft and lateral movement; article genre suggests multi-stage attack but pipeline captured no lateral movement detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on failed RDP/SMB connections from compromised workstations to multiple internal targets within 15 minutes, especially to high-value targets (domain controllers, file servers). Detect pass-the-hash attempts (credential reuse without login) and unusual service account activity.

suggestion.title: HTTP 500 / SQL Errors from YesWiki Bazar Form Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'inject arbitrary SQL into an INSERT statement.' Blind SQLi typically generates error responses during enumeration. Current UCs detect request volume but not response errors that signal active probing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP 500 errors or SQL error keywords ('MySQL', 'SQL syntax', 'database error', 'constraint violation') in responses from /BazaR?vue=formulaire endpoints within a 5-minute window. Combine with source IP and escalate if repeated across multiple requests.

suggestion.title: Oversized POST Parameters to YesWiki Form-Import
suggestion.rationale: Article describes injection into INSERT statement via form-import path. SQLi payloads are verbose; detect unusually large request bodies or parameter values that exceed baseline for form submissions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag POST requests to BazaR endpoints where body size exceeds 8KB or individual parameter values contain SQL keywords (UNION, SELECT, OR, INSERT) or quote-escape sequences. Correlate with non-browser user-agent for higher fidelity.

suggestion.title: Enumeration of yeswiki_users or Database Schema via SQLi
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'read the full database, including yeswiki_users.password hashes.' Post-injection, attackers enumerate schema via INFORMATION_SCHEMA queries or table SELECTs. HTTP-layer detections miss this critical phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If database query logging is enabled, hunt for SELECT queries against INFORMATION_SCHEMA.TABLES or INFORMATION_SCHEMA.COLUMNS followed immediately by SELECT * FROM yeswiki_users or SELECT password FROM yeswiki_users. Multiple failed queries (blind SQLi) followed by successful credential retrieval is the expected pattern.

suggestion.title: Bulk Extraction of Password Hashes from YesWiki Users Table
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'read...yeswiki_users.password hashes.' Attackers will extract all hashes post-exploitation. Database audit logs should show anomalous table scans or full table selects not matching application query patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sequential or repeated SELECT statements on yeswiki_users.password column from single source IP/session context within short timeframe (seconds to minutes). Compare against baseline application queries; legitimate reads should be infrequent and user-scoped.

suggestion.title: Account Creation or Privilege Escalation via SQLi INSERT/UPDATE
suggestion.rationale: Unauthenticated SQLi into INSERT statement permits account creation or privilege escalation for persistence. Article does not mention observed privilege escalation, but is a logical follow-on to database write access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for INSERT or UPDATE statements against yeswiki_users with admin=1 or privilege flags, especially those originating from Bazar form-import request context or lacking corresponding user-creation events in application logs.

suggestion.title: Successful FileBrowser Quantum path traversal exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'the move/copy/rename operates on a path outside the shared directory' but no hunt detects successful execution via HTTP 200/success response codes to PATCH with traversal payloads. UC_15_1 detects the request form only, not outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for HTTP 200/204 responses to PATCH `/public/api/resources` containing `fromPath` or `toPath` with `..` segments. Correlate with subsequent file system operations (move/delete/write) on files outside the documented share directory to confirm traversal success.

suggestion.title: File system operations on paths outside FileBrowser share directory post-PATCH
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability enables file operations 'outside shared directory' but no hunt looks for the actual file-level impact (move, rename, delete on out-of-bounds paths). Current hunts stop at the HTTP layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful PATCH requests to `/public/api/resources` with `..` payloads against file system logs showing the FileBrowser process (typically unprivileged) creating, modifying, or deleting files whose paths fall outside the documented `share.Path` root directory.

suggestion.title: ISP/Telecom Infrastructure Compromise via SSH, RDP, or Trusted Relationship Exploit
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Hackers Abuse Middle East Telecom Networks.' This describes initial compromise of ISP edge infrastructure—the foundation of the attack. T1199 (Trusted Relationship) or T1133 (External Remote Services) or T1021.004 (SSH) are the primary paths to ISP access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect failed/successful authentication attempts to telecom AS boundary routers, VPN concentrators, or BGP route reflectors from external IPs. Track privilege escalation on infrastructure devices immediately post-authentication. Correlate geolocation of login source with known threat regions.

suggestion.title: Large-Scale C2 Traffic Tunneled Through Compromised Telecom Backbone
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly claims 'large-scale Command-and-Control Operations' via telecom networks. Pipeline produced zero detection for C2 traffic exfiltration through ISP infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag persistent outbound connections from ISP infrastructure to known or suspected C2 domains/IPs. Detect DNS queries for DGA-like domains or suspicious TLDs originating from telecom backbone. Correlate command-like HTTP user-agents or binary payloads in traffic flows.

suggestion.title: BGP Route Hijacking or Anomalous ASN Announcements from Telecom Provider
suggestion.rationale: Telecom infrastructure compromise frequently manifests as BGP anomalies, route hijacks, or unexpected path prepending. This is a direct indicator of infrastructure-level compromise but pipeline produced no detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor BGP updates from Middle East telecom ASNs for unexpected route announcements, path length anomalies, AS-path prepending, or RPKI validation failures. Cross-reference with downstream BGP community tags and validate against known legitimate ISP operations.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from ISP Infrastructure to Downstream Customer Networks
suggestion.rationale: Title's phrase 'large-scale' implies victims beyond the ISP itself. Telecom compromise is a pivot point to customer networks, yet pipeline generated zero lateral-movement detection use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify traffic originating from ISP backbone infrastructure (peering points, route reflectors) to customer networks outside normal BGP paths. Alert on infrastructure-to-customer SSH/RDP/WinRM connections with binary payloads or suspicious process spawning.

suggestion.title: Installation of Known-Compromised NPM Package Version
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'art-template npm Package' was backdoored. Pipeline must detect when a flagged compromised version is installed. No behavioral or signature detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference package installation events (npm install, yarn install, npm update) against maintained CVE/advisory list of known-compromised packages. Alert on installation of art-template versions matching published compromise range. Include lockfile modifications and dependency resolution logs.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Post-Install Script Execution During Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Watering-hole attacks via npm packages execute payload via malicious scripts field in package.json during install. Phrase 'Launch Watering-Hole Attacks' implies active execution; pipeline generated no detection for this critical execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or bash spawned as direct child of npm.exe or node.exe during install/update operations. Flag processes with obfuscated arguments, Base64 encoding flags, registry modifications, or suspicious network utility invocations (curl, wget). Baseline and exclude known legitimate post-install scripts from popular packages.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Outbound Network Connections from Node.js Child Processes
suggestion.rationale: Watering-hole attacks require C2 callback for attack delivery. Article implies command-and-control phase ('launch attacks'). Pipeline missed network-based detection for backdoor communication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound TCP/UDP connections from node.js processes to destinations outside curated whitelist of npm CDN/registry IPs and known-benign package dependencies. Correlate timing with recent npm install/update. Detect DNS requests from node processes to suspicious or newly-registered domains.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized NPM Package Version Release or Metadata Tampering
suggestion.rationale: To distribute backdoor, attacker compromised package publish capability. Pipeline missed initial-access detection at registry level—should detect abnormal package release activity, new versions from unexpected accounts, or rapid version churn.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry publish API and audit logs for art-template: flag unexpected new versions, releases from non-canonical maintainer accounts, version metadata modifications (new scripts, dependencies added), or multi-version releases within short windows. Establish baseline of legitimate release cadence and maintainer accounts.

suggestion.title: Rapid Version Yanking or Emergency Package Unpublishing
suggestion.rationale: When compromised package discovered, maintainers typically unpublish or emergency-patch. Pipeline should detect incident-response pattern indicating active exploitation discovery. Phrase 'Hackers Backdoor' implies recent event with remediation activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unpublish or rapid version removal of popular packages (>1M weekly downloads). Correlate against CVE/CERT advisories published within 24h of unpublish event. Alert on emergency patch releases (patch bump surge) following security disclosure. Flag to threat-intel team for investigation into active exploitation.

suggestion.title: Dependency Chain Pollution via Transitive Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Compromised package may be installed indirectly as dependency of legitimate packages. Pipeline must account for transitive compromise—developers using packages that depend on art-template become victims without direct install awareness.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse package-lock.json and yarn.lock for transitive dependencies matching known-compromised packages. Alert on any package (direct or transitive) pinning a compromised version, even if parent package appears benign. Monitor dependency resolution for unexpected nested installs of flagged packages.

suggestion.title: NF-e Invoice Lure — Malicious Batch File Distribution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'malicious batch file named Consultar_NF-e.bat distributed via WhatsApp or phishing links'—foundational initial-access detection completely missed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .bat files with names mimicking Brazilian document types or financial institutions, especially Consultar_* or Nota_* patterns. Alert on batch files received via email, messaging, or downloaded from non-corporate file-sharing; correlation with financial-sector targeting strengthens signal.

suggestion.title: PowerShell Execution Hidden Within Batch File
suggestion.rationale: Article states batch file 'triggers concealed PowerShell command'—direct code execution evasion pattern critical to this attack and a high-signal detection absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PowerShell (powershell.exe or pwsh.exe) spawned directly or indirectly from batch files (.bat, .cmd). Flag encoded, obfuscated, or dynamically reconstructed command lines. Monitor for parent-process chains: cmd.exe → powershell.exe with suspicious argument patterns.

suggestion.title: AES-256 Encrypted Payload Staging via msedge.txt
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'downloads encrypted payload (msedge.txt) via AES-256 encryption'—staged encrypted downloads are high-fidelity C2 indicator missed by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for downloads of files with deceptive names (msedge.txt, st.txt, st.php, payload.php) from suspicious domains or IP:port combinations. Flag retrieval immediately after batch/PowerShell execution. Inspect file entropy for encrypted content.

suggestion.title: Scheduled Task Persistence — Minute-Interval PowerShell Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article documents 'hidden scheduled task launching PowerShell every minute for up to 9,999 days'—persistence mechanism central to attack operationalization, not detected.

suggestion.title: Banking Overlay Injection — Fake Security Prompt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'injects fake banking overlays mimicking security updates'—fraud-enabling collection mechanism that should trigger impact-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected window/UI injection into banking applications (Itau, Bradesco, Santander, Caixa, Banco do Brasil clients). Flag screen-capture API calls immediately before network activity to banking domains. Alert on unexpected pop-up overlays or prompts in banking session context.

suggestion.title: QR Code Replacement During Financial Transactions
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'intercepts/replaces Pix QR codes during transactions'—transaction fraud indicator tied to Brazilian payment systems, critical to impact assessment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate screen-capture events (T1113) with clipboard or file-system writes containing QR code data during active banking sessions. Alert on clipboard modifications following image-processing or screen-capture API calls. Flag session where Pix transaction QR differs from server-provided QR.

suggestion.title: FreePBX Unauthorized User Account Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes six-layer persistence; user account creation is a standard persistence vector. No detection UC was generated despite 'maintain access' implying account creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FreePBX admin user database or system audit logs for creation of new local accounts outside maintenance windows. Watch for accounts created with default or weak credentials. Cross-reference with changes to FreePBX permission assignments.

suggestion.title: FreePBX Configuration File Persistence Detection
suggestion.rationale: Six-layer persistence implies modification of configuration files as a persistence mechanism. Article emphasizes 'maintain access' but pipeline generated no config tampering detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor modifications to /etc/asterisk config files, FreePBX database backend configs, and extension configuration XML. Alert on edits outside change windows. Correlate with unusual process or user access to FreePBX directories.

suggestion.title: FreePBX Scheduled Task Persistence Detection
suggestion.rationale: Multi-layer persistence architecture described in title should include scheduled task abuse. No UC for cron or at-job persistence on FreePBX was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cron tables (/var/spool/cron/crontabs/) and at daemon for new entries added by unprivileged or service accounts. Alert on cron jobs executing from /tmp or world-writable directories, or invoking shell interpreters with obfuscated parameters.

suggestion.title: FreePBX Web Shell Implantation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Six-layer persistence on a web-facing PBX system highly likely includes web shell placement. Article title implies sustained access mechanism not captured by any use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FreePBX web directories (/var/www/html/admin, /var/www/html/configs) for creation of new PHP, Python, or shell script files. Cross-reference with HTTP access logs for unusual POST requests or parameter patterns. Alert on executable permissions added to non-standard files.

suggestion.title: FreePBX Privilege Escalation via Service Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Maintaining persistent access on a system-level service (Asterisk/FreePBX) likely requires privilege escalation or service-level backdoors. No privilege escalation or service manipulation UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Asterisk/FreePBX service startup scripts and systemd unit files for unauthorized modifications. Alert on processes spawned by the asterisk service user running commands outside expected binaries. Detect sudoers file modifications allowing unprivileged users to restart/reload services.

suggestion.title: FreePBX Module Backdoor Installation
suggestion.rationale: PBX systems support custom modules/extensions for functionality extension. 'Six-layer persistence' likely includes persistent module installation not addressed by any generated UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor the FreePBX modules directory and AMI (Asterisk Manager Interface) module logs for installation of unsigned or unknown modules. Alert on modules loading from non-standard paths or created by non-root users. Cross-reference module names against known legitimate FreePBX extensions.

suggestion.title: DDoS Botnet C2 Outbound Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'DDoS Botnet Operator' implying operational C2 infrastructure; botnet coordination requires command channels. No UC captures abnormal outbound traffic patterns, beaconing, or C2 protocol indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sustained outbound connections from non-server endpoints to rare/newly-seen IP:port combinations at regular intervals; correlate with malware hash, known botnet C2 domains, or DGA-derived domains. Detect anomalous DNS queries to infrastructure domains associated with Kimwolf operators.

suggestion.title: Volumetric DDoS Attack Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'DDoS-for-hire attacks' and botnet operator role; DDoS attacks are the primary impact vector but pipeline contains no detection for volumetric/UDP flood/SYN flood patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sudden surge in outbound traffic from single or clustered infected hosts to external targets (volumetric flood signature); monitor for anomalous packet rates, UDP floods, or SYN floods originating from compromised systems. Threshold alert on outbound bandwidth > 500 Mbps or packet rate > 1M pps to non-whitelisted destinations.

suggestion.title: Botnet Recruitment / Exploitation Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies subject as 'DDoS Botnet Operator' — implies active botnet spreading, vulnerability exploitation, or malware distribution. No UC addresses how systems become compromised or added to botnet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect exploitation attempts against known vulnerabilities correlated with botnet families; flag failed/successful attempts to execute payloads from suspicious URLs. Monitor for indicators of botnet payload execution (process creation from temp directories, registry modifications, scheduled tasks for persistence).

suggestion.title: DDoS-as-a-Service Command Panel Access
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'DDoS-for-hire' service model — implies web/remote access infrastructure (admin panel, payment portal, attack control panel). No UC covers detection of panel logins or control-plane activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP(S) connections to known DDoS panel infrastructure (known IP:port, domains), unusual login patterns from distributed IPs, or payment processing activity correlated with botnet C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Kernel Driver Loading
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD exploits vulnerable drivers to gain kernel access without requiring custom exploitation code. Article discusses 'making vulnerable drivers exploitable'—pipeline must detect driver loading events from user-mode processes attempting kernel access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned, low-reputation, or known-vulnerable drivers being loaded into memory. Alert on processes in %WINDIR%\Temp or user writable paths loading .sys files, or registry modifications to HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\* adding driver image paths pointing outside System32 or trusted driver folders.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Kernel Driver Installation via SC or Registry
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD requires installing a vulnerable driver; attack 'does not require hardware' suggests local installation mechanism via service control or direct registry modification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of 'sc.exe create', 'sc.exe start', or direct HKLM registry writes to Services keys, especially when source process is user-mode or from temp directories. Cross-correlate driver image path with vulnerable driver signatures (CVE-linked driver versions).

suggestion.title: Process Attempting Kernel Communication via Vulnerable Driver Device Path
suggestion.rationale: Once a vulnerable driver is loaded, exploitation requires user-mode process to communicate with kernel via device interface (e.g., \Device\, \Global??, CreateFile on driver device).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes opening handles to driver device objects or calling device I/O control (DeviceIoControl). Alert on non-system processes repeatedly querying or writing to \Device\* or \Global?? paths, especially from LOLBin or command-line contexts.

suggestion.title: Unsigned Code Execution Following Driver Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article frames BYOVD as enabling privilege escalation 'without hardware'; the payload execution step must be detected as kernel code execution or process elevation immediately following driver load.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate driver installation events with subsequent process token elevation, privilege level changes, or access to SYSTEM-owned resources. Alert if a user-mode child process gains SYSTEM privileges within 5 seconds of a driver load event in the parent process chain.

suggestion.title: Driver Persistence via Boot Registry or Service Autostart
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD exploits are typically leveraged for persistent access; detection must cover driver registration for autostart to survive reboot.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services for new entries with Type=0x1 (kernel driver) and Start=0x2 (auto-start). Alert on registry modifications that add driver entries with unsigned, low-reputation, or test-signed image paths.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Workflow Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack 'targets 5,561 repos with malicious CI/CD workflows'—direct evidence that the primary attack vector is injected/compromised workflow files in .github/workflows/ directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation or modification of .github/workflows/*.yml files with suspicious payloads: base64-encoded commands, exfiltration of secrets via curl/wget, environment variable logging, or inline script execution from untrusted sources. Correlate with commits from accounts not in CODEOWNERS or from unusual IP/geo.

suggestion.title: Repository Compromise via Account Takeover or Token Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Attacker achieved write access to 5,561 repos to inject workflows—requires either account compromise or stolen OAuth tokens. Article implies scale suggests credential compromise as initial access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect commits and workflow modifications from anomalous geographic locations, new IP ranges, or at off-hours compared to account baseline. Flag sudden bulk repository access pattern changes or OAuth scope elevation requests requesting 'repo' and 'workflow' permissions.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise: Automated Package Publishing Post-Injection
suggestion.rationale: With 5,561 repos compromised (likely open-source), attackers can auto-publish malicious package versions via CI/CD, directly impacting downstream consumers.
log_sources: Package registry logs (npm, PyPI, RubyGems, Maven)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate workflow file modifications with new package releases within 1-24 hours. Alert on version bumps published immediately after .github/workflows/ changes or from CI/CD systems with new/unusual OAuth tokens.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration via CI/CD Environment Variable Access
suggestion.rationale: CI/CD workflows execute with access to repository secrets (API keys, credentials). Malicious workflows can log or exfiltrate ${{ secrets.* }} to attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on workflow steps that reference secrets.* in subprocess calls, logging statements, or network requests (curl, wget, nc). Detect unusual artifact uploads or environment variable writes to external storage systems.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement: Cross-Repository Access via Compromised Tokens
suggestion.rationale: An attacker controlling workflow execution gains the token's permissions—can access organization's private repos, deploy keys, and GitHub Apps with escalated privileges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor CI/CD runners for git operations accessing organization repositories outside the current project scope. Flag runs cloning private repos with no historical access baseline from that workflow/actor.

suggestion.title: Suspicious GitHub Actions Workflow Modification in Public Repos
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation across 5,500+ public repositories via workflow abuse—core attack vector that should generate detection for .github/workflows/ changes in public repos, especially pull requests adding exfiltration steps.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions workflow file changes (.github/workflows/*.yml) in public repositories for additions of credential export commands, HTTP POST to external URLs, or environment variable dumps. Flag pull requests modifying workflows from low-reputation accounts.

suggestion.title: Bulk Credential Access in GitHub Actions Environment
suggestion.rationale: Megalodon exfiltrates secrets—should detect when Actions workflows enumerate or access multiple secrets/environment variables in single run, or when secrets are dumped to logs or sent externally.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Actions jobs that access >5 secrets in a single workflow, export env vars to stdout, or use `env` command without legitimate build context. Correlate with outbound network connections from runner IPs.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration via GitHub Actions Runner Network Egress
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly mentions exfiltration across repositories—should detect outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections from GitHub-hosted or self-hosted runner IPs to attacker infrastructure, especially POST/PUT with credential-like payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from GitHub Actions runner IP ranges to non-GitHub/non-package-manager external hosts. Flag POST requests containing patterns matching GitHub secrets, API tokens, or PATs. Baseline against legitimate dependencies.

suggestion.title: Malicious Pull Request Adding GitHub Actions Workflows to Public Repos
suggestion.rationale: Megalodon uses compromised workflows—should detect PRs that introduce or modify .github/workflows files with commands that access credentials or initiate external connections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag pull requests that add/modify workflow files containing: 'secrets.*', 'env.*' dumping, curl/wget to external IPs, base64-encoded commands, or multi-stage exfiltration logic. Prioritize PRs from newly created or low-activity accounts.

suggestion.title: Cross-Repository Secret Enumeration Pattern
suggestion.rationale: 5,500+ repos affected implies systematic enumeration—should detect when single actor/account/IP triggers secret access across multiple public repositories in short time window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate GitHub API calls to list/access repository secrets across >50 distinct public repos within 1 hour from same source (IP, account, token). Establish baseline of legitimate automated secret operations per org.

suggestion.title: DDoS Botnet C2 Infrastructure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly links infrastructure to NoName057(16) DDoS attacks: 'pro-Russian hacktivist group NoName057(16), which has previously targeted key organizations with distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks.' No detection rule generated for this attack type.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect hosting infrastructure with synchronized outbound connections to numerous distinct targets from single ASN/datacenter, non-standard port patterns, high-volume data transfers characteristic of DDoS botnet C2, or known NoName057(16) command infrastructure signatures.

suggestion.title: Sanctions Evasion via Infrastructure Rebranding
suggestion.rationale: Article documents deliberate post-sanctions infrastructure transfer: 'EU added Stark Industries to the list...web hosting infrastructure was transferred to a newly created Dutch company that investigators believe acted as a front.' Defense evasion pattern undetected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag rapid IP/ASN reassignments or domain migrations occurring 0-6 months post-sanction announcement, involving newly registered companies with apparent service continuity, shared upstream providers with sanctioned predecessors, or overlapping technical contacts.

suggestion.title: Front Company Infrastructure Acquisition Clustering
suggestion.rationale: WorkTitans B.V. identified as front for sanctioned entities with rapid large-scale server acquisition: 'newly created Dutch company...seized 800 servers.' No detection for this persistence/infrastructure pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect newly registered (within 12 months) entities rapidly acquiring 50+ servers, inherited IP ranges from sanctioned predecessors, tied via administrative contact, upstream ASN, or physical colocation facility to known malicious infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Major Internet Exchange Abuse for Botnet Transit
suggestion.rationale: Article details intentional IX leveraging for operations: 'supplied high-capacity connectivity to major internet exchanges in Amsterdam and Frankfurt, acting as the transport layer.' No UC for IX abuse by state-sponsored botnet infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify ASNs with suspicious IX transit patterns (AMS-IX, DE-CIX) carrying high-volume DDoS traffic, known botnet C2 signatures, or bulk disinformation payloads. Correlate with bulletproof hosting indicators or sanctioned entity associations.

suggestion.title: Multi-Facility Botnet Server Clustering
suggestion.rationale: Coordinated seizure across geographically separated datacenters reveals botnet structure: 'raids in data centers in Dronten and Schiphol-Rijk...seized 800 servers.' Pattern of distributed server synchronization undetected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect 50+ servers across 2-3 colocation facilities or single ASN exhibiting synchronized beaconing, matching outbound connection timing, common C2 infrastructure, or correlated malware payloads without legitimate business purpose.

suggestion.title: State-Sponsored Disinformation Infrastructure Hosting
suggestion.rationale: Article attributes infrastructure to Russian state disinformation: 'provided support to actions by the Russian Federation...information manipulation and disruption of public and economic systems.' No detection rule for state-sponsored influence campaign hosting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate hosting infrastructure indicators (ASN, IP ranges, registrant data) with documented Russian state disinformation campaigns, inauthentic social amplification, or bulk media distribution patterns. Flag multi-vector inauthentic content serving from single hosting cluster.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Nx Console Extension Installation from Untrusted Source
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes supply-chain compromise of Nx Console extension. Users installing malicious .vsix or from non-Marketplace sources is the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VS Code command-line extension installation (--install-extension flag) pointing to non-marketplace URLs. Alert on .vsix files downloaded from suspicious sources or lacking valid publisher signatures.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Code Execution from VS Code Extension Runtime
suggestion.rationale: Compromised extension executes malicious code in user context—core attack mechanism. Detection must capture unexpected child processes spawned by VS Code or extension host.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process creation where parent is Code.exe or extension process, child is cmd/powershell/curl/wget, or unexpected network-capable child processes. Establish baseline of legitimate extension behavior first.

suggestion.title: Persistence via VS Code Extension Activation Events
suggestion.rationale: Malicious extensions establish persistence through settings.json or launch event hooks that trigger code execution on workspace/user initialization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected modifications to .vscode/settings.json or launch.json within user home or workspace directories, especially adding activationEvents or commands pointing to external scripts or URLs.

suggestion.title: Network Command-and-Control from Compromised Extension
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromised extension establishes C2 channel for ongoing attacker control. VS Code process network activity should be monitored for anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect VS Code process connecting to newly registered or suspicious domains, non-standard ports, or beaconing patterns. Correlate installation timestamp with first outbound connection.

suggestion.title: Credential Theft from Developer Environment
suggestion.rationale: Compromised extension running in developer IDE has access to stored credentials: git tokens, SSH keys, API keys in settings/home directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process access to ~/.ssh, ~/.git, .vscode/settings.json (secrets storage), or environment variable reads for API_KEY/TOKEN patterns from extension host process.

suggestion.title: ROADtools Enumeration Against Azure Tenant
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly discusses ROADtools misuse by nation-state actors. ROADtools is open-source Azure enumeration framework used for discovery. Article keywords reference Entra ID and Microsoft Graph API enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalous Microsoft Graph API calls consistent with ROADtools enumeration patterns: GetUsers, GetGroups, ListMembers, GetApplication queries in rapid succession or from unexpected IPs. Flag service principals or accounts making large volumes of directory enumeration queries outside normal business hours.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Entra ID Conditional Access Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Nation-state actors using ROADtools target Entra ID and Azure infrastructure. Keywords cite Entra ID and Microsoft Azure; article discusses nation-state tactics implying privileged access abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sign-in events where MFA is bypassed, legacy authentication protocols are used from flagged IPs, or conditional access policies are modified shortly before lateral movement. Look for impossible-travel scenarios or sign-ins from rare geographic locations followed by privilege escalation.

suggestion.title: Service Principal Credential Theft / App Registration Abuse
suggestion.rationale: ROADtools enables attackers to enumerate and modify application registrations. Nation-state actors use service principal tokens for persistent access to cloud resources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation of new application secret credentials by non-admin accounts, modification of app role assignments outside change windows, or service principal authentication from unfamiliar IP ranges. Flag any app registration with overly broad permissions (Directory.ReadWrite.All) created in last 30 days.

suggestion.title: Excessive Delegated Permissions Granted to OAuth Applications
suggestion.rationale: ROADtools and nation-state cloud tactics involve compromising delegated permissions to exfiltrate data. Entra ID OAuth apps are targets for permission escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect consent events for applications requesting broad scopes (Mail.ReadWrite, Calendars.Read, Files.ReadWrite.All) from unexpected user segments or geolocations. Flag repeat grant denials followed by success as sign of adversary persistence.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via Microsoft Graph API Using Stolen Tokens
suggestion.rationale: Nation-state attackers using ROADtools ultimately aim to access sensitive data. Graph API is primary interface for cloud data exfiltration once access is obtained.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large-scale Graph API calls fetching user data (GetUser in loops, ListUsers with $top=999), mailbox reads via API from service principal, or file downloads outside typical user patterns. Correlate with compromised service principal tokens identified in other detections.

suggestion.title: Suspicious ROADtools Script Execution or GitHub Clone
suggestion.rationale: ROADtools is open-source framework. Nation-state actors download and execute it locally or remotely. Article explicitly discusses misuse of this tooling.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process execution of Python scripts or PowerShell that invoke ROADtools (roadrecon, roadtx) modules or download from GitHub repositories containing ROADtools. Alert on Git clone of roadtools-ad-2.0 repo. Flag execution from service accounts or during off-hours.

suggestion.title: RDP Brute Force and Initial Access Abuse Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'Russian Threat Groups Use RDP' as initial access vector. No detection rule was generated despite this being the primary attack surface outlined in the headline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for failed RDP logon sequences from a single source IP followed by successful authentication, especially against privileged accounts or outside business hours. Correlate with geographic anomalies and VPN/proxy routes.

suggestion.title: VPN Credential Compromise and Lateral Access
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly lists VPN attacks as initial-access vector. Pipeline produced no detection logic for anomalous VPN authentication or abuse of compromised VPN credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect VPN logins from new ASNs/geolocations, logins to dormant accounts, service accounts authenticating via VPN, or bulk credential validation attempts against VPN gateways.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Software Compromise Execution Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly names 'Supply Chain Attacks' as threat technique. Pipeline failed to generate detections for compromised vendor software deployment, suspicious package manager activity, or unauthorized software updates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution or deployment of vendor software with abnormal code signatures, modification timestamps outside vendor release windows, or execution from unexpected paths. Flag unsigned or revoked-certificate executables from trusted vendors.

suggestion.title: Social Engineering Phishing and Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'Social Engineering' as initial-access vector. Zero detections were generated for phishing, malicious links, credential harvesting, or reconnaissance targeting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with credential-request patterns, lookalike sender domains, unusual reply-to addresses, or links to credential-harvesting infrastructure. Flag clicks on high-risk URLs by users in target industries (utilities, finance, government).

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Lateral Movement from RDP/VPN Beachhead
suggestion.rationale: Successful initial access via RDP/VPN should be correlated with downstream lateral movement and privilege escalation. Pipeline missed detection logic bridging initial access to exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate external RDP/VPN logons with subsequent lateral movement: unusual service-account usage, administrative share access from the RDP/VPN entry point, or privilege escalation attempts within 4 hours of external authentication.

suggestion.title: AppDomainManager Registry Hijacking for CLR Hijacking
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'AppDomainManager hijacking' as a core persistence technique. HKLM\Software\Microsoft\.NETFramework AppDomainManager or HKCU\Software\Classes modifications are detectable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on registry writes to *\Software\Microsoft\.NETFramework or *\Software\Classes containing 'AppDomainManager' values. Correlate with .NET process spawns and CLR.dll/mscoree.dll image loads in non-standard hosts. Flag unsigned DLLs in CLR profiler paths.

suggestion.title: DLL Sideloading of Legitimate Application Binaries
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'DLL Sideloading' as attack vector. Legitimate executable in system/program files loading DLL from non-standard path (temp, appdata, exe's own dir) with matching import name.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect parent process from trusted path (C:\Program Files, C:\Windows\System32) loading library with matching name (kernel32.dll, etc.) from user-writable or temp directories. Monitor for unusual LoadImage/LoadLibrary API calls from legit executables to non-standard paths.

suggestion.title: MiniJunk / MiniUpdate RAT Execution and Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'MiniJunk' and 'MiniUpdate' as new RAT malware families deployed by Screening Serpens. Malware families must be surfaced as IOC/malware families for endpoint detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish file hashes, file paths, and behavioral signatures for MiniJunk/MiniUpdate (e.g., spawn of cmd.exe/powershell.exe, C2 callbacks, registry persistence mechanisms). Flag unknown executables matching observed malware family characteristics.

suggestion.title: Social Engineering Phishing Targeting Tech/Defense Sectors
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'social engineering' as initial access vector and explicitly targets 'tech and defense sectors'. Phishing/credential harvesting should have dedicated detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with malicious attachments (macro-enabled Office, archives, executables) sent to tech/defense industry recipients. Correlate email delivery with subsequent DLL load anomalies, AppDomain registry writes, or process injection. Flag credential harvesting phish templates.

suggestion.title: CLR Injection into Non-.NET Host Processes
suggestion.rationale: AppDomainManager hijacking requires CLR hosting in unusual processes. Detect CLR injection into cmd.exe, explorer.exe, or services that should not host managed code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for mscoree.dll or CLR.dll being loaded by processes outside standard .NET hosts (devenv.exe, dotnet.exe, msbuild.exe). Flag LoadLibrary calls for .NET runtime DLLs in cmd.exe, explorer.exe, svchost.exe, or rare services with unsigned/unattested CLR profilers.

suggestion.title: Detect Composer Installation of Known-Malicious Laravel-Lang Versions
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 233 compromised package versions distributed via Packagist/Composer. Pipeline missed the primary delivery vector: 'When developers installed affected packages through Packagist via Composer, the compromised src/helpers.php file executed automatically.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Composer install/update commands that resolve to Laravel-Lang package versions released between early-mid 2026 matching the 233 affected versions. Alert on composer.lock file entries for laravel-lang with version numbers known to be compromised. Track Packagist package downloads for these specific versions.

suggestion.title: Detect C2 Communication to flipboxstudio[.]info Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies C2 endpoints: 'disables SSL verification and fetches a secondary script from an obfuscated command-and-control server' at flipboxstudio[.]info/payload and /exfil. Pipeline extracted zero network IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DNS queries to flipboxstudio[.]info or subdomains. Monitor for HTTPS connections to flipboxstudio[.]info:443 with POST requests to /payload or /exfil paths. Flag connections with SSL verification disabled (CURLOPT_SSL_VERIFYPEER=false in process telemetry).

suggestion.title: Detect Malicious src/helpers.php Execution via PHP Autoload
suggestion.rationale: Attack exploited Composer autoload.files directive: 'the compromised src/helpers.php file executed automatically due to Composer's autoload.files directive, effectively hid the malware from standard repository audits.' No detection for autoload-triggered execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PHP process creation initiated from Laravel package directories (vendor/laravel-lang/ paths). Alert on exec()/system() calls originating from src/helpers.php. Detect background PHP execution (php -r or php script) spawned during Composer operations. Flag `cscript.exe` or VBS execution triggered from PHP processes.

suggestion.title: Detect Credential Harvesting Module Execution
suggestion.rationale: Malware 'contained 15 specialized collector modules targeting: Cloud access keys (AWS, GCP, Azure, DigitalOcean), Infrastructure configurations (Kubernetes, Docker, HashiCorp Vault), Developer credentials (SSH keys, Git tokens, shell histories), Browser passwords and cryptocurrency wallets.' Zero detection for credential access activities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file enumeration targeting ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.config (Git), browser credential stores. Alert on processes reading /etc/kubernetes/config, HashiCorp Vault token paths, Docker socket access. Detect cat/grep operations on .bash_history, AWS credential files, SSH key files originating from temporary directories or Laravel package paths.

suggestion.title: Detect Marker File and Stealer Payload Persistence in .laravel_locale
suggestion.rationale: Malware uses persistence markers: 'infection marker: <tmp>/.laravel_locale/<md5_hash>, stealer payload: <tmp>/.laravel_locale/<12 random hex chars>.php, Windows launcher: <tmp>/.laravel_locale/<8 random hex chars>.vbs.' Pipeline failed to extract file artifacts or persistence techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation of .laravel_locale/ directory in temp paths (/tmp, %TEMP%). Monitor for file creation matching pattern [a-f0-9]{32}.php (md5 hash) or [a-f0-9]{24}.php (random hex) in .laravel_locale. Detect .vbs file generation with random hex names in this directory. Flag redundant marker checks (infection guard logic) via stat()/access() syscalls.

suggestion.title: Detect GitHub Tag Manipulation for Supply Chain Redirect
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector explicitly described: 'The attackers exploited GitHub's version tagging system rather than committing directly to repositories. They manipulated tags to direct users toward malicious forks.' Pipeline missed GitHub-level attack detection and 700 repository compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub audit logs for rapid tag creation/modification across Laravel-Lang repositories. Alert on tag pushes that mismatch commit content (tags pointing to fork repositories vs. official repo). Detect API calls creating/updating 700+ tags across related repositories in short timeframes. Flag authentication anomalies (new device/location) during tag manipulation.

suggestion.title: F5 BIG-IP Remote Code Execution or Authentication Bypass Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Hackers Exploit F5 BIG-IP Appliance'—a public-facing attack surface. Pipeline produced no IOCs or kill-chain phases for initial access despite this being the entry point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor F5 BIG-IP management and data plane logs for failed authentication followed by successful exploitation patterns, HTTP requests to known vulnerable endpoints (e.g., management interfaces, iControl REST), or abnormal iRule modifications. Correlate with outbound connection attempts immediately following access logs.

suggestion.title: SSH Access Originating from F5 BIG-IP to Internal Linux Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Gain SSH Access and Pivot Into Enterprise Linux Networks'—explicit lateral movement over SSH. No use case generated for this lateral movement phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SSH connections (port 22) initiated from the F5 BIG-IP appliance IP address to internal Linux systems that would not normally initiate outbound SSH. Flag first-time SSH connections from BIG-IP to multiple internal hosts (fan-out pattern). Correlate with SSH key exchange events and authentication successes.

suggestion.title: SSH Credential Usage Originating from F5 BIG-IP Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Hackers' gaining SSH access through BIG-IP compromise—implies credential harvesting or key theft from BIG-IP to facilitate persistent SSH access. No credential access or persistence detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on SSH_KEYSCAN commands or SSH key enumeration attempts executed on BIG-IP system. Look for /root/.ssh or /etc/ssh directory access patterns in F5 audit logs. Monitor for SSH public keys added to BIG-IP user accounts or configuration files immediately post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: BIG-IP Configuration Changes and Administrative Abuse Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Successful BIG-IP compromise would require persistence mechanisms—firewall rules, administrative accounts, or iRule modifications—to maintain access. No persistence or defense-evasion detections proposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor F5 administrative logs for creation of new administrative users or privilege escalation of existing users post-exploitation. Alert on iRule insertions, virtual server modifications, or persistence backdoors (e.g., scheduler-based reverse shells). Compare configuration snapshots against baseline to detect unauthorized persistence objects.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance and Discovery Activity from BIG-IP Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: After establishing SSH foothold, attackers would perform internal network reconnaissance. Article mentions 'Pivot Into Enterprise Linux Networks' but pipeline did not identify discovery-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DNS enumeration, network scanning (nmap, ping sweeps), and ARP broadcasts originating from the compromised BIG-IP. Flag queries for internal Linux hostnames, AD domain controllers, or databases from BIG-IP. Monitor for HTTP requests to internal management interfaces or cloud API endpoints.

suggestion.title: Composer Autoloader Execution of Suspicious Helper Files
suggestion.rationale: Article states malicious code 'loads automatically via composer's autoloader feature' via injected src/helpers.php. No detection for unexpected file execution during dependency loading.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor composer install/update operations for execution of unexpectedPHP files in vendor/laravel-lang paths. Detect src/helpers.php instantiation outside known package sources. Alert on PHP process spawned from vendor directories with suspicious environment or argument patterns.

suggestion.title: Bulk Cloud Provider Credential Access from Single Process
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malware 'systematically strips...cloud access keys for AWS, GCP, Azure, and DigitalOcean' plus 'Kubernetes profiles, Docker tokens, and HashiCorp Vault secrets.' No detection for credential enumeration across multiple cloud providers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect single process reading from ~/.aws, ~/.gcp, ~/.azure, ~/.ssh, ~/.docker, ~/.kube, and ~/.vault consecutively within seconds. Flag PHP processes accessing environment variables and config files for multiple cloud platforms in rapid succession.

suggestion.title: Password Manager Database and Browser Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies stealer harvests 'saved browser passwords, cryptocurrency wallets, and password manager databases.' No detection for bulk access to credential storage locations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process reading from browser credential stores (Chrome/Firefox/Safari key databases), 1Password/LastPass/Bitwarden config directories, and cryptocurrency wallet files (e.g., .bitcoin, .ethereum) in same execution context.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise via GitHub Tag Spoofing
suggestion.rationale: Article reveals 'GitHub allows version tags to point to commits from a fork...attacker...created tags pointed to commits in a malicious fork.' Detection gap for malicious composer package resolution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor composer require/update operations for package resolution to non-official GitHub repos or unexpected commit SHAs. Alert when laravel-lang/* packages resolve to forks or commits outside primary maintainer namespace. Track composer.lock for integrity deviations.

suggestion.title: Shell History and Environment Variable Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article states stealer collects 'shell history files' and developer credentials. No detection for bulk history file access during suspicious PHP execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP process reading ~/.bash_history, ~/.zsh_history, ~/.fish_history, and /root/.bashrc sequentially. Alert on getenv() calls for AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, GCP_PROJECT_ID, AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION_ID, and similar credential environment variables from non-standard callers.

suggestion.title: Cryptocurrency Wallet and Private Key Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'cryptocurrency wallets' harvested alongside 'SSH private keys.' No detection for bulk enumeration of wallet and key files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process enumerating ~/.bitcoin, ~/.ethereum, ~/.monero, ~/.cardano directories and reading private key files. Flag PHP processes with filesystem recursion through home directories targeting .key, .pem, and wallet configuration files.

suggestion.title: Composer Package Repository Commit Rewrite / Unauthorized Tag Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'every tag across multiple composer packages rewritten'—detection must identify abnormal repository history rewrites (git push -f), bulk tag creation/deletion, or version commits authored outside normal maintainer patterns. No detection use case was generated for this core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor composer package repositories (GitHub, GitLab) for force-push operations rewriting git history, bulk tag deletions followed by recreation, or commits modifying package source code authored from anomalous geographies/IPs relative to known maintainers. Alert on changes to composer.json that introduce new dependencies or modification of autoload paths.

suggestion.title: CI/CD Environment Variable Exfiltration via Composer Post-Install Script
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack to 'steal CI secrets.' Malicious code likely injected in package post-install hooks that enumerate and exfiltrate GitHub Actions secrets, CI tokens, AWS credentials. No detection rule addresses this credential_access phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In CI/CD contexts (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI), detect composer install/update spawning child processes that access or transmit environment variables with prefixes GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS_, COMPOSER_AUTH, or other secret patterns. Flag outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections from package-manager child processes to non-package-registry domains (curl/wget to attacker infrastructure).

suggestion.title: Composer Installation Without Lock-File or Signature Verification
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain compromise succeeds if CI pipelines trust package versions without hash/signature verification. Article implies widespread installation of compromised versions; detection should identify CI jobs installing packages without integrity checks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on CI workflows executing 'composer install' without '--no-scripts' flag (disables post-install code execution) or without composer.lock pinning. Detect installations from non-canonical sources (mirrors, forks, git branches) rather than packagist.org. Flag use of '--no-verify' or skipped package signature validation in CD pipelines.

suggestion.title: Malicious Package Post-Install Script: Credential Access & Network Egress
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks typically embed malicious code in post-install scripts that executes with full process privileges. Article implies code execution to steal CI secrets; no use case captures post-install hook anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor child processes spawned during 'composer install' for unusual activity: spawning shells (bash, sh, powershell), reading /proc/self/environ or env vars, making outbound connections (curl, wget, nc), accessing /etc/passwd or ~/.ssh, or writing to temp directories. Baseline normal post-install behavior per known package and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Composer Package Dependency Version Pinning in CI Context
suggestion.rationale: Compromised packages force installations to specific malicious versions. Article indicates 'every tag rewritten'; detection should surface when CI lock-files pin to versions with commit hashes or timestamps misaligned from upstream.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In CI workflows, alert when composer.lock references package versions where: commit SHA does not match upstream main branch, timestamp predates or post-dates normal release cycle for maintainer, package is installed from fork/mirror rather than packagist.org, or version is pinned to development branch instead of release tag.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Package Maintainer Account Activity & Credential Compromise Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates attacker compromised 'multiple composer packages'—likely via stolen maintainer credentials or account takeover. No detection rule for anomalous maintainer behavior (unusual login geographies, bulk commits, credential resets).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on package maintainer accounts: logins from new geographies/VPNs, bulk repository operations (mass commits, tag rewrites, access-level changes) outside normal activity patterns, credential-reset events followed by package commits within minutes, or commits authored by account but from unfamiliar commit authorship email/IP addresses.

suggestion.title: HTTP Access to LiteSpeed cPanel Plugin Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Title states CVE-2026-48172 exploited to run scripts—indicates unauthenticated or improper authentication bypass to a cPanel plugin web endpoint is the initial vector. No article body describes the endpoint path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to cPanel plugin URIs (e.g. /litespeed/, /plugins/litespeed) for unusual methods (POST with script payloads), missing auth headers, or external-IP access. Baseline legitimate cPanel admin traffic and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Shell Execution via LiteSpeed Process Parent
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Exploited to Run Scripts as Root'—indicates shell script execution under elevated privilege. Command shells should never spawn from LiteSpeed HTTP worker processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bash/sh/perl/python execution with parent process=LiteSpeedHTTP or cPanel-related daemon, particularly with working directory outside normal web/plugin paths or with base64-encoded command-line arguments.

suggestion.title: Root UID Process Spawning from Web Service Context
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly: 'Run Scripts as Root'—detection must capture privilege escalation from web-service user to UID=0.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect fork/exec of shell processes with effective_uid=0 where parent is a web-service daemon (LiteSpeed, httpd, cPanel). Cross-reference with auth/sudo logs for prior privilege-escalation calls.

suggestion.title: Malicious File Write to LiteSpeed Plugin Directory
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation of cPanel plugins typically involves uploading or writing malicious .so, .pl, or .sh files to plugin directories. No article body identifies specific payload filenames.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor writes to /usr/local/lsws/plugins/, /etc/cpanel/, or plugin-specific paths with file extensions .so, .sh, .pl, or .pm. Flag if writes correlate in time with HTTP requests to plugin endpoints.

suggestion.title: Persistence via cPanel Cron or Task Scheduling
suggestion.rationale: Post-RCE persistence on cPanel systems typically leverages cron jobs or cPanel's built-in task scheduler, not described in article body but standard in cPanel compromise post-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on writes to /etc/cron.d/*, /var/spool/cron/crontabs/* with suspicious payloads (reverse shells, C2 beacons). Monitor cPanel WHM task API calls for automated job registration with non-standard intervals.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48172 Indicator of Compromise
suggestion.rationale: CVE number in title should be extracted as first-class IOC to enable blocking of known-vulnerable plugin versions and correlation with threat-feed threat-actor activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inventory installed LiteSpeed plugin and cPanel versions. Flag hosts running LiteSpeed versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-48172. Cross-check with HTTP logs for exploitation attempts during vulnerable window.

suggestion.title: Malicious Package Installation Detected
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly references 'Supply Chain Attack Targets Laravel-Lang Packages'—pipeline should have generated detection for suspicious package download/installation patterns characteristic of supply-chain compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect composer/package manager execution with network callbacks to unfamiliar registries or suspicious domains. Monitor for installation of packages with version numbers recently modified or packages from accounts with suspicious creation dates.

suggestion.title: Post-Installation Credential Access
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'credential stealer' payload—this defines the attack's primary objective. Pipeline failed to suggest detection for credential enumeration or access after package execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for spawning of credential-access tools (mimikatz, lastpass-cli, browser-based credential APIs) post-package-installation. Detect abnormal file reads from credential stores (.ssh, browser profiles, password managers) by processes spawned from package-installation contexts.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration over HTTP/DNS
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealer payload necessarily exfiltrates harvested credentials; article body likely details C2 infrastructure or beacon patterns. Pipeline should detect egress of credential material to external hosts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on high-entropy data (base64, JSON blobs containing passwords/tokens) egressing from application context post-package-install. Monitor DNS queries to attacker-controlled domains; flag outbound HTTP POST requests with credential-like patterns in bodies.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Stolen Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealer harvests credentials for lateral spread; supply-chain attacks often pivot to internal infrastructure. Pipeline missing detection for use of stolen creds for lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect logon events using credentials harvested from post-install credential access. Flag failed authentication attempts from IPs/hosts where malicious package was installed, followed by successful logons from external IPs using harvested accounts.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Code Execution in Package Context
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks typically obfuscate malicious code to evade static detection. Article describes credential stealer—implying embedded code in package. No detection suggested for obfuscated/encoded payload execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for base64 decoding, hex unpacking, or dynamic code evaluation (eval, exec, assert) spawned from package-installation entry points. Flag unsigned or unusual module/assembly loads from temp directories post-package-install.

suggestion.title: Package Metadata Tampering or Version Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromise often involves publishing malicious versions alongside legitimate ones. Pipeline should detect version jumps, retroactive updates, or packages with suspicious metadata patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate package-manager logs with Composer/npm registries to detect installation of versions with unexpectedly high version numbers, unsigned checksums, or packages from newly-created maintainer accounts. Alert on versions removed/yanked shortly after release.

suggestion.title: Asset Exposure: Unpatched Drupal Core Instances (CVE-2026-9082)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs to 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer.' Requires inventory of Drupal versions and comparison against CVE-2026-9082 vulnerability status with Federal due date 2026-05-27.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify all Drupal Core instances in environment. Cross-reference version against vendor advisory for CVE-2026-9082. Flag instances running affected versions (unpatched as of 2026-05-27) for immediate remediation. Prioritize exposed internet-facing instances.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection Exploit Attempts Targeting Drupal Database API
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability is exploited 'via specially crafted requests sent with the database abstraction API.' Requires detection of SQL injection payloads targeting Drupal database query endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests with SQL keywords (UNION, SELECT, OR, 1=1) or hex/encoded SQL payloads targeting Drupal db abstraction endpoints. Correlate with HTTP 200 responses or 500 errors containing SQL error messages. Flag source IPs against threat intel for known vulnerability scanners.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation Post-SQL Injection Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'could allow for privilege escalation.' Detection requires monitoring Drupal user/role tables and OS-level events for unauthorized privilege changes following exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Drupal user audit logs and database for unexpected role/permission escalation (e.g., non-admin user elevated to administrator). Correlate timing with preceding SQL injection attempts or web server process anomalies. Flag accounts modified outside normal change-management windows.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution via Drupal SQL Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'remote code execution' as outcome. Detection requires process creation and command-line artifacts from web server processes handling Drupal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected shell or script interpreter invocation (bash, python, perl, powershell) spawned from Drupal web server processes (apache, nginx, php-fpm). Correlate with preceding SQL injection indicators. Monitor for suspicious command-line arguments (reverse shells, file downloads, permission changes).

suggestion.title: Web Server Log Anomalies: Drupal Exploitation Signatures
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'specially crafted requests' as attack vector—these leave signatures in web server access and error logs. Detection benefits from pattern matching on known Drupal exploit signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search web server access logs for requests bearing SQL injection patterns (double-encoded payloads, unusual parameter nesting, binary/hex payloads in query strings) to Drupal endpoints. Baseline normal query patterns; flag statistical outliers. Correlate with 5xx errors containing database error messages.

suggestion.title: LNK Shortcut Executing Remote PowerShell Script
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'Attackers use LNK shortcuts to covertly execute PowerShell scripts hosted on external resources.' Attackers email ZIP containing LNK that calls out to download and execute external PowerShell.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .lnk file creation from email or browser downloads, followed by child processes of explorer.exe or cmd.exe launching powershell.exe with URL parameters or encoded script blocks. Look for rundll32 or cmd /c executing .lnk files.

suggestion.title: PowerShell Registry Persistence with Suspicious Process Names
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'Creates "Run" registry key "YandexBrowser_setup" for "$temp\fixed.ps1" startup' as persistence mechanism. PowerShell drops payload then modifies HKLM/HKCU Run keys with benign-looking but suspicious names.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell (or cmd) modifying registry paths HKLM:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run or RunOnce with values pointing to .ps1 files in temp directories or with names mimicking legitimate software (YandexBrowser, ChromeSetup, etc.).

suggestion.title: termsrv.dll DLL Hijacking for Multi-User RDP Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Multi-user RDP by patching termsrv.dll' as persistence and lateral-movement technique. Indicates RDP service DLL is being replaced or patched in-memory or on-disk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process access or modification of termsrv.dll in System32 (unsigned binary load or timestamp anomalies, especially from non-system processes). Detect RDP service (svchost -k termsvcs) loading unsigned or modified termsrv.dll. Alert on in-memory patching attempts via CreateRemoteThread targeting lsass/svchost.

suggestion.title: Reverse SSH Tunnel Establishment and OpenSSH Binary Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'Reverse SSH tunneling' and 'Patched OpenSSH' as C2 mechanisms. Indicates SSH binaries are replaced and used to tunnel inbound connections or maintain reverse shells.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SSH processes spawned from non-standard locations (temp dirs, %AppData%, etc.) or unsigned binaries. Monitor for outbound SSH connections from non-traditional SSH clients or unusual command-line arguments (reverse port-forwarding flags -R, -L, -D). Baseline and alert on patched or modified ssh.exe binaries.

suggestion.title: RevSocks and Tor Traffic for Proxy Tunneling
suggestion.rationale: Article title and body reference 'ReverseSocks' and 'Tor tunneling' as persistence/C2 channels. Indicates SOCKS proxy and Tor are used to obfuscate and tunnel command traffic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unknown binaries (RevSocks, revsocks.exe, tun2socks, or custom SOCKS implementations) spawning with network activity. Detect Tor client processes (tor.exe) or Tor traffic patterns (connections to known Tor directory servers, SOCKS5 handshakes on unusual ports). Alert on processes modifying firewall rules to allow unusual SOCKS or tunnel ports.

suggestion.title: Credential Extraction from Browser Stores via PowerShell/VBScript
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'PowerShower::Payload (credential grabber)' as a dedicated stage executing after initial compromise. Indicates in-memory or direct access to browser credential stores.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PowerShell or VBScript (wscript.exe, cscript.exe) accessing browser credential database paths (%AppData%\Microsoft\Edge, \Chrome\User Data, Firefox profiles). Detect access to DPAPI protected data or calls to credential APIs from non-browser processes. Alert on PowerShell imports of System.Security.Cryptography or COM object creation for credential access (InternetExplorer.Application, etc.).

suggestion.title: Detect SQL injection payloads in HTTP requests targeting Drupal
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'specially crafted requests to trigger arbitrary SQL injection' and 'exploitable without authentication'. No UC generated to detect these request patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web access logs for SQL injection keywords (UNION, SELECT, DROP, INSERT, OR 1=1, etc.) in request parameters and POST bodies targeting Drupal paths (admin, user, db_*, etc.). Correlate with PostgreSQL database backend to confirm target surface.

suggestion.title: Detect unusual SQL queries on PostgreSQL after CVE-2026-9082 exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'trigger arbitrary SQL injection on sites using PostgreSQL' and 'could result in...information disclosure'. No use case for detecting injected SQL at the database layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected UNION-based queries, multi-statement queries, or high-privilege queries originating from web application accounts. Establish baseline of normal Drupal database activity and flag deviations in query structure, table access patterns, or execution context.

suggestion.title: Detect privilege escalation after SQL injection exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'could result in remote code execution, privilege escalation'. No detection rule for post-exploitation privilege escalation activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution with elevated privileges spawned by web server processes (apache, nginx, php-fpm) after SQL injection activity is detected. Flag new process creation with UID/GID changes or sudo invocations from web application context.

suggestion.title: Detect data exfiltration from PostgreSQL via Drupal SQLi
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability enables 'unauthorized access, modification, or deletion of database data' and 'information disclosure'. No use case monitors for data being extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect large or unusual outbound connections from Drupal application server to external hosts coinciding with high-volume database reads. Monitor for DNS queries to suspicious domains or data-staging patterns in outbound traffic volume.

suggestion.title: Identify vulnerable Drupal instances by version targeting
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies affected versions (8.9.x, 10.4.x-10.6.x, 11.0.x-11.3.x). No IOC or detection rule generated to identify exposed instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Passive asset inventory: fingerprint Drupal version from X-Generator headers, /user/register pages, or /misc/drupal.js file hashes. Cross-reference against CVE-2026-9082 affected versions (Drupal 8.9, 10.4.x <10.4.10, 10.5.x <10.5.10, 10.6.x <10.6.9, 11.x <11.x.10) to identify at-risk hosts.

suggestion.title: VPN Service IOC Enumeration and Blocking
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly names 'First VPN Dismantled' indicating a specific service was used by ransomware groups for C2 and infrastructure evasion. Article should list IOCs (service domains, IP ranges, certificate fingerprints) tied to this VPN infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for network connections to known VPN service endpoints associated with the dismantled infrastructure.
