Alert on client certificate patterns or specific VPN protocol signatures (OpenVPN, WireGuard, proprietary) linked to the takedown. Block ASNs and IP ranges publicly attributed to the service.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Group Enablement Through VPN Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates 25 ransomware groups relied on this VPN for operations. Pipeline should identify which groups, establish observed TTPs for their use of this infrastructure, and propose detections for group-specific callouts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For each identified ransomware group, correlate process execution and network behavioral signatures with known VPN client deployment patterns. Alert on lateral movement or beaconing immediately after VPN client installation or connection establishment.

suggestion.title: VPN Client Distribution and Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Ransomware operators would have distributed VPN client software (executables, MSIs, scripts) to compromised infrastructure. Article should surface file hashes and distribution vectors used by threat actors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of unsigned or suspicious VPN client binaries on systems with known ransomware indicators. Alert on script-based VPN client installation via PowerShell, batch, or shell commands. Block known malicious hashes of VPN clients linked to threat actor distribution.

suggestion.title: Law Enforcement Takedown Recovery: Infrastructure Pivot Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes a 'global takedown' by law enforcement, meaning threat actors will likely migrate to alternative infrastructure. Pipeline should propose behavioral detections for rapid C2 pivoting post-takedown.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-takedown, monitor for sudden shifts in network destinations, DNS query patterns, or certificate signers used by previously-identified ransomware groups. Alert on rapid reconnection to new VPN providers or custom C2 infrastructure from systems previously linked to this VPN.

suggestion.title: Access to Typosquatted FIFA Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'uses a domain that looks close enough to FIFA... containing small additions or involves other changes' hosted at fifa26.shop. No initial-access detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and HTTP requests to domains with 'fifa' + numeric variations (fifa26, fifa2026) or lookalike TLDs (.shop, .online, .site) that don't resolve to official FIFA IP ranges. Alert on first request; escalate if followed by form submission.

suggestion.title: Fake Registration Form Harvests PII
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'asks for the usual things such as your name, email address, and phone number' via 'fake registration form may not look strange'. No detection for credential harvesting to suspicious domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests with email + phone fields to typosquatted FIFA domains. Flag when verified email domains and phone patterns are submitted to unregistered infrastructure. Correlate with prior DNS/reputation checks.

suggestion.title: Payment Card Data Exfiltration via Fake Checkout
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'Once you enter your card details, it goes straight to the people behind the fake site' and 'your payments details would travel into the hands of the cybercriminal'. No payment-card detection rule created.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for credit card PAN/CVV submission (16-digit patterns, CVV fields) to non-official FIFA domains. Apply DLP signatures for payment card exfiltration. Escalate if correlated with prior registration submissions.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email with Malicious FIFA Link
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'others click on ads on social media or links in email messages forwarded by someone who didn't check the address properly'. Email-based phishing vector not detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails containing World Cup/FIFA references with hyperlinks to non-official domains. Correlate email sender reputation with target domain WHOIS age. Alert on clicks to typosquatted infrastructure within 72 hours of World Cup 2026.

suggestion.title: Social Media Ad Click-Through to Phishing Site
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Some victims may reach these websites through sponsored search results, while others click on ads on social media'. Ad-based initial access not detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track HTTP referrers from social platforms (facebook.com, instagram.com) or search engines to typosquatted FIFA domains. Flag if referrer domain contains World Cup/ticket keywords. Correlate with subsequent form submissions to same destination.

suggestion.title: F5 BIG-IP Remote Code Execution Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title and description establish F5 BIG-IP edge appliance as initial access vector ('exposed F5 BIG-IP edge appliance'). Pipeline generated no IOCs or detections for this critical access point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor F5 BIG-IP admin interfaces and REST API endpoints for exploitation attempts targeting known CVEs (e.g., CVE-2023-46805, CVE-2024-21914). Look for unusual POST requests to /mgmt/ or /api/ paths, shell execution spawned from BIG-IP processes, or unexpected outbound connections from the appliance to internal infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Confluence Vulnerability Exploitation and Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Description states pivot 'to an internal Confluence server for credential theft.' Pipeline missed detection for Confluence exploitation phase ('Multi-stage attack...pivoted to an internal Confluence server').
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect exploitation of Confluence template injection or authentication bypass (likely CVE-2023-22515). Look for unusual POST requests to Confluence pages, JSP file creation in Confluence directories, unexpected process execution within Confluence runtime, or lateral movement via Confluence service accounts.

suggestion.title: Kerberos Relay Attack Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'threat actor attempted Kerberos relay' and 'Kerberos relay and lateral movement.' Pipeline generated no detection for this credential-access / lateral-movement technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for NTLM relay or Kerberos delegation abuse: unusual Kerberos forwardable-ticket requests, multiple logons using service account credentials within short timeframes, cross-protocol relay attempts (HTTP → Kerberos), or unconstrained delegation abuse. Look for requests to Kerberos Distribution Center (KDC) from unusual processes or source IPs.

suggestion.title: Credential Theft from Confluence and Identity Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Description highlights 'credential theft and identity compromise' via Confluence. Pipeline failed to generate detection use cases for credential harvesting or identity abuse following access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk credential access or harvesting: unusual database queries against Confluence credential stores, token generation or session enumeration, abnormal authentication patterns (e.g., service account authentication from unexpected locations), or identity provider (IdP) manipulation following Confluence compromise.

suggestion.title: Linux Process Execution and Persistence Post-F5 Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'Multi-stage Linux intrusion via F5.' No detection generated for command execution, persistence mechanisms, or post-exploitation activity on Linux systems following edge appliance compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-F5 compromise, detect shell invocation or script execution on Linux systems: bash/sh spawned from unexpected parents, cron job modifications, sudoers file edits, or unexpected service/daemon creation. Monitor for reverse-shell patterns or data exfiltration commands.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Edge Appliance to Internal Confluence
suggestion.rationale: Attack narrative describes pivot from edge F5 appliance to internal Confluence server. Pipeline missed lateral-movement detection spanning network boundary.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect lateral movement from DMZ/edge (F5) to internal network (Confluence): unusual outbound connections from F5 appliance to internal IP ranges, exploitation traffic patterns, or use of edge appliance to stage attacks against internal services. Monitor for service account usage originating from edge infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Prometheus Malware Execution via Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'Prometheus Phishing Malware' targeting government entities. Pipeline should have generated detection for user-initiated malware execution following spearphishing, covering attachment open, link click, or staged payload download.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for process execution chain where Office/PDF reader spawns child processes with suspicious characteristics (unsigned, living-off-land tools, network I/O) shortly after file access from outlook temp dirs or download folders. Correlate with network beaconing to known C2 or high-entropy domains.

suggestion.title: Ghostwriter Phishing Campaign Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies Ghostwriter as the attribution for a coordinated phishing campaign targeting Ukraine government. Pipeline should have generated detection for bulk phishing emails with shared indicators (sender domain spoofing, lure themes, attachment metadata).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails arriving at Ukrainian government organization mailboxes with sender addresses spoofing internal/trusted domains, containing Prometheus-characteristic attachments (obfuscated .exe, DLL side-load pairs) or URLs shortened/obfuscated to bypass URL inspection.

suggestion.title: Prometheus Command & Control Communication
suggestion.rationale: Prometheus malware in phishing campaign implies C2 callback infrastructure. Pipeline missed detection for post-exploitation C2 checkins, which are deterministic once malware beacons.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for sustained outbound connections from government endpoints to non-canonical ports/domains immediately after Prometheus execution, with pattern-based C2 signatures (regular callback intervals, GET/POST patterns consistent with stolen-data exfil).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Office Macro or Shellcode Injection
suggestion.rationale: Prometheus as phishing payload typically uses Office macro downloader or signed-binary DLL injection. Article title indicates malware but pipeline did not surface detection for the delivery mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Office process (WINWORD, EXCEL) with VBA_MACRO_BLOCK registry bypass or policy violation, followed by spawning regsvcs/regasm/rundll32 with suspicious DLL paths. Flag mismatch between registered DLL versions and on-disk timestamps.

suggestion.title: Blind SQLi Response-Time Spike on Vulnerable Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'blind SQLi extraction loop' requiring character-by-character conditional queries. Each extraction attempt induces sleep-based delays. Response time from Bazar endpoint should spike 5-60x baseline during exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP response time percentiles (p95, p99) for /BazaR?vue=formulaire* endpoint. Flag sustained response-time spikes >5 seconds (typical SQL time-based blind sleep injection: SLEEP(5) or similar) in rolling 1-minute windows. Baseline endpoints should respond <500ms.

suggestion.title: Database Schema Enumeration via SQLi
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'read the full database, including yeswiki_users.password'. Blind SQLi exfiltration requires prior schema discovery (table names, column names, data types). Look for rapid sequential conditional queries against information_schema.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag rapid sequential queries (10+ in 60s) against information_schema.* or mysql.* catalog tables when originating from the web application process or the Bazar application context. Schema enumeration precedes data extraction in blind SQLi.

suggestion.title: Password Hash Extraction from yeswiki_users Table
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names target: 'read the full database, including yeswiki_users.password hashes'. Direct detection: anomalous SELECT queries on the password column of the users table.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on SELECT queries targeting yeswiki_users.password column (or * from yeswiki_users) when issued from the Bazar form-import handler context or unauthenticated web sessions. Legitimate application logic should not bulk-select hashes.

suggestion.title: SQL Error Spike on Bazar Form-Import Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Blind SQLi exploitation generates SQL syntax errors, type errors, or database exceptions during payload testing. The article is an INSERT sink; injected WHERE/UNION clauses will trigger parse errors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate 5+ SQL errors (syntax, type mismatch, constraint violation) in 5-minute window against requests to Bazar endpoint from single source IP. Blind SQLi fuzzing produces error storms during extraction loops.

suggestion.title: FileBrowser Quantum public share PATCH path traversal exploitation (UC_16_1)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes the exploit: 'fromPath and toPath body fields...filepath.Join collapses .. segments...sanitizer never sees the traversal.' Pre-formed detection logic with Splunk SPL exists in Recommended hunts section; pipeline failed to extract or generate it.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PATCH requests to /public/api/resources endpoint containing '..' traversal sequences in fromPath or toPath JSON body fields. High-fidelity indicator because the traversal pattern (quoted '..' in these specific fields) is exploitation-specific, not legitimate usage.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance: volumetric PATCH fuzzing on FileBrowser public endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article labels recon phase separately in UC_16_2. Attacker enumerates valid 'hash' parameter values and probes endpoint feasibility with 10+ PATCH requests within 5m window—article explicitly provides this volumetric threshold.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sustained PATCH request volume (≥10 requests in 5m) to /public/api/resources from single source with 3+ unique 'hash' values. Indicates hash enumeration or endpoint discovery before exploitation attempt.

suggestion.title: Successful unauthorized file move/copy outside share boundary
suggestion.rationale: Article states the vulnerability 'allows file ops outside shared directory.' Detection gap: post-exploitation impact where move/copy/rename succeeds with HTTP 200 but targets paths semantically outside the share root.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate PATCH requests to /public/api/resources with traversal patterns (fromPath/toPath containing '..' + hash parameter) that return HTTP 200 with file modification timestamps indicating the operation succeeded on files outside the configured share directory.

suggestion.title: Path traversal via symlink creation in public share PATCH context
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'move/copy/rename' operations but does not explicitly exclude symlink creation as an evasion vector. Attacker could chain symlink creation with traversal to access arbitrary filesystem.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PATCH requests to /public/api/resources endpoint that create symbolic links within the shared directory, especially when the symlink target path contains '..' or references paths outside share root.

suggestion.title: C2 Beacon Activity from Telecom ASN Ranges
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'Large-Scale Command-and-Control Operations' abusing telecom networks. This is the primary attack pattern described in the title and should trigger detection for suspicious outbound C2 communications originating from telecom provider IP space.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sustained, periodic outbound connections from telecom provider ASNs to known or suspected C2 infrastructure. Flag connections with abnormal patterns (unusual ports, encrypted payloads, geographically incongruent destinations) originating from telecom network ranges.

suggestion.title: Telecom Infrastructure Compromise via Credential Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'abuse' of telecom networks, implying credential theft or lateral movement within telecom provider environments. This is the initial compromise mechanism enabling C2 abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on failed/successful login attempts targeting telecom provider admin accounts, VPN concentrators, or network management platforms. Correlate with unusual administrative actions (BGP/DNS config changes, network rule modifications) within 2 hours of credential compromise.

suggestion.title: BGP/DNS Route Hijacking from Telecom ASNs
suggestion.rationale: Telecom infrastructure abuse at scale implies manipulation of routing or DNS to redirect traffic. Article context of 'Middle East telecom abuse' suggests geographic traffic redirection or C2 infrastructure masquerading.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor BGP announcement anomalies and DNS query patterns from telecom ASN networks. Flag unexpected route advertizements, DNS NXDOMAIN spikes, or DNS zone transfers targeting critical infrastructure domains during off-hours.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Detection in Telecom Backbone Networks
suggestion.rationale: Phrase 'abuse of Middle East telecom networks for large-scale operations' indicates actors moved laterally through interconnected telecom backbone systems to establish persistent C2 infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unusual inter-ASN traffic patterns, SSH/RDP brute-force attempts across telecom provider boundaries, or execution of remote administration tools on network infrastructure devices. Flag rapid multi-hop connections traversing telecom backbone segments.

suggestion.title: Malware Staging on Compromised Telecom Hosting
suggestion.rationale: Large-scale C2 operations require staging infrastructure. Telecom network abuse implies malware/C2 payload hosting on compromised telecom provider servers or CDN nodes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious file transfers or web server activity on telecom infrastructure IPs. Flag HTTP/HTTPS GET requests for executable payloads, PowerShell script downloads, or shellcode from telecom ASN ranges with low prevalence in environment.

suggestion.title: Persistent Backdoor Installation on Telecom Network Devices
suggestion.rationale: Article context of 'large-scale C2 operations' requires persistent access mechanisms. Telecom network devices (routers, load balancers, management servers) are logical persistence targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected firmware/OS updates on telecom network devices, suspicious cron/scheduled task creation on telecom provider management servers, or library/module injection patterns in network infrastructure binaries.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation or Version Downgrade
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes attack vector as backdoored 'art-template npm Package'—compromise occurs at install time. Pipeline generated zero detections for malicious package acquisition.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install/require operations targeting 'art-template' or widely-used packages for unusual version strings, mismatched registry sources, unexpected installation paths, or installations by processes never before observed installing packages. Correlate with known backdoored version hashes.

suggestion.title: Post-Install Script Execution from npm Lifecycle Hooks
suggestion.rationale: Backdoored npm packages commonly execute via postinstall hooks. Article's 'launch watering-hole attacks' implies active exploitation post-install, but pipeline missed this execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag execution of postinstall, install, or uninstall npm lifecycle scripts—especially those spawning child processes, calling curl/wget, modifying system files, or establishing network connections. Alert on obfuscated or base64-decoded payloads within scripts.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Network Egress from Node.js Process Tree
suggestion.rationale: Watering-hole attacks imply C2 communication and downstream compromise propagation. Article's scope is 'Launch Watering-Hole Attacks' but pipeline extracted zero command-and-control or exfiltration use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for egress connections initiated by node.js processes or spawned from node_modules directories to unexpected/external destinations. Flag periodic beaconing patterns, DNS resolution of suspicious domains, or TLS connections with anomalous SNI/certificate chains.

suggestion.title: File Integrity Violation on npm Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromise via backdoor injection means package files differ from upstream registry. Pipeline failed to suggest hash-based or integrity-check detections despite this being the hallmark of trojanized packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm cache and node_modules for file modifications post-installation or checksum mismatches against official npm registry metadata. Alert on unexpected .js files added to package directories or modifications to core package entry points (index.js, lib/).

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance or Credential Theft from Compromised Package Context
suggestion.rationale: Backdoored packages used for watering-hole attacks often perform reconnaissance (OS info, user enumeration) or credential harvesting. Article scope is broad exploitation, but pipeline provided no detection for data collection post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of system reconnaissance commands (whoami, systeminfo, uname) spawned from Node.js contexts or node_modules. Flag access to credential stores (.ssh, .aws, browser cookies, git configs) from package installation contexts.

suggestion.title: Mass or Correlated Compromise Pattern (Watering-Hole Wave Detection)
suggestion.rationale: Attack explicitly targets downstream users of backdoored package in bulk ('watering-hole'). Pipeline should generate a correlation use case to detect compromise waves across multiple endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate suspicious behavior (unexpected child processes, network connections, file modifications) across multiple machines where all originate from the same npm package version, installation timestamp, or dependency tree. Flag statistical anomalies in behavioral clustering by package digest.

suggestion.title: NF-e Invoice Phishing Email Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'NF-e Invoice Lures' as attack vector. NF-e is Brazil's electronic invoicing standard; emails mimicking fiscal documents are the initial access method.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on emails with NF-e, SEFAZ, or Brazilian tax authority spoofing in subject/body paired with executable attachments or suspicious links. Flag emails to non-finance recipients claiming invoice issues or payment disputes.

suggestion.title: Malicious Batch File Execution from Email Context
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'malicious batch files' as the delivery payload. No detection provided for .bat/.cmd execution chains following email opens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cmd.exe or batch process launch from Downloads, Temp, or Outlook cache with parent matching email client or browser. Flag batch with obfuscated commands (FOR, CALL, environment variable substitution) or spawning secondary executables.

suggestion.title: Banana RAT Process & Network Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'Banana RAT' as delivered malware. Zero signature-based or behavioral detections extracted despite this being the payload objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process execution with known Banana RAT hashes or command-line patterns. Correlate batch file execution with subsequent outbound connections to non-standard ports or known C2 infrastructure. Monitor file creations in system/temp immediately post-batch execution.

suggestion.title: Double Extension & Executable Masquerading as Document
suggestion.rationale: Batch file delivered via NF-e lure implies masquerading. Article states delivery via 'malicious batch files' attached to invoice-themed emails—batch should appear as invoice document.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when email attachments have double extensions (e.g., Nota.pdf.bat) or batch files with document-mimicking icons/names. Correlate with legitimate invoice document keywords in email body.

suggestion.title: Batch File Deobfuscation & Encoded Payload Execution
suggestion.rationale: Batch loaders for RATs typically use obfuscation (SETLOCAL EnableDelayedExpansion, variable encoding, escape sequences). Article mentions batch delivery but no evasion pattern detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect batch execution with heavy use of caret (^) escaping, delayed expansion variables, or FOR loops encoding commands. Flag batch files that write intermediate PE files to disk or stage code in registry before execution.

suggestion.title: Brazil-Targeted Tax/Invoice Phishing Campaign
suggestion.rationale: NF-e is Brazil-specific fiscal system; geographic targeting signal missed. Article: 'NF-e Invoice Lures'—suggests Brazil-focused operation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate NF-e phishing emails with recipient organizations having Brazilian business units, Portuguese language, or known BR-targeted malware. Check sender reputation against known spoofed BR government domains or tax authority names.

suggestion.title: FreePBX Web Shell Placement Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'six-layer persistence' on FreePBX systems. Web shell placement in /var/www/html or admin directories is a standard first persistence layer for compromised web applications. No detection suggested despite this being a foundational persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .php, .phtml, .php5 file creation or modification in FreePBX web-accessible directories (/var/www/html, /var/www/freepbx, admin folders). Correlate with suspicious parent process (curl, wget, or web server process writing outside normal patching windows).

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Cron Job Creation on PBX Systems
suggestion.rationale: Six-layer persistence implicitly includes scheduled task abuse. No detection for cron modifications despite cron being standard Unix persistence vector on FreePBX (which runs on Linux/Unix). Article mentions 'maintaining access' which requires reliable re-execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /etc/cron.d/, /etc/cron.daily/, and per-user crontabs for additions by root or asterisk user outside maintenance windows. Detect cron entries executing reverse shells, wget/curl payloads, or scripts in /tmp or /var/tmp.

suggestion.title: SSH Authorized Keys Persistence on FreePBX User Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Six-layer persistence on a system compromised for 'maintaining access' requires out-of-band SSH persistence. No detection suggested for ~/.ssh/authorized_keys modification, which is critical for persistence independent of password changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor additions to /home/*/.ssh/authorized_keys and /root/.ssh/authorized_keys files. Alert on writes by processes running as non-root, or root writes outside SSH service context. Correlate with process execution of echo, cat, or text editors.

suggestion.title: FreePBX Configuration File Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article describes maintained access over time ('maintain access on compromised systems'). No detection for FreePBX configuration modifications (freepbx.conf, database config, SIP settings) that could enable backdoor extensions or call forwarding.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor modifications to /etc/freepbx/ config files, asterisk.conf, and FreePBX database tables (users, extensions, devices) outside of legitimate admin activity. Detect creation of hidden extensions or forwarding rules pointing to attacker-controlled numbers.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Reverse Shell Process from FreePBX Daemons
suggestion.rationale: Six layers of persistence requires command execution layer. No detection suggested for reverse shell execution from asterisk, httpd, or FreePBX daemons. Article's 'maintain access' premise requires interactive shell callback.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor asterisk, httpd, and FreePBX web-server processes spawning bash, sh, nc, python, perl, or /dev/tcp connections. Alert on outbound connections on non-standard ports (not SIP 5060, 5061, RTP 10000-20000) from these daemons.

suggestion.title: Kernel Module or Rootkit Installation on FreePBX
suggestion.rationale: Six-layer persistence at kernel level is implied. No detection for .ko module insertion, insmod/modprobe execution, or rootkit signatures. This represents the deepest persistence layer and highest evasion risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor execution of insmod, modprobe, or depmod on FreePBX systems. Alert on .ko file creation in /lib/modules/. Track dmesg for kernel module load messages. Correlate with unusual /sys/module/ directory listings.

suggestion.title: Detect DDoS Botnet Command and Control Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'DDoS Botnet Operator' and arrest 'Over DDoS-for-Hire Attacks'—implies C2 infrastructure for botnet coordination. Zero C2 detection rules generated despite impact-phase operation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large-scale outbound UDP traffic patterns consistent with DDoS botnet C2 or amplification attack staging. Flag unusual DNS resolution volumes to dynamic/bulletproof hosting. Detect process execution launching network tools (curl, wget, nc) with DDoS payload parameters.

suggestion.title: Detect Service Exhaustion / Network-Based DDoS Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article subject is 'DDoS-for-Hire Attacks'—T1499 Service Exhaustion and T1498 Network Denial of Service are the primary attack techniques. Pipeline generated zero use cases for these impact-phase vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sudden spike in failed connection attempts to a single target across multiple source IPs (volumetric DDoS). Track HTTP/HTTPS GET request floods (T1499.001). Monitor DNS query floods and NTP/DNS amplification patterns (T1498.002). Correlate with ISP/CDN DoS mitigation reports.

suggestion.title: Identify Botnet-Compromised Hosts via Outbound Attack Traffic
suggestion.rationale: DDoS-for-hire operation implies infected/recruited bot machines executing attacks. Article states 'Kimwolf DDoS Botnet'—should generate detection for compromised endpoints launching attacks, not just ingress.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect endpoint processes spawning high-volume network traffic to multiple non-whitelisted destinations. Flag binaries downloaded from suspicious sources that immediately initiate connection floods. Monitor for scheduled tasks or persistence mechanisms typically used to maintain botnet agents.

suggestion.title: Flag Kimwolf Threat Actor Infrastructure and Aliases
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Kimwolf' as the operator. Pipeline extracted zero threat actor names despite this being primary identifier for threat hunting and blocking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create blocklist for known Kimwolf C2 domains, bulletproof hosting ASNs, and DDoS panel URLs. Hunt for WHOIS records, SSL certificates, or nameserver patterns historically associated with Kimwolf infrastructure. Monitor for phishing/recruitment emails advertising DDoS-for-hire services.

suggestion.title: Detect DDoS-for-Hire Service Monetization and Customer Communications
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'DDoS-for-Hire Attacks'—implying customer solicitation, payment processing, and attack coordination. No use cases address threat-actor to customer communication channels or billing infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify DDoS-for-hire marketplace domains, Telegram channels, or forums advertising attack services. Track cryptocurrency payment wallets or conversion services linked to botnet operators. Monitor for solicitation emails or posts recruiting compromised hosts or selling botnet access.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Vulnerable Driver Load via User-Mode Application
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD attacks hinge on loading a vulnerable-but-legitimate driver that was not intended for exploitation. The pipeline missed the core execution pattern: user-mode processes loading drivers that expose kernel-level memory mapping or callback manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for user-mode process creation followed by direct or indirect driver loading via LoadLibrary, DriverKit APIs, or SetupDiInstallDevice. Correlate with unsigned or rarely-seen drivers. Look for process access to kernel objects (\Device\) or registry writes to SYSTEM hive driver paths.

suggestion.title: Unsigned or Vulnerable Driver Image Load
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD specifically exploits legitimate but vulnerable drivers. The attack phrase indicates drivers are loaded without integrity checks; the pipeline should flag unsigned driver images or drivers with known CVEs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on image load events for drivers with invalid or missing code signatures, or drivers with known BYOVD-applicable CVEs (e.g., Gigabyte driver, ASRock tool, MSI). Cross-reference driver name and version against public BYOVD driver repositories.

suggestion.title: Kernel Callback or Memory Mapping Exploitation Patterns
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD attacks abuse kernel callbacks (PsCreateProcessNotifyRoutine, PsLoadImageNotifyRoutine) or direct kernel memory mapping exposed by vulnerable drivers. The pipeline missed detection of abnormal inter-process communication or kernel memory access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes opening handles to kernel objects with high privilege demand (\Device\PhysicalMemory, \Global??, etc.), or abnormal IPC patterns between user-mode and driver-mode. Flag processes using WinDbg, direct kernel object manipulation (DKM), or GDI handles for unintended kernel access.

suggestion.title: Registry Modification for Vulnerable Driver Persistence
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD attacks may register vulnerable drivers in SYSTEM hive or modify driver load order to ensure automatic execution. The article likely describes persistence mechanics the pipeline completely missed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services for new driver entries or service creation with Start value 2 (auto-load) or 3 (manual). Alert on additions of vulnerable drivers or unusual driver service properties (ImagePath pointing to unusual locations, DisplayName anomalies).

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Driver Enumeration or Probing
suggestion.rationale: Attackers first identify which vulnerable drivers are present on a system before exploiting them. The pipeline should have flagged discovery patterns: file system scans for driver names, registry enumeration of installed drivers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes enumerating SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services (driver registry hive), scanning Windows\System32\drivers, or querying GetDriverInfo APIs. Cross-reference with known vulnerable driver names (Gigabyte SmartByte, ASRock Tool Box, etc.).

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion via Legitimate Driver Masquerade
suggestion.rationale: The core BYOVD concept is evading detection by using 'legitimate' signed drivers instead of custom malware. The pipeline should surface detection of driver abuse that bypasses endpoint security (DSE bypass via vulnerable driver).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for known BYOVD driver loads that are then immediately followed by suspicious system operations (SYSTEM process spawning, LSA modification, token impersonation). Flag DSE (Driver Signature Enforcement) bypass indicators: unsigned driver loads on systems where DSE is supposed to be enabled.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Workflow File Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'malicious CI/CD workflows' as attack vector; pipeline produced no detection logic for workflow poisoning
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub repository audit logs and webhook events for .github/workflows/*.yml additions or modifications in forked/mirrored repos, especially with suspicious run commands that invoke curl, wget, or base64-encoded PowerShell. Flag workflows adding new secrets or env vars.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Credentials Access from CI/CD Environment
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 5,561 repos targeted; malicious workflows would steal repository secrets, PATs, or deploy keys—no detection UC for secret exfiltration
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GitHub Actions runs where secrets are accessed outside normal build/deploy context, or GitHub API token usage from non-standard runner IPs. Monitor for base64-encoded credentials passed via environment variables to external curl requests.

suggestion.title: Outbound Network Connections from GitHub Actions Runners
suggestion.rationale: Malicious workflows must exfiltrate code/secrets to attacker infrastructure; article implies data theft but pipeline captured no network-based detection logic
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected outbound HTTPS/HTTP connections from GitHub-hosted runners to non-GitHub ASNs, especially to newly registered or high-entropy domains. Establish baseline of expected egress (package registries, artifact repos); flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Repository Clone/Fork to External Storage
suggestion.rationale: 5,561 repos targeted suggests attacker may exfiltrate entire repo contents; no UC for detecting bulk repository downloads or exports
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub audit logs for `git clone` operations from runner IPs to external hosts, or API calls exporting repository data (archive downloads). Alert on mass downloads of private repo contents across multiple projects by single PAT or SSH key.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Repository Access Patterns from Compromised Repos
suggestion.rationale: Article states repos were directly targeted; should detect lateral movement or privilege escalation via GitHub API from compromised contexts
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag runs where a compromised repo's CI/CD token is used to access unrelated repos, modify collaborators, or list organization secrets. Alert on creation of new deploy keys or personal access tokens from workflows.

suggestion.title: Malicious Pull Request or Commit Injection to Source Repos
suggestion.rationale: Attack methodology likely involves code injection into repos via PRs or direct commits; pipeline found no detection for source-code tampering in supply-chain context
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect commits/PRs that add or modify GitHub Actions workflows, build scripts, or CI configuration files in quick succession across multiple repos. Alert on bypass of branch protections or unusual merge patterns from service accounts.

suggestion.title: Malicious GitHub Actions Workflow Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly references 'Mass GitHub Actions Secret Exfiltration.' Attack vector is workflow-based credential theft across 5,500+ repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect .github/workflows/*.yml files containing secret extraction patterns (GITHUB_TOKEN, custom secrets access) paired with outbound exfiltration commands. Flag workflows with base64-encoded credentials, environment variable enumeration, or HTTP POST to non-standard endpoints.

suggestion.title: GitHub Secrets Credential Access and Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Mass exfiltration implies programmatic harvesting of GitHub repository secrets. Article describes credential theft at scale across thousands of repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual patterns of secrets access within Actions workflows: repeated GITHUB_TOKEN reads, enumeration of custom secret variables, bulk artifact uploads containing credential strings, or workflows accessing repository secrets not declared in dependency manifest.

suggestion.title: Bulk Workflow Injection Across Multiple Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Scale of 5,500+ affected repositories indicates automated, bulk injection. Article describes 'Mass GitHub Actions Secret Exfiltration' implying coordinated attack across unrelated codebases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation or modification of .github/workflows files across dozens of unrelated repositories within short time window. Alert on identical workflow file content appearing in multiple repos, or single GitHub account/IP injecting workflow files into repos with no prior connection.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration Traffic from GitHub Actions Runner
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Secret Exfiltration.' Attackers must establish outbound command-and-control or staging channels from Actions infrastructure to retrieve stolen credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTP/S requests from GitHub Actions runner IPs to previously unknown or low-reputation domains. Flag curl/wget commands with base64-encoded payloads, POST requests with gzipped content, or DNS queries for attacker-controlled domains during workflow execution.

suggestion.title: GitHub Account Compromise or Session Hijacking
suggestion.rationale: 5,500+ repository compromise requires either maintainer account takeover, GitHub platform vulnerability, or supply-chain attack. Initial access via T1078.004 (Cloud Accounts).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub accounts of popular maintainers for unusual activity: logins from new geolocations, suspicious IP addresses, unusual session duration, or bulk repository access shortly after unrecognized login. Correlate with subsequent .github/workflows/ modifications.

suggestion.title: Secret Leakage in GitHub Actions Logs
suggestion.rationale: Exfiltration of GITHUB_TOKEN and custom secrets may be exposed in workflow logs, error output, or debug artifacts uploaded by compromised workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan Actions workflow logs for exposed GitHub tokens, API keys, and repository secrets. Detect workflows that echo environment variables, upload logs containing credentials, or expand secrets into publicly-accessible artifacts.

suggestion.title: Detect DDoS Attack Attribution to Pro-Russian Hacktivist Group Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly links infrastructure to attack execution: 'Danish authorities and infrastructure providers linked WorkTitans to attacks by the pro-Russian hacktivist group NoName057(16), which has previously targeted key organizations with distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for volumetric DDoS patterns (TCP/UDP floods, ICMP echoes) originating from autonomous systems associated with seized hosting infrastructure or known colocation facilities in Amsterdam/Frankfurt. Correlate sudden traffic spikes from single ASN with NoName057(16) claims of responsibility and known target patterns.

suggestion.title: Detect Hosting Infrastructure Transfer to Evade Sanctions
suggestion.rationale: Article describes defense-evasion through shell company: 'Following this restriction [EU sanctions], the web hosting infrastructure was transferred to a newly created Dutch company that investigators believe acted as a front for the sanctioned entities' (WorkTitans/THE.Hosting created after Stark Industries sanctioned on May 20).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag bulk domain re-pointing to newly registered entities within 30 days of EU sanctions announcements. Monitor for infrastructure re-announcement via different ASNs by recently incorporated companies. Detect nameserver glue record changes for domains previously hosted on sanctioned providers, especially when new registrants share registration facilitators or payment methods.

suggestion.title: Detect Colocation and Transit Supply-Chain Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article describes intermediary infrastructure abuse: 'Mirhosting, based in Almere, operated physical servers, provided colocation, and supplied high-capacity connectivity to major internet exchanges in Amsterdam and Frankfurt, acting as the transport layer through which Stark's traffic entered Europe.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for IP ranges previously advertised by sanctioned entities (Stark Industries) being re-announced or transited through intermediary ASNs (particularly Almere-based providers). Track colocation facilities announcing prefixes inconsistent with their published customer base. Alert on high-capacity eastbound traffic from Amsterdam/Frankfurt exchanges to Russian/Belarusian targets.

suggestion.title: Detect Newly Registered Front-Company Hosting Operations
suggestion.rationale: Article documents shell entity creation: 'the name of this Dutch entity is WorkTitans B.V. and provides hosting services under the brand THE.Hosting' (founded after Stark Industries sanctioned, re-using same infrastructure).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Dutch company registrations (KvK database) for new hosting/connectivity service providers founded within 30 days of sanctions. Flag when newly registered companies re-advertise IP blocks formerly owned by sanctioned entities. Cross-correlate hosting brand registrations with parent company officer names and previous employment.

suggestion.title: Detect Infrastructure Re-use for Disinformation and Information Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies non-DDoS attack operations hosted on infrastructure: 'provided support to actions by the Russian Federation that undermine democracy and security, including through information manipulation and disruption of public and economic systems.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify patterns consistent with disinformation infrastructure: bulk domain registrations in waves, rapid DNS changes, CDN usage for rapid content replication, email marketing infrastructure supporting phishing/manipulation. Correlate domain clusters registered via same registrar/payment method with takedown incidents of hosting providers.

suggestion.title: Detect Financial Flow to Sanctioned Entities via Hosting Service Payments
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes resource provision to sanctioned actors: 'the suspects indirectly provided economic resources to Russian and Belarusian entities sanctioned by the European Union.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor hosting provider payment flows for cryptocurrency transactions or shell-company wire transfers from sanctions-evasion networks. Flag bulk server allocations (800+ servers seized) paid by recently registered entities. Track payment method changes and billing address shifts for accounts serving sanctioned jurisdictions.

suggestion.title: VS Code Extension Process Spawning Child Processes
suggestion.rationale: Extension compromise enables arbitrary code execution; title states 'compromised' extension. Pipeline should detect suspicious child processes spawned from VS Code/extension contexts, yet generated zero detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned or anomalous child process creation from %ProgramFiles%\Microsoft VS Code\Code.exe or extension host processes. Flag PowerShell, cmd.exe, or net.exe spawned from extension runtime with parent=Code.exe and grandparent not standard (launch, debugger, vscode). Supply-chain compromises typically shell out.

suggestion.title: Malicious VS Code Extension Installation/Update from Untrusted Source
suggestion.rationale: The attack vector is compromised extension distribution. Title indicates extension was compromised, likely implying malicious version. No detection for extension download or installation anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on extension .vsix file writes to %USERPROFILE%\.vscode\extensions\, especially from non-Microsoft Marketplace URLs. Monitor for extensions installed via registry modification or package manager commands (npm, nuget) with atypical version strings or unsigned publishers.

suggestion.title: Credential/SSH Key Access from VS Code Process Context
suggestion.rationale: Development environments hold SSH keys, .aws/credentials, GitHub tokens. Compromised extension gains access to developer's secrets. Pipeline extracted no detection for credential harvesting from extension process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Code.exe or vscodesrv.exe reading files in %USERPROFILE%\.ssh\, %USERPROFILE%\.aws\, %USERPROFILE%\.kube\, or .git\config. Alert on reads to credential storage (LSASS, Windows Credential Manager) initiated from extension runtime. Developers rarely access these interactively from IDE.

suggestion.title: Development Repository Exfiltration via Extension
suggestion.rationale: Compromised extension in developer's IDE can read source code at rest. Article title mentions 'compromised' extension with no detection logic for bulk source theft or repository access anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Code.exe or extension processes recursively reading entire repository directories (.git, src/, test/) and sending compressed or encoded payloads to external HTTPS/DNS. Monitor for unusual volume of file read operations from single extension process in short time window.

suggestion.title: VS Code Extension Registry Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Extensions can persist via registry auto-load, startup tasks, or modified user settings. No detection rule for extension-based persistence vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor modification of HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Software\Microsoft\VS Code\extensions registry key, particularly additions of unsigned or unsigned extensions with 'autoStart' or 'onStartupFinished' flags. Flag new .vscode/settings.json or keybindings.json with unusual task definitions or command overrides.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Shared Development Repository
suggestion.rationale: Compromised extension exfiltrates credentials, then attacker pivots to Git server, artifact repository, or shared infrastructure. No detection for lateral movement post-exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate credential exfiltration from VS Code process with subsequent authentication to git.company.com, Azure DevOps, GitHub Enterprise, or artifact repositories from external IP or novel geolocation. Flag commits authored by compromised developer accounts from non-standard clients or at unusual times.

suggestion.title: Suspicious ROADtools or Azure Enumeration Tool Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names ROADtools as attack vector; cloud intrusion framework misuse is core narrative. Pipeline should detect ROADtools module import, binary execution, or characteristic PowerShell enumeration patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution with ROADtools signatures, PowerShell import of AD/Azure enumeration modules, or Get-MgUser/Get-MgGroup calls from non-admin accounts. Correlate bulk user enumeration with single service principal.

suggestion.title: Entra ID Account Discovery at Scale via Microsoft Graph API
suggestion.rationale: Article keywords include 'Entra ID', 'Microsoft graph API', and 'Cloud Cybersecurity'. ROADtools specializes in bulk enumeration of users, groups, and roles. Phrase 'nation-state tactics' signals organized reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect abnormal volume of Microsoft Graph API calls for user/group enumeration, especially filter+list patterns characteristic of ROADtools. Flag service principals with no prior admin history performing AAD queries.

suggestion.title: Cloud Password Policy and Conditional Access Rule Discovery
suggestion.rationale: ROADtools enumerates password policies, MFA enforcement, and conditional access rules to identify weak targets. Standard reconnaissance step in cloud APT playbooks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Get-MsolPasswordPolicy, Get-ConditionalAccessPolicy, or equivalent Graph API calls by non-privileged accounts. Alert if caller is a newly-created service principal or external app.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Application or Service Principal Credential Creation Post-Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses 'nation-state tactics'—follow-on to discovery is credential theft/creation for persistence. ROADtools findings enable privilege escalation via app consent abuse or secret rotation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate large-scale Entra ID discovery activity with subsequent creation of new service principal secrets or OAuth client credentials. Flag if new creds issued minutes after enumeration burst.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Azure Automation Runbook or Logic App Execution
suggestion.rationale: Post-discovery, nation-state actors leverage cloud automation services for lateral movement and command execution. Article scope is 'nation-state tactics in cloud'—operational infrastructure abuse expected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Runbook execution triggered by new/unknown service principal. Monitor Logic App creation + execution within minutes of large-scale cloud enumeration. Baseline normal automation access patterns.

suggestion.title: RDP Brute Force and Unauthorized Access Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Russian Threat Groups Use RDP ... for Initial Access' but pipeline surfaced zero RDP-specific detection. RDP is a high-frequency attack vector requiring failed/successful login detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences of failed RDP login attempts to privileged accounts within short time windows, or successful RDP logins from unexpected geographies, IPs, or outside business hours. Correlate with known botnet IP ranges.

suggestion.title: Suspicious VPN Connection Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Russian Threat Groups Use ... VPN ... for Initial Access' but pipeline omitted any VPN-focused detection. VPN abuse enables post-compromise persistence and lateral movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag VPN logins from high-risk ASNs, impossible-travel geographies, or new IP/user combinations. Monitor for VPN access followed within minutes by PowerShell, WMI, or process-injection activity indicative of post-compromise reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Software Deployment Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article cites 'Supply Chain Attacks' as an initial vector but pipeline captured no supply-chain or software-deployment detection logic. This is a low-noise, high-impact technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected or out-of-band software installations from trusted vendors, especially build tools, IT management utilities, or cloud-infrastructure SDKs. Cross-hash against threat intelligence and alert if child processes spawned by legitimate supplier binaries show process-injection, network reconnaissance, or credential-access behavior.

suggestion.title: Phishing and Spearphishing Email Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title includes 'Social Engineering for Initial Access' but pipeline generated zero email-based detection. Phishing is the primary vector for Russian threat groups targeting organizations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails from external senders with URL redirects to known phishing/credential-harvesting domains, or PDFs/Office attachments containing suspicious macros. Correlate email recipients with org-chart data and known Russian targeting profiles. Alert if recipients click malicious links and follow with password-entry or malware execution within 10 minutes.

suggestion.title: Multi-Vector Initial Access Progression
suggestion.rationale: Article describes *multiple concurrent* Russian initial-access methods but pipeline failed to model the progression (phishing → VPN login → RDP lateral move). Sequential patterns are more specific than isolated vector detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create composite timeline: detect users who are phishing targets AND subsequently log in via VPN within 24–72 hours, OR attempt RDP sessions to critical systems. Clustering across similar user cohorts (executives, IT staff) raises confidence significantly.

suggestion.title: Automated Vulnerability Enumeration Against Project Glasswing
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states '10,000+ 0-Days' uncovered, establishing systematic reconnaissance activity. Pipeline generated zero detection coverage for bulk vulnerability discovery or enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on high-volume network service scanning, cloud API enumeration, or automated vulnerability scanning tools targeting Project Glasswing infrastructure. Baseline tool spawning consistent with network/cloud reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Claude Mythos Preview Tool Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title identifies 'Claude Mythos Preview' as the discovery mechanism. Pipeline failed to generate detection for this named tool's execution or scanning activity against sensitive infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Claude Mythos Preview process creation or API calls, particularly with arguments targeting cloud infrastructure, repositories, or internal projects. Flag unexpected invocations from automation tools.

suggestion.title: Bulk Account and Infrastructure Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Uncovering 10,000+ vulnerabilities requires enumeration of cloud accounts, services, and resources. Article phrase 'uncovers' implies reconnaissance-phase enumeration; pipeline omitted credential/account discovery coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk ListUsers, ListRoles, ListBuckets, ListSecrets, or equivalent cloud enumeration API calls from unusual service accounts or automation contexts.

suggestion.title: Large-Scale Vulnerability Data Export or Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Discovery of 10,000 vulnerabilities implies generation and potential export of a detailed vulnerability dataset. Pipeline did not suggest exfiltration-phase detection for bulk report export.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on large data transfers, archive creation, or report generation containing vulnerability intelligence or reconnaissance findings from Project Glasswing systems.

suggestion.title: Malicious Package Version Deployment Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 233 versions of Laravel-Lang packages were compromised. Should detect when applications pull these specific malicious versions from package repositories or when package manifests suddenly pin to new versions without code review patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for composer.json/composer.lock modifications pulling Laravel-Lang versions released during the attack window (dates not in article body), especially bulk deployments across multiple applications or sudden version pins without corresponding security patches in logs.

suggestion.title: GitHub Repository Bulk Update Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Attack involved 700 GitHub repos being hacked to push malicious Laravel-Lang packages. Should detect unusual commit velocity, new committer additions, or mass commits of dependency files without review.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk commits across multiple repos in short timeframe, commits from new/dormant accounts, commits bypassing branch protections, or mass dependency file modifications (composer.json) without corresponding PR reviews or maintainer sign-off.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Package Integrity Verification Failure
suggestion.rationale: 233 malicious versions imply hash/signature bypass or absent verification. Should alert when package hashes diverge from public registries or when signature verification is disabled in deployment configs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Composer or other package managers pulling packages with mismatched hashes against known-good registries, disabled signature verification, or certificate pinning bypasses in CI/CD configurations.

suggestion.title: GitHub Account Compromise Indicators
suggestion.rationale: 700 repo compromise implies credential theft or session hijacking of maintainer accounts. Should detect unusual IP origins for commits, new SSH keys added, OAuth apps authorized, or API token creation from anomalous locations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on: GitHub login/pushes from new geolocations, new SSH keys added by dormant accounts, new OAuth apps authorized, API tokens created outside normal CI/CD workflows, or commits from IPs not matching org VPN/office ranges.

suggestion.title: Downstream Application Code Execution from Malicious Dependencies
suggestion.rationale: Compromised Laravel-Lang runs localization code in consuming applications. Should detect execution patterns from within package directories, unusual process spawning, or network connections initiated by vendor/ paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PHP/Laravel process execution originating from vendor/laravel-lang/ directory, child processes spawned by PHP processes during localization functions, or network connections to attacker C2 from application processes.

suggestion.title: Bulk Backdoored Maintainer Account Detection
suggestion.rationale: Attack pattern (700 repos compromised, 233 versions published) suggests either maintainer account takeover or impersonation. Should detect new maintainers added in bulk or legitimate maintainers suddenly publishing many versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect new maintainers added to 700+ repos in cluster, legitimate maintainers suddenly publishing multiple versions in 24-48hr window without commit history, or packages released by accounts with no prior release history.

suggestion.title: F5 BIG-IP Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'Hackers Exploit F5 BIG-IP Appliance'—indicates active exploitation of known or zero-day F5 vulnerability. No detection UC generated for initial compromise vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor F5 BIG-IP management and data plane interfaces for exploit attempts: malformed HTTP requests, unusual query parameters in admin endpoints, POST/PUT requests to sensitive paths, and responses indicating command execution (shell meta-characters in params). Correlate with vulnerability scanner signatures or known F5 CVE payloads.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized SSH Access Post-F5 Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attackers 'Gain SSH Access' after F5 compromise. Pipeline did not generate detection for this critical access method.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on SSH connections originating from F5 BIG-IP management IP or internal network segments controlled by F5. Establish baseline SSH users/IPs for F5 system accounts; flag deviations. Look for SSH sessions with short connection durations (indicative of command execution), unusual times, or originating from F5 subnet.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Network Appliance to Enterprise Linux
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Pivot Into Enterprise Linux Networks' as the attack objective. Pipeline missed detection for this critical lateral-movement phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network flows from F5 BIG-IP to internal Linux servers on ports 22, 445, 5985, 3389, or other common lateral-movement channels. Correlate with failed/successful authentication attempts on target Linux hosts. Alert on processes spawned by unusual users or SSH sessions followed by process execution.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation on Compromised Linux Post-SSH Access
suggestion.rationale: Article implies multi-step attack requiring privilege escalation to 'pivot' effectively, but no detection UC for Linux privilege escalation generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on privilege escalation attempts (sudo, su, UAC bypass, SUID exploitation) on Linux hosts within 5 minutes of new SSH session initiation. Flag sudo execution without tty, use of /usr/bin/sudo with unexpected binaries, or kernel module loading post-SSH access.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Execution via SSH on Linux
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker pivoting into Linux networks, implying command execution post-SSH. Pipeline generated no detection for post-compromise activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process execution spawned from SSH sessions with high entropy command names, base64-encoded arguments, shell redirects to network sockets, or execution of tools commonly associated with reconnaissance (nmap, hashcat, mimikatz, etc.). Alert on child processes of SSH daemons executing privileged commands.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via SSH Tunnel Post-F5 Compromise
suggestion.rationale: High-severity attack likely culminates in data extraction; article title indicates pivoting into Linux networks typically precedes collection/exfil. No UC generated for post-exploitation persistence or C2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SSH connections from compromised Linux hosts for sustained data transfer patterns: high byte counts, unusual protocols tunneled over SSH (socks, port forwarding), or reverse SSH tunnels. Correlate large file reads on Linux hosts with SSH session initiation and egress traffic spikes.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise – Malicious PHP Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes package compromise as the delivery vector; no use case exists to detect installation or loading of the backdoored Laravel-Lang versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor composer.json modifications, package-lock updates, or Packagist repository API calls for suspicious Laravel-Lang package versions. Correlate installation timestamps with process spawning of unusual PHP child processes or network connections outside normal application behavior.

suggestion.title: Credential Stealer Execution – Cross-Platform PHP Payload Activation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes delivery of 'cross-platform credential stealer'; no detection for PHP process spawning with credential-harvesting indicators or in-memory string patterns consistent with credential exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PHP or apache2/nginx processes spawning cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or sh with suspicious argument patterns (registry queries, credential manager access, /etc/passwd reads, SSH key enumeration). Cross-reference with unexpected parent-child process chains from web server contexts.

suggestion.title: Credential Access – Environment Variable and Config File Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Cross-platform credential stealer typically targets .env files, config files, and shell history; no UC addresses file reads for Laravel .env, .git/config, AWS credentials, SSH keys, or shell history from PHP runtime.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PHP process file-read patterns for .env, .git/, .aws/, .ssh/, .bash_history, /etc/passwd, /etc/shadow access. Flag reads from contexts that don't match typical application initialization (e.g., mid-request reads to credential files, reads followed by network exfiltration).

suggestion.title: Exfiltration – Credential Stealer Data Transmission
suggestion.rationale: No use case detects unusual egress from compromised PHP application to attacker-controlled C2 infrastructure following credential harvesting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP/HTTPS POST or GET requests from PHP process to newly registered or low-reputation domains carrying Base64 or gzip-compressed payloads. Correlate with credential file reads within preceding 60 seconds. Monitor for unusual DNS queries from application servers to non-whitelisted resolvers.

suggestion.title: Persistence – PHP Backdoor Injection into Application Autoload or Bootstrap
suggestion.rationale: Article implies ongoing compromise; no detection for persistent backdoor mechanisms such as .htaccess rewrite rules, composer autoload corruption, or index.php prepend statements.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor .htaccess modifications, composer.json/vendor/autoload_real.php alterations, and PrependedFile injection into PHP.ini equivalents. Alert on file-write events to bootstrap or autoload paths outside scheduled deployment windows, especially those adding obfuscated or base64-encoded PHP code.

suggestion.title: Composer Package Repository Tag Rewrite Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Every Tag Across Multiple Composer Packages Rewritten'—direct VCS manipulation evidence. Pipeline missed fundamental supply-chain initial-access indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Composer package repositories for unauthorized tag creation, deletion, or force-pushes across multiple packages. Detect when tag commit references diverge from expected upstream without developer commits. Flag coordinated tag rewrites affecting Laravel-Lang and dependent packages.

suggestion.title: CI/CD Environment Secret Access from Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Attack goal is to 'Steal CI Secrets'—malicious injected code must read CI_*, GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS_KEY environment variables. Zero use cases for this credential-access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag getenv(), env(), or $_SERVER/ENV variable enumeration from PHP processes running in vendor/ directories during composer install. Alert on exfiltration of CI environment variables via HTTP requests, DNS exfil, or webhook calls from package installation phase.

suggestion.title: Malicious Post-Install/Post-Update Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attack leverages Composer script hooks to execute attacker code. Article implies injection via package metadata but pipeline extracted zero execution-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected post-install-cmd or post-update-cmd entries in composer.json that execute shell/PHP code. Monitor for modifications to auto-generated autoload.php in vendor/. Alert on PHP execution from Composer directories that doesn't match known library code signatures.

suggestion.title: CI Runner Outbound Network Traffic to Attacker Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Stolen CI secrets must be exfiltrated—malicious package establishes C2 connection. Pipeline generated zero network-detection use cases for data exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTPS/HTTP connections from CI/CD runners to unknown hosts during composer install phase. Flag DNS queries for suspicious domains resolved during package installation. Alert on high-entropy outbound payloads consistent with credential exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Composer Lock File Integrity Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Rewritten tags would modify composer.lock—defenders must detect unauthorized lock file changes outside normal dev workflows.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor composer.lock file for modifications outside normal CI/CD update workflows. Compare lock file hash/signature against expected developer commits. Alert when package commit refs don't match upstream repository heads.

suggestion.title: Version Downgrade or Forced Package Downgrade Attack
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks often use pinned malicious versions. Pipeline should detect forced downgrades to compromised tags or lock-in of infected versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when composer.lock pins packages to non-standard, unsigned, or historically-flagged version tags. Detect forced package-version locks that persist across CI runs without developer authorization. Monitor for version downgrades to tags not matching semantic versioning conventions.

suggestion.title: LiteSpeed cPanel Plugin CVE-2026-48172 Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly mentions CVE-2026-48172 as actively exploited; pipeline generated zero use cases. Should detect HTTP requests to cPanel LiteSpeed plugin endpoints with exploitation payloads or POST requests containing suspicious script/command parameters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cPanel HTTP logs for requests to LiteSpeed plugin endpoints (/cgi-bin/*, /var/www/html extensions) with suspicious query parameters, encoded payloads, or script directives. Spike detection on POST requests from non-administrative IPs to plugin endpoints.

suggestion.title: Script Execution as Root from cPanel Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability exploited 'to run scripts as root' — pipeline missed privilege escalation detection entirely. Should alert on cPanel/httpd processes spawning child processes (shell, python, bash) with UID 0.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when cPanel or web server processes (httpd, php-fpm) spawn shell interpreters (/bin/bash, /bin/sh, /usr/bin/python) with process parent UID in unprivileged range but executed with UID 0. Look for cmdline arguments indicating script execution or system command concatenation.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Command Execution from cPanel Plugin Directory
suggestion.rationale: Privilege escalation via plugin implies arbitrary code execution path. Pipeline should detect execution of binaries or scripts from plugin/module storage locations with elevated privileges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution from cPanel plugin directories (/opt/cpanel/plugins/litespeed, /var/cpanel/addons) with process token elevation or setuid execution. Flag any execution of non-whitelisted scripts or compiled binaries from these paths.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48172 Vulnerability Indicator Detection
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline should have indexed CVE identifier as primary IOC; no IOCs extracted at all. Should create detection anchored on version checking and vendor telemetry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag installations with LiteSpeed cPanel plugin versions in vulnerable range; monitor for failed/successful vulnerability probes (HTTP 40x responses to exploit endpoint, successful script execution returns); correlate with known exploit signatures if available.

suggestion.title: Nginx Worker Child Process Execution - Poolslip RCE
suggestion.rationale: Article abstract states 'Code Execution Attacks'. Nginx RCE typically manifests as unexpected child processes spawned by worker threads or suspicious system calls within Nginx privilege context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned by Nginx worker processes with suspicious executable paths, inline shell invocation, or network socket creation. Monitor for ProcessCreate events where parent=nginx and command deviates from expected static content serving or proxy patterns.

suggestion.title: Malformed HTTP Payloads Targeting Nginx Pool Allocation
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability name 'poolslip' suggests exploitation via pool management logic—requires crafted HTTP requests with buffer/allocation side effects. Article states vulnerability 'enables' attacks but provides no readable detail on request format.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests with abnormal Content-Length values, oversized headers, or malformed chunked transfer encoding that exceed Nginx default buffer thresholds (client_body_buffer_size, proxy_buffer_size). Correlate with Nginx worker crashes or unexpected memory growth.

suggestion.title: Nginx Memory Exhaustion and Connection Pool Saturation - DoS
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Enables DoS'. Pool-based DoS attacks exhaust thread/connection limits or trigger memory leaks in memory-pool management—should manifest as resource exhaustion metrics.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Nginx memory growth rate, thread pool queue depth, and active connection count. Alert on sustained connection-per-second spikes, high rates of failed/reset connections, or Nginx respawning workers (SIGKILL→restart cycle). Baseline normal and detect 5x+ deviation.

suggestion.title: Nginx Reconnaissance for Pool Configuration or Status Exposure
suggestion.rationale: Poolslip exploitation likely requires reconnaissance of Nginx configuration. Attackers may probe for stub_status or config information leakage prior to crafting exploit payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect requests to /nginx_status, /server-status, /status endpoints or requests probing for config reflection. Look for repeated failed requests to diagnostic paths and patterns consistent with fuzzing Nginx tunable parameters (worker_processes, worker_connections).

suggestion.title: Nginx Service Restart or Crash Due to Poolslip Trigger
suggestion.rationale: Pool exploitation may cause worker crashes or daemon restart. Should detect anomalous service-state changes correlating with attack payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid Nginx process termination and respawn (ngxtop, systemctl restart events, or parent-process death with high exit codes). Correlate restart timestamps with HTTP error spikes (502, 503) or connection resets in access logs within ±5 second window.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Execution from Vendor Directory
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks via Laravel packages execute code in vendor/ context. Article states attack 'targets Laravel-Lang packages' implying code execution path.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned from PHP vendor directories or with parent process in vendor/. Filter on common benign vendors. Correlate with package install/update events.

suggestion.title: Credential Access from PHP Application Context
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealer malware component. Article explicitly names 'credential stealer' payload embedded in Laravel packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file system reads targeting .env, credential stores, config files containing secrets from PHP processes. Flag registry access to credential manager or DPAPI calls from web application context.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Outbound Connections from Laravel Application
suggestion.rationale: Credential exfiltration to attacker infrastructure. Supply chain malware must beacon to C2 or exfil endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate Laravel/PHP outbound destinations. Alert on unexpected DNS queries or TLS connections to new/rare domains from application servers. Correlate with credential access events.

suggestion.title: Package Manager Activity Preceding Credential Theft
suggestion.rationale: Attack vector is compromised composer/npm package. Article indicates 'targets Laravel-Lang packages' meaning installation or update event precedes execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate composer install/update commands with subsequent PHP process creation and network/credential events. Flag if package timestamps suggest recent compromise or version mismatch.

suggestion.title: Unexpected File Modification in Laravel Vendor Directory
suggestion.rationale: Backdoored package files. Supply chain attack introduces malicious code into vendor directory during installation.
