suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor vendor/laravel-lang/* for file modifications outside of installer process. Alert on new .php files or modifications to existing ones without corresponding legitimate package updates.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Shared Credentials from Compromised Laravel App
suggestion.rationale: Stolen credentials enable attacker to pivot. Credential stealer payload extracts secrets that may grant access to other systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on authentication using credentials harvested from Laravel environment (.env, config/database.php, etc.). Track source IPs of failed logins correlating with public IPs seen in C2 traffic.

suggestion.title: Drupal Core Public Exposure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states CISA KEV entries are 'currently being exploited' against 'exposed assets' and recommends 'asset-exposure hunt.' The product 'Drupal Core' must be inventoried on public-facing networks as the exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Drupal Core installations accessible from the internet using web service fingerprinting, HTTP header analysis, or vulnerability scanner output. Prioritize hosts with public IP addresses or DNS records resolving externally. Cross-reference with asset inventory to confirm patch status relative to 2026-05-27 deadline.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-9082 SQL Injection Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'specially crafted requests sent with the database abstraction API' as the exploitation vector. Web application logs and database logs must be monitored for abnormal queries targeting Drupal's database layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Drupal endpoints for SQL injection patterns (single quotes, SQL keywords, UNION-based payloads, time-based stacked queries) and database logs for anomalous queries executed with unexpected privileges or context. Flag requests with payloads targeting Drupal's database abstraction API.

suggestion.title: Drupal Vulnerable Version Inventory Gap
suggestion.rationale: Article warns 'patch lag is the silent killer' and establishes federal remediation deadline of 2026-05-27. Any gap between vulnerability scanner assertions of 'not vulnerable' and actual running versions must be resolved before deadline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner output for instances flagged as not-vulnerable due to patching. Cross-reference with software asset inventory and CMDB to confirm version. Alert on any Drupal instances with Drupal Core versions that should be patched per vendor advisory. Verify patching status against federal due date.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PowerShell script execution from LNK shortcut
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attackers emailing ZIP archives containing LNK files that execute external PowerShell scripts. This is the primary infection vector but generated no detection logic. Phrase: 'Attackers use LNK shortcuts to covertly execute PowerShell scripts hosted on external resources.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for cmd.exe or powershell.exe spawned by lnk files via Windows Explorer, especially with /c parameter and remote URLs. Alert on powershell.exe downloading and executing scripts with suspicious naming patterns (fixed.ps1, payload execution). Correlate with parent processes associated with archive extraction.

suggestion.title: Registry Run key persistence with PowerShell startup command
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly documents persistence via HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run with value name 'YandexBrowser_setup' pointing to $temp\fixed.ps1. No detection rule was generated. Phrase: 'Creates "Run" registry key "YandexBrowser_setup" for "$temp\fixed.ps1" startup.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for registry modifications to HKCU/HKLM CurrentVersion\Run where value names match browser names (YandexBrowser, GoogleChrome, etc.) but point to .ps1 files in temp directories or suspicious paths. Alert especially on entries combining legitimate-sounding names with PowerShell/cmd/cscript execution.

suggestion.title: Reverse SSH tunnel and custom SSH patching for persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'reverse SSH tunneling' and 'patched OpenSSH' as C2 channels. No corresponding detection for SSH abuse, port forwarding, or modified SSH binaries. Phrase: 'Reverse SSH tunneling. Patched OpenSSH.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on SSH connections from compromised hosts with reverse port forwarding flags (-R), especially on non-standard SSH ports. Monitor for anomalous SSH process execution (different binary hash, unsigned, or from unusual paths). Detect ssh.exe child processes or unexpected SOCKS listener establishment on high ports.

suggestion.title: termsrv.dll patching for multi-user RDP access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Multi-user RDP by patching termsrv.dll' as a persistence/lateral movement technique. No detection logic captured this. Phrase: 'Multi-user RDP by patching termsrv.dll.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor termsrv.dll in System32 for unsigned modifications, version changes, or hash mismatches against known good baselines. Alert on attempted modifications via rundll32 or cscript with patch/inject flags. Cross-correlate with suspicious RDP session events and concurrent user logins from same host.

suggestion.title: RevSocks and Tor tunnel establishment for C2 redundancy
suggestion.rationale: Article names RevSocks and Tor as C2 channels: 'Tor tunneling PowerCloud Browser checker' and 'RevSocks'. No detection for these SOCKS tunnel tools or protocol signatures. Phrase: 'Reverse SSH tunneling Patched OpenSSH RevSocks Tor tunneling PowerCloud.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for RevSocks binary execution and network signatures (SOCKS5 handshakes on non-proxy ports, suspicious localhost listeners on ephemeral ports). Correlate Tor client initialization with process execution from temp/admin directories. Alert on unusual destination ports paired with SOCKS proxy behavior, especially combined with SSH connections.

suggestion.title: Multi-stage payload execution chain with credential harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article describes staged execution: LNK → PowerShell → fixed.ps1 → VBCloud dropper → PowerShower → credential grabber. This attack chain with 'credential grabber' payload has no corresponding detection. Phrase: 'PowerShower::Payload (credential grabber).'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process chains with 5+ hops starting from archive extraction. Monitor for credential dumping behavior (lsass access, mimikatz-like calls, screen capture APIs, clipboard access). Correlate PowerShell script downloads with subsequent cred-theft patterns. Flag execution of tools named or behaving like PowerShower, credential dumpers, or browser data exporters.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection Payload Detection in HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers use 'specially crafted requests to trigger arbitrary SQL injection'—need detection for malicious SQL syntax in web request parameters targeting Drupal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Drupal endpoints for SQL injection patterns: UNION SELECT, comment sequences (--, /*), quote escaping, and boolean conditions (1=1). Correlate with web application firewall blocks and HTTP 50x responses from vulnerable Drupal versions.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Database Query Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies PostgreSQL as the vulnerable database and notes SQL injection 'trigger arbitrary SQL injection'—need detection for malformed queries in database activity logs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL error logs and audit for syntax errors, unexpected schema access, malformed SQL with embedded comments, UNION operations, or case statements from non-administrative users. Correlate with upstream web layer injection attempts.

suggestion.title: Database Privilege Escalation Post-SQLi
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could result in remote code execution, privilege escalation'—attackers may escalate database privileges or grant admin roles after successful injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GRANT statements, role assignments, or privilege modifications targeting Drupal database objects. Flag creation of new super-users or admin roles following SQL injection detection. Correlate with unusual database access patterns.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Database Access Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability is 'exploitable without authentication'—attackers access Drupal database directly without valid web application login credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect database connections to Drupal schema occurring without corresponding authenticated HTTP sessions to Drupal endpoints. Flag direct database connections originating from web server processes and off-hours access from non-standard source IPs.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration from Drupal Database
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates 'information disclosure' as impact—successful SQL injection enables extraction of sensitive data (users, credentials, content) from the Drupal database.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large SELECT queries on sensitive Drupal tables (users, node, field_data_*), unusual data exports, and volume anomalies in database outbound traffic. Flag queries extracting password hashes or session tokens.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution via SQL Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'could result in remote code execution'—PostgreSQL exploitation may enable RCE via command execution or process spawning from database context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected process spawning from Drupal web server or PostgreSQL daemon. Detect file writes to web directories from database processes, shell command execution from database service accounts, or command-and-control callbacks from compromised application context.

suggestion.title: VPN C2 Infrastructure Used by Ransomware – Network Beacon Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes a VPN service used as C2 by 25 ransomware groups: the takedown targeted this shared infrastructure. Pipeline should flag outbound connections to known C2 VPN endpoints (IPs/domains of the dismantled service).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify hosts establishing persistent outbound connections to VPN service endpoints (typically UDP 500, 1194, 443). Correlate connection timing with known ransomware C2 beacon patterns. Flag organizational egress to VPN service IPs previously published in takedown notices.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Payload Delivery via VPN Tunnel – File Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes ransomware groups using the VPN to distribute payloads. Pipeline should capture detection logic for payloads staged through identified VPN infrastructure during the takedown window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for execution of ransomware samples (hash or behavioral signature) preceded by VPN connection events. Alert on file creation patterns (rapid encryption, .tmp staged payloads) correlated with VPN session establishment.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Through Compromised VPN Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article's mention of '25 groups' using the same infrastructure implies credential sharing or account compromise. Pipeline should include detection for account reuse patterns and impossible-travel scenarios across the VPN.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag multiple distinct ransomware group indicators (malware signatures, TTPs, C2 domains) authenticating from the same VPN IP within short time windows. Alert on geographically impossible VPN access patterns (user in US, then Russia within minutes).

suggestion.title: Law Enforcement VPN Takedown – Historical IoC Invalidation
suggestion.rationale: Article title indicates VPN infrastructure was dismantled. Pipeline should surface takedown timeline and mark any IOCs extracted from the VPN as historical/stale post-takedown.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-takedown, monitor for continued attempts to connect to dismantled VPN endpoints—indicates adversaries with outdated C2 configs or new groups inheriting playbooks. Threshold alerts if legitimate traffic to the IPs persists (misconfiguration vs. persistence).

suggestion.title: Ransomware Group Clustering via Shared VPN Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article reveals 25 separate ransomware groups shared one VPN service. Pipeline should enable correlation: hosts connecting to this VPN should be cross-referenced against IOCs from multiple ransomware families to identify shared infrastructure reuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build a composite alert: if a host connects to VPN infrastructure AND exhibits behavioral/file indicators of Ransomware Family A AND Domain B hosting is known associated with Family C, escalate as multi-family C2 overlap. Useful for attribution and supply-chain risk.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted Domain Registration Targeting Major Events
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'uses a domain that looks close enough to FIFA' and defines typosquatting as 'a domain name that closely resembles the legitimate one, but contains small additions'—core IOC acquisition technique for this attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS resolution and passive DNS feeds for newly registered domains with Levenshtein similarity <3 to high-value brands (FIFA, World Cup, ticketing platforms) within 30–90 days of major sporting events. Flag registrations using .shop, .site, .online TLDs or hosted on privacy registrars.

suggestion.title: Cloned E-Commerce Phishing Site Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes imposter site that 'copies the look and feel of FIFA's official site, including the colors, layout, navigation and ticketing flow'—full site cloning pattern typical of phishing infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SSL certificate issuance, WHOIS registrations, and HTTP response bodies for high string-similarity matches to legitimate e-commerce/ticketing sites. Correlate certificate issuer reputation, issuing CA patterns, and hosting provider ASNs against known phishing infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Fake Registration Form Harvesting Personal Data
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'fake registration form' collects 'name, email address, and phone number'—credential and PII harvesting via deceptive forms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to suspicious domains for submission patterns containing personal identifiers (email, phone, name fields). Correlate with domains flagged as typosquatted or newly registered. Alert on form submissions followed by payment-related requests.

suggestion.title: Credit Card Data Harvesting via Fake Checkout Pages
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Once you enter your card details, it goes straight to the people behind the fake site'—payment card collection as primary objective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to suspicious domains for credit card patterns (16-digit sequences, CVV fields, cardholder names). Correlate with non-PCI-DSS-certified infrastructure. Alert on payment submissions to domains with event-related typosquatting or brand spoofing indicators.

suggestion.title: Phishing Link Distribution via Sponsored Search and Social Media
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies distribution vectors: 'Some victims may reach these websites through sponsored search results, while others click on ads on social media or links in email'—initial access via paid ad networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web gateway logs for HTTP referrers from Google Ads, Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, and email platforms (Office 365, Gmail) leading to typosquatted domains or brand-spoofing sites. Alert on high-velocity clicks from sponsored channels to newly registered or suspicious infrastructure.

suggestion.title: F5 BIG-IP RCE exploitation attempt detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'exposed F5 BIG-IP edge appliance' as initial access vector; no use case generated despite this being the entry point for the entire kill chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor F5 BIG-IP admin panels and REST API endpoints for exploitation patterns (e.g., CVE-2024-47535, CVE-2024-47534 attempt signatures). Alert on unusual process spawning or network connections originating from F5 service accounts or administrative interfaces.

suggestion.title: Confluence server exploitation and file write attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'pivoted to an internal Confluence server'; no detection use case provided for Confluence RCE, file upload, or template injection patterns that likely enabled the compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Confluence RCE exploitation attempts (e.g., template injection, gadget chain deserialization) via POST requests to Confluence endpoints with suspicious payloads. Monitor for process execution (Java child processes) spawned by Confluence service accounts, especially shell invocation.

suggestion.title: Kerberos relay attack detection on Linux
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'threat actor attempted Kerberos relay and lateral movement' but no use case captures relay authentication abuse patterns or NTLM/Kerberos protocol anomalies on Linux hosts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Kerberos relay tools (e.g., krbrelayx, Impacket ntlmrelayx) execution on Linux; detect unusual NTLM authentication flows between Linux systems and Windows targets, or attempts to abuse HTTP→LDAP/LDAPS relay vectors.

suggestion.title: Linux credential extraction and credential access pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article core claim is 'credential theft and identity compromise' from Confluence; no use case for credential harvesting tools, SAM/shadow file access, or memory dumping on Linux targets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution of credential extraction tools (mimikatz, hashcat, crackmapexec, pypykatz) or suspicious access to /etc/shadow, /home/*/.ssh, /root/.bash_history. Monitor for in-memory credential scraping via ptrace() or /proc/*/mem access.

suggestion.title: Multi-stage payload staging and execution on Linux
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'multi-stage' attack implying intermediate payloads or shellcode; no use case for shell script execution, encoded payload decode-and-exec patterns, or suspicious download→execute chains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious bash/sh process chains with curl/wget piped to shell, detection of hex/base64 decode followed by exec, or temporary script creation in /tmp with immediate execution. Flag unusual parent-child process relationships (e.g., Java→bash→curl).

suggestion.title: F5 to Linux pivot lateral movement
suggestion.rationale: Article describes lateral movement from F5 edge appliance to internal Linux Confluence; no use case for detecting cross-zone pivots, SSH abuse from edge devices, or internal scanning originating from compromised appliances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SSH or RDP connections originating from F5 administrative interfaces to internal Linux/Windows targets. Monitor for unusual network scanning (nmap, masscan) from edge appliance IP ranges. Alert on non-standard ports (2222, 2223, etc.) used for lateral movement.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email to Ukraine Government Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article title directly states 'Ghostwriter Targets Ukraine Government Entities with Prometheus Phishing Malware' — phishing is the initial attack vector. No UC generated despite clear attack narrative.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for emails sent to Ukraine government domains (.ua, government entity addresses) originating from newly registered domains or suspicious sender profiles. Flag messages with .exe, .dll, .scr, .lnk, .xls(m) attachments or links to zip archives. Correlate with phishing reporting tool submissions.

suggestion.title: Prometheus Malware Execution
suggestion.rationale: Prometheus is the named malware payload in the article title. Pipeline should have surfaced process execution, file write, or registry signatures associated with this family.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of suspicious child processes spawned from Microsoft Office, WinRAR, or Explorer with low code-signing integrity. Monitor for .tmp/.scr files written to %APPDATA%, unusual registry modifications in Run/RunOnce keys, or command-line arguments obfuscated with quotes/carets.

suggestion.title: Ghostwriter C2 Beacon Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article describes targeting of government entities; implies post-compromise C2. No network IOCs or C2 detection logic generated despite this being standard for malware-focused threat reports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify DNS queries or HTTP POST requests to newly registered Cyrillic or Russian-sounding domains from Ukraine government networks. Flag command servers responding with short TTLs (<300s) or non-standard ports for HTTP/HTTPS. Correlate successful C2 indicators with lateral movement attempts.

suggestion.title: Office Document Macro/DDE Execution
suggestion.rationale: Prometheus phishing campaigns commonly rely on Office documents with embedded macros or DDE triggers. Attack flow not reconstructed despite malware name implying document-based delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Office application (winword.exe, excel.exe) spawning child processes (cmd.exe, powershell.exe) without user interaction. Alert on suspicious macro execution or DDE formula strings in Office files opened from email. Track document temp folder writes followed by executable creation.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Fake Portal
suggestion.rationale: Phishing campaigns targeting government entities typically include credential-stealing objectives. No use case generated for detection of harvested credentials, brute-force attempts post-phishing, or lateral movement from stolen accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate password change events from Ukraine government IDs within hours of phishing campaign dates. Monitor for password spray or brute-force attempts originating from non-government IP ranges against government email systems. Track web server logs for POST requests to fake SSO/portal pages mimicking government authentication.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection Keywords in Bazar Form POST Parameters
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'inject arbitrary SQL into an INSERT statement'—no detection for actual SQL syntax in form data. Gap: monitoring for UNION, SELECT, SLEEP(), BENCHMARK(), information_schema, mysql.*, sqlite_* in POST bodies targeting FormManager.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to YesWiki Bazar form-import endpoints for SQL keywords in form parameters and request body. Flag UNION, SELECT, DELETE, SLEEP(N), BENCHMARK(), WAITFOR DELAY, information_schema, or concatenation operators. Alert on requests from unauthenticated sources (no session cookie). Exclude legitimate admin/developer POST activity via source IP whitelist.

suggestion.title: Database Error Messages in HTTP Response Body
suggestion.rationale: SQLi exploitation triggers database errors visible in responses. Article implies database access without noting error-based exfiltration signatures or schema disclosure patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests to Bazar endpoint followed by HTTP 200/500 responses containing SQL error strings: MySQL ('supplied argument', 'column count'), PostgreSQL ('syntax error', 'relation does not exist'), SQLite ('near', 'syntax error'). Correlation with preceding requests to same endpoint in short time window (5-minute span) suggests iterative enumeration.

suggestion.title: Unusual yeswiki_users Table Access — Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker can 'read the full database, including yeswiki_users.password hashes'—no post-exploitation detection for unauthorized password table access. Directly addresses credential access phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag database queries originating from web-app user account targeting yeswiki_users table SELECT operations, especially with UNION, concatenation, or outbound data operators (INTO OUTFILE, dumpfile). Baseline: YesWiki app should rarely query yeswiki_users directly outside normal auth. Spike in queries suggests exfiltration attempt.

suggestion.title: Time-Based Blind SQLi Detection — Response Latency Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Blind SQLi exploitation via SLEEP() creates temporal signatures. Article references 'blind SQLi extraction loop'—no detection of abnormal response times or progressive delays characteristic of bit-by-bit enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for Bazar form-import endpoint response time (typically <1s). Flag POST requests returning responses with 15-60+ second delays or SLEEP()/BENCHMARK() strings in URL parameters. Alert on sequences of multiple delayed responses from same source IP within short time window, indicating iterative blind SQL enumeration.

suggestion.title: Web Server Outbound Connection Immediately Following Bazar Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates 'read the full database'—data must be exfiltrated. Gap: no correlation between exploitation requests and subsequent data exfiltration to external hosts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect web server process (apache/nginx/yeswiki) initiating outbound TCP/UDP connections to non-whitelisted IPs/FQDNs or establishing large data transfers (>1MB) within 5-10 minutes after spike in POST requests to vulnerable Bazar endpoint. Correlate source IP of malicious requests with egress destination timing.

suggestion.title: YesWiki Version Fingerprinting — Pre-Exploitation Reconnaissance
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability affects 4.6.1, 4.6.2, doryphore-dev specifically. No detection for pre-exploitation version scanning or fingerprinting of YesWiki installations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests to YesWiki version disclosure endpoints (/README, /VERSION, /docs, /.git/config, /admin/settings) or HEAD requests to root path. Detect User-Agent strings associated with web scanners (Nikto, Acunetix, Burp, sqlmap) targeting YesWiki domains. Correlate reconnaissance activity with subsequent exploitation attempts from same source IP.

suggestion.title: FileBrowser Quantum public share PATCH path traversal (CVE-2026-44542)
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'fromPath and toPath body fields ... joined with trusted d.share.Path BEFORE the downstream sanitizer runs' and 'filepath.Join collapses .. segments during the join, the sanitizer never sees the traversal.' Pipeline missed the core exploitation signal: HTTP PATCH with .. in JSON request body to /public/api/resources endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PATCH requests to FileBrowser public share API (/public/api/resources) where the JSON request body contains fromPath or toPath fields with .. traversal sequences. Correlate with HTTP 200/204 responses to confirm exploit success. High fidelity when hash parameter is present (indicates authenticated share access).

suggestion.title: FileBrowser file system impact: unauthorized file operations outside share root
suggestion.rationale: Article describes impact as 'move/copy/rename operates on a path outside the shared directory.' This requires file-system-level detection beyond HTTP logs. Pipeline missed the post-exploitation signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file move/copy/rename operations originating from FileBrowser process (executable path, service account) that target paths outside the configured share root directory. Alert on successful file operations to system directories or parent traversals to /../ locations.

suggestion.title: Volumetric PATCH probing against FileBrowser public share (pre-exploit reconnaissance)
suggestion.rationale: Article tags T1595.002 (Vulnerability Scanning). Pipeline should detect scanning behavior before exploitation. Attacker likely probes multiple hash parameters or path values to identify vulnerable shares.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sustained or spiking volume of PATCH requests to /public/api/resources endpoint from single source, especially with varying hash parameter values or rapid sequential requests. Medium confidence; correlate with lack of corresponding GET requests (normal share browsing).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-44542 vulnerability exposure assessment
suggestion.rationale: Article provides CVE but pipeline produced no asset-hunting recommendation. Asset owners running vulnerable versions (identify via version strings in HTTP headers or app pages) are exposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search network traffic and asset scans for FileBrowser instances exposing public share endpoints. Correlate version strings (Server headers, /admin pages, or service metadata) against known-vulnerable versions of FileBrowser Quantum. Prioritize assets with public IP exposure and active internet-facing public share features.

suggestion.title: Sustained Egress from Telecom ASNs to External C2 Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Large-Scale Command-and-Control Operations' leveraging telecom networks; this necessitates sustained outbound traffic for C2 callbacks and data staging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify high-volume, repetitive data transfers from telecom operator ASNs to uncommon destination ports and ASNs. Monitor for DNS queries from network devices to unusual external domains, or persistent connections on non-standard C2 ports (8080, 8443, custom ephemeral ranges) deviating from baseline customer traffic.

suggestion.title: Administrative Access Abuse on Telecom Network Devices
suggestion.rationale: Compromise of 'networks' for sustained C2 requires breaching management planes; title implies attackers achieved lasting access to core infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag logons to routers, switches, and management platforms (RADIUS/TACACS+ servers, AAA appliances) from non-standard geographies or after-hours. Correlate credential spray attempts against network infrastructure with successful authentications. Monitor for backdoor service accounts or scheduled tasks persisting on network devices.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Across Telecom Core Backbone Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Access to 'telecom networks' implies multi-hop lateral movement from entry points to core backbone or international gateways where C2 can be sustained at scale.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SSH/RDP sessions between network management stations and routing/switching infrastructure. Monitor for remote execution tools (psexec, ssh -X) on network devices. Flag protocol scanners (nmap, zmap) or credential enumeration utilities running on backbone access points.

suggestion.title: Bulk Extraction of Subscriber Metadata from Telecom Databases
suggestion.rationale: Large-scale C2 operations typically harvest customer/subscriber data; telecom networks provide unique access to call detail records, authentication logs, and customer information systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify batch export operations from subscriber databases, CDR systems, or identity management platforms. Monitor for unusual SQL queries returning large result sets, bulk data dumps via TFTP/SCP, or file transfers from billing/customer-care servers to external destinations.

suggestion.title: Telecom Network Configuration and Firewall Rule Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Attackers maintaining large-scale C2 ops would exfiltrate routing configs, ACLs, and firewall policies to maintain persistent access and evade detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag backup/config exports from core routers, firewalls, or load balancers followed by file transfers to external IPs. Monitor unauthorized device config reads by service accounts or automation systems. Detect TFTP/SCP/FTP usage on normally air-gapped management networks.

suggestion.title: DDoS Amplification or BGP Hijacking via Compromised Telecom Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Telecom networks offer unmatched reach for C2 amplification attacks; attackers may weaponize infrastructure for DDoS or BGP route hijacking to expand impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify volumetric traffic spikes from telecom IPs to external targets. Monitor BGP route advertisements from operator ASNs announcing unexpected prefix ranges. Alert on ICMP/DNS reflection attacks sourced from telecom infrastructure or large-scale packet floods with spoofed source IPs.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation from Untrusted Registry
suggestion.rationale: Article headline establishes backdoored npm package as initial access vector. Pipeline should detect installation of art-template or similar supply-chain compromises.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm install/npm ci commands installing art-template or similar template packages. Track process parent (npm) spawning child processes. Cross-reference installed versions against known-malicious version manifests.

suggestion.title: Execution from npm node_modules Directory
suggestion.rationale: Watering-hole and backdoor attacks execute malicious code when the package is instantiated. Title phrase 'Watering-Hole Attacks' implies code execution from the compromised package at runtime.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag child processes spawned by Node.js interpreters running code from node_modules/art-template or similar paths. Detect unusual process chains: npm → node → cmd.exe, powershell, or curl with network I/O.

suggestion.title: Watering-Hole Payload Delivery Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'Watering-Hole Attacks' as the attack goal. Pipeline must surface detection for HTTP/DNS beaconing and payload staging characteristic of watering-hole campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTP requests from Node.js processes to unusual domains. Monitor for DNS queries from npm runtimes to adversary-controlled C2 infrastructure. Flag multi-stage payload indicators: small initial beacon → larger second-stage binary transfer.

suggestion.title: npm Package Dependency Chain Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromise often includes malicious transitive dependencies or package.json modifications. Article phrase 'Backdoor Popular art-template npm Package' implies nested or hidden payload delivery mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Audit package.json and package-lock.json for unusual dependency versions, unexpected transitive pulls, or install scripts that execute non-standard commands (curl, powershell, base64 decode).

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised Shared Package
suggestion.rationale: Watering-hole attacks often target multiple downstream users. Should detect when a single compromised package install cascades to multiple hosts or accounts within an org.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate npm install events for art-template across multiple hosts within a time window. Flag if follow-on process execution patterns (beaconing, credential access) appear consistently post-install.

suggestion.title: Batch File Execution from Email Attachment
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'malicious batch files' and 'NF-e Invoice Lures'—a direct email→attachment→execution attack chain. Zero use cases generated for this foundational attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect user download/opening of .bat or .cmd file attachments from email, especially those with invoice-themed subject lines or spoofed sender domains. Alert if batch file lands in temp directory and is immediately executed.

suggestion.title: CMD.exe or PowerShell Spawned from Batch Script
suggestion.rationale: Attack sequence stated in title: batch file → RAT deployment. Pipeline must detect cmd.exe/powershell child processes originating from recently-written batch files in user temp folders.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on cmd.exe or powershell.exe spawned as child process of a .bat or .cmd file located in %TEMP%, %AppData%, or Downloads. Flag if command line contains encoded payloads or suspicious network utilities.

suggestion.title: Banana RAT Malware Family Signature Detection
suggestion.rationale: Banana RAT is named in title as the payload. Pipeline should surface known Banana RAT file hashes, process names, registry artifacts, or behavioral signatures (if provided in article body). Zero malware IOCs extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for known Banana RAT process names, file paths, mutex patterns, or API call sequences. Cross-reference against malware sample repositories for variants mentioned in threat intel feeds.

suggestion.title: NF-e Invoice Phishing Attachment Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states lures use 'NF-e Invoice' theme—a Brazil-specific financial document targeting. Pipeline should flag NF-e-themed emails as high-risk social engineering. No initial-access detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify emails with NF-e (Nota Fiscal Eletrônica) keywords, spoofed Brazilian tax authority (SEFAZ) sender addresses, or invoicing-language body text. Correlate with executable/script attachment types to flag impersonation.

suggestion.title: Banana RAT C2 Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Banana RAT is a remote access trojan; article establishes it reaches out for command & control. Pipeline failed to generate network-layer detection for C2 communication patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections from newly-spawned cmd.exe or unknown processes to known or suspected C2 domains. Look for unusual User-Agent strings, POST requests with suspicious payload encoding, or connections to Brazil-based infrastructure.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-64328 / CVE-2025-57819 Exploitation Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies two FreePBX vulnerabilities as primary infection points: post-authentication command injection in filestore module (CVE-2025-64328) and pre-authentication SQL injection in Endpoint module (CVE-2025-57819). Article notes 'patching an already-infected host leaves the cron infrastructure running and the malware fully capable of re-establishing itself.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FreePBX filestore module for POST requests with shell metacharacters or command separators (;, |, &, $(), backticks). Alert on SQL injection patterns in Endpoint module requests containing UNION, SELECT, OR 1=1. Correlate with subsequent PHP file creation in /admin/modules/ directories.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Cron Job Polling (1-3 minute intervals)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Layer 1 persistence as 'Cron polling: Downloads and re-executes dropper every 1-3 minutes from C2.' This abnormal polling frequency from legitimate FreePBX cron paths is a detection opportunity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /etc/cron.d/ and /var/spool/cron/crontabs/ for entries with sub-5-minute intervals downloading/executing from HTTP(S) endpoints. Alert on curl/wget/wget2 invocations spawned by cron with URLs containing /k.php or similar patterns. Focus on newly created cron entries touching /dev/null or redirecting to /tmp/.

suggestion.title: Shell Profile Injection for Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Layer 2: 'Shell profile injection: Re-infection triggers on root login and system reboot.' This represents modification of .bashrc, .bash_profile, .zprofile to re-execute malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modifications to ~/.bashrc, ~/.bash_profile, ~/.zprofile, /root/.bashrc, /etc/profile.d/* that introduce base64-encoded content or download commands. Correlate with subsequent process spawning from shell initialization contexts. Watch for changes to these files outside configuration management windows.

suggestion.title: Immutable File Attribute Setting on System Files
suggestion.rationale: Article describes Layer 3: 'Immutable crontab copies: Eight protected copies in hidden directories with file attributes blocking deletion even by root.' This requires chattr +i or equivalent to lock files, which is anomalous for legitimate crontabs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of chattr (especially chattr +i) on cron-related files, .bashrc, .bash_profile, or .php files. Monitor for chattr invocations with privileges outside patching/hardening windows. Flag attempts to set immutable attributes on files in /var/spool/cron/, /var/www/html/admin/modules/, or hidden directories like /.cron/ or /.bin/.

suggestion.title: Webshell Detection in FreePBX Modules
suggestion.rationale: Article states Layer 5: 'Webshell distribution: Twelve+ locations across FreePBX web tree' and specifically mentions 'license.php location: /var/www/html/admin/modules/freepbx_ha/'. Article notes watermark string 'trace_e1ebf9066a951be519a24140711839ea' and file hashes (d40180f7, 995e6304, 039d648b) for JOMANGY variants.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for .php files in non-standard FreePBX locations (/admin/modules/freepbx_ha/, /var/www/html/admin/modules/ with file creation timestamps after system baseline). Scan for watermark string 'trace_e1ebf9066a951be519a24140711839ea' in PHP source. Monitor HTTP requests to /z/post/root.php, /z/post/noroot.php, /k.php. Hash-match against known JOMANGY variants (b506fc82, 100259af, d40180f7, 995e6304, 039d648b).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Hidden System Accounts (FreePBX Context)
suggestion.rationale: Article documents 18 hidden accounts across privilege tiers, with 'account names like asterisk, freepbx_user, and spamfilter deliberately chosen to blend into the legitimate account list.' Lists specific UID-0 backdoor accounts: newfpbx, newfpbxs, xhimax, centos, admin, support, issabel, sangoma, emo. Article notes SHA1 hash 6ea9c6d2d932532a4cd44c7974fb1a0a87dbfcf9 for MySQL web panel injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on user account creation (useradd, passwd, adduser) with UIDs matching legitimate FreePBX accounts but with suspicious usernames (newfpbx, xhimax, centos, issabel, sangoma, emo, sugarmaint, supermaint, supports). Cross-reference /etc/passwd against baseline. Monitor for UID-0 or UID-999 accounts outside expected service account set. Query MySQL for password hashes matching 6ea9c6d2d932532a4cd44c7974fb1a0a87dbfcf9.

suggestion.title: Detect Anomalous Outbound UDP Traffic Patterns
suggestion.rationale: DDoS botnet articles typically describe botnet C2 communication and attack traffic. A botnet operator's infrastructure implies large-scale outbound flooding (UDP floods are standard in DDoS attacks). This should have been detected from any mention of 'DDoS attacks' or 'botnet operator.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sources generating sustained high-volume UDP traffic to multiple external destinations, or traffic with unusually high packet counts and low byte-per-packet ratios (typical of flooding). Correlate source IPs against known botnet indicators.

suggestion.title: Detect DDoS-for-Hire Service Registration and Domain Hosting
suggestion.rationale: The title explicitly mentions 'DDoS-for-hire attacks'—this implies a service with customer-facing infrastructure. Domain registration, payment infrastructure, and service websites should have been extracted as IOCs or detection opportunities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag domains recently registered to abuse registrars or hosting providers known for bulletproof hosting. Monitor for newly registered domains with DNS patterns consistent with service advertisements or C2 proxying. Cross-reference with payment processors linked to prior DDoS-for-hire operations.

suggestion.title: Detect Botnet Malware Deployment and Command Execution
suggestion.rationale: Any DDoS botnet operator arrest would reference malware samples, distribution vectors, or victim machine compromise. Pipeline should have extracted file hashes, deployment methods, or execution patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of unsigned binaries matching known botnet signatures or behavioral patterns (e.g., early child processes spawning network communication, persistence mechanisms). Monitor for mass deployment via email, web, or supply-chain vectors if malware distribution details are mentioned in investigation.

suggestion.title: Detect Command-and-Control Communication (Botnet C2)
suggestion.rationale: Botnet operators maintain C2 infrastructure to issue commands and receive status updates from infected machines. Any article on a botnet operator MUST reference C2 domains, IP addresses, or communication protocols. None were extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound traffic to known Kimwolf C2 IP addresses or domains. Monitor for beaconing behavior (regular check-ins), unusual port usage, or encrypted tunnels matching botnet profiles. Correlate source machines for clustering indicative of large-scale compromise.

suggestion.title: Detect DDoS Attack Launch from Botnet Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: The core of the article is the DDoS-for-hire service itself—the attacks launched on behalf of customers. Attack traffic patterns, target profiles, and victim sectors should inform detection use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for characteristics of DDoS attacks: sudden spike in traffic from diverse sources to single target, volumetric flooding (UDP/ICMP), protocol-based attacks (SYN floods), or application-layer attacks. Correlate attack sources against known botnet IP ranges or ASNs associated with Kimwolf infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Detect Operator Infrastructure (Financial, Administrative, Hosting)
suggestion.rationale: Law enforcement arrested an operator in Canada—this implies traceable infrastructure (servers, email accounts, payment processors, infrastructure providers). Pipeline should flag administrative artifacts linking the operator to botnets or DDoS service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag servers, domains, or IP ranges registered to known Kimwolf operator identities or alternate personas. Monitor hosting provider abuse channels for reports of operator infrastructure. Cross-reference operator email/payment accounts with other botnets or cybercriminal forums.

suggestion.title: Unsigned or Malicious Kernel Driver Load
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD fundamentally requires loading a vulnerable driver. Article title: 'Making Vulnerable Drivers Exploitable Without Hardware—The BYOVD Perspective' establishes that driver loading is the attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .sys file creation, driver registry modifications (HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services), and unsigned kernel-mode module loads. Correlate with user-mode process context to identify exploitation attempts. BYOVD typically loads drivers from predictable, writable paths or via registry service entries.

suggestion.title: Kernel-Mode Code Execution from Unprivileged Process
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD exploits vulnerable drivers to achieve kernel code execution without hardware. The attack chain necessarily transitions from user-mode process to kernel-mode privilege.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag processes that call kernel APIs via IOCTL (I/O Control Code) handlers on vulnerable drivers, or correlate user-mode process spawning with unexpected kernel privilege grants. Look for CreateRemoteThread or WriteProcessMemory targeting system processes after driver load.

suggestion.title: Service Installation with Vulnerable Driver Binary
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD attacks often persist via Windows service registration pointing to a vulnerable driver. Article implies 'exploitable without hardware'—indicating repeated access to the driver for privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for service creation (sc create, New-Service, registry writes to HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\*\ImagePath) where ImagePath points to .sys files in suspicious locations (Temp, AppData, Downloads). Correlate with known vulnerable driver versions.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Kernel Memory Read/Write via Driver IOCTL
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD exploits expose arbitrary kernel memory access. The phrase 'Making Vulnerable Drivers Exploitable Without Hardware' indicates leveraging driver functionality for unintended kernel operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes issuing DeviceIoControl calls to driver handles with patterns of repeated kernel memory access. Monitor for processes accessing SYSTEM-integrity memory regions, modifying kernel structures, or patching security-relevant kernel code (e.g., EPROCESS tokens, access control lists).

suggestion.title: Exploitation of Known Vulnerable Driver (CVE Correlation)
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD campaigns rely on specific vulnerable drivers (e.g., RTCore64, Gigabyte EC, ASUSTeK EC). Article title 'Vulnerable Drivers Exploitable' implies specific CVEs are discussed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain a list of known-vulnerable drivers (hashes, names, versions) tied to public BYOVD campaigns. Alert on ImageLoad events matching vulnerable driver hashes, or on .sys files written to disk matching known-vulnerable signatures. Correlate with process ancestry to identify delivery mechanism (email, download, lateral movement).

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion via Driver-Based EDR Bypass
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD enables bypassing kernel-level security (EDR, antivirus). Drivers are often 'legitimate but vulnerable,' implying defensive bypass.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes attempting to disable or tamper with security-product kernel modules (e.g., modifying PsSetCreateProcessNotifyRoutine, unhooking kernel callbacks). Detect reads/writes to security driver memory regions via vulnerable driver IOCTL handlers. Flag processes with unexpected kernel-mode access after driver load.

suggestion.title: Suspicious GitHub Workflow Creation or Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'malicious CI/CD workflows' injected into repositories. The core mechanism of the attack is workflow creation/modification which would be detectable via GitHub API logs or repository audit trails.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for programmatic creation or modification of .github/workflows YAML files across multiple repositories in short timeframes. Alert on workflow files that execute commands to exfiltrate environment variables, secrets, or build artifacts. Correlate with unusual GitHub API token usage patterns.

suggestion.title: Credential Access from CI/CD Environment Variables
suggestion.rationale: Malicious workflows injected into CI/CD pipelines would have access to repository secrets and environment variables. Detection of unauthorized reads or exfiltration of CI_* or SECRET_* environment variables to external URLs indicates compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect workflow jobs that invoke commands to dump environment variables (env, printenv, $ENV) or access GitHub token files. Flag network connections from CI runners to non-whitelisted external domains carrying suspicious payloads. Monitor for base64-encoded or zipped environment output in job logs.

suggestion.title: Mass Repository Compromise Pattern — Unusual Fork or Commit Activity
suggestion.rationale: Attack targeted 5,561 repositories, implying either bulk compromise of shared accounts or widespread exploitation of a common vector. Detection of simultaneous malicious commits or workflow additions across unrelated repos suggests coordinated compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on commits or workflow files added to >100 unique repositories within a 1-hour window from the same actor or API token. Detect commits with suspicious metadata (generic messages, auto-generated names, non-human author patterns). Flag if commits modify or create workflows in repos with no prior workflow activity.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Build Artifacts or Repository Secrets
suggestion.rationale: Malicious workflows in CI/CD systems commonly exfiltrate secrets, SSH keys, API tokens, and build artifacts to attacker-controlled infrastructure. Detection of data egress from CI runners to external URLs indicates payload delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTPS/HTTP POST requests from GitHub Actions runners or CI agents to unusual domains carrying Base64-encoded, gzipped, or chunked data. Detect DNS queries from CI infrastructure to newly registered domains. Flag workflow logs mentioning curl/wget to external IPs or domains not in approved artifact repositories.

suggestion.title: Detection of Compromised GitHub Personal Access Tokens (PATs) in Logs
suggestion.rationale: If 5,561 repos were compromised, attackers likely obtained or generated GitHub PATs. Exposure of valid tokens in workflow logs, error messages, or exfiltrated data indicates credential compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search workflow logs and artifact storage for GitHub token patterns (ghp_*, ghs_*, ghu_*). Alert on PAT creation events for service accounts followed by atypical API usage (bulk repo access, secret reads). Detect tokens with unusual scopes or repositories accessed outside normal developer workflows.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Workflow Modification in Public Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack mechanism: 'mass GitHub Actions secret exfiltration across 5,500+ public repositories'—implies modification of Actions workflows to execute attacker code. Pipeline extracted zero detection logic for this initial compromise vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub audit logs and API activity for unexpected modifications to .github/workflows/ files in public repositories. Flag workflow YAML changes that add new environment variables, secrets access, or outbound network calls in low-contributor repos. Correlate with commit author reputation and PR approval patterns.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Secrets Access via GitHub Actions Job Runtime
suggestion.rationale: Core attack objective stated in title: 'secret exfiltration'—attacker runs code in Actions context with access to GITHUB_TOKEN and repository secrets. No detection proposed for anomalous secrets enumeration or access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect jobs in GitHub Actions that reference unusual secrets or environment variables outside normal repo workflows. Flag env-var dumps in logs, base64-encoded output of secrets, or dynamic secret enumeration via GH CLI. Alert on GITHUB_TOKEN used to access unrelated repos' secrets API.

suggestion.title: Egress to Attacker-Controlled Exfiltration Point from GitHub Actions Runner
suggestion.rationale: Attack requires command-and-control or data staging: 'exfiltration...across 5,500+ repositories' implies centralized data collection to attacker infrastructure. No network-based detection proposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network traffic from GitHub-hosted runners for unexpected outbound connections to non-GitHub domains, particularly suspicious TLDs or newly registered domains. Flag jobs that curl/wget to external IPs, pipe output to remote servers, or use uncommon protocols (SMTP, FTP, raw sockets) for data exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Bulk Workflow Activity Spike in Non-Owned Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Phrase 'mass...across 5,500+ public repositories' indicates coordinated, large-scale deployment. No volume or anomaly-based detection suggested for orchestrated attack campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify unusual clustering of workflow modifications, new Actions job executions, or secrets access across disjoint repositories within short time window. Correlate by modified YAML content hash, shell command signatures, or exfiltration endpoint overlap to detect supply-chain or mass-compromise campaigns.

suggestion.title: GitHub Token Reuse Across Unrelated Repository Contexts
suggestion.rationale: GITHUB_TOKEN in Actions is scoped per-repo by default. Exfiltration at scale suggests either token reuse, escape to org-level tokens, or bulk compromise of multiple token issuances—none of which are detection targets in pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when a single GITHUB_TOKEN or GitHub app credential is observed accessing multiple unrelated repos' secrets, especially across repos not connected by ownership or CI/CD dependency. Flag org-level token creation without justification and subsequent cross-repo secret queries.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Logs Deletion or Suppression Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Sophisticated attack would attempt to cover tracks: 'mass' exfiltration requires evasion to avoid detection. Pipeline proposed no defense-evasion detections for log tampering or evidence removal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect jobs that attempt to delete or modify GitHub Actions run logs, artifacts, or audit entries post-exfiltration. Flag use of GitHub API to purge workflow logs, disable audit logging, or restrict repository visibility immediately after suspicious job execution.

suggestion.title: Traffic to seized C2 infrastructure netblocks
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 800 seized servers in Dronten and Schiphol-Rijk that 'enabled cyberattacks' and hosted DDoS infrastructure; detecting flows to/from these facilities post-seizure signals threat actor pivoting or infrastructure rebuild.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on network flows destined to historical Stark Industries / WorkTitans IP ranges; correlate with DDoS tool ports (high-numbered UDP, TCP 445, 3389) or typical C2 callbacks to identify active threat operations post-seizure.

suggestion.title: Shell company registration following EU sanctions
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Following this restriction [EU sanctions on Stark Industries], the web hosting infrastructure was transferred to a newly created Dutch company [WorkTitans B.V.] that investigators believe acted as a front'; rapid B.V. entity creation post-sanction signals evasion strategy.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Dutch B.V. registrations within 30–60 days of EU sanctions on known malicious hosters; cross-reference ASN ownership changes and colocation facility transfers (Mirhosting) to detect infrastructure rehoming.

suggestion.title: Colocation facility hand-off to sanctioned-entity infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies Mirhosting as 'the transport layer through which Stark's traffic entered Europe' providing 'physical servers, colocation, and supplied high-capacity connectivity to major internet exchanges in Amsterdam and Frankfurt'; detecting such intermediation enables supply-chain interdiction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor colocation facilities for sudden BGP prefix origin changes, large inter-facility data transfers, or re-announcement of previously seized IP ranges through new carriers; flag unusual spike in traffic between Mirhosting and newly-formed Dutch ISPs.

suggestion.title: DDoS infrastructure signatures attributed to NoName057(16)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly links seized infrastructure to 'pro-Russian hacktivist group NoName057(16), which has previously targeted key organizations with distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks'; detecting tool/botnet footprints on seized servers identifies active threat operations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate HTTP and DNS patterns from seized Stark/WorkTitans IP space with documented NoName057(16) DDoS campaign signatures (specific UA strings, rogue DNS registrars, characteristic netflow attack patterns) to detect ongoing or resurrected botnet C2 channels.

suggestion.title: Passive DNS correlation to identify sanctioned-entity hosted malware
suggestion.rationale: Article describes hosting enabling 'cyberattacks' and 'interference operations'; passive DNS records of domains historically resolving to seized infrastructure reveal malware families and customer organizations tied to Russian/Belarusian sanctioned entities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query passive DNS for all domains that resolved to Stark Industries and WorkTitans IP ranges; cross-reference against OFAC/EU sanctions lists and known Russian government IT infrastructure to uncover hosted malware C2 domains and disinformation staging infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Compromised VS Code Extension Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article title establishes compromised extension delivery; typical for supply-chain attacks where malicious version is available for auto-update or direct installation from marketplace.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect installation or activation of Nx Console extension versions matching known-compromised release tags, or unexpected extension downloads/installs triggered by low-privileged user context. Monitor VSCode extension folder (.vscode/extensions) for creation/modification of nx-console binaries outside normal update windows.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Network Connection from VS Code Process
suggestion.rationale: Compromised extensions typically exfiltrate secrets, tokens, or source code to attacker C2; article does not specify C2 infrastructure but supply-chain attacks on dev tools universally attempt data ex-filtration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound connections from code.exe or related VS Code child processes to non-standard ports or ASNs outside development-tool vendors (GitHub, npm, Azure, GitLab). Correlate with absence of user-initiated browser activity in same timeframe.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Child Process Execution from VS Code Extension
suggestion.rationale: Compromised extensions can spawn shells, downloaders, or credential-theft tools; absence of process-execution detection in generated use cases is a critical gap for extension-based supply-chain attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cmd.exe, powershell.exe, curl, wget, or script interpreters spawned as children of code.exe or extension-bundled Node process (node.exe running from .vscode/extensions). Alert on absence of corresponding user shell history or IDE UI interactions.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Developer Environment
suggestion.rationale: Extension-based supply-chain attacks target developer secrets: SSH keys, API tokens, cloud credentials in environment or source control; pipeline produced no detection for credential access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file reads by VS Code or extension processes targeting .ssh, .aws, .kube, .git, or .env files in user home directories. Flag environment variable enumeration (set, env, Get-ChildItem env:) triggered from extension context.

suggestion.title: Bulk Source Code or Artifact Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Compromised dev tools often harvest entire codebases and build artifacts for IP theft; no exfiltration detection rule was generated despite HIGH severity classification.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high-volume file reads from project root directories followed by unusual HTTPS or DNS tunneling over extended sessions. Correlate extension-process file access patterns with network data volume spikes to non-vendor IPs.

suggestion.title: ROADtools Execution via Azure CLI or PowerShell
suggestion.rationale: Article title and keywords reference ROADtools as the central attack tool. 'ROADtools' is explicitly named; attackers must execute the framework to perform Azure reconnaissance and attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for ROADtools commands and modules (e.g., roadtx, graphrunner) invoked via PowerShell, CLI, or Python. Look for child processes spawning Azure CLI (az.cmd/az.ps1) or Microsoft Graph SDK imports.

suggestion.title: Entra ID Token Manipulation via ROADtools
suggestion.rationale: Keywords explicitly mention 'Entra ID' and 'Microsoft Graph API'; ROADtools is specifically designed to enumerate and abuse Entra ID objects. Article likely details token theft or manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous access token requests to Microsoft Graph API, service principal token requests from untrusted sources, and bulk Entra ID object enumeration via Microsoft Graph (users, applications, service principals, groups).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Azure Application Registration or Service Principal Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Nation-state attackers using ROADtools typically create or hijack Azure applications/service principals for persistence. Keywords include 'Entra ID', 'Microsoft Graph API', suggesting app-level compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation of new applications or service principals with high API permissions (Graph, Azure, Azure Storage). Detect unusual credential updates (certificates, secrets) on existing apps and abnormal consent grants by non-admin users.

suggestion.title: Azure Role Assignment Escalation
suggestion.rationale: ROADtools includes modules for Azure RBAC manipulation. Nation-state actors would escalate privileges to maintain cloud access. Keywords confirm Azure/Entra ID focus.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid or unusual role assignments to Service Principals or users (especially Global Admin, Contributor, Owner roles). Flag assignments from low-privilege or external identities.

suggestion.title: Microsoft Graph API Enumeration or Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Keywords explicitly list 'Microsoft Graph API'; ROADtools and nation-state actors leverage it for reconnaissance (user/org discovery) and exfiltration (mail, SharePoint, Teams). Article clearly focuses on this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bulk or untypical Microsoft Graph calls (e.g., /users, /applications, /servicePrincipals, /mail). Detect large data pulls from Exchange, SharePoint, or Teams via Graph. Correlate with Service Principal or app token usage.

suggestion.title: Nation-State Actor IOC Correlation (Curious Serpens, Midnight Blizzard, Void Blizzard)
suggestion.rationale: Keywords name three threat actors. Article title indicates 'Nation-State Tactics'. Pipeline should extract actor names and correlate with known IOCs, TTPs, and infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference actor names (Curious Serpens, Midnight Blizzard/UTA0355, Void Blizzard) against known indicators: C2 domains, compromised Azure tenant IDs, malicious app registrations, and phishing infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Nezha CVE-2026-46716: POST /api/v1/cron with privilege escalation bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'The cron routes POST /api/v1/cron...are wired through commonHandler (any authenticated user) rather than adminHandler, and the per-server permission check on cron creation has a vacuous-true bypass.' This is the initial exploitation vector requiring dedicated detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST /api/v1/cron requests from RoleMember accounts (privilege level 1) that successfully create cron tasks or modify server permissions. Flag requests with empty server arrays or CronCoverAll flag set to true, indicating intent to compromise multiple monitored endpoints.

suggestion.title: Nezha agent: credential dumping via shell execution (post-exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'nezha-agent spawning credential-access shell commands on Linux' targeting '/etc/passwd and /etc/shadow' (T1003.008). Pipeline missed the post-exploitation detection phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process spawning from nezha-agent or shell children of nezha-agent with command lines accessing /etc/shadow, /etc/passwd, or invoking cat/grep/awk against these files. Correlate process tree to confirm child spawning from compromised agent.

suggestion.title: Nezha agent: outbound connection to cloud instance metadata service
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'nezha-agent outbound network connection to cloud instance-metadata service' with T1552.005 (Unsecured Credentials). Targets include 169.254.169.254, metadata.google.internal, metadata.azure.com — all standard cloud credential-harvesting IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate outbound network connections from nezha-agent processes to 169.254.169.254 or *.metadata.*.* domains against process inventory. Flag any IMDS/GCP/Azure metadata requests originating from Nezha agent parent process or shell children.

suggestion.title: Nezha API: RoleMember account invoking admin-only functionality
suggestion.rationale: Article's core finding: 'RoleMember (Role==1)' should not have access to cron routes, but 'commonHandler (any authenticated user)' allows bypass. This is broken access control (T1078, T1068).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Nezha API logs for authenticated requests where Role==1 (RoleMember) successfully invokes /api/v1/cron modifications or reads. Establish baseline of which user roles should touch cron endpoints; flag any low-privilege role bypassing expected authorization gates.

suggestion.title: Nezha: scheduled cron task creation with embedded shell commands
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies T1053.005 (Scheduled Task) as persistence mechanism. Should detect cron payloads containing command execution syntax, not just task creation events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect POST /api/v1/cron request bodies for presence of shell metacharacters, command substitution ($(), backticks), piping (|), output redirection (>, >>), or known credential-dumping commands (cat, curl, wget to metadata endpoints).

suggestion.title: Compromised Laravel-Lang Package Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states '233 Versions of Laravel-Lang Packages' compromised—pipeline extracted zero detection strategy. Any composer install/update pulling from versions 1–233 is execution of attacker code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on composer install/update commands targeting laravel-lang package. Cross-reference installed version against known-compromised version list (all versions through stated compromise). Escalate if execution occurs in production web-application context with outbound network access.

suggestion.title: GitHub Repository Unauthorized Commit Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates '700 GitHub Repos' were hacked to inject malicious code. Pipeline missed detection for indicators of GitHub account compromise or unauthorized source code modification preceding package publication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub API logs for unusual sign-in patterns to laravel-lang maintainer accounts (new IPs, new devices, off-hours activity). Alert on commits from non-maintainer accounts, commits bypassing code-review, or rapid version-bump commits without corresponding issue/PR discussion.

suggestion.title: Malicious Code Injection in PHP Autoload
suggestion.rationale: Article implies malicious code was injected into packages themselves—'233 Versions' means autoload or bootstrap files were modified. Pipeline did not identify detection for suspicious autoload directives in composer.json.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse composer.json in vendor/laravel-lang/ for suspicious autoload targets (eval, system, passthru, shell execution, unexpected external URLs). Alert if autoload scripts create network sockets, modify system files, or execute code outside vendor directory during package installation.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Package Verification Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 233 compromised versions distributed via package manager. Missing detection for composer.lock hash mismatches or signature verification failures that would catch installed package tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare installed laravel-lang package file hashes against official Packagist repository checksums recorded at installation time. Alert when hash divergence is detected post-installation or when composer.lock contains version number not present in official package history.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Network Activity from Package Vendor Directory
suggestion.rationale: Compromised packages likely exfiltrate data or establish C2. Article does not specify payload, but pipeline should flag network I/O originating from /vendor/laravel-lang/ execution context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound DNS queries and HTTP/HTTPS connections initiated from PHP processes executing from vendor/laravel-lang/ directory. Alert on connections to non-standard ports, newly-registered domains, or IPs with high malware association. Baseline against legitimate package update/telemetry traffic.

suggestion.title: Batch Package Version Update Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article states '700 GitHub Repos' hacked—suggests coordinated release of 233 malicious versions. Pipeline missed detection for sudden spike in laravel-lang version updates across enterprise environment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when more than 10 machines deploy new laravel-lang versions to composer.lock within 1-hour window. Investigate if version numbers cluster around a specific minor/patch release. Cross-check against deployment schedules; unpredictable batch updates suggest compromised dependency resolver or supply chain incident.

suggestion.title: F5 BIG-IP Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Exploit F5 BIG-IP Appliance.' No UC captures attacks against this critical initial-access vector in the output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor F5 BIG-IP access logs and tmsh audit trails for exploitation signatures targeting known CVEs (e.g., 2022-41622, 2023-46805 family). Detect anomalous POST requests to management endpoints, command-injection patterns in config parameters, and HTTP status sequences consistent with successful exploitation.

suggestion.title: SSH Access Originating from F5 BIG-IP System
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attackers using F5 to 'Gain SSH Access'—implies the compromised appliance becomes an SSH client. This is abnormal and should trigger detection of outbound SSH from the F5.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on SSH connections (outbound from F5 or inbound to Linux from F5 IP) that deviate from baseline. Most F5 deployments do not initiate SSH; flag any F5→Linux SSH sessions as anomalous unless explicitly whitelisted. Correlate F5 compromise indicators with downstream SSH access.

suggestion.title: Post-F5-Pivot Reconnaissance in Enterprise Linux Networks
suggestion.rationale: Article phrase: 'Pivot Into Enterprise Linux Networks.' Implies active discovery post-compromise. No UC captures this reconnaissance phase on Linux hosts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Within 1 hour of suspicious SSH login (especially from F5 or new sources), detect rapid-fire execution of discovery commands: ps, netstat, ip, hostname, whoami, id, uname, df, lsb_release, cat /etc/passwd. Correlate process chains to identify coordinated reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: SSH Credential Abuse or Key Installation for Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Pivoting 'via SSH' implies either stolen credentials or persistence via SSH keys. Must detect unauthorized ~/.ssh/authorized_keys modifications or SSH key creation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthorized appends/modifications to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, creation of new SSH keys in /root or service accounts, changes to sshd_config enabling weak auth, and mass key distribution across Linux hosts.

suggestion.title: Credential or SSH Key Exfiltration from F5 Storage
suggestion.rationale: F5 stores SSH keys and credentials for management/federation. Pivoting requires access to these; detect theft of F5 credential stores or backup configs containing authentication material.
log_sources: file access logs for /var/prompt or credential directories
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect access to F5 credential managers, SSH key stores, UCS backup file reads, or config exports by non-standard processes or users. Flag download of F5 system backups that may contain SSH keys or hashed credentials used for Linux access.

suggestion.title: Command Execution on F5 Appliance (Post-Exploitation)
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation of F5 enables command execution. Article implies attacker gained control; detect tmsh command injection, root shell access, or file writes to F5 filesystem.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor F5 tmsh logs for unauthorized administrative commands (write, create, modify on system partitions), shell access, or script execution. Detect POST requests with command-injection payloads ($(cmd) or backticks) in config parameters or REST API calls.

suggestion.title: Compromised PHP Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Laravel-Lang PHP Packages Compromised'—packages are installed via Composer or direct inclusion, making installation events a critical detection point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for package manager activity (composer install/update) targeting known-compromised laravel-lang/* packages. Detect execution of installation scripts or package bootstrapping that deviates from normal package initialization. Alert on Composer lock-file changes that introduce compromised versions or new malicious dependencies.

suggestion.title: Credential Stealer Payload Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Cross-Platform Credential Stealer'—malware operates on multiple platforms and actively harvests credentials, requiring detection of credential access and encryption key material.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes spawned from PHP interpreters accessing Windows credential managers (LSASS dumps, SAM registry access), credential vaults, or SSH key directories (/home/*/.ssh, $HOME/.gnupg). Monitor for suspicious file reads from password managers or browser credential stores. Flag network connections from PHP child processes to exfiltration endpoints.

suggestion.title: Malicious Package Integrity Deviation
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attack implies package integrity compromise; pipeline must detect when installed package files diverge from official published hashes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare hash of installed laravel-lang/* files against official Packagist or GitHub releases. Flag mismatches, particularly in core language files or autoload bootstrap sequences. Monitor Composer lock-file for unexpected package version downgrades or version pins that deviate from project configuration.

suggestion.title: Cross-Platform Credential Stealer C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Cross-Platform'—malware requires C2 infrastructure to exfiltrate stolen credentials; detect outbound communication from compromised PHP processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and HTTP/HTTPS connections initiated by PHP processes (php, php-fpm, laravel artisan) to non-whitelisted external IP ranges. Flag unusual user-agents or POST requests containing credential-like strings (base64-encoded serialized arrays, JSON with password fields). Correlate timing with package installation events.

suggestion.title: Package Autoload Bootstrap Tampering
