suggestion.rationale: PHP packages use autoloaders; compromised laravel-lang packages likely inject payload via bootstrap or autoload_files entries, a common supply-chain technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor creation or modification of Composer autoload_files or vendor/composer/autoload_*.php scripts in laravel-lang/* directories. Detect execution of PHP code from atypical vendor subdirectories or suspicious eval() calls within package loading chain. Alert on vendor/autoload.php being rewritten post-installation.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Harvested Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealer must exfiltrate collected data; requires detection of bulk credential transmission and encryption key material in transit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect large POST/PUT requests or gzip-compressed uploads from PHP processes containing serialized credential objects. Monitor for simultaneous credential access (multiple password manager/vault reads) followed by network transmission. Flag creation of temporary encryption keys or obfuscated strings in PHP memory or temp files.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48172 cPanel LiteSpeed Plugin RCE Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title and severity explicitly identify 'exploited to run scripts as root' — execution phase and privilege escalation are the core attack vector. Pipeline failed to capture any detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected child process spawning from cPanel LiteSpeed plugin processes (httpd, lsphp, litespeed) running shell interpreters or scripts. Alert on process execution with UID 0/SYSTEM integrity spawned from web-facing plugin code paths outside normal maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Script Execution from Web Plugin Context
suggestion.rationale: Core impact: 'run scripts as root.' Pipeline missed privilege escalation detection despite explicit title statement of root execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when process creation chain shows web service account (www-data, nobody, cpanel user) spawning child with UID 0 or elevated token integrity. Flag inline script/command execution inheriting root context from parent plugin process.

suggestion.title: Suspicious cPanel Plugin File Write and Execution
suggestion.rationale: CVE exploitation requires writing or modifying plugin files; article mentions script execution but pipeline surfaced no file-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cPanel plugin directories (/usr/local/cpanel/plugins, plugin-specific paths) for file creation/modification outside maintenance windows. Alert on executable or script writes followed by immediate process execution in privilege_escalation context.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Process Execution from Nginx Worker
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Code Execution Attacks'—poolslip enables arbitrary command execution via Nginx. Should detect spawning of shells, interpreters, or reverse shells from nginx/www-data processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned by nginx worker (UID www-data or nginx) that are not typically legitimate (shells, perl, python, curl to external IPs, binary downloads). Baseline expected children and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Nginx Service Restart/Crash Spike
suggestion.rationale: Title cites DoS attacks enabled by poolslip. Detect rapid Nginx service restarts, worker process crashes, or supervisor respawning as symptom of exploitation attempts or successful DoS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor nginx process lifecycle events for >3 restarts in 5 minutes or >10 worker crashes/hour. Correlate with HTTP request spikes or malformed request patterns in access logs.

suggestion.title: Exploitation Pattern: Malformed HTTP Requests to Nginx
suggestion.rationale: Poolslip is a Nginx vulnerability requiring specific request payloads to trigger. Should detect HTTP requests containing poolslip-specific patterns (buffer overflow padding, memory poisoning headers, or unusual URI/header combinations).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest Nginx access logs; flag requests with abnormally large or malformed Content-Length headers, repeated null bytes, oversized URI paths, or non-printable characters in request headers. Correlate timing with service crashes.

suggestion.title: Resource Exhaustion from Single Nginx Process
suggestion.rationale: DoS impact mentioned; poolslip may trigger resource leaks or per-request memory bloat. Detect when single nginx worker consumes >50% system memory or CPU, or accumulates file descriptors without release.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal Nginx worker resource usage by version. Flag sustained memory growth >30% in single worker, sustained CPU >80% for >2 minutes, or open FD count doubling in <10 seconds.

suggestion.title: Nginx Configuration Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation persistence; attacker may modify nginx.conf, proxy rules, or include files to maintain access or exfiltrate data. Monitor config integrity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any modification to /etc/nginx/*, /usr/local/nginx/*, or included .conf files outside of approved change management. Capture hash of nginx binary and monitor for replacement.

suggestion.title: Reverse Shell or Data Exfil from Compromised Nginx
suggestion.rationale: Code execution impact requires detection of post-exploitation behavior: outbound connections to C2, data piping to external servers, or common reverse-shell patterns from nginx process context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag outbound connections initiated by nginx process to non-whitelisted external IPs/ports. Detect common reverse shell patterns (bash -i >& /dev/tcp/*, nc -e /bin/sh, curl to script download). Alert on base64 or hex-encoded data in HTTP request bodies.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Installation or Execution of Compromised Laravel-Lang Packages
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'Supply Chain Attack Targets Laravel-Lang Packages'—packages are the attack delivery vector. Detection must identify installation, load, or execution of affected Laravel-Lang versions prior to other malicious behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Composer package installations and PHP process executions for Laravel-Lang package versions matching known compromise indicators. Flag unexpected child processes or network connections spawned immediately after package execution. Correlate with package integrity validation failures.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting Activity Originating from Web Server or PHP Runtime
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Credential Stealer' payload—detection must identify credential access attempts. Phrase 'Credential Stealer' indicates primary malicious behavior executed from compromised package context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify processes spawned from PHP-FPM or web server contexts accessing Windows Credential Manager, credential storage APIs, browser cookie/credential databases, or SSH key locations. Flag API calls to credential enumeration functions (LogonUser, CredEnumerate, etc.) from web contexts.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Credentials from Web Application Context
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain credential stealers must exfiltrate harvested data. 'Credential Stealer' payload implies attacker-controlled destination for stolen credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP/S traffic from web server/PHP processes for POST requests with credential-like patterns (base64-encoded strings, JSON payloads containing username/password fields, or large data blobs). Flag connections to domains outside legitimate package repositories or CDNs. Correlate timing with credential access events.

suggestion.title: File Integrity Violations in Vendor or Package Directories
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain compromise requires code injection into package files. Detection relies on identifying unexpected modifications to Laravel-Lang or vendor directory contents.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor vendor/, node_modules/, or package-specific directories for file creation or modification events outside of legitimate package manager operations. Flag PHP files with obfuscated code patterns, eval() calls, or base64-encoded strings. Compare against file hash baselines of known-good package versions.

suggestion.title: Command and Control Beaconing from Compromised Package Execution
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealers establish C2 communication for payload updates or exfiltration coordination. Supply chain attacks often persist via beaconing infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify DNS queries or HTTP connections from PHP/web server processes to infrastructure absent from legitimate package dependency feeds. Baseline normal Laravel and PHP repository traffic. Flag periodic connection attempts suggesting beaconing behavior. Cross-reference with threat intelligence on attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated or Encoded Payloads Within Package Source Code
suggestion.rationale: Malicious packages typically obfuscate credential stealer code to evade detection. 'Credential Stealer' payload suggests obfuscation mechanisms hiding malicious intent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan package PHP files for base64_decode(), eval(), gzip compression, or reflection-based code execution patterns. Flag files with entropy signatures indicating packed or encrypted code. Monitor process memory for credential stealer signatures during execution.

suggestion.title: Public-Facing Drupal Asset Exposure Hunt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and invokes T1190 context (public-facing applications). Federal patch deadline (2026-05-27) demands rapid inventory of unpatched Drupal installations accessible from the internet.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Drupal installations via HTTP response signatures (Server headers, /admin/modules endpoint, CHANGELOG.txt fingerprinting). Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner for CVE-2026-9082 detections. Flag any unpatched versions or instances still exposed 7+ days before patch deadline.

suggestion.title: Drupal SQL Injection — Specially Crafted Database API Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article pinpoints attack vector: 'specially crafted requests sent with the database abstraction API.' This is the exploitation mechanism; SQL injection detection must focus on database layer anomalies, not just HTTP payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Drupal database abstraction API logs and PHP error logs for SQL syntax errors, UNION-based injection signatures, time-based blind SQL injection patterns, and malformed API payloads. Alert on repeated failed API calls from same source IP (scanning) or single requests with embedded SQL keywords.

suggestion.title: Post-SQL-Injection Privilege Escalation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states SQL injection 'could allow for privilege escalation'—this is a distinct kill-chain phase. Pipeline reconstructed no escalation activity despite it being explicitly mentioned.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-exploitation, detect rapid privilege elevation within Drupal: user role promotion to admin/super-admin, database user privilege grants, sudo invocations from web process context. Correlate timing with SQL injection attempt windows.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution via SQL Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states SQL injection enables 'remote code execution'—this impact phase is completely absent from pipeline kill chain. Must detect command execution spawned post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious process spawning from Drupal/PHP worker context: shell execution, reverse shells, wget/curl for payload retrieval, code interpretation (perl/python/bash). Alert on process creation from web root or unexpected system calls (exec, system, passthru) timing-correlated with exploitation window.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-9082 Vulnerability Scanner Detection & Remediation Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'match against your vulnerability scanner' and sets federal patch deadline 2026-05-27. Pipeline must create detection for scanner alerts and remediation gap tracking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate CVE-2026-9082 scanner detections with asset inventory. Prioritize internet-facing/DMZ instances. Track time-to-remediation and escalate any unpatched instances within 5 days of federal deadline (2026-05-27). Integrate with ticketing to enforce deadline compliance.

suggestion.title: Drupal Database API Payload Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'specially crafted requests'—generic SQL injection detection may miss API-layer polyglot payloads. Need API-specific signature/behavioral analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Drupal database abstraction API for oversized payloads, parameter encoding anomalies (hex/octal/unicode bypasses), NULL bytes, or API calls with unusual parameter combinations. Alert on repeated errors from same source (brute-force API fuzzing).

suggestion.title: LNK File in Archive Executing PowerShell
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'The group is back to sending out archives containing malicious shortcuts that launch PowerShell scripts.' Email phishing with ZIP→LNK→PowerShell is the initial infection vector. No detection UC was generated for this clearly observable chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for cmdline execution of powershell.exe with parent process explorer.exe or winrar, particularly from Temp folders. Detect archive extraction events followed by LNK file creation/execution. Alert on suspicious download→extract→execute patterns within minutes.

suggestion.title: Registry Persistence via Run Key with Decoy Application Name
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'Creates "Run" registry key "YandexBrowser_setup" for "$temp\fixed.ps1" startup'. The use of legitimate app names as Run key values for unsigned scripts is evasion. Pipeline captured no persistence detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Run registry keys reference Temp folder PowerShell scripts, especially with values spoofing legitimate apps (YandexBrowser, etc.). Cross-reference Run key execution against installed applications—if key name implies software that is not installed, escalate.

suggestion.title: termsrv.dll Patching for Multi-User RDP Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Multi-user RDP by patching termsrv.dll' and 'Patched OpenSSH'. Direct modification of system DLLs to enable unauthorized RDP sessions is a persistence and lateral-movement technique. Zero UCs generated for this.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for modification of System32\termsrv.dll or OpenSSH binaries. Detect RDP session count exceeding expected baseline (multi-session indicator). Alert on unsigned or patched versions of RDP/SSH binaries alongside unexpected network connections.

suggestion.title: Reverse SSH Tunnel and RevSocks Proxy Chain Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Reverse SSH tunneling', 'Patched OpenSSH', 'RevSocks Tor tunneling'. Multiple tunneling layers (SSH, RevSocks, Tor) establish covert C2 channels. Pipeline failed to suggest detections for tunnel initiation or known RevSocks indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PowerShell or cmd spawning ssh.exe with -R (reverse tunnel) or -D (SOCKS proxy) flags. Detect RevSocks process execution or outbound connections to known Tor entry nodes. Monitor for sustained TCP/UDP tunnels from internal hosts to external infrastructure.

suggestion.title: PowerCloud Browser Fingerprinting Tool Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'PowerCloud Browser checker' as a new tool used by Cloud Atlas. This tool appears designed for environment reconnaissance. No UC captures execution or behavioral signatures of this tool.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline behavior for PowerCloud tool (if binary/script signatures become available). Monitor for reconnaissance behavior: browser enumeration, plugin detection, system fingerprinting via PowerShell Get-ItemProperty queries on HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall and browser directories.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Integrated Grabber Component
suggestion.rationale: Article structure references 'PowerShower::Payload (credential grabber)' as a payload component. The article mentions dumping credentials but pipeline extracted no credential-access detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PowerShell execution of credential enumeration cmdlets (Get-LocalUser, net user, wmic useraccount, Win32_UserAccount). Detect access to SAM/SECURITY registry hives or credential vaults. Alert on child processes of PowerShell executing mimikatz-like utilities or LSASS access.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection Payloads Against Drupal Database API (Unauthenticated)
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers send 'specially crafted requests' that 'trigger arbitrary SQL injection on sites using PostgreSQL.' No HTTP-layer detection UC proposed despite this being the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST/GET requests to Drupal endpoints for SQL metacharacters and keywords (UNION, SELECT, DROP, INSERT, EXEC, etc.) in parameter values—URL-encoded, double-encoded, or comment-obfuscated. Cross-reference with Drupal version fingerprinting or requests to known database abstraction API paths.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Unexpected Query Execution and Error Spike Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names PostgreSQL as the targeted database engine and notes 'exploitation attempts are now being detected.' No database activity detection UC generated despite PostgreSQL being the specific attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on syntax errors, permission-denied exceptions, and unexpected DDL/DCL (ALTER, DROP, GRANT) from non-admin database connections. Correlate with HTTP 400/500 responses or WAF SQL injection blocks from the same source IP within a tight time window.

suggestion.title: Database Privilege Escalation via Injected SQL
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly cites 'privilege escalation' as an impact of successful SQL injection exploitation. No detection UC proposed for unauthorized GRANT, ALTER ROLE, or CREATE USER commands executed through the database layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GRANT or ALTER ROLE commands that elevate non-superuser database accounts to superuser/admin. Correlate with preceding SQL injection error patterns or anomalous query sequences from the same session.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution Post-SQL-Injection Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states the vulnerability 'could result in remote code execution' and confirms exploitation attempts are underway. Pipeline proposed zero post-exploitation RCE detection despite explicit mention of RCE as a confirmed risk.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag shell processes (bash, sh, cmd.exe, powershell) spawned from the Drupal application user context (www-data, apache). Alert on execution of data exfiltration utilities (pg_dump, mysqldump, curl, wget) from the web server process after SQL injection indicators.

suggestion.title: Drupal Version Fingerprinting and Scanning Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerable version ranges (8.9.x, 10.4.x–10.6.x, 11.0.x–11.3.x). Pipeline generated no reconnaissance detection for version-disclosure or fingerprinting requests that typically precede targeted exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for requests to /CHANGELOG.txt, /admin, or version-info endpoints followed by SQL injection attempts from the same IP within minutes. Establish baselines for legitimate update checks and alert on scanning-to-exploit sequences.

suggestion.title: Detect VPN Service Abuse for C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 25 ransomware groups abusing a VPN service for command-and-control. Should detect anomalous VPN provider traffic patterns, rapid C2 reconnection attempts, and lateral movement post-VPN entry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag persistent outbound connections to known VPN service IP ranges over suspicious ports; correlate multiple internal hosts tunneling through same VPN endpoint within short timeframe; alert on DNS resolutions for VPN provider domains from non-corporate proxies.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Group Infrastructure Takedown Pivot
suggestion.rationale: Article describes dismantled VPN infrastructure. Should detect hosts that had active C2 sessions to seized IP ranges; use timeline overlap between takedown and observed C2 activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference network logs for connections to infrastructure IPs extracted from law-enforcement seizure notices; identify beaconing patterns in weeks prior to takedown; correlate with known ransomware process execution signatures.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Payroll Monitor for Known Group TTP Escalation
suggestion.rationale: Article names 25 specific ransomware groups (implied by title). Should create detection logic around each group's known tools, lateral-movement patterns, and file-encryption activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For each confirmed ransomware group from article, alert on file operations consistent with their known payload (file extensions, encryption marker files, parallel encryption threads); detect execution of group-specific tooling (Cobalt Strike beacons for LockBit, etc.).

suggestion.title: VPN Service Registration and Credential Theft Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article describes ransomware abuse of legitimate VPN service. Should detect when compromised credentials for VPN services appear in credential-stealer logs or dark-web leak aggregators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor dark-web intelligence feeds and credential-leak databases for mentions of VPN service provider credentials; correlate compromised user accounts with internal host activity; detect infostealer payload execution on internal machines.

suggestion.title: Detect Initial Access via VPN Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article implies ransomware groups gained initial access via compromised or rogue VPN accounts. Should detect anomalous first-login patterns from new or unusual geographies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on VPN login followed immediately by lateral-movement attempts or privileged-account enumeration; detect logins from TOR exit nodes or known-malicious IP ranges; flag rapid VPN connection churn from same source IP.

suggestion.title: Post-Takedown C2 Fallback Detection
suggestion.rationale: After VPN infrastructure seizure, ransomware operators typically pivot to backup C2 (alternate VPN, bulletproof hosters, P2P). Should monitor for traffic surge to secondary infrastructure post-takedown.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In the days/weeks after published takedown, spike-detect outbound connections to newly registered domains and bulletproof-hoster ASNs; correlate with payloads signed by same certificates as seized C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted Domain Registration Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'typosquatting, which involves on a domain name that closely resembles the legitimate one' with example fifa26.shop. Attacker acquires confusingly-similar domains as core infrastructure tactic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for domain registrations with Levenshtein distance ≤2 from FIFA/World Cup brand domains, especially resolving to bulletproof hosting or free DNS providers. Flag newly-registered domains matching World Cup event timeline with visual similarity to legitimate authority sites.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email Delivery with Spoofed Tickets/Merchandise Links
suggestion.rationale: Article states victims click 'links in email messages forwarded by someone who didn't check the address properly'. Email is explicit delivery vector with URL spoofing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect mass emails promoting World Cup tickets/merchandise with hyperlinks to typosquatted domains where href text differs from actual URL domain. Flag emails with spoofed FIFA sender addresses or 'forwarded by' patterns sent during peak ticket-demand periods.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Counterfeit Registration Forms
suggestion.rationale: Article details fake registration collecting 'name, email address, and phone number' that appears legitimate. 'If you expect to create a FIFA ID before buying tickets, a fake registration form may not look strange at first.' Explicit PII/credential harvesting attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate form submissions to typosquatted domains collecting email, phone, name fields with high volume, geographic diversity, and rapid abandonment (harvest-then-discard pattern). Flag forms with inputs matching FIFA credential schema hosted outside official FIFA infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Fraudulent Payment Gateway Capture
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly shows payment flow: 'Once you enter your card details, it goes straight to the people behind the fake site.' Final stage captures payment data. 'Purchasing' jersey figures show payment redirect to attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP POST submissions of payment card data (CC number, CVV, expiry) to non-PCI-compliant domains. Monitor for payment form checkouts on typosquatted domains where final payment-processing domain differs from initial site. Flag card data exfiltration patterns.

suggestion.title: Malicious Sponsored Search and Social Media Ads
suggestion.rationale: Article notes 'Some victims may reach these websites through sponsored search results, while others click on ads on social media.' Ad platforms distributing to phishing infrastructure is initial access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ad networks for promotions of typosquatted FIFA/World Cup domains with merchandising/ticketing claims. Correlate malicious ad campaigns with spike in reports of credential theft and fraud around event dates. Flag ad accounts distributing to infrastructure with DNS/hosting overlap.

suggestion.title: Website Visual Cloning for Social Engineering
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker copying 'the look and feel of FIFA's official site, including the colors, layout, navigation and ticketing flow' to normalize victim behavior and bypass caution. 'Much like the official FIFA site, the imposter site also asks you to register.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect websites with CSS/HTML/JavaScript code similarity >80% to official FIFA World Cup site or official merchandise store. Flag shopping flows on non-official domains that generate no actual ticket/merchandise transactions. Monitor for identical product catalogs and pricing across multiple fraudulent domains.

suggestion.title: F5 BIG-IP Unauthenticated RCE via Configuration Utility
suggestion.rationale: Article describes initial compromise of 'F5 BIG-IP Virtual Edition running version 15.1.201000, which had reached end-of-life on December 31, 2024,' tied to CVE-2026-39455 Configuration utility vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthenticated HTTP POST requests to F5 BIG-IP configuration endpoints (typically port 443) from external sources. Alert on version detection strings indicating 15.1.2xx, 15.1.3xx ranges. Look for command execution attempts (curl, wget, bash invocations) spawned from F5 tmsh or f5-admin-shell processes.

suggestion.title: Confluence Credential Harvesting from XML Config Files
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'harvested credentials from configuration files, including server.xml and confluence.cfg.xml' after pivoting through F5.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file access to Confluence-sensitive config paths (/opt/atlassian/confluence/conf/server.xml, confluence.cfg.xml) by unexpected process owners or from non-standard tool contexts. Monitor for cat, grep, strings, or base64 commands targeting these files. Flag any read access from SSH processes on the Confluence host outside maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Kerberos Relay Attack via Captured Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'Kerberos relay attacks' as part of the exploitation chain against Windows domain infrastructure after credential harvesting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for Kerberos TGT requests from non-Windows source IPs (Linux-originating attack evident from article context). Alert on multiple Kerberos AS-REQ/TGS-REQ sequences originating from a single external IP within short time windows. Correlate with failed authentication attempts followed by successful Kerberos relay patterns (TGT reuse across multiple service principals).

suggestion.title: PetitPotam Coercion and Relay Attack Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'using netexec with PetitPotam coercion and DNS manipulation tooling to target a domain controller.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP CONNECT requests to domain controller IPs from external or compromised internal Linux hosts. Alert on EfsRpcEncryptFileEx RPC calls (PetitPotam signature) to DC endpoints. Correlate with subsequent NTLM authentication attempts and Kerberos relay activity. Flag netexec execution with -u, -p, and relay flags targeting DC ports.

suggestion.title: Cross-Platform Credential Misuse: Linux-to-Windows Auth
suggestion.rationale: Article describes harvested credentials from Linux Confluence server being 'turned against Windows infrastructure' and leveraged for 'Kerberos relay attacks,' indicating auth traffic from Linux origin to Windows domain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Windows NTLM or Kerberos authentication attempts originating from non-Windows source IPs (especially Azure ranges if F5 is cloud-hosted) using credentials harvested from Confluence. Alert on successful authentication from Linux-attributed IP ranges followed by RPC or SMB sessions. Monitor for netexec command execution on domain resources with credentials matching Confluence configuration file captures.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-33073 Domain Controller Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'CVE-2025-33073' as the target vulnerability exploited against domain controller as part of the relay attack chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for exploitation signatures of CVE-2025-33073 targeting domain controller ports. Alert on RPC connections to vulnerable DC processes combined with PetitPotam coercion indicators. Flag attempts to manipulate DNS records from external sources prior to DC exploitation (article mentions 'DNS manipulation tooling').

suggestion.title: Phishing Email Containing Prometheus Malware Attachment
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'phishing malware' campaign; no use case generated for phishing-stage detection despite this being the primary initial-access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails with suspicious file attachments (executables, Office macros, scripts) sent to Ukrainian government domains or users. Alert on attachment file hashes matching known Prometheus samples and emails with lures targeting government entities.

suggestion.title: Prometheus Malware Process Execution and Registry Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Prometheus malware execution phase completely absent from kill-chain output; no detection guidance provided for post-compromise behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious process creation, DLL injection, or file writes consistent with Prometheus execution. Monitor for process names, file paths, or command-line patterns associated with Prometheus samples.

suggestion.title: Command and Control Traffic to Prometheus C2 Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Kill-chain completely empty; C2 communication is standard in malware campaigns and should have been reconstructed from article.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from Prometheus-infected endpoints to known C2 servers. Monitor for beaconing patterns, unusual ports, encrypted tunnels, or domain names associated with campaign infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Archive or Dropper Downloaded by Government Users
suggestion.rationale: Phishing often uses downloadable archives or Office documents with embedded malware; no detection for file download stage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when Ukrainian government network users download .zip, .rar, or Office files from attacker-controlled URLs. Correlate download events with subsequent Prometheus process spawning.

suggestion.title: YesWiki Bazar form-import volumetric POST requests
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly recommends hunting for high-volume POST requests to BazaR form-import endpoint as blind SQLi extraction loop signature: 'allows any unauthenticated visitor...to inject arbitrary SQL'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect 20+ POST requests in 5-minute window to URL pattern *BazaR*vue=formulaire* from single source IP. Indicates volumetric extraction loop typical of blind SQL injection enumeration.

suggestion.title: Non-browser User-Agent exploitation of YesWiki Bazar endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies tooling detection: 'Non-browser User-Agent against YesWiki Bazar form-import endpoint...exploit tooling' with examples: Python-urllib, curl, Go-http-client, Java, PowerShell, wget.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests to *BazaR*vue=formulaire* endpoint with User-Agent matching automated tools (Python, curl, Go, Java, PowerShell, wget, libwww-perl). Legitimate browser traffic would use browser user-agents.

suggestion.title: SQL syntax keywords in YesWiki Bazar form-import POST parameters
suggestion.rationale: Article describes SQL injection sink: 'inject arbitrary SQL into an INSERT statement'. Attackers must send SQL keywords (UNION, SELECT, OR, AND, etc.) in POST parameters to exploit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect POST parameter payloads to *BazaR*vue=formulaire* endpoint for SQL metacharacters and keywords (UNION, SELECT, INSERT, WHERE, OR 1=1). Flag if parameter values contain unencoded SQL syntax.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated database queries on YesWiki Bazar form-import
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes: 'unauthenticated visitor...inject arbitrary SQL...read the full database, including yeswiki_users.password hashes'. Detection must correlate unauthenticated HTTP access with backend database activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate unauthenticated POST requests to Bazar endpoint with unexpected database queries (SELECT FROM yeswiki_users, SELECT FROM yeswiki_*). Flag if database reads occur from unauthenticated web session.

suggestion.title: YesWiki version exposure scan
suggestion.rationale: Article lists vulnerable versions: '4.6.1 / 4.6.2 / current doryphore-dev'. Asset-centric hunt to identify exposed vulnerable instances before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for YesWiki instances in asset inventory or web application discovery tools. Identify version 4.6.1, 4.6.2, or doryphore-dev branch. Cross-correlate with external vulnerability scanner results flagging GHSA-jwvv-qr7q-cv8j.

suggestion.title: Detect C2 Beaconing from Telecom Networks
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'command-and-control operations' using telecom infrastructure. C2 beacons are the operational fingerprint of this attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound traffic from Middle East telecom ASNs for regular, predictable beacon intervals to external IPs/domains. Alert on small request / large response patterns, encrypted payloads, or DNS tunneling originating from telecom network segments.

suggestion.title: Detect Initial Compromise of Telecom Management Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: Attackers must first breach telecom infrastructure to abuse it. Title implies systematic access, likely via exposed management consoles, credential compromise, or supply-chain exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag login attempts to telecom OSS/BSS platforms, VPN endpoints, and network management interfaces from anomalous geolocations or outside maintenance windows. Alert on credential spray, brute-force patterns, and unusual service accounts.

suggestion.title: Detect Lateral Movement Within Telecom Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Scale of 'large-scale operations' implies post-compromise lateral movement to reach critical network nodes and establish C2 persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor SSH, RDP, and proprietary telecom management protocol traffic between network segments from unexpected sources or ports. Flag successful connections from previously compromised hosts to management interfaces.

suggestion.title: Detect Data Exfiltration via Telecom C2 Channels
suggestion.rationale: Large-scale operations imply persistent data collection and staged exfiltration using established C2 infrastructure within telecom networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate sustained C2 traffic with large, recurring data movements from customer/enterprise segments through telecom networks. Alert on data transfers matching automated exfil patterns (timing, volume, protocol anomalies).

suggestion.title: Detect Persistence Mechanisms on Telecom Network Devices
suggestion.rationale: Sustaining large-scale C2 requires persistence beyond beaconing: scheduled tasks, rootkits, or firmware modifications on routers, firewalls, VoIP infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalous scheduled tasks, cron jobs, and firmware/configuration changes on telecom network devices not traceable to authorized vendors or administrators.

suggestion.title: Detect DNS Abuse for C2 Command Resolution
suggestion.rationale: C2 infrastructure must be resolved; scale suggests DNS tunneling, DGA activity, or fast-flux patterns originating from compromised telecom networks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on high-frequency DNS queries from telecom networks to newly registered or low-reputation domains. Flag DNS tunneling patterns (TXT queries, unusually long subdomains) and DGA-like behavior.

suggestion.title: npm Package Manifest or Version Mismatch
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Hackers Backdoor Popular art-template npm Package' — indicates package versioning anomaly or manifest tampering that should be detectable via registry metadata changes
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm registry for unexpected version bumps, signature verification failures, or checksum mismatches on popular packages. Flag installations where package hash does not match registry records or where version history shows suspicious gaps or retractions.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Dependency Added to Popular Package
suggestion.rationale: Backdoor implies injected malicious code or dependency — 'Hackers Backdoor' suggests code addition detectable via source code or dependency tree anomalies
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new or unexpected dependencies added to popular packages, especially transitive dependencies that execute at install time. Flag packages that introduce dependencies not previously present in historical versions or from untrusted registries.

suggestion.title: Installation-Time Code Execution from Compromised npm Package
suggestion.rationale: Backdooring npm package typically executes at install/postinstall phase — article mentions attack delivery mechanism but pipeline missed execution detection
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected process spawning, outbound network connections, or file writes during npm package installation. Flag postinstall scripts that invoke suspicious commands, download payloads, or establish network connections to unknown domains.

suggestion.title: Watering Hole Redirection or C2 Beacon from Compromised Dependency
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'Launch Watering-Hole Attacks' — implies C2 communication or redirect infrastructure that should be detectable as anomalous network traffic from affected systems
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected DNS queries or HTTP connections originating from systems using the compromised art-template package. Alert on connections to attacker-controlled watering-hole infrastructure, especially if traffic patterns differ from legitimate package functionality.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement or Reconnaissance via Compromised Development Environment
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromise targeting developers implies potential for lateral movement once code is integrated into projects — 'Watering-Hole Attacks' suggests targeting development infrastructure
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: After detecting art-template installation, monitor host for unexpected process creation, credential enumeration, or network scanning. Flag attempts to access upstream build systems, artifact repositories, or other sensitive infrastructure from hosts where compromised package was installed.

suggestion.title: NF-e-Themed Phishing Email with Batch File Attachment
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'NF-e Invoice Lures' and 'Malicious Batch Files' as the attack vector. Pipeline missed initial-access detection: 'Hackers Use NF-e Invoice Lures to Deliver Banana RAT'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for email messages with NF-e or Portuguese invoice-themed subject lines and filenames containing 'nota fiscal', 'invoice', or currency references (R$, BRL), coupled with suspicious attachment extensions (.bat, .cmd, .com). Correlate recipient domain with known finance/procurement roles.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Batch File Execution from Downloads or Temp Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states delivery mechanism is 'Malicious Batch Files': T1059.003 execution vector is the core exploitation step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag batch file execution (.bat, .cmd) launched from Downloads, Temp, AppData/Local/Temp, or %USERPROFILE% directories. Enrich with parent process analysis (explorer.exe, outlook.exe, chrome.exe). Baseline expected batch execution and alert on anomalies, especially those with obfuscated or concatenated command syntax.

suggestion.title: Banana RAT Process and Registry Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: Article title names 'Banana RAT' as the delivered payload. Pipeline failed to capture malware family-specific indicators: process names, registry keys, or network signatures associated with this family.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for Banana RAT-specific registry persistence paths (HKCU/HKLM run keys, scheduled tasks, WMI event subscriptions). Monitor for process names or command-line patterns associated with Banana RAT (e.g., characteristic mutex names, unique registry subkeys, encoded strings). Correlate with batch file execution within preceding 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: Banana RAT Command & Control Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article describes delivery of a RAT ('Banana RAT'), implying C&C callback. No detection use cases were generated for network-based C2 detection, which is critical for a remote-access trojan.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from batch-executed processes or their children. Flag non-standard ports (high TCP/UDP port ranges, 8080, 8888, custom obfuscated ports) originating from user-owned processes. Correlate with DNS requests to newly registered or suspicious domains. Baseline typical outbound traffic for the user and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Double-Extension or Archive-Hidden Batch Files in Email
suggestion.rationale: NF-e lures often use obfuscation to mask executable files (e.g., 'Invoice_20240515.pdf.bat' or batch inside ZIP/RAR). Article title does not mention this, but is a standard tactic in malware delivery; worthy of explicit detection to prevent initial execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect attachments with double extensions (*.pdf.bat, *.xlsx.cmd) or batch files nested in password-protected archives. Monitor for batch file extraction from archives followed by immediate execution. Cross-reference sender domain against known phishing infrastructure or known-bad domains.

suggestion.title: Batch File Attempting to Download or Execute Additional Payloads
suggestion.rationale: Batch files are often used as downloaders or loaders for secondary payloads (Banana RAT in this case). Pipeline should have surfaced T1105 and T1570 indicators: 'Malicious Batch Files' strongly suggests secondary staging.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor batch files for inline wget, curl, bitsadmin, or certutil commands (common downloaders in batch scripts). Correlate with outbound HTTP(S) requests to non-standard ports or suspicious URLs. Flag batch execution immediately followed by child process creation (e.g., cmd.exe spawning msiexec, powershell, or rundll32).

suggestion.title: FreePBX Unauthorized Administrative Account Creation
suggestion.rationale: Title references 'six-layer persistence'—creating privileged accounts is a foundational persistence mechanism. Article context implies attackers established administrative footing; lack of detection for abnormal account creation in FreePBX systems is a critical gap.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation of new admin/superuser accounts in FreePBX via Asterisk user database (manager.conf, users.conf) or direct database writes to asterisk.user. Baseline administrator accounts and alert on new additions outside change windows.

suggestion.title: FreePBX Module or Extension Installation Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Persistence via custom modules/extensions is a common FreePBX attack vector. Article title emphasizes 'six-layer' persistence—module injection/loading is a likely layer. Pipeline did not surface this despite it being endemic to FreePBX targeting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected .so module additions to /usr/lib/asterisk/modules or dynamic module loading via 'module load' commands in Asterisk logs. Alert on modules outside approved inventory with focus on custom/unsigned modules.

suggestion.title: FreePBX Scheduled Callback or Cron-Based Reverse Shell
suggestion.rationale: The 'six-layer persistence' phrasing suggests layered, independent persistence mechanisms. Scheduled tasks (cron, at, systemd timers) are standard fallback persistence layers absent from pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search cron jobs and systemd timers on FreePBX systems for entries referencing shell invocation, network communication (curl, nc, wget), or suspicious execution paths. Alert on jobs created outside documented maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: FreePBX Dial Plan or IVR Modification for Persistence
suggestion.rationale: FreePBX-specific persistence layer: attackers can embed AGI scripts or modify dialplan contexts to execute commands or initiate callbacks. This domain-specific persistence vector is absent from pipeline analysis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected AGI script registrations or dialplan extension additions pointing to external URLs or suspicious local scripts. Cross-reference extensions.conf modifications with change control logs.

suggestion.title: Asterisk Configuration File Persistence (manager.conf Backdoor)
suggestion.rationale: Attackers can insert manager accounts into manager.conf to maintain AMI (Asterisk Manager Interface) access—a critical C2 channel. Pipeline missed this common FreePBX persistence layer despite 'six-layer' emphasis.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected [user] sections or read/write permissions added to manager.conf. Monitor AMI connection logs for unusual source IPs or authentication patterns post-compromise.

suggestion.title: Web Shell in FreePBX Web Interface Directory
suggestion.rationale: FreePBX runs a PHP-based web interface (/var/www/html/freepbx or /usr/share/freepbx). Web shell placement is a standard post-compromise persistence layer. Title's 'six-layer' architecture likely includes web-level persistence not surfaced by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected .php files in /var/www/html/freepbx with focus on recently modified files, files with suspicious function calls (exec, shell_exec, system), or files created outside normal maintenance. Cross-reference with web access logs for non-standard request patterns.

suggestion.title: Botnet Command and Control Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Title establishes 'DDoS Botnet Operator' — implies C2 infrastructure and regular beacon traffic. Pipeline failed to generate detection for botnet communication phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect periodic outbound connections from compromised hosts to known or suspected botnet C2 servers. Monitor for DNS queries to known botnet domains and anomalous callback patterns during off-hours.

suggestion.title: Volumetric DDoS Attack Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'DDoS-for-Hire Attacks' — the actual attack execution phase. Pipeline generated no detection for sustained flood traffic or attack orchestration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sudden spike in outbound traffic volume from botnet-infected hosts to a single or multiple targets. Monitor for UDP/ICMP floods, SYN floods, or HTTP GET floods originating from distributed sources.

suggestion.title: Botnet Payload Delivery and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title references 'DDoS Botnet' — payload must be delivered and executed on compromised hosts. No detection use case for initial compromise or persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious process execution from staged files, unusual script interpreter invocations (cmd.exe, PowerShell), and file writes to temporary directories followed by execution.

suggestion.title: Kimwolf Botnet Host Enrollment Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title establishes botnet operation — detection must cover host compromise and enrollment into botnet. Likely via malicious link or exploit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect compromised host establishment of connectivity to Kimwolf C2 infrastructure within 24 hours of suspicious email or web-based delivery. Correlate web browsing events with subsequent new network connections.

suggestion.title: Arrested Operator Infrastructure Takedown Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Operator Arrested in Canada' — law enforcement action implies seized infrastructure. Pipeline should flag C2 domain/IP takedowns and sinkholed botnet callbacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for failed C2 callback attempts to known Kimwolf infrastructure, sudden drops in botnet beacon frequency (indicating sinkhole redirection), and DNS NXDOMAIN responses to previously active C2 domains.

suggestion.title: Unsigned or Revoked Kernel Driver Load
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD attacks rely on loading vulnerable but signed drivers to bypass kernel protections. Article title establishes 'Vulnerable Drivers Exploitable' as core attack vector—must detect unauthorized driver loading.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned driver loads via kernel image-load events or registry driver installation. Flag loads of drivers with known CVEs (e.g., rtcore64.sys, gdrv.sys, asusio.sys, nvidia_smi). Correlate process initiating load with privilege level and trust anchors.

suggestion.title: Known Vulnerable Driver Execution
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD exploits leverage known-vulnerable drivers to escalate privileges. Article centers on making vulnerable drivers 'exploitable'—must track execution of drivers on public exploit lists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain a driver IOC list (CVE-mapped vulnerable drivers: Gigabyte APP Center, ASUSTeK OEM IOCTL, etc.). Alert on execution of any driver from this list. Correlate with subsequent privileged process spawning or kernel-mode syscall patterns.

suggestion.title: Kernel-Mode Syscall Anomaly Post-Driver Load
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD attacks use vulnerable drivers to issue privileged syscalls (e.g., NtSetInformationFile, NtProtectVirtualMemory) that bypass user-mode protections. Article implies hardware-independent privilege escalation via drivers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ETW kernel events for syscalls issued through driver ioctl handles immediately after driver load. Flag patterns: user-mode process → driver ioctl → privileged syscall from kernel context. Baseline legitimate driver syscall patterns per environment.

suggestion.title: IOCTL Fuzzing or Privilege Escalation Payload Delivery
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD attacks send crafted ioctl requests to vulnerable drivers to trigger escalation. Article subtitle 'Without Hardware' indicates software-only exploitation—detectable via ioctl call patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes calling DeviceIoControl or sending ioctl requests to kernel drivers with non-zero control codes targeting known vulnerable drivers. Flag repeated ioctl calls in short time spans (fuzz-like patterns). Cross-check with process privilege level at call time.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion via Vulnerable Driver (EDR Bypass)
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD enables kernel-mode code execution to disable EDR and security tools. Article framing 'exploitable without hardware' implies defeating software-based protections, a core BYOVD post-exploitation use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious termination or unloading of security processes (EDR agents, AV services, ELAM drivers) following vulnerable driver load. Flag driver loads immediately followed by security service crashes or unloads. Monitor WMI event subscriptions or filter driver removal after driver image load.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions YAML Modification in Fork/PR
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly references 'Malicious CI/CD Workflows'—detection should key on suspicious modifications to .github/workflows/ files, GitHub Actions YAML config changes, or workflow_run event handlers that execute arbitrary scripts. This is the primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation or modification of .github/workflows/*.yml files with inline script commands (run:, shell:) or external script pulls (curl | bash). Flag workflows triggered on pull_request_target or workflow_run that access repo secrets or modify code. Correlate with rapid file changes across multiple repos in short timeframe.

suggestion.title: Bulk Repository Compromise Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Title states '5,561 Repos' targeted—suggests coordinated multi-repo attack or shared supply-chain vector. Need detection for rapid sequential repo mutations, identical malicious workflow additions across org, or shared attacker-controlled account activity across repos.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Aggregate repo audit logs by push event source IP or actor identity. Alert on single actor/IP modifying workflows in >10 repos within 1-hour window. Correlate with repo creation date, maintainer dormancy, or orphaned projects (low activity repos vulnerable to takeover).

suggestion.title: CI/CD Runner Command Injection via Workflow Secrets Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Malicious CI/CD workflows typically extract GitHub secrets, credentials, or SSH keys. Detection should monitor for environment variable exfiltration, secret reference syntax usage in echo/curl commands, or outbound data transfer from CI runners.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor CI/CD build logs for references to ${secrets.*} or ${{ secrets.* }} patterns in command strings, curl/wget commands sending data to non-repo domains, or base64-encoded credential strings in logs. Flag outbound HTTPS/DNS from CI IPs to low-reputation domains.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Git Commit Activity by CI Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Malicious workflows may auto-commit code changes, poison dependencies, or modify configuration files. Detection needs to catch commits pushed by bot/service accounts during off-hours or outside normal CI patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag commits from bot/automation accounts that contain suspicious patterns: network callbacks, reverse shells, privilege escalation code, or dependency overrides. Correlate commit authorship, timestamp (off-hours), and repo scope (same account pushing to many unrelated repos).

suggestion.title: GitHub OIDC Token Misuse for Cross-Cloud Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Modern CI/CD attacks chain GitHub OIDC tokens to assume AWS/Azure/GCP roles. 'Megalodon' title and large-scale targeting suggests infrastructure breach or supply-chain poisoning—likely includes cloud credential harvesting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for OIDC token assertions from GitHub Action runners, especially to unfamiliar Azure App Registrations or AWS IAM roles. Flag role assumption chains where runner context doesn't match deployment target. Correlate with repo ownership and organization boundaries.

suggestion.title: Dependency Injection via Workflow Build Artifact Poisoning
suggestion.rationale: CI/CD workflows generate build artifacts (binaries, packages, container images). Malicious workflows may inject malware upstream. Detection should monitor artifact registry pushes and image builds from compromised repos.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for package/image pushes from GitHub Actions runners to public registries using leaked credentials or service identities. Flag builds from repos with suspicious workflow modifications, especially if pushed to production registries or widely-used library paths.

suggestion.title: Suspicious GitHub Actions Workflow File Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes mass GitHub Actions secret exfiltration—malicious workflow creation/modification is the core attack vector ('Mass GitHub Actions Secret Exfiltration Across 5,500+ Public Repositories'). Pipeline extracted no detection for this primary initial-access technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for .github/workflows/*.yml files created or modified in public repositories by new or suspicious accounts. Flag workflows containing env exfiltration logic (curl to external domains, base64-encoded output, ${{ secrets.* }} access), absent from repository history, or authored by accounts with no prior commits.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of GitHub Secrets via Actions Step Output
suggestion.rationale: Campaign is explicitly titled 'Secret Exfiltration'—article must describe mechanism for stealing GITHUB_TOKEN or repository secrets. No detection exists for secrets being accessed and leaked.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GitHub Actions jobs accessing GITHUB_TOKEN, GITHUB_RUN_ID, or secrets via ${{ secrets.* }} in commands that produce output to external services. Correlate secret variable usage with outbound HTTP POST/GET to non-GitHub domains within the same action step.

suggestion.title: Outbound Credential Exfiltration from GitHub Actions Runner
suggestion.rationale: 5,500+ repositories had credentials stolen—article must specify exfiltration mechanism. No use case detects secret data egress to attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP/HTTPS requests from GitHub Actions runners to external (non-GitHub) domains carrying patterns consistent with credential exfiltration: base64-encoded token-length strings, secret variable substitution, JSON payloads with key-value pairs matching GitHub token format, or uncommon TLDs.

suggestion.title: Mass Adoption of Malicious GitHub Action Across Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Attack scaled to 5,500+ repos—implies shared malicious action or workflow template reused across victims. Pipeline missed detection for this supply-chain amplification pattern and actor reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid, concurrent adoption of newly published GitHub Actions by multiple unrelated public repositories within short timeframe. Flag actions created by low-reputation or newly-created accounts, or released days before campaign date. Cross-correlate action namespace/version across compromised repos.

suggestion.title: Workflow Execution Triggered via External Webhooks or workflow_dispatch
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 5,500+ repos exfiltrated—suggests automated triggering mechanism or attacker invoking workflows en masse. Pipeline produced no detection for abnormal workflow invocation patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect workflows executed outside normal push/PR triggers (e.g., scheduled (on: schedule), manual (workflow_dispatch), or webhook). Flag jobs with high failure rate, execution from non-standard runner environments, or workflows returning suspicious output (encoded data, token patterns).

suggestion.title: Sanctioned Entity Infrastructure Transfer Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'Following this restriction, the web hosting infrastructure was transferred to a newly created Dutch company that investigators believe acted as a front for the sanctioned entities.' This is a classic evasion pattern—detection should flag rapid company creation followed by infrastructure migration from sanctioned entities.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate WHOIS registration of newly formed companies with IP/ASN transfers originating from sanctioned entity infrastructure within 30–90 days of the entity's sanction listing. Pivot on shared hosting provider, payment methods, or registrant obfuscation. Flag companies registered in jurisdictions known for sanctions evasion.

suggestion.title: Hosting Provider Abuse by Sanctioned Entities
suggestion.rationale: Core of article: 'web hosting company...provided support to actions by the Russian Federation that undermine democracy and security, including through information manipulation and disruption of public and economic systems.' The abuse modality is explicit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor hosting providers' abuse complaint rates and abuse email communications for rapid provisioning of infrastructure to newly registered entities. Correlate high-volume DDoS traffic egressing from a single provider's ASN coupled with simultaneous infrastructure transfers. Flag providers offering bulletproof hosting characteristics (minimal abuse response, high tolerance for malicious traffic).

suggestion.title: Pro-Russian Hacktivist DDoS Infrastructure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article links infrastructure to NoName057(16): 'Danish authorities and infrastructure providers linked WorkTitans to attacks by the pro-Russian hacktivist group NoName057(16), which has previously targeted key organizations with distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify infrastructure historically or currently hosting DDoS botnet C&C or reflectors. Correlate ASN/IP ranges of infrastructure providers (Mirhosting: Almere; data centers: Dronten, Schiphol-Rijk) against DDoS traffic spike timelines. Track public disclosures of NoName057(16) targeting patterns and match against observed inbound traffic anomalies from those ASNs.

suggestion.title: Multi-Tier Hosting Infrastructure Layering
suggestion.rationale: Article describes explicit layering: 'Mirhosting...operated physical servers, provided colocation, and supplied high-capacity connectivity to major internet exchanges in Amsterdam and Frankfurt, acting as the transport layer through which Stark's traffic entered Europe to reach the WorkTitans infrastructure.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect infrastructure layering by correlating peering relationships at major European IXPs (Amsterdam AMS-IX, Frankfurt DE-CIX) with newly registered hosting companies and upstream colocation providers. Flag patterns where traffic egresses through high-capacity colocation providers before reaching edge infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Rapid Malicious Company Formation Post-Sanction
suggestion.rationale: Stark Industries founded 'shortly before Russia's invasion of Ukraine' (Feb 10, 2022), then sanctioned May 20, 2025, after which 'the web hosting infrastructure was transferred to a newly created Dutch company.' Pattern: sanction → immediate re-registration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag rapid company registrations (within 30 days) in same jurisdiction as sanctioned entity, using similar registrant obfuscation, operating in identical business verticals (hosting), and with overlapping technical infrastructure (ASNs, name servers, IP ranges).

suggestion.title: Colocation Provider Abuse by Sanctioned Entities
suggestion.rationale: Mirhosting in Almere 'provided physical servers, provided colocation, and supplied high-capacity connectivity.' Colocation is the transport layer for the abuse. Mirhosting's denial ('claimed they quickly intervened') is a common evasion claim.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor colocation providers for rapid customer turnover, abuse complaint patterns, and customers without legitimate business footprint. Cross-reference colocation ASNs against sanctions lists and OSINT on historical abuse.

suggestion.title: Suspicious VS Code Extension Installation or Rapid Update
suggestion.rationale: Article describes extension compromise distributed via update; must detect anomalous extension installation or mass rapid updates that inject malicious code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor VS Code extension marketplace API calls, file writes to extension directories (~/.vscode/extensions, %USERPROFILE%\.vscode\extensions), and rapid sequential updates. Correlate timestamps with known compromise window and suspicious child process spawning.

suggestion.title: Malicious Code Execution from VS Code Extension Sandbox
suggestion.rationale: Compromised extension executes arbitrary code in user context; detection must flag process creation spawning from extension directory or VS Code parent process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation where parent is code.exe or command line references paths within extension directories. Flag PowerShell, cmd.exe, or native binary execution with working directory in .vscode\extensions.

suggestion.title: Extension-Based Registry Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Payload achieves persistence by modifying HKCU registry for launch arguments, shell integration, or autostart hooks tied to VS Code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor writes to HKCU\Software\Microsoft\VSCode (extension settings), HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run with code.exe references, and shell context menu modifications. Correlate with extension installation timestamps.

suggestion.title: Network Communication Initiated by VS Code Process
suggestion.rationale: Malicious payload within extension initiates C2 or data exfiltration; outbound connections from code.exe to non-Microsoft infrastructure is strong compromise indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag DeviceNetworkEvents where InitiatingProcessName=code.exe and RemoteIP/RemoteUrl are not whitelisted Microsoft, GitHub, or npm domains. Baseline legitimate VS Code update and extension traffic; alert on anomalies post-compromise window.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from .git, .ssh, .env via Compromised Extension
suggestion.rationale: VS Code typically has file access to developer credentials (SSH keys, .git config, API tokens, .env); compromised extension can read and exfiltrate these.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file access (QueryName/CreateKey) from VS Code or spawned child processes to %USERPROFILE%\.ssh, .git/config, and %APPDATA%\Local\Temp\*.env files. Correlate reads with suspicious network egress or process spawning.

suggestion.title: Fileless or Staged Payload Dropped to Temp/Startup by Extension
suggestion.rationale: Extension drops second-stage executable to staging directories for persistence or lateral movement; files written from extension path to %TEMP% or Startup folders indicate active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate FileCreated events in %TEMP%, %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\Start Menu\Programs\Startup with VS Code or extension process context. Hash new files and check against threat feed. Alert on double extensions or obfuscated names.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Microsoft Graph API Enumeration via Service Principal
suggestion.rationale: Article core subject: 'Open-source framework ROADtools is being misused by threat actors for cloud intrusions'—ROADtools specializes in Graph API reconnaissance (users, groups, applications, service principals). Zero UCs detect suspicious Graph API bulk enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high-velocity Microsoft Graph API GET requests for bulk user/group/service-principal enumeration, directoryObjects, or application queries from atypical service principals or IP ranges. Focus on filter patterns and request clustering consistent with automated reconnaissance.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Service Principal Credential Issuance and Usage
suggestion.rationale: Nation-state actors (Curious Serpens, Midnight Blizzard) abuse service principal credentials for persistence and lateral movement in cloud tenants. Article describes 'cloud intrusions' via Entra ID. No UC for anomalous service principal sign-ins or token requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on service principal sign-ins from unexpected geographies or IPs, client-credential flows from interactive contexts, and newly created or modified service principal credentials outside change windows. Flag token requests to high-value resources (Exchange, SharePoint, Teams).

suggestion.title: Device Code Flow Authentication Abuse
suggestion.rationale: ROADtools signature attack: device code OAuth flow to bypass MFA and gain persistent cloud access. Article addresses 'nation-state tactics in the cloud.' No UC for unattended device code authentication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect device code flow requests (/devicecode endpoint) completed without human interaction, followed by sign-ins from ROPC clients or non-interactive applications. Flag when device code flows occur outside corporate IP ranges or from compromised devices.

suggestion.title: Bulk Azure Resource Enumeration and Policy Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: ROADtools enumerates subscriptions, storage accounts, key vaults, and conditional access policies; actors modify policies to bypass controls. Article mentions 'cloud intrusions.' No UC for bulk resource discovery or policy tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequential Azure resource API calls (list subscriptions, storage accounts, VMs, key vaults) from a single principal. Monitor for unusual modifications to conditional access policies, MFA settings, or authentication methods via API.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Application Consent and High-Risk Permission Grants
suggestion.rationale: ROADtools attackers grant Directory.ReadAll, Mail.Read, and other high-risk permissions to malicious applications. Article addresses Entra ID attacks. No UC for anomalous consent or permission escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag applications being granted Directory.ReadAll, Mail.ReadWrite, or AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All permissions by non-admins or from unusual contexts. Monitor consent from users outside developer groups or consent flows initiated by service principals.

suggestion.title: Cross-Tenant Lateral Movement via Cloud Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Article describes nation-state actors moving laterally between tenants and on-premises AD. No UC for detecting cross-tenant token abuse or tenant-hopping behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect authentication tokens or credentials from one tenant being used to access resources in a different tenant. Flag principals without prior history in a tenant suddenly accessing resources there. Correlate on-premises AD auth with Azure access in same timeframe.

suggestion.title: Execution of Exploit Payloads Against Project Glasswing
suggestion.rationale: Headline states '10,000+ 0-Days in Project Glasswing'—successful exploitation would manifest as anomalous process execution, privilege escalation, or unexpected system behavior on affected infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process creation telemetry for unusual child processes, unexpected privilege escalation, or system call anomalies on systems running Glasswing components. Alert on suspicious binary execution or shellcode indicators.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access and Credential Abuse Against Claude Mythos Preview
suggestion.rationale: Title identifies 'Claude Mythos Preview' as the discovery source. Service compromise would be detected via unauthorized authentication, anomalous API activity, or credential exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag anomalous API token usage, service account credential abuse, and unusual authentication patterns targeting Anthropic/Claude infrastructure. Monitor for debug-build artifact access or exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance and Vulnerability Scanning of Glasswing Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Discovery of '10,000+ 0-Days' implies prior scanning, enumeration, and vulnerability research activities that precede exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect large-scale scanning behavior: port enumeration sweeps targeting Glasswing infrastructure, suspicious DNS queries for Glasswing or Anthropic domains, rapid probing across multiple assets within a short timeframe.

suggestion.title: RoleMember authentication to Nezha /api/v1/cron endpoint followed by privilege-escalated cron execution
suggestion.rationale: The vulnerability explicitly states 'cron routes POST /api/v1/cron and PATCH /api/v1/cron/:id are wired through commonHandler (any authenticated user) rather than adminHandler, and the per-server permission check on cron creation has a vacuous-true bypass.' This is the initial-access and privilege-escalation step the pipeline missed entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for HTTP POST requests to /api/v1/cron or PATCH /api/v1/cron/:id from accounts with RoleMember status, followed by successful responses. Correlate with absence of an AdminApproval or CanExecuteOnServer permission check failure. Look for requests with 'servers' payload set to empty array or overly broad server selector.

suggestion.title: Cross-tenant cron task creation via vacuous-true authorization bypass
suggestion.rationale: Article states the 'per-server permission check on cron creation has a vacuous-true bypass.' This is the persistence mechanism—RoleMember creates a task on servers they should not have access to.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for cron tasks created via Nezha API with cross-tenant implications. Look for task creation events where the user account lacks direct server-level permissions but the request succeeds anyway. Correlate POST /api/v1/cron requests with subsequent cron execution logs showing commands running in unexpected security contexts.

suggestion.title: Nezha API missing authentication or role-boundary enforcement on administrative endpoints
suggestion.rationale: The core vulnerability is 'RoleMember (Role==1) can run shell on every server' via endpoints meant for RoleAdmin only. No hunt was generated for the root-cause: missing or misconfigured authz on commonHandler-wired routes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline successful authentication + authorization to Nezha /api/v1/cron by role. Alert when Role=1 (RoleMember) accounts successfully invoke operations that should require Role=0 (RoleAdmin). Track HTTP 200/201 responses on admin-tier API calls from non-admin authenticated users.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized server enumeration or sideways movement via Nezha agent on multiple hosts
suggestion.rationale: A RoleMember exploiting this can 'run shell on every server.' The discovery phase (T1057, process enumeration implied) suggests attackers will use compromised agents to pivot. No hunt targets lateral movement indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when a single compromised Nezha agent spawns process discovery commands (ps, netstat, ifconfig) in rapid succession across multiple monitored servers, or when the Nezha agent's parent shell opens new SSH/RDP connections to other hosts in the same tenant or across tenants.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Laravel-Lang Package Version Releases
suggestion.rationale: Article states '233 Versions of Laravel-Lang Packages' were compromised. Pipeline should detect abnormal release velocity and version bumping patterns. Phrase: 'Compromised 233 Versions of Laravel-Lang Packages'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package repositories (Packagist) for Laravel-Lang releases with abnormal frequency, unusual commit metadata, or mismatched code signatures. Flag installations of versions falling within the 233 compromised versions to detect lateral spread.

suggestion.title: Mass GitHub Repository Activity After Credential Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates '700 GitHub Repos' were hacked to inject malicious code. Should detect credential compromise via abnormal repo activity. Phrase: 'Hacking 700 GitHub Repos'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag accounts with logins from unusual geographies/IPs immediately followed by mass commit or branch activity, especially to package-distribution repos. Look for repos normally inactive becoming suddenly active or code pushed outside normal development windows.

suggestion.title: Malicious Code Execution via Dependency Installation
suggestion.rationale: Developers installing compromised Laravel-Lang packages will execute embedded malicious code. No UC generated for post-install execution. Phrase: 'Compromised...Packages'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process spawning or network connections immediately following `composer install` or `php artisan` commands that resolve to Laravel-Lang dependencies. Track unexpected child processes from PHP interpreters, especially curl, wget, or shell spawning.

suggestion.title: Package Hash / Signature Mismatch on Installed Modules
suggestion.rationale: Compromised versions will have altered hashes or missing signatures. No UC for validating package integrity. Phrase: 'Compromised 233 Versions'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare installed Laravel-Lang package hashes against Packagist official metadata. Alert on hash mismatches, missing signatures, or version-to-hash pairings not in the official repository. Cross-reference against Composer lock files.

suggestion.title: Unusual Access to Compromised Package Metadata
suggestion.rationale: Spike in downloads or unusual geographic distribution of compromised versions should trigger alerts. Not captured by pipeline. Phrase: '700 GitHub Repos' suggests scale and intentionality requiring distribution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Packagist API and CDN logs for abnormal download patterns on Laravel-Lang within the 233 compromised versions. Baseline against historical trends. Alert on geographic distribution outside developer concentrations.

suggestion.title: F5 BIG-IP CVE Exploitation Attempt Detection
