Flag domains with HTML rendering identical or >85% similar to official fifa.com. Correlate high-volume form submissions from different users to same domain with phishing-feed intelligence.

suggestion.title: Fake Payment Gateway Activity and Card Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Once you enter your card details, it goes straight to the people behind the fake site' and shows payment form capture. Pipeline failed to map collection phase or detect payment-fraud infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST submissions of credit card data to payment endpoints on non-PCI-compliant hosts or domains not registered with official FIFA merchant processors. Alert on payment form HTML served from typosquatted domains or SSL certificates issued recently. Correlate with abnormal outbound connections to attacker payment-processing gateways.

suggestion.title: Phishing Campaign Distribution via Social Media and Email
suggestion.rationale: Article describes multiple delivery channels: 'sponsored search results, ads on social media or links in email messages forwarded by someone who didn't check the address properly.' Pipeline did not map initial-access vectors or email/social phishing detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails and ads containing FIFA/World Cup 2026 keywords with embedded links to typosquatted domains. Monitor click-through events on suspicious FIFA-related links from bulk campaigns. Correlate sender reputation, DKIM/SPF failures, and URL shortening services with phishing-feed intelligence.

suggestion.title: Website Cloning and Infrastructure Acquisition for Impersonation
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes visual/functional cloning: 'copies the look and feel of FIFA's official site, including the colors, layout, navigation and ticketing flow' with side-by-side comparison. Pipeline failed to map infrastructure acquisition (T1583.006) or detect website clone patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor certificate transparency logs for SSL issuance on FIFA-themed domains. Correlate CSS/layout similarity to official FIFA site (favicon hash, stylesheet URLs, JavaScript libraries) with WHOIS registration metadata. Alert on hosting infrastructure supporting multiple FIFA-impersonation domains.

suggestion.title: Event-Driven Bulk Phishing Domain Registration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes targeted timing: 'in the run-up to major events' with emphasis on urgency ('interested, impatient and...worried that the tickets...will sell out'). Pipeline missed pattern detection for event-correlated infrastructure acquisition.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate WHOIS domain registrations, DNS zone creation, and SSL certificate issuance for clusters of FIFA-related domains registered within 7–14 days of World Cup event announcements or ticket-sale windows. Flag registrants with history of event-driven phishing campaigns.

suggestion.title: F5 BIG-IP Initial Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'From edge appliance to enterprise compromise'—F5 is the confirmed attack entry point. Zero detection use cases generated despite being primary initial access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor F5 BIG-IP admin interfaces and known vulnerable endpoints for exploitation attempts. Track anomalous login post-compromise and outbound command channels from appliance to internal systems.

suggestion.title: Confluence Credential Exfiltration Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'Confluence server for credential theft and identity compromise.' No credential access detection use cases surfaced despite explicit mention of theft activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk Confluence user enumeration, export requests targeting credential stores or user lists, and authentication from non-standard client IPs/user-agents after F5 compromise.

suggestion.title: Kerberos Relay Attack Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'threat actor attempted Kerberos relay.' Pipeline mapped zero techniques for this privileged attack primitive.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Event IDs 4768, 4769 for pre-auth encryption type downgrades, forged TGTs, and unusual TGT requests from service accounts. Correlate with NTLM signing disabled on critical assets.

suggestion.title: Edge-to-Internal Lateral Movement via Confluence
suggestion.rationale: Attack pivots from external F5 to internal Confluence server. Article: 'Multi-stage' and 'Linux intrusion' suggest OS-variant lateral movement techniques not extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SSH or direct service-to-service connections from compromised F5 appliance to internal Linux systems and Windows servers hosting Confluence. Flag compromised service-account usage post-Confluence breach.

suggestion.title: Defender EDR Evasion Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Microsoft Defender detected, blocked, and unraveled the attack.' Defender's observable blocks should translate to evasion detection use cases; none extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor process execution and network activity for obfuscation, credential dumping tools, and exploitation frameworks detected post-F5 compromise. Correlate with Defender block timestamps.

suggestion.title: Prometheus Malware Delivery via Spearphishing
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Prometheus Phishing Malware' as the attack mechanism. No detection use case was generated for phishing-borne malware execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor emails targeting .gov.ua or impersonating Ukrainian government domains. Detect Prometheus binary execution (DLL injection, process hollowing patterns) following suspicious email attachment opens. Flag rapid file copies and registry modifications post-detonation.

suggestion.title: Prometheus Command-and-Control Communication
suggestion.rationale: Phishing-delivered Prometheus implies C2 callback and command execution, but no network detection was proposed.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTPS/HTTP connections to non-whitelisted external infrastructure from affected government workstations. Detect DNS queries for domains matching Prometheus C2 patterns (high entropy subdomains, newly registered .xyz/.top/.online domains hoisting Ukrainian targets).

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Prometheus Execution
suggestion.rationale: Prometheus malware implicitly harvests credentials from compromised Ukraine government systems, enabling lateral movement. No credential theft or use-case was mapped.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect memory access by Prometheus process to LSASS, clipboard APIs, and keylogging patterns (GetAsyncKeyState, SetWindowsHookEx). Monitor for failed/brute-force logons using stolen credentials from government email domains days following phishing campaign.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised Government Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Successful Prometheus deployment in government networks implies stolen credentials used for internal reconnaissance and lateral movement; no post-compromise detection was provided.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for logons by government user accounts from non-standard geolocations, off-hours, or impossible travel times post-phishing. Detect AD enumeration (Get-ADUser, dsquery), network scanning, and sensitive file access by newly-compromised service accounts.

suggestion.title: Ghostwriter Infrastructure Reuse Detection
suggestion.rationale: Ghostwriter is a known Russian-affiliated threat actor with observable patterns. Pipeline missed attribution-driven IOC correlation against historical Ghostwriter C2, sender domains, and phishing templates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference sender domains, reply-to addresses, and hosting ASNs against prior Ghostwriter-attributed phishing campaigns (OSINT: abuse.ch, VirusTotal, Shodan). Flag typosquatted .ua domains or compromised legitimate government subdomains matching historical actor patterns.

suggestion.title: Malware Persistence via Registry or Scheduled Tasks
suggestion.rationale: Article describes targeting of government entities; Prometheus persistence mechanisms (registry run keys, WMI event subscriptions, scheduled tasks) should be detected to prevent re-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious Registry modifications (HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run, HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\Windows\Load) containing Prometheus binary paths. Detect WMI event subscriptions or scheduled tasks executing unsigned binaries from AppData or Temp folders.

suggestion.title: SQL injection pattern detection in YesWiki Bazar endpoint POST body
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'inject arbitrary SQL into an INSERT statement'—core attack mechanism. Pipeline generated zero detections for SQL keywords (UNION, SELECT, OR 1=1, comments, time-delay signatures). Direct request-body content inspection is missing entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search HTTP POST requests to */bazar/*vue=formulaire* for SQL keywords in decoded body (UNION SELECT, OR\s+1\s*=\s*1, ';\s*--, SLEEP\(, BENCHMARK\() with case-insensitive matching. Correlate with HTTP 200-201 responses to identify blind SQLi success indicators.

suggestion.title: Database credential hash access post-exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attacker 'read the full database, including yeswiki_users.password hashes'—credential access (T1110, T1040) is the objective, but zero detection generated. No hunt for password column reads or user table enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor database query logs for SELECT statements targeting password, hash, or credential columns in yeswiki_users table preceded by unauthenticated HTTP requests. Look for UNION-based extraction patterns and result set size anomalies.

suggestion.title: YesWiki version enumeration and vulnerable asset discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies affected versions '4.6.1, 4.6.2, doryphore-dev'—recon phase (T1595.002) requires identifying deployments. No detection for version banners, fingerprinting probes, or version disclosure endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to YesWiki version-disclosure paths (/?version, /CHANGELOG, /doc/version, robots.txt) or responses containing version strings matching 4.6.1-4.6.2 patterns. Correlate with subsequent Bazar endpoint probing from same source.

suggestion.title: Large-scale data exfiltration following SQLi exploitation success
suggestion.rationale: Article implies attacker extracts 'full database'—exfiltration (T1041) phase unaddressed. No detection for outbound data transfer, staging, or C2 beaconing post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal outbound traffic from YesWiki application servers. Trigger on sustained large-volume outbound connections (>100 MB), unusual destination ASNs, or exfiltration-tool user agents (curl, wget to non-standard ports) initiated immediately after successful SQLi payload indicators.

suggestion.title: FormManager::create() parameter tampering and bypass attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerable sink as 'FormManager::create()'—application-layer code path. Detect direct parameter manipulation, missing CSRF tokens, or type-confusion attacks targeting form creation logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for POST requests with form-creation parameters (FormManager, vue=formulaire) where request lacks expected CSRF token, has duplicate/malformed parameters, or uses type-confusion payloads (array vs string inputs where string expected).

suggestion.title: FileBrowser Quantum successful PATCH exploitation with confirmed response codes
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'allows file ops outside shared directory'—move/copy/rename operations must complete successfully. Recommended hunts detect payloads but not confirmed exploitation; impact phase requires HTTP 200/204 confirmation with correlated request/response timing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PATCH requests with fromPath/toPath traversal payloads that receive 200 or 204 response codes and are followed within 5 seconds by GET requests to endpoints outside the share path, indicating successful file relocation. Correlate HTTP logs with web server access logs to confirm the target file is now accessible from an unintended location.

suggestion.title: FileBrowser Quantum public share hash enumeration with invalid-share error patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article requires 'hash' parameter in public share URL, implying attackers must discover valid share hashes before exploitation. Recommended UC_20_2 detects volume but not the reconnaissance intent; 404 or 403 error patterns distinguish guessing from legitimate use.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sequences of PATCH requests to /public/api/resources with unique hash parameter values that receive 403 Forbidden or 401 Unauthorized responses (invalid share), followed by a successful 200 response to a different hash. This indicates hash enumeration + successful pivot. Set baseline tolerance for failed hashes per source IP and time window.

suggestion.title: FileBrowser Quantum path-sanitizer bypass via backend exception logs
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability in `resourcePatchHandler` sanitizer being skipped due to early filepath.Join in `publicPatchHandler`. Exploitation attempts should produce detectable exception patterns. No use case for application-layer detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse FileBrowser Quantum backend logs for exceptions or panics originating from `filepath.Join`, `publicPatchHandler`, or path validation code during or immediately after PATCH requests. Correlate timing with suspicious HTTP activity. Baseline exception rates per path-handling function and alert on 3x+ deviation.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized file system operations outside FileBrowser Quantum share root
suggestion.rationale: Article describes impact: files are moved/copied/renamed 'outside the shared directory.' HTTP-level detection confirms requests but not impact; file system monitoring closes the detection loop.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: If the FileBrowser Quantum process can be monitored, detect file operations (rename, move, copy) performed by the FileBrowser service account on paths outside the configured share root directory. Correlate timing and source paths. Flag operations that move files into world-readable directories or system paths.

suggestion.title: Detect Art-Template Package Versions with Backdoor Signatures
suggestion.rationale: Article states versions 4.13.3, 4.13.5-4.13.6 were weaponized; npm.js and dependency manifests should be scanned for these pinned versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for npm install/require of art-template versions 4.13.3, 4.13.5, or 4.13.6 in build logs, CI/CD pipelines, or dependency manifests. Cross-reference package-lock.json or yarn.lock for pinned vulnerable versions.

suggestion.title: Detect Malicious Domain IOCs in Bundle Dependencies
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline injected hardcoded domains v3.jiathis[.]com, utaq[.]cfww[.]shop, l1ewsu3yjkqeroy[.]xyz into npm bundles; scanning source and transpiled bundles for these strings is a direct detection vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan .js files in node_modules and built bundles for literal domain strings v3.jiathis.com, utaq.cfww.shop, and l1ewsu3yjkqeroy.xyz. Monitor DNS requests and HTTP requests to these domains. Flag any script tag injection containing these domains in runtime network events.

suggestion.title: Detect Safari Browser Fingerprinting Patterns on iOS
suggestion.rationale: Article states implant 'fingerprints site visitors' and 'only activates on Safari running on iOS 11.0 through 17.2.' Fingerprinting scripts with iOS/Safari detection logic are a clear behavioral signature.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect JavaScript that conditionally branches on user-agent checks for Safari and iOS version strings (11.0-17.2). Look for feature-detection code patterns that isolate Safari/iOS targets. Flag unusual fingerprinting data exfiltration to external domains.

suggestion.title: Detect C2 Beaconing Every 10 Seconds to Coruna Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states malware 'beacons victim data to command-and-control servers every ten seconds.' Regular 10-second interval network traffic is a strong behavioral signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for regular (periodic) outbound connections to C2 domains at ~10-second intervals. Baseline DNS and HTTP request frequency per asset; flag traffic with 9-12 second periodicity to art-template implant domains. Correlate with session key cecd08aa6ff548c2 or campaign code CHMK6IG08F42496C22 in request bodies.

suggestion.title: Detect Script Loader Injection in npm Bundles Across Releases
suggestion.rationale: Article describes evolution: v4.13.3 used obfuscation to hide loaders, v4.13.5-4.13.6 removed obfuscation and injected plaintext loaders into browser bundles. Scanning for unexpected <script> injections into art-template outputs is actionable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare transpiled/minified JavaScript output from art-template across version boundaries. Flag new <script> tags or loader function calls not present in baseline builds. Monitor build artifact checksums (SHA-256: f31bdd069fe7966ae11be1f78ee5dd44445938856dd1df12379e0e84a6851f5c) against known clean builds.

suggestion.title: Correlate CVE-2024-23222 Exploitation Attempts with iOS 17.2 Cutoff Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Article notes malware exits silently on iOS 17.3+ and correlates this to CVE-2024-23222 (WebKit patch), indicating intentional targeting of unpatched versions for browser-level exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Safari crashes or WebKit exploitation attempts on iOS 11.0-17.2. Flag CVE-2024-23222 exploitation payloads. Correlate with art-template dependency presence. Alert if unpatched iOS devices with art-template dependency attempt access to Coruna-linked domains.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Batch File Execution from Email/Downloads Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'Deliver Banana RAT Through Malicious Batch Files'—batch files are the primary execution vector and should trigger behavioral detection when spawned from typical email/download staging directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect .bat or .cmd files created or executed from Downloads, %Temp%, or email client temporary directories. Alert if execution occurs within minutes of file creation (indicates fresh extract-and-run) or if parent process is explorer.exe or an email client.

suggestion.title: NF-e Themed Phishing Email with Batch File Attachment
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'NF-e Invoice Lures'—NF-e is Brazil's electronic invoicing standard. Detection should look for emails with invoice-themed subject lines (Portuguese language, 'NF-e', 'Nota Fiscal') and .bat/.cmd/.exe attachments.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for inbound emails with Portuguese keywords (NF-e, Nota Fiscal, Fatura) in subject or body, containing file attachments with extensions .bat, .cmd, .scr, or double-extensions (.pdf.bat). Correlate with file reputation (unknown/malicious hashes).

suggestion.title: Batch File Spawning Scripting Engine with Suspicious Arguments
suggestion.rationale: RAT delivery chains typically use batch files as initial stagers that then spawn PowerShell or cmd.exe with encoded/obfuscated commands. Article describes batch file as delivery mechanism, implying execution chaining.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .bat/.cmd files (parent process) spawning powershell.exe, pwsh.exe, or cmd.exe children, especially if parent filename is uncommon, comes from Downloads/Temp, or command line contains encoding switches (-enc, -e, -EncodedCommand) or suspicious operators (|, >, IEX).

suggestion.title: Banana RAT C2 Beaconing Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'Banana RAT' as the delivered payload. C2 communication is inherent to RAT function; detection should monitor for known Banana RAT infrastructure or behavioral patterns (periodic outbound connections, specific User-Agents, port usage).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound HTTP/HTTPS connections to known Banana RAT C2 domains or IPs (if available in threat intelligence). Alternatively, detect periodic beaconing behavior (regular interval callbacks from suspicious processes) or connections to uncommon ports from newly spawned batch/PowerShell processes.

suggestion.title: Registry Persistence via Batch/PowerShell Process
suggestion.rationale: RAT payloads typically establish persistence mechanisms. Batch files spawning processes that modify registry Run/RunOnce keys indicate infection establishment, a step between execution and command-and-control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when processes spawned from batch files or PowerShell attempt to write to HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run* or HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run* keys, especially with values pointing to suspicious file paths or command lines.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Cron Job Creation on FreePBX
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'six-layer persistence' on FreePBX systems. Cron is a standard Linux persistence vector. Zero cron-based detections in pipeline output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for crontab modifications or /etc/cron.d file writes from www-data, asterisk, or fop user contexts. Alert on cron entries executing shell commands to non-standard ports, external IPs, or spawning reverse shells. Baseline legitimate FreePBX maintenance tasks.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Web Shell Upload to FreePBX Web Root
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'hackers use' persistence mechanisms but no detection for PHP/web-accessible uploads, common FreePBX attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PHP file creation in /var/www/html/admin/modules, /var/www/html/rest, and web-root after compromise. Correlate with web server access logs (POST to upload endpoints returning 200) followed by execution of recently-created PHP via php-fpm process spawning shells.

suggestion.title: FreePBX Database Module Injection Persistence
suggestion.rationale: FreePBX stores modules/configuration in MySQL. Article references persistence layers but pipeline generated no database-level detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor MySQL databases (freepbx, asterisk) for unauthorized INSERT/UPDATE operations adding modules with suspicious names or paths. Flag database modifications from www-data user executing non-standard module registration queries outside maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Outbound Reverse Shell Callback from FreePBX Process
suggestion.rationale: Persistence requires C2 communication. Article headline establishes 'maintained access' but no command-and-control detection present.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound connections from apache2, php-fpm, or asterisk processes to non-standard ports (8888, 4444, 5555) or suspicious external IPs. Alert on process trees: php-fpm spawning sh/bash with immediate network callbacks, baseline against known VOIP trunk traffic.

suggestion.title: Asterisk Configuration Persistence via Extensions.conf Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article title mentions '6-layer persistence.' Asterisk config files (/etc/asterisk/*.conf) are filesystem-level persistence vectors not covered by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor /etc/asterisk/extensions.conf, sip.conf, iax.conf for unauthorized additions of dial patterns pointing to attacker IPs, SIP peer definitions with non-standard addresses, or exten rules calling external contexts. Flag file modifications outside change-control windows with suspicious timing.

suggestion.title: DDoS Botnet Command & Control Beaconing Detection
suggestion.rationale: DDoS-for-hire operations require C2 infrastructure to coordinate attacks across compromised hosts. Article explicitly establishes 'Kimwolf DDoS Botnet' but pipeline produced zero C2 communication indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for regular heartbeat connections (beaconing) to rare or malicious IP destinations on non-standard ports. DDoS botnets typically use HTTP/HTTPS tunneling or custom protocols for C2. Flag internal hosts with anomalous outbound connection patterns: high frequency, low data volume, consistent timing intervals.

suggestion.title: Botnet Malware Execution from User-Writable Paths
suggestion.rationale: Botnets execute malware on compromised systems via exploitation or social engineering. Title describes botnet operations but no execution-phase indicators were extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unsigned or suspicious executables spawned from %TEMP%, %APPDATA%, Downloads, or other user-writable directories. Flag process injection patterns (suspicious parent-child relationships). Monitor for scriptable interpreters (PowerShell, cmd.exe, VBScript) executing from non-standard locations or with obfuscated command-line arguments.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Outbound Traffic Volume from Internal Hosts
suggestion.rationale: DDoS attack participation generates distinctive traffic signatures—high-volume outbound data. Article explicitly states 'DDoS attacks' but no impact-phase detection was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on internal hosts sending anomalously high packet counts or sustained data volume to external destinations (especially UDP or fragmented traffic). Establish baseline per-host traffic profiles and flag deviations. Detect participation in known DDoS attack patterns (botnet-sourced volumetric attacks).

suggestion.title: Kimwolf Threat Actor Infrastructure Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'Kimwolf' as the threat actor, establishing actor attribution. Pipeline did not surface actor name or correlate against known infrastructure/IOCs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference network observables against threat intelligence on Kimwolf infrastructure (C2 domains, hosting provider IPs, ASNs, malware hashes). Detect DNS lookups and HTTP requests to previously sinkholed or takedown Kimwolf C2 domains. Monitor for malware samples attributed to Kimwolf botnet family.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Driver Loading via Service Registry Modification
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD exploits require loading vulnerable drivers, typically via service registry paths (HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services). Pipeline produced no detection for this critical execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor registry modifications to HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\* for ImagePath values pointing to suspicious or unsigned driver binaries. Correlate with process execution attempting to load these services via reg.exe or sc.exe.

suggestion.title: Execution of Known Vulnerable Drivers by Hash
suggestion.rationale: Article title implies specific vulnerable drivers are discussable. Pipeline extracted no driver hashes, filenames, or signatures despite this being core IOC data for BYOVD detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain hash allowlist of signed-but-vulnerable drivers (e.g., Intel EPTM, NVIDIA, MSI driver families). Alert on unsigned kernel modules or signed drivers loaded from non-standard paths or by unusual parent processes.

suggestion.title: Kernel-Mode Code Execution via Driver Exploitation Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD is fundamentally a kernel privilege escalation technique. Pipeline identified no kernel-level execution indicators such as suspicious ring0 callbacks, interrupt descriptor table (IDT) hooks, or driver entry point anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on suspicious driver loading patterns: mismatched module base addresses, drivers loaded with unusual privilege levels, or drivers that modify kernel structures (ETW disabling, ACL removal, etc.).

suggestion.title: BYOVD-Specific Evasion: Security Tool Disabling via Driver
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD privilege escalation often precedes defensive measure tampering. Article context implies evasion. Pipeline detected no defense evasion indicators like EDR process termination, minifilter driver removal, or ETW tracing disablement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate driver loading activity with immediate subsequent termination of security tools (MsMpEng.exe, sense.exe), ETW provider disabling, or minifilter driver detach operations.

suggestion.title: Service Installation Anomalies Associated with Unsigned Drivers
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD often requires registering drivers as services. Pipeline saw no detection for service creation tied to driver artifacts or suspicious parent process contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sc.exe or reg.exe operations creating/modifying services with ImagePath values pointing to .sys files in user-writable or temporary directories. Alert on service DisplayName / Description fields that mismatch the binary's legitimate vendor.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Workflow Modified by Unusual Principal
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'malicious CI/CD workflows' targeting 5,561 repos — suggests attackers injected or modified .github/workflows YAML files. No UC generated despite being the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation or modification of .github/workflows/*.yml files in repositories, particularly by service accounts, newly provisioned identities, or during off-hours. Correlate with GitHub audit logs showing unexpected workflow_dispatch or push events from foreign IPs. Alert on workflows containing curl/wget exfiltration commands, credential retrieval from GitHub secrets, or lateral movement patterns.

suggestion.title: Credential Exfiltration via CI/CD Secrets Access
suggestion.rationale: Malicious CI/CD workflows typically steal SECRETS and PATs. Article describes attack targeting 5,561 repos — implies systematic credential harvesting. No UC was generated for this high-risk pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect jobs that reference GitHub.token, secrets, or environment variables, then transmit data to external domains. Look for base64-encoded credential dumps in CI logs, unusual curl/PowerShell POST requests to attacker infrastructure, or rapid PAT generation followed by deletion.

suggestion.title: Batch Repository Compromise via Common Delivery Mechanism
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline targeted 5,561 repos suggests infrastructure-wide or supply-chain compromise, not isolated incidents. No UC captures how attackers gained initial write access to so many repos simultaneously.
log_sources: AuditEvent (GitHub: bulk user/org provisioning, PAT creation, repository setting
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk repository setting modifications (default branch, branch protection rules, webhook additions) across multiple repos by single principal in short timeframe. Flag service accounts with unexpected write access to large repo sets. Detect mass PAT creations or GitHub App installations across organizational scope.

suggestion.title: CI/CD Runner Process Execution Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Malicious workflows execute arbitrary code in CI environments. Article implies large-scale execution but no UC targets suspicious runner process behavior, syscalls, or file system activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor CI runner processes (GitHub Actions runner, system-wide runners) for execution of unusual binaries (curl, nc, socat, python -m http.server), shell invocations of encoded payloads, or process spawns from unexpected working directories. Baseline legitimate workflow behavior per org and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: GitHub API Anomaly — High-Volume Secret/Token Operations
suggestion.rationale: Attackers accessing 5,561 repos likely performed API recon, secret enumeration, or mass token operations. Article implies API-driven attack but no use case targets GitHub API audit anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag sustained sequences of API calls querying repository settings, secrets metadata, or deployment keys across multiple repos by single principal, especially from non-browser user agents or unusual geolocations. Alert on failed auth followed by successful escalation within same session.

suggestion.title: Webhook Creation in Compromised Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Standard post-compromise persistence: attackers inject webhooks to exfiltrate future commits or re-inject malicious code. Article implies persistence but pipeline generated no detection for webhook abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation or modification of repository webhooks pointing to external IPs, especially unregistered/non-org-managed domains. Correlate with unusual push events. Alert if webhook targets internal-looking URLs (192.168.*, 10.0.0.*) or known C2 IPs.

suggestion.title: Suspicious GitHub Actions Workflow Modification in Public Repos
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Mass GitHub Actions Secret Exfiltration' — core attack vector is malicious workflow file injection or modification to enable secret theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor commits modifying .github/workflows/ files in public repositories for addition of run steps that access secrets context or export GitHub tokens. Flag workflows referencing previously-unused credentials or external HTTP endpoints.

suggestion.title: Secrets Exfiltration via GitHub Actions Run Steps
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'secret exfiltration' — pipeline should detect workflows that access secrets() and transmit them off-platform.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate: (1) workflow accessing GitHub secrets or github.token, (2) base64/hex encoding or compression of secret data, (3) HTTP POST or curl command to external domain. Single detected occurrence = alert; three occurrences in one repo = incident.

suggestion.title: Large-Scale Repository Injection Pattern Detection
suggestion.rationale: Attack affected '5,500+ public repositories' — requires pattern-level detection beyond single-repo analysis. Pipeline should flag distributed compromise signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect single account or coordinated account set modifying workflows across 10+ unrelated public repositories within 24-hour window. Threshold: >15 repos/day indicates automation or mass compromise exploitation.

suggestion.title: Public Repository Takeover via Pull Request Injection
suggestion.rationale: 5,500+ repos suggests supply-chain attack via PR merge or account compromise. Initial access vector not reconstructed by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag PRs modifying .github/workflows/ from newly-created accounts (<30 days old) or accounts with low contribution history on target repo. Correlate with repositories lacking required code review or branch protection policies.

suggestion.title: GitHub Token/Secret Exposure in Workflow Logs
suggestion.rationale: Exfiltration campaign likely harvested secrets from repository settings. Logs themselves may leak credential values if workflows mishandle them.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan workflow execution logs for output containing patterns matching GitHub token format (ghp_*, ghu_*, ghs_*) or repository secret values. Alert on echo/print statements in run steps that output secrets context or environment variables.

suggestion.title: Detect AI-Targeted Credential Harvesting Against Healthcare/Staffing Orgs
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses security posture for healthcare (St. Luke's) and staffing (ManpowerGroup), sectors known as high-value targets for identity compromise and lateral movement. If article describes threats these orgs faced or identity-based attacks in AI context, detection gap exists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for phishing campaigns, credential stuffing attempts, or MFA bypass attempts targeting employees at healthcare and staffing organizations. Focus on AI/LLM-generated phishing content or automated social engineering tools.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthorized AI Model Access or Training Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'securing AI foundations'—implies potential risks of unauthorized access to AI systems, training data theft, or model poisoning. Pipeline should have flagged detection for these data-plane threats.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual data exfiltration volumes from AI model directories, training data repositories, or MLOps infrastructure. Detect downloads of model weights, dataset exports, or high-entropy data flows to external IPs.

suggestion.title: Detect Malicious Prompt Injection or Model Abuse in Healthcare/Staffing Context
suggestion.rationale: If article discusses AI governance for these sectors, it implicitly acknowledges risks of prompt injection, jailbreaks, or LLM abuse that could have compliance/patient-safety impact. No detection logic was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor API logs for suspicious prompts, repeated adversarial inputs, or unusual parameter injection attempts against AI systems. Flag requests attempting to extract training data, bypass safety guardrails, or generate harmful output.

suggestion.title: Shell Company Registration Immediately Post-Sanctions
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Following this restriction, the web hosting infrastructure was transferred to a newly created Dutch company that investigators believe acted as a front for the sanctioned entities.' WorkTitans B.V. created immediately after Stark Industries sanctioned to evade restrictions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect newly incorporated entities sharing infrastructure, payment methods, or jurisdiction with recently sanctioned organizations. Flag business registrations <30 days post-sanctions with matching industry vertical and upstream provider overlap.

suggestion.title: Colocation Provider Infrastructure Abuse for Sanctioned Transit
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'Mirhosting...provided physical servers...and supplied high-capacity connectivity to major internet exchanges in Amsterdam and Frankfurt, acting as the transport layer through which Stark's traffic entered Europe.' ISP/colocation provider abused as sanctioned infrastructure transit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor colocation and Tier-1 ISP egress for traffic patterns attributable to sanctioned entities. Detect abnormal routing changes, capacity spikes from known malicious ASNs, or infrastructure migration events preceding law enforcement action.

suggestion.title: Hosting Infrastructure Supporting Pro-Russian DDoS Botnet
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Danish authorities and infrastructure providers linked WorkTitans to attacks by the pro-Russian hacktivist group NoName057(16), which has previously targeted key organizations with distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate observed DDoS attack signatures (botnet command patterns, traffic fingerprints) with hosting infrastructure ownership and ASN assignments. Flag hosting providers hosting known DDoS C2 or command relays for NoName057(16) or similar threat actors.

suggestion.title: Massive Multi-Location Server Seizure Precursor
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'FIOD conducted multiple raids in data centers in Dronten and Schiphol-Rijk...seized 800 servers, laptops, phones, and administrative records.' Detect patterns preceding large-scale law enforcement infrastructure takedown.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for coordinated availability drops affecting 100+ servers from a single ASN/data center, mass DNS record deletions, or unexpected BGP prefix withdrawals. These patterns may indicate law enforcement seizure or suggest future disruption risk.

suggestion.title: Sanctioned Entity Infrastructure Acquisition via Front Company
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The [Dutch] web hosting company...provided support to actions by the Russian Federation...' and later 'the web hosting infrastructure was transferred to a newly created Dutch company.' Detect sanctions-evasion hosting acquisition patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify newly registered infrastructure (ASNs, hosting accounts, domains) acquired by entities with known ties to sanctioned organizations or sanctioned individuals. Flag account registrations using shell company addresses or payment proxies.

suggestion.title: GitHub Repository Unauthorized Code Commit to Package Repos
suggestion.rationale: Article states hackers 'Hacking 700 GitHub Repos' to inject malicious code into Laravel-Lang packages. Attackers must commit/push code to these repositories. Article phrase: 'Hackers Compromised 233 Versions of Laravel-Lang Packages by Hacking 700 GitHub Repos'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect commits to Laravel-Lang package repositories from previously-unused maintainer accounts, from new IP ranges, or outside normal activity windows. Flag commits containing obfuscated PHP, base64-encoded payloads, eval()/include chains, or suspicious external domain references. Correlate with GitHub auth anomalies (new 2FA device, PAT creation).

suggestion.title: Malicious Package Version Publication to Packagist Registry
suggestion.rationale: 233 compromised versions were published to package registry. Detections needed at registry level for suspicious publish events. Article phrase: 'Compromised 233 Versions of Laravel-Lang Packages'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Packagist for unexpected version bumps from Laravel-Lang maintainers, rapid successive publishes, or versions containing initialization-stage PHP code (vendor/autoload, composer.json scripts). Detect obfuscated code, eval()-based execution, or cryptographic operations in package initialization that deviate from baseline Laravel-Lang code patterns.

suggestion.title: Host Installation of Compromised Laravel-Lang Package Versions
suggestion.rationale: Developer and production hosts downloading and installing malicious versions via Composer. Detection needed at victim endpoint. Article phrase: '233 Versions of Laravel-Lang Packages' + implicit wide distribution via package manager
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In CI/CD logs and application deployment artifacts, detect installation of Laravel-Lang from affected version range without pinned constraints. Flag Composer install/update commands pulling from Packagist registry during build pipeline. Correlate with first evidence of payload execution.

suggestion.title: GitHub Account Compromise via Credential Theft or MFA Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Attackers gained write access to 700 repos, indicating stolen credentials or account takeover of maintainers. Article phrase: 'Hacking 700 GitHub Repos'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect GitHub logins to maintainer accounts from new geographies, new devices, or with User-Agent anomalies. Alert on: PAT (Personal Access Token) generation without user interaction, disabling/re-enabling 2FA, SSH key additions, or repository write events from dormant accounts. Cross-check login IP reputation and velocity anomalies.

suggestion.title: PHP Code Execution from Compromised Laravel-Lang Package Initialization
suggestion.rationale: Malicious payload embedded in packages executes when Laravel applications bootstrap and load the localization library. Article phrase: 'Compromised 233 Versions' + implicit code injection via package compromise
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In web application logs, detect unexpected PHP code execution during vendor/ directory initialization or Laravel-Lang autoload phase. Flag shell_exec(), system(), eval(), or proc_open() calls not in security baseline. Detect child processes spawned from PHP interpreter, suspicious DNS queries from app context, or outbound TCP connections during initialization.

suggestion.title: F5 BIG-IP Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title states 'Exploit F5 BIG-IP Appliance' but pipeline extracted no IOCs or kill-chain phase for initial access. Public-facing appliance exploitation is a primary vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor F5 BIG-IP management and data-plane interfaces for exploitation signatures (CVE-2024-XXXX payload attempts, malformed requests targeting known F5 RCE vectors). Correlate failed exploitation attempts with subsequent successful management console access or unusual process spawning on the appliance.

suggestion.title: SSH Lateral Movement from F5 to Linux Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Gain SSH Access and Pivot Into Enterprise Linux Networks'—clear lateral movement vector. Pipeline surfaced no detection for this phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SSH connections originating from F5 BIG-IP appliance (by hostname/IP) to internal Linux systems, especially successful ones. Pivot on success rate: >3 successful SSH authentications from F5 to different Linux hosts within 5m suggests reconnaissance or lateral movement post-compromise.

suggestion.title: Command Execution on Linux Systems Post-F5 Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article describes pivoting to 'Enterprise Linux Networks'—implies code execution, not just access. No execution-phase detection suggested by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process creation on Linux systems immediately following successful SSH authentication from F5 appliance. Flag unusual parent processes (sshd spawning shells with atypical arguments), command obfuscation (base64, hex encoding), or execution of non-standard shells (bash -i, nc, perl) within 2 minutes of F5→Linux SSH event.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from F5 BIG-IP Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Compromised F5 appliances often contain cached AD credentials, SSH keys, or API tokens. No credential-access phase in pipeline output despite title implying persistence across multiple systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file system access to F5 sensitive paths (/config, /tmesh, /shared) following exploitation. Monitor for spawning of credential-dumping tools (grep, cat, find) targeting config files or private key directories. Alert on exfiltration of .pem, .key, or config files post-compromise.

suggestion.title: Persistence via SSH Key Injection on Linux Post-Pivot
suggestion.rationale: 'Pivot into Enterprise Linux Networks' implies sustained access. Pipeline missed detection for persistence mechanisms attackers would establish after gaining initial SSH foothold.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthorized writes to ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on Linux systems, especially after F5-sourced SSH sessions. Flag creation of new user accounts on Linux systems within 10m of F5 compromise detection. Correlate file modifications on /etc/sudoers with successful SSH logins from F5.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration from Linux Systems Post-Pivot
suggestion.rationale: Article title implies successful enterprise compromise via pivot. No exfiltration-phase detection generated despite '[CRIT]' severity and multi-system scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large data transfers from compromised Linux systems over unusual ports/protocols (ssh tunnels, HTTP POST, scp) following F5 pivot event. Detect spawning of data-copying tools (tar, zip, rsync, dd) on Linux systems correlated with F5-sourced SSH sessions. Flag reads of sensitive files (/etc/shadow, /root/.ssh) by non-root processes post-F5-compromise.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Laravel-Lang Package Version Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article title states packages were compromised; typical supply-chain attacks poison specific versions. Need detection for unexpected package version changes or out-of-band package downloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor composer.json/composer.lock for unexpected laravel-lang version pins or detections of package installation from non-standard repositories. Baseline known-good hashes.

suggestion.title: Cross-Platform Credential Stealer Execution from PHP
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly describes delivery of credential stealer; title also specifies cross-platform capability, indicating multi-OS malware payloads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PHP processes spawning unusual child processes, accessing OS credential stores (LSA, keychain, /etc/shadow equivalents), or opening network connections to non-standard ports from web service accounts.

suggestion.title: Malware Payload Injection via Composer Auto-loader
suggestion.rationale: Laravel-Lang is a localization package auto-loaded by Composer; compromised package executes on application bootstrap, not user action.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor vendor/laravel-lang/ directory for unexpected file modifications post-installation. Track PHP process command lines that include vendor/autoload.php execution with suspicious parent/sibling processes.

suggestion.title: Detect Composer Installation of Compromised Laravel-Lang Packages
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies four packages as fully compromised: 'Packagist has unlisted the packages' laravel-lang/lang, laravel-lang/http-statuses, laravel-lang/attributes, laravel-lang/actions. Need detection on composer.lock/composer.json presence and installation attempt.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on execution of composer require/install with any version of laravel-lang/lang, laravel-lang/http-statuses, laravel-lang/attributes, or laravel-lang/actions. Flag composer.lock entries naming these packages. Cross-reference installation timestamps against May 22-23, 2026 compromise window.

suggestion.title: Detect Malicious Helpers.php Execution via Composer Autoload
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'An injected helpers.php file was wired into Composer's autoload.files entry, causing it to run on every PHP request'. This is the persistence/execution mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PHP process loading src/helpers.php from vendor/laravel-lang/* directory. Monitor for autoload.files entries being dynamically loaded. Correlate execution with recent composer install/update operations.

suggestion.title: Detect Network Callbacks to flipboxstudio[.]info C2
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies C2 domains: 'fetches a second stage from https://flipboxstudio[.]info/payload and executes it in the background. Collected data is encrypted and shipped out to https://flipboxstudio[.]info/exfil'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any DNS query or HTTP/HTTPS connection attempt to flipboxstudio[.]info from PHP processes or child processes. Flag /payload and /exfil endpoints. Correlate timing with composer-based Laravel-Lang installation.

suggestion.title: Detect Credential and Secrets Exfiltration Post-Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes second-stage stealer walking through: 'Cloud provider credentials (AWS, GCP, Azure), Kubernetes kubeconfig, Vault tokens, CI/CD secrets, SSH keys, .env files, browser data, password manager vaults, crypto wallets, messaging tokens'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PHP processes or children reading .env files, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.kube/config, ~/.ssh/, browser profile directories, or password manager vault files. Monitor for reads of multiple credential sources in short timeframe. Correlate with network callbacks to flipboxstudio[.]info.

suggestion.title: Detect Post-Exfiltration File Deletion and Anti-Forensics
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'After exfiltration, the stealer attempts to delete its dropped files to slow down forensic recovery.' Indicates detection window post-theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on deletion of recently-created files in temporary directories (tmp, %TEMP%) by PHP or child processes, especially if preceded by reads of sensitive credential files and network egress to flipboxstudio[.]info. High confidence signal of active compromise.

suggestion.title: Detect Git Tag Manipulation in Laravel-Lang Organization Forks
suggestion.rationale: Article explains mechanism: 'the attacker pointed Git tags to commits in an attacker-controlled fork, exploiting how Packagist resolves tags from GitHub. A Git tag created within an organization can resolve to a commit in a fork outside that organization.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation of Git tags in laravel-lang/* organization that point to commits outside official repositories. Monitor Packagist ingestion logs for tags resolving to fork commits. Flag tag creation bursts across multiple repositories within seconds.

suggestion.title: Composer Package Repository Tag Overwrite
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Every Tag Across Multiple Composer Packages Rewritten'—no detection for unexpected package version/tag mutations in package repositories or local composer.lock mismatches.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor composer package registry for unexpected tag rewrites, version rollbacks, or hash mismatches between local locks and remote manifests. Alert on tag updates to production packages outside release windows or automated bot accounts.

suggestion.title: CI Environment Variable / Secret Access Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack goal as 'Steal CI Secrets'—pipeline missed detection for exfiltration of GitHub Actions secrets, deployment tokens, or CI environment variables.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect when build jobs dump, exfiltrate, or access CI secrets (GitHub tokens, AWS keys, deploy certs) to unexpected destinations. Alert on environment variable enumeration or attempts to write secrets to logs.

suggestion.title: Malicious Code Injection in Package Build Output
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain rewrite implies injected malicious code into package tags—no detection for unexpected code additions or obfuscated PHP/Laravel code in published releases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate package file structures and detect new files, obfuscated functions, or exfiltration stubs added post-compromise. Compare shipped hashes against expected source commits.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Package Repository Authentication Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Attacker 'rewrote' tags across multiple packages—suggests compromised repository credentials or lack of commit signature validation. No detection for unauthorized package pushes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unsigned or improperly signed commits to package repositories, pushes from anomalous IPs/accounts, or tag creates/deletes lacking maintainer approval. Enforce GPG-signed releases.

suggestion.title: Composer Autoload or Install Hook Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attack via Composer likely leverages post-install scripts or autoloaders—pipeline did not suggest detection for malicious composer.json scripts or autoloader injections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor composer scripts (post-install-cmd, post-update-cmd) for unexpected shell commands, curl/wget to external URLs, or credential references. Baseline allowed scripts per environment.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Stolen CI Token Reuse
suggestion.rationale: Exfiltrated CI secrets enable follow-on attacks—no detection for reuse of stolen GitHub/GitLab tokens from unfamiliar IPs or to access other repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect stolen CI tokens used from IPs outside corporate/CI provider networks. Alert on token reuse to access repositories not in the original job's scope.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48172 LiteSpeed Plugin Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Title establishes active exploitation of LiteSpeed cPanel plugin (CVE-2026-48172); no IOC extraction or detection logic was attempted despite this being the core threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cPanel/LiteSpeed plugin interfaces for HTTP requests containing CVE-2026-48172 exploitation payloads (command injection patterns targeting plugin endpoints). Track failed and successful requests to /litespeed/ or related plugin paths with special characters or script tags. Cross-reference with vulnerability scanner data for unpatched LiteSpeed versions.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Script Execution via LiteSpeed Process
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'Run Scripts as Root'—a privilege escalation outcome. Pipeline extracted no detection for unauthorized root execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on LiteSpeed parent processes spawning child processes with root privileges, especially if initiated from non-root LiteSpeed service account. Monitor for execution of shell scripts, perl, python, or bash invoked with uid/gid 0 under unexpected parent processes.

suggestion.title: cPanel Plugin File Modification Indicative of Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability in cPanel plugin implies file-based persistence; pipeline missed detecting plugin file tampering despite this being a standard post-exploitation indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline cPanel LiteSpeed plugin directory (typically /usr/local/lsws/admin/html/ or vendor-specific paths) and alert on unauthorized writes, renames, or deletions. Flag modifications to plugin .php, .so, or .conf files outside normal maintenance windows. Cross-check against known LiteSpeed plugin versions.

suggestion.title: Nginx Poolslip Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'Enables DoS and Code Execution Attacks.' Pipeline produced no detection for exploitation attempts against this publicly disclosed Nginx flaw.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Nginx access logs for malformed or oversized HTTP requests targeting connection pooling mechanisms, coupled with abnormal HTTP status codes (50x errors, connection resets) within short time windows. Cross-reference source IPs against known Nginx exploit distribution vectors.

suggestion.title: Nginx Process Execution via Code Execution Payload
suggestion.rationale: Article title specifies 'Code Execution' capability. No UC addresses post-exploitation command execution from Nginx worker processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes spawned from Nginx worker (nginx -g daemon off or www-data UID) that are not expected (e.g., bash, sh, curl, wget, perl). Flag unexpected outbound connections from Nginx processes.

suggestion.title: Nginx-Induced Denial of Service Traffic Spike
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'DoS' as attack outcome. Pipeline did not surface volumetric or resource-exhaustion detection for Nginx-based DoS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Nginx error logs for connection pool exhaustion, upstream timeouts, or rapid connection churn. Correlate with network metrics: sustained high request rate to single Nginx instance from distributed sources, or internal connection pool saturation (listen queue overflow).

suggestion.title: Nginx Configuration/Memory Corruption Anomaly
suggestion.rationale: Poolslip implies memory safety bug in Nginx connection pooling. No UC targets in-process corruption or segfault signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Nginx worker crashes (segmentation fault, core dump) coinciding with suspicious request patterns in preceding access logs (malformed headers, chunked encoding abuse, oversized payloads). Check dmesg/kernel logs for memory protection violations.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Package Publication from Unusual Geoip or ASN
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights 2FA-gated publishing to prevent unauthorized uploads. Pipeline should have generated detection for publishing activity from locations/networks atypical for the maintainer—'against supply chain attacks' implies threat actors attempt to publish malicious versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm package upload events for deviations in source IP geolocation, ASN, or user-agent consistency vs. historical maintainer behavior. Flag uploads from VPNs, shared hosting, or new geographies with same account during non-business hours.

suggestion.title: Package Version Spike or Dependency Mutation Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks typically inject malicious code into established packages. Pipeline should detect rapid version increments or unexpected new dependencies that differ from baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare package manifests across versions: flag new dependencies not declared in prior versions, unusual bundled scripts, or version increments >3 minor versions in <24h with mismatched changelog.

suggestion.title: Successful Authentication Post-2FA Requirement Enforcement
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 2FA-gating as defense. Detect accounts that bypass or delay 2FA enablement, or logins that complete despite 2FA requirement policy.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for successful publishes or account changes from accounts with 2FA disabled/exempted after organizational policy enforcement date, or successful auth without 2FA challenge completion recorded.

suggestion.title: Reuse of Compromised npm Credentials Across Attacker Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks reuse stolen credentials. Article's 2FA control is preventive; detection should identify credential reuse patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-correlate npm account logins with known attacker infrastructure (C2, malware distribution, phishing domains). Flag accounts authenticating from IPs/domains previously linked to threat intel feeds.

suggestion.title: Installation of Package Versions Not Published by Declared Maintainer
suggestion.rationale: Downstream of package compromise: detect when installed package version's publisher metadata does not match expected maintainer roster or contains new/revoked maintainers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: On install, verify package version's publishing account is in the known maintainer list. Flag installations where publisher was added <7 days prior or is a new account publishing a pre-existing package.

suggestion.title: npm Registry Typosquatting or Namespace Confusion Attempts Post-Enforcement
suggestion.rationale: While 2FA hardens account hijacking, attackers may shift to related packages (typosquats, scoped variants). Detections should capture variant uploads.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for new package uploads with names Levenshtein-close (<2 edits) to popular packages, or scoped/@attacker/popular-lib variants. Cross-reference with domain registration and certificate issuance for corresponding domains.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Package Installation from Laravel-Lang Registry
suggestion.rationale: Article title specifies 'Targets Laravel-Lang Packages' — the supply-chain vector itself. Pipeline failed to generate detection for unauthorized or malicious package installation, which is the initial access mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for composer install/update operations targeting Laravel-Lang packages from non-standard mirrors. Alert on version jumps that bypass lock-file constraints or downloads from untrusted registries.

suggestion.title: Credential Stealer Execution from Installed Dependencies
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'Credential Stealer' payload — pipeline missed detection for credential-access activity triggered by malicious package code execution in development environment contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect spawning of credential-access utilities (vaultcmd, Get-Credential, ssh-keygen) from PHP/composer process context. Alert on access to .ssh/, .aws/, .azure/ directories from vendor/ code paths.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Stolen Development Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealer implies network exfiltration — pipeline failed to generate detection for suspicious outbound connections from development machines transmitting stolen secrets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTPS POST/GET from PHP processes to non-whitelisted external domains carrying base64/gzip-encoded payloads or environment variable data.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated Malware Code in Package Vendor Directory
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attack delivers malicious code inside Laravel package — pipeline should detect suspicious file creation/modification in vendor/laravel-lang-* with obfuscation signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor vendor/ directories for newly created PHP files containing eval(), base64_decode(), or gzip-compressed payloads. Alert on post-installation file modifications outside normal package update windows.

suggestion.title: Package Lock File Tampering or Forced Version Downgrade
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attack implies attacker modified package versioning or lock constraints — pipeline should detect composer.lock manipulation forcing installation of malicious versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected modifications to composer.lock outside scheduled dependency updates. Detect composer update commands on pinned Laravel-Lang packages or lock-file rewrites that bypass version constraints.

suggestion.title: Drupal CVE-2026-9082 Scanner Match
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-9082 — match against your vulnerability scanner' as the baseline hunt. Pipeline generated zero use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when vulnerability scanner reports CVE-2026-9082 against assets running Drupal Core. Correlate with patch status and Federal due date 2026-05-27 to flag remediation lag.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection Patterns Against Drupal Database API
suggestion.rationale: Article names 'specially crafted requests sent with the database abstraction API' as the exploitation method. Pipeline did not surface HTTP/WAF-level injection detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SQL injection syntax (UNION, OR 1=1, SLEEP, hex-encoding) in parameters/POST bodies targeting Drupal query endpoints. Baseline benign admin queries; flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Privilege Escalation Post-SQL Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'could allow for privilege escalation.' Pipeline missed the privilege-escalation phase and privilege-grant anomaly detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SQL UPDATE/INSERT against users, roles, or capability tables. Flag if such queries originate from the database abstraction API or follow SQL-injection-like payloads. Alert on new admin accounts or privilege grants with unusual source IPs.

suggestion.title: Drupal Process RCE Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'remote code execution' as a direct outcome. Pipeline failed to construct detection for RCE activity following privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect spawning of shells, interpreters, or system commands (sh, bash, php -r, system()) from the Drupal web-server process or UID after privilege-escalation indicators. Look for reverse shells and data exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Drupal Core Unpatched Instances Post-Federal Deadline
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and Federal due date 2026-05-27. Pipeline ignored inventory-based patch compliance entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query all Drupal instances for version < [patched]. Cross-reference against 2026-05-27 deadline. Flag any vulnerable instance still in active use post-deadline.

suggestion.title: Spearphishing ZIP with LNK Shortcut Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Cloud Atlas remains consistent in using phishing. In the observed campaigns, the attackers emailed a ZIP archive containing an LNK file as an attachment.' This is the entry point; LNK files executing PowerShell from external URLs should trigger immediate alerts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect ZIP attachments containing .LNK files in email gateways. Alert on LNK shortcut execution (explorer.exe or cmd.exe spawning lnk processing). Correlate with subsequent PowerShell.exe process invocations pointing to external HTTP/HTTPS URLs.

suggestion.title: Remote PowerShell Code Execution via IEX/DownloadString
suggestion.rationale: Article describes LNK files invoking 'PowerShell scripts hosted on external resources' and the first dropped stage (fixed.ps1) executing additional downloads. This multi-stage PowerShell pattern is highly malicious.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PowerShell process creation with network callouts to attacker-controlled domains. Alert on scriptblock logging containing IEX, DownloadString, or wget operations. Correlate parent process (lnk handler) with child PowerShell sessions.

suggestion.title: Registry Run Key Persistence Masquerading as YandexBrowser
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'Creates "Run" registry key "YandexBrowser_setup" for "$temp\fixed.ps1" startup'. This camouflages a PowerShell script startup mechanism using a legitimate software name.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKCU/HKLM \Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run for suspicious values pointing to temp-folder .ps1 files. Flag misspelled app names (YandexBrowser_setup vs YandexBrowser). Cross-correlate with process creation from registry-launched scripts.

suggestion.title: Reverse SSH Tunnel Persistence and C2 Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article documents 'Reverse SSH tunneling' and 'Patched OpenSSH' as active persistence and command channels. Reverse tunnels establish inbound access from external SSH servers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on outbound SSH (port 22 or non-standard ports) from internal hosts to external IPs, especially sustained connections. Monitor for OpenSSH process creation and arguments indicating reverse tunnel setup (-R flag). Flag svchost.exe or suspicious parents spawning SSH.

suggestion.title: Tor Proxy/Tunnel Initialization for Backup C2
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Tor tunneling' is used as a backup control channel. Detection of Tor client execution or traffic to Tor directory authorities indicates secondary C2 activation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DNS queries to Tor directory servers or onion-resolving nameservers. Alert on tor.exe process creation. Monitor for HTTPS traffic tunneled through local SOCKS5 proxies from endpoints not in allow list.

suggestion.title: termsrv.dll Patching for Multi-Session RDP Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Multi-user RDP by patching termsrv.dll'. This in-memory modification bypasses Windows single-session-per-user RDP limits, enabling persistent multi-user backdoor access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file modifications to System32\termsrv.dll (hash mismatch, timestamp anomalies, unsigned patches). Monitor for lsass.exe spawning multiple RDP session handlers concurrently. Alert on successful RDP login attempts when TermService session limit is exceeded.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection Pattern Detection in Drupal Database API Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'allows specially crafted requests to trigger arbitrary SQL injection' and confirms 'exploit attempts are now being detected in the wild.' Detection must occur at initial request stage before injection reaches database.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Drupal core database API endpoints for SQL injection payloads. Alert on requests containing UNION, OR 1=1-like patterns, comment delimiters (-- or /**/) or parameterized query anomalies targeting the abstraction layer.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Unauthorized Query Execution from Web Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability 'allows specially crafted requests to trigger arbitrary SQL injection on sites using PostgreSQL.' Detection at database layer confirms injection execution success.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL query audit logs for suspicious queries executed under the Drupal service account that access sensitive tables (user credentials, admin data, site configuration) or use unexpected SQL constructs inconsistent with application baseline.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Remote Code Execution from Web Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could result in remote code execution.' SQL injection serves as pivot to arbitrary code execution; process-level detection essential for impact mitigation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected child processes spawned from web server processes (apache, nginx, php-fpm) executing system shells or command utilities. Correlate process execution with timing of SQL injection exploit attempts from web logs.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Database Privilege Escalation Post-Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'privilege escalation' as explicit impact. Attackers leverage SQL injection to alter database roles, create superuser accounts, or modify access controls.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL for CREATE USER, ALTER ROLE, GRANT statements executed outside normal administrative workflow. Flag role modifications or privilege grants following suspicious injection-pattern SQL activity.

suggestion.title: Sensitive Data Exfiltration via Injected SELECT Queries
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'information disclosure' as direct impact. Attackers use SQL injection to extract user records, credentials, and configuration data from Drupal database.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL audit logs for SELECT queries accessing high-value tables (user, user_data, admin tables, configuration) executed outside standard application access patterns or returning unexpectedly large result sets.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-9082 Vulnerable Drupal Version Deployment Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies affected versions (Drupal 8.9.x, 10.4.x–10.6.x, 11.0.x–11.3.x). Identify infrastructure still running unpatched versions susceptible to active exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect web servers serving Drupal versions matching the vulnerable ranges (8.9, 10.4–10.6, 11.0–11.3) via response headers, X-Generator tags, or known Drupal URI patterns. Alert on any requests to vulnerable instances.

suggestion.title: Detect Lateral Movement via Dismantled VPN Infrastructure Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article states VPN was 'used by 25 ransomware groups'—a direct C2 and lateral movement enabler. Title establishes active multi-group coordination through the service.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate historical connections to dismantled VPN endpoints with subsequent internal lateral movement (e.g., process execution, SMB shares, RDP). Flag hosts that connected to the VPN 7+ days before the takedown, then show abnormal outbound command activity post-takedown.

suggestion.title: Detect Ransomware C2 Obfuscation via VPN Tunnel Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Title confirms VPN as infrastructure for 25 ransomware groups—primary C2 obfuscation layer. Groups relied on this tunnel for command delivery and data steering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for bursty, recurring connections to VPN endpoints followed within minutes by process spawning (cmd.exe, powershell). Detect anomalous DNS queries originating from VPN-tunnel IPs. Alert on TLS certificates issued to VPN endpoint IPs within last 90 days.

suggestion.title: Monitor Ransomware Group Pivot to Backup C2 Infrastructure Post-Takedown
suggestion.rationale: Global dismantling of shared infrastructure forces 25 groups to relocate. Article states takedown occurred—threat actors will register new VPN/proxy services within days. Detection must proactively identify new attack infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-takedown, flag WHOIS registrations and SSL certificates from historical ransomware-group registrant names or associated email domains. Monitor for new VPN service signups from known threat-actor ASNs. Correlate bulletproof hosting registrations with leaked credential databases for group members.

suggestion.title: Detect High-Volume Data Exfiltration via VPN Tunnels

Prioritize suspicious TLDs (.shop, .online, .info, .store). Alert on clustering of registrations around major tournament event windows with similar name patterns.

Track successful logins shortly after suspicious HTTP activity on management ports (8443, 443).

Flag authentication attempts to Confluence from IP addresses associated with edge appliances or non-user-originating sources within the same timeframe.

suggestion.title: Credential Theft from Confluence

Monitor for ntlmrelayx, responder, or similar tools spawning with network relay parameters.

suggestion.title: Linux Process Execution Anomalies Post-Compromise

Flag parent-child process chains indicating shell injection from network-facing services.

suggestion.title: Confluence Admin Panel Unauthorized Access

Flag password spraying against Confluence default accounts or recently created admin accounts.

suggestion.title: Spear-Phishing Email with Malicious Attachment or Link

Flag messages with .exe, .scr, .zip attachments or shortened/obfuscated links.

suggestion.title: Office Document Macro Execution Post-Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Prometheus phishing campaigns typically deliver weaponized Office documents; no detection logic exists for macro/template injection execution chain.

suggestion.title: Prometheus Malware Command-and-Control Callback

suggestion.title: PowerShell Execution from Suspicious Parent (Phishing Context)

suggestion.title: Ukraine Government Credential Harvesting via Phishing Link

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Compromised Government Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Post-phishing credential theft enables lateral movement in government networks; no detection hypothesis for intra-network reconnaissance or privilege escalation.

suggestion.title: YesWiki FormManager SQLi Payload Pattern — UNION/Comment Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'inject arbitrary SQL into an INSERT statement'; UNION-based and comment-based SQLi are standard extraction techniques. Pipeline did not generate payload-pattern detection despite describing SQL injection directly.
