suggestion.rationale: Article states 'inject arbitrary SQL into an INSERT statement.' Blind SQLi extraction loops (as described: 'extraction loop') require iterative requests with error or timing feedback. SQL syntax errors, database exceptions, or response time anomalies would surface in HTTP logs and WAF logs during exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor requests to BazaR/formulaire endpoint for 5xx error responses (500, 502, 503) or response bodies containing SQL error strings ('syntax error', 'database error', 'UNION SELECT', 'MySQL error'). Correlate with high-frequency requests to the same endpoint within short time window, indicating SQLi feedback-driven data extraction.

suggestion.title: High-volume UNION SELECT or time-based payload variants to Bazar form-import — CVE-2026-46670 blind SQLi techniques
suggestion.rationale: Blind SQLi extraction requires either UNION-based or time-based SQL payloads. Article describes 'extraction loop' but doesn't specify technique. Detection should look for characteristic injection patterns: UNION SELECT, SLEEP(), BENCHMARK(), IF() conditionals in POST parameters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse POST bodies to BazaR/formulaire endpoint and flag requests containing SQL keywords/functions in parameter values: UNION, SELECT, SLEEP, BENCHMARK, IF, OR 1=1, comment sequences (--), stacked queries. Correlate with response timing anomalies or repeated requests with incrementally modified payloads.

suggestion.title: Bulk retrieval of yeswiki_users table via database query anomaly — CVE-2026-46670 password hash exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states end goal: 'read the full database, including yeswiki_users.password hashes.' Database query logs would show unusual SELECT patterns on the users table during exploitation. Detection gaps at the database layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor MySQL query logs for SELECT * FROM yeswiki_users or full-column password hash retrieval from authenticated YesWiki application context, especially queries containing UNION, time-based conditionals, or batch retrieval syntax. Flag queries that extract the password column en masse.

suggestion.title: YesWiki version identification and vulnerable version enumeration — CVE-2026-46670 asset inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies affected versions: 4.6.1, 4.6.2, doryphore-dev. Organizations must first identify vulnerable instances. Version disclosure may appear in HTTP headers, Generator meta tags, or default documentation paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan or monitor for HTTP responses from YesWiki instances revealing version strings in headers (Server, X-Powered-By, etc.), meta tags (Generator), or README/version files at default paths. Flag version strings matching 4.6.1, 4.6.2, or branch identifiers containing 'doryphore'.

suggestion.title: POST parameter probing on Bazar form-import endpoint — CVE-2026-46670 injection point discovery
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation begins with discovering which form parameters are vulnerable. Before SQLi payload injection, attacker would probe parameters with special characters or modified values to identify the injection point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sequences of POST requests to BazaR/formulaire endpoint within short time window with incrementally modified parameter names or values—especially those containing SQL metacharacters (quotes, parentheses, SQL keywords), malformed payloads, or null/empty values. Pattern indicates fuzzing for vulnerable parameter.

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing from Telecom Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly describes 'command-and-control operations.' Pipeline should flag outbound C2 patterns (beaconing, DNS tunneling, HTTP POST callbacks) originating from telecom provider networks or compromised telecom customer accounts. Article phrase: 'large-scale command-and-control operations.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalous outbound connections from telecom infrastructure (AS/BGP anomalies, infrastructure-level egress) to known or suspected C2 domains. Baseline expected services (BGP route updates, peering traffic) and alert on deviations. Correlate with internal DNS queries to external C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Telecom Network Infrastructure Unauthorized Access
suggestion.rationale: Attackers must first compromise telecom systems before establishing C2. Title references 'abuse' of networks, implying prior unauthorized access. Missing detection for lateral movement or privilege escalation within ISP/telecom admin consoles. Article phrase: 'Hackers Abuse Middle East Telecom Networks.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous logins to telecom provider admin portals (unusual geolocation, off-hours, impossible travel), exploitation of telecom-specific management interfaces (OSS/BSS), and lateral movement to network operations centers. Flag RDP/SSH access patterns inconsistent with normal telecom operations staff behavior.

suggestion.title: Large-Scale Bot Activation and Coordination
suggestion.rationale: Description of 'large-scale operations' implies botnet deployment or mass account compromise. Pipeline should detect batch activation or synchronized beacon events across multiple telecom customer accounts or infrastructure segments. Article phrase: 'large-scale command-and-control operations.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on clustered process execution patterns (same malware hash, same parent process) across multiple telecom infrastructure endpoints in narrow time window. Monitor scheduled task creation in batch across multiple systems. Correlate execution with newly observed network connections.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration from Telecom Provider Networks
suggestion.rationale: C2 infrastructure abuse typically enables data theft from target organizations. Telecom networks hold sensitive customer records, call metadata, and billing data. Pipeline should flag exfiltration patterns from network perimeter. Article phrase: Title indicates operational success, implying data collection and exfil as end goal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual egress volume from telecom infrastructure to non-whitelisted external IPs. Alert on protocols typically used for exfil (raw sockets, DNS tunneling, ICMP tunneling). Correlate with large internal data access patterns (database queries, file system enumeration) on sensitive systems.

suggestion.title: Telecom Management Interface Persistence Mechanisms
suggestion.rationale: Attackers maintaining 'large-scale' operations require persistent backdoor access. Missing detection for webshells, account creation, or credential harvesting in telecom OSS/BSS systems. Article phrase: Sustained operations imply persistence established.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor telecom management interfaces for new service account creation, privileged group membership changes, and unexpected file writes to web application directories. Alert on failed authentication followed by success to same account within minutes (credential stuffing). Track changes to firewall rules and access control lists in ISP infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Suspicious BGP/DNS Infrastructure Modifications
suggestion.rationale: Leveraging telecom networks for C2 may involve DNS hijacking, BGP announcement manipulation, or MITM positioning at ISP level. Pipeline should flag infrastructure-level control indicators. Article phrase: 'Abuse of telecom networks' suggests control over routing or DNS services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthorized BGP route announcements or withdrawals from telecom ASNs. Alert on DNS SOA/NS record modifications for customer or internal domains hosted on telecom nameservers. Correlate with DNSSEC validation failures or unexpected DNS delegation changes.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Post-Install Script Execution from npm Package
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states 'backdoor' of npm package; post-install hooks are the canonical supply-chain attack vector in Node.js ecosystems. Article mentions 'launch[ing]' attacks, implying active code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor child processes spawned by npm/yarn install or node_modules/.bin/ executables, especially those communicating over the network or accessing sensitive system resources. Unusual parent-child process relationships (npm → curl, wget, powershell) are high-confidence indicators.

suggestion.title: Network Exfiltration from npm Package Installation Context
suggestion.rationale: Watering-hole attacks require command-and-control communication. Article title mentions 'launch[ing] attacks' but no C2 infrastructure is extracted; pipeline should detect outbound traffic from package manager or node_modules context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag DNS queries or TCP/UDP connections initiated by npm, node, or processes spawned during package installation to non-standard domains or IP addresses outside internal infrastructure. Establish baseline of legitimate registry endpoints (registry.npmjs.org, etc.) and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Compromised npm Package Detection via Manifest Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks often modify package.json or introduce unexpected dependencies. Pipeline should detect packages with sudden dependency inflation, new maintainers, or version bumps with suspicious code changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package.json file modifications during npm install, or compare installed package hashes against public npm registry. Alert on version downgrades or unsigned package installs.

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance Activity from npm-Installed Malware
suggestion.rationale: Watering-hole attacks typically enumerate system/environment before exfiltration. Article mentions 'attacks' but no reconnaissance phase is mapped. Post-install payloads often call whoami, uname, env, etc.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect system discovery commands (whoami, uname -a, env, systeminfo) spawned in the context of node_modules or npm install. High-confidence indicator if these are chained together within seconds.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Modifications to Global npm Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Backdoored packages may alter .npmrc or npm config to persist or redirect future installs. Pipeline missed this lateral persistence vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor writes to ~/.npmrc, /etc/npm*, or node global config paths. Alert on unexpected registry URL changes, new authentication tokens, or post-install script additions.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email with Invoice-Themed Attachment
suggestion.rationale: Article states hackers use 'NF-e Invoice Lures' as initial vector but no phishing detection rule was generated. Absent from both IOCs and use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect inbound emails with NF-e, invoice, or fiscal-themed subjects containing .bat, .cmd, .vbs, or password-protected Office attachments. Correlate with employee profile (Brazilian-region focus likely). Alert on rapid attachment extraction to temp directories.

suggestion.title: Malicious Batch File Execution from Email Temp Path
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Malicious Batch Files' as delivery mechanism. No execution-phase detection exists despite this being the critical handoff point from initial access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor .bat/.cmd execution originating from email client temp folders (%TEMP%, Downloads, Outlook cache). Flag execution within 2 minutes of file creation. Alert on batch files invoking cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or wscript with Base64 or escaped-character encoding.

suggestion.title: Banana RAT Malware Artifact Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title names 'Banana RAT' explicitly but zero malware-specific IOCs (hashes, file paths, registry keys, C2 domains) were extracted. Pipeline failure to surface this key indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest known Banana RAT file hashes, behavioral signatures (registry persistence keys, mutex names, C2 port patterns). Detect Banana RAT process execution chain: batch → cmd/PowerShell → injected child process with command-line obfuscation or DLL side-loading.

suggestion.title: Batch-to-PowerShell Execution Chain
suggestion.rationale: Batch files frequently leverage PowerShell for payload execution; no chaining detection created despite being standard malware pattern and directly implied by 'batch file' delivery mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cmd.exe or batch file spawning powershell.exe with suspicious arguments: -encodedcommand, -enc, IEX, FromBase64, -NoProfile, -Hidden, or -WindowStyle Hidden. Alert if parent process chain includes .bat file and command contains obfuscation or remote download (http, ftp, \\\).

suggestion.title: RAT Command & Control Session Detection
suggestion.rationale: Banana RAT by definition establishes persistent C2. No network or behavioral detection use case was generated to identify C2 callback or command execution, leaving post-execution phases unmonitored.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound connections from newly spawned processes to external IPs (especially Brazil-hosted infrastructure or VPS providers) on non-standard ports (>10000). Detect failed DNS resolutions followed by direct IP connection. Correlate with process creation time and suspicious parent batch/PowerShell execution.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PHP File Creation in FreePBX Web Root
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'six-layer persistence'; web shells are standard persistence mechanisms in VoIP appliances. Expected to see detection of .php files written to /var/www/html or /opt/freepbx directories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PHP file creation or modification in FreePBX web-accessible directories. Trigger on .php files written by www-data or asterisk user to /var/www/html, /opt/freepbx, or /var/www/freepbx with low historical frequency. Exclude legitimate patch updates and admin changes.

suggestion.title: Scheduled Task Persistence via Cron Entries
suggestion.rationale: Multi-layer persistence strategies typically include cron jobs for command execution. Article states 'six-layer' implying multiple redundant mechanisms; cron is a standard layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect new or modified crontab entries for asterisk, www-data, or root users. Watch for crontab -e commands, writes to /etc/cron.* directories, or execution of crontab with suspicious arguments. Baseline normal cron activity and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: FreePBX Database Persistence via Authentication Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Phrase 'six-layer' implies non-filesystem persistence. FreePBX uses MySQL/MariaDB; attackers typically insert backdoor admin accounts or modify authentication stored procs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for modifications to FreePBX database files (/var/lib/mysql/ or /opt/freepbx/asteriskdb*) or direct mysql/mariadb command execution with DDL/DML statements. Alert on ALTER USER or INSERT into credentials tables. Correlate with infrequent database access patterns.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PHP Include Path Configuration Modification
suggestion.rationale: Persistent code injection via auto_prepend_file or auto_append_file in php.ini is a stealth persistence mechanism. Article's 'six-layer' suggests defense evasion via configuration tampering.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for modifications to /etc/php.ini, /etc/php/*/apache2/php.ini, or /opt/freepbx php configuration files. Specifically watch for changes to auto_prepend_file or auto_append_file directives. Baseline the hash of php.ini and alert on unexpected changes.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized System Command Execution from FreePBX Process Context
suggestion.rationale: Six-layer persistence implies execution capability for maintaining access. FreePBX compromises typically spawn reverse shells or execute malicious payloads from asterisk/www-data context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect shell command execution (bash, sh, nc, curl, wget) spawned from asterisk, www-data, or other FreePBX-associated processes. Flag process creation with parent PID pointing to httpd, php-fpm, or asterisk. Alert on network-based payloads (curl/wget) or reverse shells (nc/bash -i).

suggestion.title: Configuration File Tampering on FreePBX System
suggestion.rationale: Persistence across reboot requires configuration modifications. Article title emphasizes 'maintain access', implying changes to FreePBX config files that survive service restarts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for writes to FreePBX configuration files: /etc/asterisk/*, /opt/freepbx/etc/*, or /etc/freepbx.conf. Alert on modifications outside maintenance windows. Compare file hashes against known-good baselines. Flag additions to modules_additional.conf or similar extension-loading configuration.

suggestion.title: Detect DDoS Botnet C2 Communication Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article title references 'Kimwolf DDoS Botnet' and 'DDoS-for-Hire' operations—indicates active C2 infrastructure and command distribution. Pipeline extracted zero detection use cases for C2 traffic despite this being primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound DNS queries and HTTP/HTTPS connections from internal hosts to known Kimwolf C2 domains or to IPs associated with botnet infrastructure. Detect repeated beaconing on non-standard ports (UDP floods, icmp-based signaling). Look for anomalous traffic volumes from single hosts indicating botnet participant activity.

suggestion.title: Identify Compromised Hosts Participating in DDoS Botnet
suggestion.rationale: A DDoS-for-hire botnet requires infected hosts executing commands. Article mentions 'botnet operator'—pipeline should surface detection for process execution, network reconnaissance, and resource exhaustion consistent with bot malware.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious child processes spawned from unusual parents (wscript, rundll32, powershell) that establish outbound connections to multiple external IPs in short timeframe. Alert on processes consuming abnormal CPU/memory consistent with DDoS packet generation or socket flooding.

suggestion.title: Monitor for DDoS-for-Hire Service Recruitment & Payment Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'DDoS-for-hire attacks'—this is a criminal service. Should detect underground forum activity, cryptocurrency transactions, or messaging platform recruitment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag access to known underground marketplaces, Telegram/Discord DDoS-for-hire channels, or cryptocurrency wallets linked to Kimwolf operations. Monitor for inbound recruiting messages offering payment for botnet participation or attack targets.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Driver Load - Suspicious Integrity Level Execution
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD attacks hinge on loading known-vulnerable drivers (e.g., RTCore64.sys, GdrBypass.sys) to achieve kernel code execution and bypass EDR. No detection use case generated despite this being the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for loading of known-vulnerable drivers by low-privilege processes. Flag unsigned or self-signed driver loads followed by privilege escalation. Correlate with known BYOVD driver hash lists (RTCore64.sys, GdrBypass, Rohitabs.sys, etc.).

suggestion.title: Direct Kernel Object Manipulation (DKOM) via Vulnerable Driver
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD exploits use legitimate drivers to write arbitrary kernel memory, modifying security descriptors and token privileges. This is the exploitation phase but was not mapped to any detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect system processes (System, svchost) spawning child processes with unexpected privilege tokens. Monitor for privilege attribute token modifications in kernel events. Flag suspicious Read/WriteFile operations to /proc/mem or similar kernel memory interfaces from user-mode processes.

suggestion.title: EDR/Security Software Termination via Vulnerable Driver
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD attacks frequently use loaded drivers to disable kernel callbacks, terminate EDR agents, and patch security software in-memory. No detection for process termination or service disabling was suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes terminating security software (defender, Sentinel One, CrowdStrike) immediately following or correlated with vulnerable driver loads. Flag unexpected service stop/disable for security services. Monitor for process access attempts to security product binaries.

suggestion.title: Unsigned Driver Load in System32 or Driver Cache
suggestion.rationale: Attackers stage BYOVD drivers in standard Windows driver directories or load them via vulnerable deployment mechanisms. The article likely describes staging methods not captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation of .sys files in C:\Windows\System32\drivers or C:\Windows\drivers\etc with anomalous signing status. Monitor driver registry hives (HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services) for new entries with unsigned ImagePath references. Baseline signed drivers and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: Kernel Callback Removal Detection via Performance Counter Analysis
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation, BYOVD attacks disable kernel-mode security callbacks. Absence of expected PsSetCreateProcessNotifyRoutine callbacks may indicate successful driver-based defense evasion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for missing or disabled kernel callback routines post-driver load. Track Expected vs. Actual callback registrations. Flag drivers that unregister PsSetCreateProcessNotifyRoutine or PsSetImageNotifyRoutine without corresponding system shutdown.

suggestion.title: Detect mass GitHub workflow file creation/modification across repos
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'malicious CI/CD workflows' targeting 5,561 repos; indicates coordinated workflow injection attack requiring detection of unusual .github/workflows/* write activity.
log_sources: identity logs for GitHub credential usage
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation or modification of YAML workflow files (.github/workflows/*.yml) at scale across multiple repos in short time window by single principal. Flag repos with no prior workflow history suddenly acquiring CI/CD definitions. Correlate with credential usage anomalies.

suggestion.title: Detect credential compromise via GitHub API token exfiltration in CI/CD logs
suggestion.rationale: CI/CD compromise typically involves stealing secrets/tokens from runners or environment; 'malicious workflows' likely executed arbitrary code that leaked credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor CI/CD job logs for base64-encoded secrets, token patterns, or explicit exfiltration commands (curl/wget with Bearer tokens). Detect GitHub Actions default secrets ($GITHUB_TOKEN) being written to logs or exported to external endpoints.

suggestion.title: Detect repository fork/clone spam from compromised principal
suggestion.rationale: Coordinated attack on 5,561 repos suggests either compromised GitHub account with broad access or malicious GitHub App; behavioral anomaly of cloning/forking at industrial scale.
log_sources: network logs for git clone/fetch activity
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect single GitHub user/token initiating 10+ repository fork or clone operations within 1 hour. Flag API calls to repos across unrelated organizations. Correlate IP geolocation changes with activity spikes.

suggestion.title: Detect artifact poisoning via CI/CD build output manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Attack described as targeting repos via CI/CD workflows; supply-chain angle suggests attackers injecting malicious code into build artifacts (Docker images, npm packages, compiled binaries).
log_sources: package registry logs (npm, PyPI, Docker Hub)
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor build job output for unexpected artifact uploads post-workflow execution. Detect commits to artifact registries (npm publish, docker push) from newly created CI/CD jobs with suspicious names. Correlate artifact publish events with workflow creation timestamps.

suggestion.title: Detect GitHub Actions execution from unexpected compute context
suggestion.rationale: Malicious workflows executed; standard supply-chain attack pattern involves runner hijacking to execute attacker code, often from compromised/rogue runners.
log_sources: process execution logs from CI runners
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect CI/CD job execution initiated by user principal with no code contribution history in target repo. Flag jobs labeled as 'on: workflow_dispatch' (manual trigger) initiated by non-maintainers. Monitor for shell script injection via untrusted interpolation of GitHub context variables.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Workflow Modified to Exfiltrate Secrets
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Secret Exfiltration' via GitHub Actions. Core attack: malicious steps added to workflows to steal and transmit GITHUB_TOKEN, repository secrets, or API keys. Pipeline must detect workflow write followed by credential access and outbound exfil.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag GitHub Actions workflows that access secrets (env vars, GITHUB_TOKEN) and immediately execute curl/wget/POST commands to non-GitHub domains, especially if the exfiltration step is injected into existing workflows without documented business justification.

suggestion.title: Bulk Workflow Injection Across Multiple Public Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Article: '5,500+ public repositories' affected. Detection gap: pipeline-wide pattern of malicious workflow commits pushed to many repos in short window indicates supply-chain or mass-compromise. Must correlate workflow edits across repo boundaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when malicious workflow YAML (with curl/exfil patterns) is committed to 10+ repositories within 24 hours, especially if originating from newly created accounts, compromised tokens, or forked repos. Baseline typical workflow push velocity per actor.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Runner Initiates Outbound C2 After Secret Access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exfiltration as outcome. Detection must link credential access in runner context to outbound network connections—the actual data movement that completes the kill chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTP/S POST or DNS from GitHub Actions runner IPs to external domains immediately following access to $GITHUB_TOKEN or secrets within workflow logs. Flag base64-encoded credential-length strings in request bodies.

suggestion.title: GitHub Token Extracted via Echo or Debug Commands in Actions
suggestion.rationale: Common GitHub Actions exfil technique: workflow step echoes or exports GITHUB_TOKEN unmasked to runner output, then transmits via curl. Article describes secrets theft—must catch the extraction step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions job logs for commands that reference or output $GITHUB_TOKEN, $SECRETS, or secrets() function without legitimate masking. Flag workflows that base64-encode or URL-encode secrets for transmission.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Third-Party GitHub Action Injected into Public Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Initial vector likely: dependency on malicious action (uses clause pointing to attacker-controlled action repo). Article: 5,500+ repos suggests coordinated supply-chain compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect introduction of actions from newly created or rarely-used GitHub Action repositories into workflows, especially when action requests secrets permissions, executes shell steps, or modifies system configurations. Correlate action additions across multiple repos.

suggestion.title: GitHub Secret Accessed Immediately After Workflow Trigger in High-Volume Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article: mass campaign. Attacker likely automates secret theft across many repos. Detection: alert on abnormal secret access frequency and timing within Actions context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag workflows where secrets are accessed within the first 30 seconds of job execution, or where secrets access frequency spikes globally (many repos accessing secrets simultaneously). Correlate with outbound network connections.

suggestion.title: RoleMember privilege escalation via /api/v1/cron endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Core vulnerability surface: 'RoleMember can run shell on every server...via POST /api/v1/cron' with 'per-server permission check on cron creation has a vacuous-true bypass'. Requires detection at API request time, pre-exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST/PATCH requests to /api/v1/cron and /api/v1/cron/:id from authenticated sessions. Alert if requester's role field == 1 (RoleMember) or account lacks admin privilege. Correlate with 200-range HTTP response to confirm exploitation succeeded.

suggestion.title: Cron task creation with CronCoverAll flag and empty server scope
suggestion.rationale: Attack-specific exploitation signature from article: 'create a scheduled cron task with...empty servers...CronCoverAll'. Empty servers array + cover flag=1/true is the exploitation primitive enabling cross-tenant RCE.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect JSON request bodies of POST /api/v1/cron. Flag payloads containing 'servers':[] (empty array) OR servers:null combined with 'cover':1 or cover:true. This signature indicates attacker intent to bypass per-server permission checks.

suggestion.title: Cron-scheduled command execution on out-of-tenant servers
suggestion.rationale: Article repeatedly emphasizes 'cross-tenant RCE' as unique threat. Need post-exploitation detection: cron task executes on servers outside the creator's authorized tenant/scope.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate API logs (cron task creation, creator tenant_id) with execution evidence (nezha-agent logs, command invocation). Alert if command executes on server whose tenant_id differs from task creator's tenant, or server not in creator's scope whitelist.

suggestion.title: API endpoint access control bypass: admin routes callable by non-admin role
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability root cause: 'cron routes...wired through commonHandler (any authenticated user) rather than adminHandler'. RoleMember (role==1) should not reach admin-only endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor API access logs including user role/privilege metadata. Build baseline of legitimate role-to-endpoint pairings (role==0 for admin endpoints). Alert on role==1 requests to /api/v1/cron*, /api/v1/admin*, or other admin-gated paths.

suggestion.title: GitHub Repository Unexpected Code Modification by Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly states '700 GitHub Repos' were hacked and packages modified. The pipeline missed the core attack vector: unauthorized code commits to trusted repositories. No detection logic was created for anomalous commits or branch modifications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for commits to package/library repositories from unusual source IPs, at unusual times, or by users who don't typically contribute to those specific repos. Flag commits that bypass code review or merge directly to main/production branches. Cross-reference with known VCS credential compromise incidents.

suggestion.title: Package Integrity Verification Failure During Dependency Resolution
suggestion.rationale: Article states '233 versions' of Laravel-Lang were compromised. Downstream developers pulling packages should detect mismatches between expected hashes, signature validation failures, or unexpected content in downloaded artifacts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when package hash validation fails, GPG signature verification fails, or package content inspection tools (SBOM comparison, static analysis) detect previously-unseen code in a 'trusted' package version. Correlate against package maintainer security advisories.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Commits to Language Pack or Localization Libraries
suggestion.rationale: Laravel-Lang is a localization/language package library. The attack modified legitimate packages. Detection should flag commits to language/localization repos that introduce code outside the expected scope (non-translation strings, executable code, shell commands).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parse commits to language/translation package repos and flag those containing unexpected file types, binary content, or code patterns (eval, exec, system calls, network connections) inconsistent with translation/localization libraries. Use AST analysis or regex to detect obfuscated payloads.

suggestion.title: Wholesale Package Version Release without Corresponding Source Code Push
suggestion.rationale: The headline notes 233 compromised versions. A version bump followed by a package publish (e.g., to Packagist, PyPI) without corresponding visible git commits or tags is a strong supply chain compromise indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference package registry push logs with git commit/tag timestamps. Alert when a new package version is published to Packagist/PyPI but no corresponding git tag, release note, or code commit appears in the source repository within a reasonable window (e.g., 1 hour). Flag rapid version bumps on mature packages.

suggestion.title: Compromised GitHub OAuth Token or Session Detected by Unusual Account Activity
suggestion.rationale: Attackers hacked 700 repos to inject code into Laravel-Lang packages. This implies credential compromise (stolen tokens, compromised SSH keys, or session hijacking). The pipeline missed credential-access and initial-access mechanics entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub personal access tokens and deploy keys for: logins from unexpected geographies, bulk repository access patterns inconsistent with user's typical workflow, commits via API from non-standard user agents, or tokens used across unrelated projects. Correlate with password spray/phishing incidents.

suggestion.title: F5 BIG-IP Vulnerability Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Hackers Exploit F5 BIG-IP Appliance'—initial_access phase completely undetected by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor F5 BIG-IP appliances for exploitation patterns: HTTP requests to vulnerable management endpoints (/mgmt/, /icr/), unusual HTTP status sequences (404→200), or authentication bypass indicators. Correlate with system error logs for code execution side-effects.

suggestion.title: SSH Key Installation from Compromised BIG-IP
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Gain SSH Access'—persistence mechanism (SSH credential theft or key planting) has no corresponding detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthorized modification of SSH authorized_keys files on Linux hosts when source is F5 BIG-IP internal IP. Flag SSH key generation or export operations logged on BIG-IP appliance. Monitor for new SSH user accounts or shell spawning on appliance.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via SSH from Network Appliance
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Pivot Into Enterprise Linux Networks'—lateral movement from compromised appliance to internal Linux infrastructure undetected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SSH connections originating from F5 BIG-IP appliance IPs to internal Linux hosts on port 22. Flag connection velocity spikes (many targets in short window) or authentication failures followed by success. Alert on SSH sessions from appliance source using non-standard or service-account credentials.

suggestion.title: Command Execution on F5 BIG-IP Appliance
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation implies code execution; article body too corrupted to verify specifics, but pipeline failed to generate execution-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor BIG-IP for unexpected shell processes (bash, sh, perl) spawned by httpd, web service, or privileged daemons. Detect cron job or scheduled task creation. Flag execution from temp directories (/tmp/, /var/tmp/) or world-writable paths.

suggestion.title: Credential Enumeration Against Enterprise Linux Hosts
suggestion.rationale: Pivoting to multiple Linux systems requires credential discovery; no use case for brute-force, password-spray, or credential-file access from compromised appliance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect failed SSH login spikes from BIG-IP source IPs across multiple target hosts or accounts (password spray pattern). Monitor Linux systems for rapid authentication failures from single source. Flag SSH connection attempts using common wordlists or sequential account names.

suggestion.title: Composer Autoload Execution - Malicious helpers.php Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states malicious 'src/helpers.php' was 'automatically loaded by Composer' and 'appears in autoload section of composer.json.' This is the execution mechanism but no detection use case generated for Composer-triggered arbitrary file loading.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Composer process execution for subsequent file operations in src/ directory immediately after package install/update, particularly src/helpers.php. Establish baseline for expected helpers.php modifications per repository and alert on unexpected content changes or file execution patterns diverging from legitimate package behaviors.

suggestion.title: PHP Dropper C2 Communication to flipboxstudio[.]info
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'injected code acted as a dropper that downloaded a second payload from the attacker's command and control server at flipboxstudio[.]info.' No detection use case for PHP initiating network communication to attacker-controlled C2.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP or web server processes resolving flipboxstudio[.]info or performing HTTP requests to that domain. Flag unexpected outbound HTTPS/HTTP initiated by PHP processes in development/CI/CD environments not matching legitimate package manager traffic patterns. Correlate with Composer process spawning within preceding 5-minute window.

suggestion.title: Multi-Source Credential Harvesting - .env, SSH, Cloud, Kubernetes, Vault Access
suggestion.rationale: Payload 'harvests cloud credentials, Kubernetes secrets, Vault tokens, Git credentials, CI/CD secrets, SSH keys, browser data, cryptocurrency wallets, password managers, VPN configurations, and local `.env` configuration files.' No detection for suspicious bulk credential store enumeration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on processes accessing multiple credential repositories within short timespan: ~/.ssh/ keys, ~/.aws/ credentials, ~/.kube/ config, ~/.env files, browser profile credential stores, Vault/LastPass/1Password config directories, and CI/CD environment variable access. Establish per-host baselines and trigger on unusual credential store access velocity.

suggestion.title: Windows DebugElevator - Base64 Executable Extraction and TEMP Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'extracted a base64-encoded executable... which is written to the %TEMP% folder as a random .exe filename, and then launched.' Two-stage PHP-to-binary infection pattern with no detection use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP/Composer processes writing random-named .exe files to %TEMP% directory followed by immediate child process execution. Alert on base64 decoding operations within PHP context outputting executable files. Monitor for DebugElevator-specific process signatures accessing Chrome/Edge/Brave profile paths with DPAPI-related Registry access.

suggestion.title: Chromium Browser Credential Extraction via App-Bound Encryption Key Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states Windows infostealer 'designed to target Chrome, Brave, and Edge, and extract App-Bound Encryption keys needed to decrypt stored browser credentials.' No detection use case for Chromium browser-specific credential theft attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on non-browser processes accessing Chromium user profile Local State files, Cookies database, or Login Data stores. Flag Registry access to Chrome encryption keys (HKCU registry paths for Chromium-based browsers). Monitor for DPAPI decryption requests correlating with browser profile directory access from suspicious parent processes.

suggestion.title: GitHub Repository Tag Integrity - Unexpected Mass Tag Rewrites
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes attack mechanism: 'attackers abused GitHub version tags' and 'rewrote every existing git tag in each repository to point at a new malicious commit.' Supply chain attack vector uses tag manipulation, not code commits, requiring specific detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub org audit logs for unexpected tag force-push operations, particularly bulk tag rewrites within short time window (article shows 22:32-00:00 UTC across four repos). Alert on tags modified to point to commits in fork repositories or commits authored by unfamiliar GitHub accounts. Flag deviations from established Laravel Lang tag maintenance patterns.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Install of Compromised Laravel-Lang Package Version
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Laravel-Lang PHP Packages Compromised'—pipeline should detect package manager activity installing malicious versions. Cite: 'Laravel-Lang PHP Packages Compromised'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PHP package managers (composer, npm if polyglot) for installation of Laravel-Lang packages from untrusted or unexpected sources. Detect unusual package versions, off-schedule updates, or installs from fork/alternate registries. Windows: monitor Composer/vendor directory writes; Linux: /vendor/ path creation outside expected deployment.

suggestion.title: Cross-Platform Credential Stealer Process Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title identifies 'Cross-Platform Credential Stealer'—malware must execute on compromised hosts. Pipeline missed execution-phase detection. Cite: 'Deliver Cross-Platform Credential Stealer'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect abnormal spawning of credential harvesting tools post-package installation: env dumping (env, printenv), credential manager queries (cmdkey, security find-generic-password), SSH key access (cat ~/.ssh/id_rsa), browser password store queries. Look for execution chains where PHP/Composer process spawns shell commands outside normal application behavior.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration from Compromised Credential Stealer
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealer payload must exfiltrate stolen data; article states 'credential stealer' implying command & control or data ex-filtration. Pipeline found no C2 or network IOCs. Cite: 'Deliver Cross-Platform Credential Stealer'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor egress traffic immediately following Laravel-Lang package installation. Detect HTTP/HTTPS POST requests from PHP application processes to unexpected domains, unusual DNS lookups for subdomain enumeration or DGA patterns, encrypted tunnel establishment (stunnel, socat) spawned by PHP workers. Baseline normal Laravel-Lang vendor communication.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Compromised Vendor/Autoload Chain
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromise persistence often achieved via vendor/autoload.php or composer hooks—pipeline missed persistence techniques. Cite: 'Laravel-Lang PHP Packages Compromised' implies code execution at autoload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unauthorized modifications to vendor/autoload.php, vendor/composer/InstalledVersions.php, or Laravel-Lang package files post-installation. Detect execution of previously unmodified vendor PHP files, especially those loaded before application bootstrap. Compare file hashes against known-good package manifests.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Repository Lateral Access or Typosquatting Detection
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline should detect how compromised packages entered supply chain—typosquatting, account takeover, or repo mirror compromise. Title suggests package-level compromise but no detection for repository anomalies. Cite: 'Laravel-Lang PHP Packages Compromised'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference install logs against Packagist/composer repo metadata for package checksums and publish timestamps. Detect sudden source changes (fork URLs in composer.lock), version downgrades, or installs from unmirrored registries. Monitor Packagist/GitHub package maintainer account access for geographical/timing anomalies.

suggestion.title: Poisoned Package Version Resolution from Fork Repository
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'Packagist then ingested those tags and treated the fork commits as genuine releases' and 'a Git tag created within an organization can resolve to a commit in a fork outside that organization.' Core initial compromise mechanism completely undetected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Composer/pip/npm package resolution for cases where dependency tags resolve to commits outside official organization repositories. Alert when package manager metadata indicates version sourced from fork or attacker-controlled namespace. Track composer.lock and package-lock.json changes pointing to non-canonical sources.

suggestion.title: Malicious Autoload File Execution in Composer Vendor Chain
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'The payload was hidden in a newly added file, src/helpers.php, and registered in composer.json under autoload.files. Composer's autoloader unconditionally requires every file in that list, so the malicious code runs at the very start of the PHP request lifecycle.' Execution mechanism requires dedicated detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PHP file execution from vendor/laravel-lang/* directories, specifically src/helpers.php. Detect when vendor/autoload.php loads files unexpectedly or from attacker-controlled packages during application initialization. Alert on process spawning from PHP executed via web server context immediately after vendor includes.

suggestion.title: Outbound C2 Connections to flipboxstudio[.]info Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies specific domains: 'fetches a second stage from https://flipboxstudio[.]info/payload and executes it' and 'Collected data is encrypted and shipped out to https://flipboxstudio[.]info/exfil.' Direct IOC-based detection required.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any outbound HTTPS connections to flipboxstudio[.]info, particularly to /payload or /exfil endpoints. Monitor DNS queries for flipboxstudio[.]info resolution. Flag PHP or Apache/Nginx processes initiating these connections. Correlate with preceding events showing PHP execution from vendor directories.

suggestion.title: Systematic Multi-Category Credential Material Collection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes comprehensive credential harvesting: 'walks through a long list of sources... Cloud provider credentials (AWS, GCP, Azure)... Kubernetes kubeconfig files, HashiCorp Vault tokens, and CI/CD secrets... SSH private keys... .env files... Browser data... Password manager vaults... Cryptocurrency wallet files... Messaging and collaboration tokens.' Requires multi-technique detection strategy.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for single processes reading multiple credential source categories: ~/.ssh/*, ~/.kube/config, ~/.aws/*, ~/.vault*, KUBECONFIG environment, %LOCALAPPDATA%/Google/Chrome/*, %APPDATA%/Roaming/Slack/, browser password stores, Ethereum wallets, .env files in application roots. Alert when access to 3+ distinct credential categories occurs within minutes.

suggestion.title: Post-Exfiltration Forensic Artifact Cleanup
suggestion.rationale: Article notes: 'After exfiltration, the stealer attempts to delete its dropped files to slow down forensic recovery. On Windows hosts, the chain [truncated].' Cleanup behavior correlates with prior exfiltration and warrants anti-forensics detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for file deletion events following credential collection and outbound exfiltration. Alert on deletion chains targeting temporary directories (/tmp, %TEMP%), dropped second-stage files, or payload staging areas. Correlate file deletions with prior network egress to C2 within 60-second windows.

suggestion.title: Platform-Aware Stealer Execution Across Linux, macOS, and Windows
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'The launcher logic is platform-aware and works on Linux, macOS, and Windows.' Multi-OS payload deployment and execution requires platform-specific detection signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PHP spawning platform-native shells (bash on Linux/macOS, powershell/cmd on Windows) from web application contexts. Detect unusual binary execution in /tmp, /var/tmp, %TEMP%, or %APPDATA% following vendor file loads. Alert on process chains executing reconnaissance commands (whoami, uname, systeminfo, Get-WmiObject) from PHP or Apache contexts.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Composer Package Installation with Rewritten Git Tag
suggestion.rationale: Article core: 'Every Tag Across Multiple Composer Packages Rewritten.' When composer.lock pulls a tag hash that has been force-rewritten server-side, the installed code differs from expected source. Detection must hook composer install/update and validate package checksums.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Trigger on composer install/require commands followed by PHP file execution from vendor/ with mismatched source-tree hash or obfuscated code patterns. Flag when package version in composer.lock does not match registry canonical hash or when git checkout of tag differs from upstream.

suggestion.title: Environment Variable Exfiltration from CI/CD Process
suggestion.rationale: Attack explicitly targets CI secrets: 'Steal CI Secrets.' Malicious code injected via Composer payload enumerates and exfiltrates environment variables containing GitHub tokens, deploy keys, AWS credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect CI/CD job processes that reference sensitive environment variable names (regex: .*TOKEN.*|.*SECRET.*|.*KEY.*|.*CREDENTIAL.*) followed by write operations to non-standard locations, base64 encoding, or outbound HTTP/DNS calls. Flag curl/wget/netcat calls containing base64 blobs or credential-like strings.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Force-Push or Tag Rewrite to Repository
suggestion.rationale: Core attack mechanism: attacker gained repository access and rewrote tags. Article: 'Every Tag...Rewritten.' Detect git push --force or tag manipulation on production/shared repositories by unauthorized accounts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on git push with --force, --force-with-lease, or tag deletion/rewrite commands to shared repositories. Correlate with unusual account authentication (new SSH key, VPN, geography, time-of-day deviation). Cross-reference with package maintainer account compromise signals.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated or Base64-Encoded Payload in Installed Composer Package
suggestion.rationale: Malicious code injected into rewritten tags must evade detection. Expect obfuscation in vendor/ directory: 'Rewritten...to Steal' implies hidden payload not visible in casual source review.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-install scan vendor/ directory for suspicious PHP patterns: nested preg_replace with /e modifier, base64_decode followed by eval/assert, shell metacharacters in strings, or excessive obfuscation (high entropy, packed code). Compare installed package binary hash against registry canonical hash.

suggestion.title: Unexpected DNS or Network Callback from Build Environment
suggestion.rationale: Malicious payload must exfiltrate secrets: 'Steal CI Secrets' implies outbound communication to attacker infrastructure. Build/test jobs should have predictable network footprint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline whitelisted DNS domains and IP ranges for CI/CD pipelines (package registries, artifact repos, public CDNs). Flag DNS queries to non-whitelisted TLDs or newly-registered domains. Alert on outbound connections carrying encoded data or connecting to IPs with low reputation or no RDNS.

suggestion.title: Package Repository Maintainer Account Compromise Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Attacker must have gained write-access to push rewritten tags. Detect compromise of Laravel-Lang maintainer accounts or CI/CD deploy credentials: 'packages rewritten' requires privilege escalation or credential theft.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor maintainer account logins from unusual geography, device, or auth method. Flag new SSH keys or deploy tokens added to accounts. Detect git operations (push, tag, branch) by accounts not typically performing them. Alert on API token usage patterns deviating from baseline or tokens with repository write permissions used from unexpected sources.

suggestion.title: LiteSpeed cPanel Plugin CVE-2026-48172 HTTP Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Exploited to Run Scripts as Root' — indicates web request exploitation of plugin endpoint. Article body absent but title establishes T1190 attack vector. Pipeline generated zero UCs for public-facing app exploit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect HTTP requests to known LiteSpeed cPanel plugin paths (version-specific or enumerated endpoints) with command-injection payloads, path traversal, or file-upload attempts. Baseline legitimate plugin management traffic and alert on deviation.

suggestion.title: Root Process Spawn from Web Server Context
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes impact: 'Run Scripts as Root.' Must detect privilege escalation from apache/nobody to UID=0. Pipeline failed to suggest any privilege-escalation detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on parent processes running as web-server user (apache, nobody) spawning child processes with UID=0 or with setuid/setgid bits. Focus on shell interpreters (/bin/bash, /bin/sh) or compiled binaries from /tmp or web-writable paths.

suggestion.title: Shell Script Execution from LiteSpeed Plugin Directory
suggestion.rationale: Title: 'Run Scripts as Root' — directly indicates scripting execution post-exploitation. No use case for shell/interpreter spawning from plugin paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor execution of bash, sh, perl, or python with parent process or working directory in /usr/local/lsws/*, /opt/litespeed/*, or web-accessible cPanel plugin directories. Flag command arguments for reverse-shell patterns or credential-theft indicators.

suggestion.title: Malicious File Write to Web-Accessible LiteSpeed Directory
suggestion.rationale: Exploitation of plugin requires upload or injection of malicious code. Pipeline missed file-modification detection during initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect creation or modification of .php, .cgi, .pl, .sh files in LiteSpeed plugin directories by the web-server user, especially if the file content contains base64, hex-encoded payloads, or known malware signatures. Correlate with preceding HTTP POST requests.

suggestion.title: Network Egress from Root-Spawned cPanel Process
suggestion.rationale: Root privilege escalation almost always leads to C2 callback or persistence. Article likely contains C2 IOCs (IPs/domains), but pipeline extracted none and suggested no detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and TCP/UDP connections initiated by cPanel daemons or root-spawned descendants to external IPs. Flag queries for known malware C2 domains, newly registered domains, or IPs geographically inconsistent with the organization.

suggestion.title: Exploit Code Artifacts in Web Logs and Temporary Directories
suggestion.rationale: Proof-of-concept or multi-stage exploitation payloads often leave traces in /tmp, /dev/shm, or web-server logs. Pipeline suggested no log-based detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search web-server and cPanel logs for encoding patterns (base64, gzip, hex), common exploit/webshell file signatures, or requests with oversized payloads targeting the plugin endpoint. Correlate with unusual temp-directory file creation or wget/curl commands downloading files.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized NPM Package Publication
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'npm Adds 2FA-Gated Publishing'—implies detection should monitor for publish events circumventing 2FA or from unexpected origins. Detection is the inverse of the control.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm publish commands from IP addresses with <5 days history associated with package maintainer account, or from VPN/proxy IPs not in historical baseline. Flag publish events where 2FA verification logs are absent or show bypass patterns.

suggestion.title: Package Maintainer Account Compromise Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article's 2FA requirement implies accounts are high-value targets. 'Package Install Controls' suggests defense against account takeover leading to malicious package updates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm maintainer accounts (own 10+ packages or 10M+ weekly downloads) for: failed login bursts from credential-stuffing IPs, successful login followed by immediate package update, session tokens used from unexpected geographies within minutes.

suggestion.title: Malicious Postinstall Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Install controls referenced suggest npm detected risk in package installation phase. Postinstall scripts executing arbitrary code is the vector; detection should monitor execution patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm postinstall hooks that spawn shells, invoke curl/wget to external URLs, modify PATH, or write to sensitive directories (/etc, ~/.ssh). Flag installations where postinstall execution time exceeds 10 seconds or calls network tools.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted Package Detection
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks often use typosquatting. Article's mention of 'Package Install Controls' implies npm addresses this. Detection should identify lookalike packages.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect newly published packages (age <7 days) with names differing from top-1000 npm packages by single-character edits, case variations, or vowel omission. Flag if published by account without prior package history and installed by >10 distinct IPs within 24 hours.

suggestion.title: Downgrade Attack on Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article's 'Package Install Controls' phrasing suggests defense against version manipulation. Downgrade attacks force installation of older, unpatched package versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when npm resolves to a version older than latest available without explicit version pinning in package.json or package-lock.json. Flag rapid major.minor version changes (e.g., 8.x → 5.x) within single build or across dependency tree.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Dependency Injection via Registry Manipulation
suggestion.rationale: Controls mentioned guard against registry-layer attacks. Detection should flag when package manifests unexpectedly add or modify dependencies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for package versions where dependencies were added/modified in postinstall rather than package.json, or where a maintainer's published version differs from the same commit tag in source repository. Alert on packages that inject dependencies of other high-value packages.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Laravel-Lang Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly describes Laravel-Lang packages as vectors—pipeline must detect package manager activity (composer install/require) with version anomalies, timing mismatches to public registries, or suspicious post-install hooks. Missing entirely from output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor composer.json modifications or composer install/require commands installing Laravel-Lang; correlate installed package versions against official Packagist registry. Flag installations of unexpected versions, particularly those published outside normal maintenance windows or with unusual file hashes.

suggestion.title: Credential Stealer Post-Install Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes credential stealer malware bundled with packages. Pipeline must detect PHP code execution from vendor directories, particularly calls to credential APIs (password managers, git credentials, AWS keys, browser caches). Article title guarantees this threat but no detection coverage exists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PHP process spawning with working directory in vendor/laravel-lang/* paths, especially child processes accessing credential stores (Chrome DB, Firefox, git config, .aws, .ssh). Alert on file reads to %APPDATA%\Local\Google\Chrome or equivalent cross-platform secret locations.

suggestion.title: Package Metadata Drift Detection
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks typically insert malicious versions alongside legitimate ones. Pipeline must detect version mismatch between declared and installed package versions, or hash mismatches vs. public registry records. Not addressed in output.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare installed Laravel-Lang package hashes (from composer.lock or filesystem) against official Packagist SHA256 records. Flag mismatches or 'phantom versions' (package versions that do not exist in official repository history).

suggestion.title: Composer Lock File Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Attackers often modify composer.lock to pin compromised versions. Pipeline must baseline legitimate lock files and alert on unexpected changes, especially to Laravel-Lang pinned versions or hash fields.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor write events to composer.lock in development/deployment pipelines. Alert if Laravel-Lang entries are updated without corresponding code-review approval or CI/CD record. Baseline hash values for known-good versions.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Drupal Core Instance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies product: 'Drupal Core SQL Injection vulnerability'. Detection must enumerate unpatched instances exposed to external networks with due date 2026-05-27.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query vulnerability scanner results and asset inventory for Drupal Core instances. Alert on versions unpatched as of the federal due date 2026-05-27. Cross-reference with network exposure scans to identify public-facing instances.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection Attacks Against Drupal Database Abstraction API
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies attack vector: 'SQL injection vulnerability...via specially crafted requests sent with the database abstraction API.' This is the exploitation mechanism and warrants SQL injection detection at the WAF and application layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Drupal instances for SQL injection payloads targeting database API endpoints. Flag requests containing SQL metacharacters, UNION operators, or boolean-based injection patterns in query parameters or POST bodies.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation Within Drupal or Database Context
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states outcome: 'could allow for privilege escalation.' Detection should alert on unauthorized user role elevation or permission changes linked to SQL injection exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor database and Drupal application logs for suspicious privilege escalation events: unauthorized role assignment, permission grants, or SQL queries modifying user access controls during or after detected SQL injection attempts.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution Post-Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies outcome: 'remote code execution via specially crafted requests.' Detection must capture post-exploitation behavior after successful SQL injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected process execution, shell spawning, or file writes originating from web server processes (apache/nginx) hosting Drupal, particularly following SQL injection indicators in logs.

suggestion.title: Malicious LNK Execution Downloading PowerShell Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'attackers emailed a ZIP archive containing an LNK file' and 'LNK shortcuts to covertly execute PowerShell scripts hosted on external resources.' This is the primary initial access vector requiring dedicated detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on LNK files extracted from email-delivered ZIP archives that execute PowerShell.exe with -Command or -EncodedCommand flags downloading remote scripts. Monitor for parent process mshta.exe or explorer.exe launching cmd.exe → powershell.exe chains on systems with recent email attachment activity.

suggestion.title: YandexBrowser_setup Registry Persistence Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'Creates "Run" registry key "YandexBrowser_setup" for "$temp\fixed.ps1" startup.' This specific registry key is a direct, named IoC for Cloud Atlas persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag RegistryValueSet events where HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run or equivalent contains 'YandexBrowser_setup' pointing to any *.ps1 file in %TEMP% or user AppData. This key name is a strong Cloud Atlas indicator with minimal false positive risk.

suggestion.title: termsrv.dll Patching for Multi-User RDP Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'Multi-user RDP by patching termsrv.dll' as a payload capability. Unauthorized termsrv.dll modification is a high-fidelity lateral movement indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor System32\termsrv.dll and SysWOW64\termsrv.dll for FileModified or FileCreated events; validate digital signature and file hash against known-good baselines. Cross-correlate with RegSetValue events modifying HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\TermService parameters (e.g., fDenyTSConnections=0).

suggestion.title: Reverse SSH Tunnel Execution from Temp Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Reverse SSH tunneling' and 'Patched OpenSSH' as C2/persistence mechanisms. 'We observed the use of third-party public utilities (Tor/SSH/RevSocks) to gain a foothold in infected systems and create additional backup control channels.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag ssh.exe, sshd.exe, or patched OpenSSH execution from %TEMP%, %APPDATA%, or other non-standard directories with command-line arguments containing '-R' (reverse forwarding), '-L' (local forwarding), or '-D' (SOCKS). Alert on SSH processes establishing persistent background connections without user TTY.

suggestion.title: RevSocks SOCKS5 Proxy Tool Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'RevSocks' as explicitly deployed to 'create additional backup control channels.' RevSocks execution is a direct IoC of Cloud Atlas compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for RevSocks binary execution by name or file path from user-writable directories. Alert on unexpected SOCKS5 proxy initialization patterns or outbound connections establishing SOCKS listener ports (default 1080 or variants). Cross-check against known RevSocks process telemetry (memory patterns, string signatures).

suggestion.title: PowerShower Credential Grabber Memory/Registry Access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes payload: 'PowerShower::Payload (credential grabber).' PowerShell-based credential access typically involves LSASS, clipboard, or SAM hive reads, warranting sensitive detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag PowerShell scripts or child processes accessing LSASS (\Device\\LsaAuthenticationServer, Win32_LsassProcess), reading clipboard (Get-Clipboard, OpenClipboard API), or enumerating registry credentials hives (HKU\). Alert on rundll32.exe invoking credential provider DLLs (credui.dll, wincred.dll) from script contexts.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection Payload Detection in HTTP Requests to Drupal Endpoints
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'allows specially crafted requests to trigger arbitrary SQL injection' and 'exploitation attempts have been detected in the wild'—SOCs must detect malicious request patterns before they reach the database abstraction API.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP request logs for SQL metacharacters and keywords (UNION, SELECT, DROP, EXEC, --|comment syntax, semicolon-prefixed queries) in URL query parameters and POST body data targeting Drupal endpoints (/admin*, /user*, /search, /system*, /api*). Correlate with HTTP 5xx responses or slow query timeouts.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Database Queries from Web Application Service Account
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'trigger arbitrary SQL injection on sites using PostgreSQL'—PostgreSQL query logs must show unexpected DDL/DML (DROP, ALTER, CREATE, DELETE with malformed WHERE clauses) from Drupal application user context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on multi-table UNION statements, nested subqueries, or information_schema/pg_* table enumeration executed by the Drupal service account (www-data, apache, nginx). Flag DELETE/DROP statements against core tables (users, roles, sessions, node) lacking application-pattern justification.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Process Execution from Web Server Context Following Database Anomalies
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'could result in remote code execution'—if SQL injection achieves RCE (e.g., via PostgreSQL UDF or COPY TO execution), process spawn logs must detect shell or binary execution from web service UID in temporal proximity to SQL injection indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bash, sh, python, perl, or system utilities spawned from www-data, apache, or nginx UID. Escalate if process execution immediately follows or correlates with anomalous database queries or HTTP 500 errors on Drupal endpoints.

suggestion.title: Drupal Version Enumeration and Vulnerability Scanning
suggestion.rationale: Article lists specific vulnerable versions (8.9.x, 10.4–10.6, 11.0–11.3 with patch thresholds). Reconnaissance activity: attackers query /CHANGELOG.txt, HTTP headers, or /admin/reports/status to confirm version before exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP access logs for GET requests to /CHANGELOG.txt, /sites/default/files/, or status/version-checking URIs. Flag repeated version-probing requests from single source followed by SQL injection attempt patterns within 5 minutes.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Credential or Privilege Table Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'could result in privilege escalation'—if SQL injection compromises user or role tables, UPDATE/INSERT statements modify hashes, role assignments, or administrative flags on sensitive tables.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on UPDATE statements targeting users, roles, permissions, or sessions tables with unusual predicates (e.g., UPDATE users SET admin=1 WHERE..., UPDATE roles SET...permissions...). Flag password hash or token field modifications from non-administrative contexts.

suggestion.title: Large Data Exfiltration or Bulk Table Access Following SQL Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'resulting in unauthorized access, modification, or deletion of database data'—post-compromise, attackers bulk-read sensitive tables (users, contacts, orders, sessions, content).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequential SELECT * queries or large COPY/EXPORT operations on sensitive tables (users, field_data_*, sessions, cache) from non-standard application contexts. Correlate with network volume spikes (large data transfers out) from database host.

suggestion.title: Ransomware-linked IP and ASN historical connection analysis
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes VPN was 'used by 25 ransomware groups'—pipeline should identify the VPN provider's known ASNs, IP ranges, and domain infrastructure, then create use case to hunt retrospectively for connections from internal endpoints or exfil points to those ranges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search for historical outbound connections from Windows or Linux endpoints to known dismantled VPN provider IP ranges or ASNs. Correlate with known ransomware beacon patterns or exfiltration timestamps to identify potential compromise windows.

suggestion.title: Detection of multi-hop proxy infrastructure patterns
suggestion.rationale: VPN services inherently enable multi-hop proxying; article explicitly describes 'VPN' dismantled 'used by ransomware groups', suggesting attackers leveraged T1090.003. Pipeline should generate detection for proxy or VPN client execution on endpoints combined with anomalous egress.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for VPN client software (OpenVPN, WireGuard, proprietary clients) spawned by non-standard processes or users with concurrent non-RFC1918 network connections, or persistence via registry/startup folders for VPN configurations.

suggestion.title: Correlated ransomware actor infrastructure overlap
suggestion.rationale: Article's core finding—25 distinct ransomware groups using same VPN service—signals shared infrastructure pattern. Pipeline should create UC to detect when multiple known ransomware beacons resolve or connect to same VPN provider endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate DNS queries and network connections from separate infected hosts against known VPN provider domains and IP ranges. Flag when domains associated with distinct ransomware families (based on C2 signatures or behavioral clustering) share VPN infrastructure.

suggestion.title: VPN service infrastructure acquisition and advertising
suggestion.rationale: 'Dismantled VPN' implies the service operated openly with registration, billing, hosting. Article suggests threat actors provisioned and maintained this infrastructure. Pipeline should capture T1583.006 (Acquire Infrastructure).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for domain registration, WHOIS updates, ASN announcements, or hosting account creation tied to known VPN provider infrastructure. Flag domains registered to bulletproof hosters or privacy registrars with historical ties to ransomware groups.

suggestion.title: Typosquatting Domain Access for Event-Themed Ticketing
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly documents FIFA domain impersonation: 'relies on a common trick known as typosquatting, which involves on a domain name that closely resembles the legitimate one, but contains small additions or involves other changes'. Pipeline missed this primary attack vector entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor DNS queries and network connections to domains matching FIFA/World Cup ticketing patterns with minor character variations (e.g., fifa26, fifa-26, world-cup-2026, etc.). Alert when domain structure closely resembles but does not exactly match official registrant domains. Cross-reference newly registered domains against trademark databases.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Fake Ticketing Registration Forms
suggestion.rationale: Article describes deceptive registration forms: 'If you expect to create a FIFA ID before buying tickets, a fake registration form may not look strange at first. It also asks for the usual things such as your name, email address, and phone number.' Pipeline failed to detect credential access pattern.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP POST requests to typosquatted ticketing domains containing user registration form payloads (fields: name, email, phone). Detect anomalous user-agent strings or rapid sequential registrations from single source IPs. Correlate with phishing email campaigns referencing FIFA/World Cup.

suggestion.title: Payment Card Data Collection on Fake Checkout Pages
suggestion.rationale: Article documents financial theft: 'Once you enter your card details, it goes straight to the people behind the fake site' and 'Once entered into the form, your payments details would travel into the hands of the cybercriminal'. Pipeline missed collection-phase detection for payment data exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTPS traffic to typosquatted ticketing domains for form submissions containing credit card patterns (PAN regex, expiration fields, CVC). Alert on exfiltration of payment data to non-PCI-DSS compliant hosts or IPs outside typical payment processor ASNs. Correlate with user registration events on same domain.

suggestion.title: Phishing Link Distribution via Email and Sponsored Ads
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Some victims may reach these websites through sponsored search results, while others click on ads on social media or links in email messages forwarded by someone who didn't check the address properly.' Pipeline extracted zero initial-access detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor email for links to typosquatted World Cup/FIFA domains and alert on subjects containing urgency language ('limited availability', 'final tickets', 'official merchandise'). Flag sponsored search ads and social media posts linking to newly registered domains matching FIFA trademark patterns. Correlate sender domain reputation and DKIM/SPF validation status.

suggestion.title: Website Visual/Structural Cloning Detection for Brand Impersonation
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes impersonation fidelity: 'The site also copies the look and feel of FIFA's official site, including the colors, layout, navigation and ticketing flow, all in order to make the victim feel that the experience is legitimate.' Pipeline missed defense-evasion detection for website mimicry.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build CSS and HTML structure baselines for official FIFA/World Cup domains. Monitor for new domains serving pages with >80% structural similarity (CSS class names, page tree topology, template layout). Flag registrations of domains within 2 character edits of legitimate domains serving ticketing/merchandise pages.

suggestion.title: Event-Driven Urgency Phishing Campaign Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation of event-anticipation psychology: 'As the FIFA World Cup 2026™ draws closer, anticipation is building toward fever pitch... interested, impatient and... worried that the tickets... will sell out. Which is ultimately what makes these scams so effective.' Pipeline missed temporal/behavioral pattern for event-driven phishing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Implement calendar-triggered detection rules activating 60-120 days before major sporting events (World Cup, Olympics, Super Bowl). During these windows, increase sensitivity on email campaigns containing urgency keywords ('official', 'limited', 'last chance') and links to newly registered domains. Correlate bulk email volume spikes with event date proximity.

suggestion.title: F5 BIG-IP Configuration Utility RCE Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'SSH access to the first Linux host from a network device identified as an F5 BIG-IP load balancer' running EOL version 15.1.201000. CVE-2026-39455 is the likely attack vector but was not mapped to any detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor F5 BIG-IP appliances for unauthenticated or low-privileged access to configuration utility endpoints (typically port 443 on /tmui). Flag successful authentication followed by shell process execution (bash/sh spawned as root or admin). Alert on outbound SSH from F5 appliances to internal Linux hosts.
