suggestion.title: Confluence Remote Code Execution via Unpatched Vulnerability
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'Confluence server within the network with unpatched vulnerabilities' and 'leveraged these vulnerabilities to execute code remotely.' CVE-2025-33073 mentioned in search results. No detection coverage generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Confluence application logs and process events for unusual Java process spawning (Runtime.exec, ProcessBuilder). Alert on HTTP POST to known Confluence RCE endpoints with payloads. Track outbound network from Confluence process to external FTP or DNS servers.

suggestion.title: Python FTP Server Launch from Compromised Host
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'set up an FTP server on the initial Linux host using Python's ftplib module to transfer the custom scanning tool.' This is explicit staging infrastructure but generated zero IOCs or detection cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Python process spawning with ftplib import or python -m ftpserver execution. Alert on listening sockets on port 21 or high-numbered FTP ports from non-standard processes. Monitor file transfers into compromised Confluence via FTP on non-standard ports.

suggestion.title: Kerberos Relay Attack with PetitPotam Coercion
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'escalated into Kerberos relay attacks and exploitation of CVE-2025-33073, using netexec with PetitPotam coercion.' This is a sophisticated lateral movement technique with specific tooling (netexec, PetitPotam) that should trigger multiple detections but pipeline generated none.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for netexec process execution on compromised Linux hosts. Alert on EfsRpc (Endpoint File Service RPC) calls from Linux to Windows targets—signature of PetitPotam coercion. Flag failed Kerberos pre-authentication followed by successful relay attacks in event logs (event 4768 with relay indicators, event 4769 from unexpected sources).

suggestion.title: DNS Manipulation for Domain Controller Targeting
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions: 'DNS manipulation tooling to target a domain controller.' No DNS-based detection use case generated despite explicit statement of DNS abuse in the kill chain.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate DNS queries from compromised Linux host to domain controller hostnames with subsequent unusual DNS responses (non-authoritative replies, mismatched A/AAAA records, queries from non-DNS ports). Alert on iptables or netfilter rules modifying DNS responses on compromised host. Monitor for in-path DNS spoofing via tcpdump or similar capture.

suggestion.title: Credential Access via Confluence LDAP/Kerberos Integration
suggestion.rationale: Attack pivoted through Confluence to 'credential theft and identity compromise' and 'domain-level compromise spanning Linux hosts, an internal Atlassian Confluence server, and Windows authentication systems.' No credential theft detection mapped despite being core to the attack narrative.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Confluence process for LDAP unbind followed by credential enumeration queries (group membership, service account lookups). Alert on unusual LDAP binding attempts with cleartext credentials captured in logs. Flag Confluence spawning credential dumping tools (lsass access, /etc/shadow reads, keytab exfiltration).

suggestion.title: Spearphishing Detection - Ukraine Government

suggestion.title: Suspicious Laravel-Lang Package Installation or Update
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states '233 Versions of Laravel-Lang Packages' were compromised; pipeline ignored the entire premise of a supply-chain package compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package manager logs (composer, npm, pip) for installations or updates of Laravel-Lang packages matching the affected version range. Correlate with known vulnerable versions from CVE advisories. Flag any installation outside of approved internal mirrors.

suggestion.title: Execution from Vendor Package Directory Post-Installation
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromise typically delivers malicious payload via package files; pipeline missed the execution phase following installation ('Compromised 233 Versions').
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process execution (php, bash, python) spawned directly from vendor/laravel-lang/ or similar package directories. Flag scripts with suspicious capabilities (network, file write, credential access) executing from package installation paths.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized GitHub Repository Access or Code Push
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Hacking 700 GitHub Repos'—pipeline failed to surface repository compromise as initial compromise vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GitHub API calls showing repository access or push events from unusual IP ranges, VPN providers, or non-owner accounts. Correlate with anomalous commit authors or unusual push frequency. Flag push events to high-visibility package repositories outside business hours.

suggestion.title: Post-Install Script Execution in Malicious Package
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain package attacks commonly use composer.json scripts or install hooks to execute payload; pipeline did not capture post-installation execution flow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for parent-child process relationships where composer install, npm install, or pip install spawns unexpected child processes (curl, wget, sh, powershell). Flag execution of obfuscated or base64-encoded scripts triggered by package installation.

suggestion.title: Multiple Application Instances Exhibiting Identical Anomalous Behavior Post-Package-Update
suggestion.rationale: When a supply-chain package is compromised, affected behaviors are typically uniform across all applications using the infected version; pipeline missed lateral behavior correlation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate behavioral anomalies (unexpected outbound connections, unusual file writes, privilege escalation attempts) across multiple distinct application instances. Alert if the anomaly coincides with a package version bump and is observed on 5+ distinct hosts/applications.

suggestion.title: F5 BIG-IP Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title identifies 'Hackers Exploit F5 BIG-IP Appliance' as the initial attack vector. No detection coverage created for exploitation of this public-facing device class.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor F5 BIG-IP access logs for exploitation signatures: unusual HTTP methods, authentication bypass attempts, known F5 CVE exploit paths (e.g., /admin, /mgmt endpoints with encoding, version disclosure responses). Alert on 5xx errors coinciding with unusual POST/PUT requests to administrative interfaces from external IPs.

suggestion.title: Suspicious SSH Session from BIG-IP Management IP
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'Gain SSH Access and Pivot Into Enterprise Linux Networks.' Pipeline missed detection for SSH connections originating from compromised BIG-IP appliances pivoting to internal Linux systems.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate F5 BIG-IP management IP address as SSH source to internal Linux hosts. Alert on: SSH connections from BIG-IP appliance IP:22 to multiple internal hosts within short timeframe, especially if BIG-IP does not normally originate SSH sessions, or failed authentication attempts followed by successful access.

suggestion.title: Bulk SSH Brute Force or Key-Based Access Post-BIG-IP Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Pivot Into Enterprise Linux Networks' suggesting lateral movement phase. No detection created for subsequent credential abuse or automated access spread across Linux infrastructure after initial BIG-IP compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect high-velocity SSH authentication attempts across multiple Linux hosts from single source IP (compromised BIG-IP or attacker-controlled pivot point). Alert on threshold: >10 failed auth attempts per host or successful access to >5 internal Linux systems within 5 minutes using same or different credentials.

suggestion.title: BIG-IP System Configuration or Credential Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article does not describe full attack outcome in available body, but pivot pattern suggests attackers likely harvested BIG-IP credentials or configuration. Pipeline missed credential-access detection use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor F5 BIG-IP logs for export/backup operations (config download, certificate export), credential changes during exploitation window, or unusual API calls to credential stores. Alert on: tmsh 'save' commands, ucs/qkview generation, SSL certificate or key file reads by unprivileged processes.

suggestion.title: F5 BIG-IP Persistence Mechanism Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article title does not clarify persistence intent, but 'pivot into enterprise' pattern strongly implies attackers embedded persistent access in BIG-IP for future re-entry. No persistence detection created.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthorized user creation, privilege escalation, or cron job installation on BIG-IP during or shortly after exploitation. Monitor F5 audit logs for: new admin/operator user accounts, unauthorized iRule modifications (persistent script execution), or startup configuration changes that execute external scripts or establish reverse shells.

suggestion.title: Bulk Git Tag Rewrite to Fork Commits
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes: 'rewrote every existing git tag in each repository to point at a new malicious commit' and 'abused a GitHub feature that allows tags to point to commits in forks.' This is the supply-chain pivot point and should trigger alerts on repository management systems tracking tag mutations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk GitHub tag mutations within a short timeframe (22:32–00:00 UTC across 4 repos) pointing to non-canonical commits. Alert on organization-wide push access abuse where tags are rewritten to reference forked repository commits rather than main-branch commits.

suggestion.title: Malicious Composer Autoload Injection (helpers.php)
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'malicious file named src/helpers.php, which was automatically loaded by Composer' via 'autoload section of composer.json.' This is the execution mechanism and should be detectable at package install time.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Composer install/update operations for injection of unexpected files into autoload paths. Flag helpers.php additions to autoload sections in composer.json. Track git tag checkouts that resolve to unexpected commits containing autoload injections.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration to flipboxstudio[.]info C2
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names C2: 'downloaded a second payload from the attacker's command and control server at flipboxstudio[.]info.' Malware 'encrypts it and sends it back to the C2 server.' Developers advised to 'check for historical outbound connections to flipboxstudio[.]info.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect DNS queries and HTTP/HTTPS connections to flipboxstudio[.]info from PHP-running hosts. Monitor for encrypted POST requests with exfiltrated credential payloads. Track historical connections from dev/build environments running Laravel projects.

suggestion.title: Multi-Vector Credential File Enumeration Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Article describes regex patterns targeting: '.env files, cloud credentials, Kubernetes secrets, Vault tokens, Git credentials, CI/CD secrets, SSH keys.' Malware 'harvests' these across 'files and environment variables.' This is bulk credential discovery distinct from targeted extraction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid file access patterns scanning for .env, .ssh, .kube, .aws, .git/credentials, Vault, and password manager files. Flag processes opening 5+ credential-storage locations in sequence. Monitor for regex pattern matching against environment variable reads in non-dev contexts.

suggestion.title: DebugElevator Executable Extraction and Execution from %TEMP%
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'extracted a base64-encoded executable embedded within the file, which is written to the %TEMP% folder as a random .exe filename, and then launched.' Windows malware 'named DebugElevator... designed to target Chrome, Brave, and Edge, and extract App-Bound Encryption keys.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect base64-encoded executables written to %TEMP% and immediately executed. Flag suspicious .exe launches from %TEMP% with DPAPI/App-Bound Encryption key operations. Monitor for Chrome/Brave/Edge browser process access patterns consistent with credential decryption.

suggestion.title: Browser Password Store Access (App-Bound Encryption)
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies: 'extract App-Bound Encryption keys needed to decrypt stored browser credentials.' This is credential-specific targeting of browser storage, distinct from general process injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes accessing Chrome/Brave/Edge Local State files, DPAPI blobs, or AppData credential stores. Monitor for DPAPI decryption operations (Win32 CryptUnprotectData) against browser-scoped encryption keys. Alert on process handles to browser processes from untrusted or temporary file paths.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PHP Execution from Web Root — Laravel-Lang Context
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Cross-Platform Credential Stealer' delivered via compromised PHP package; malicious code would execute within web server process, likely in vendor directory or autoload path. Phrase: 'Deliver Cross-Platform Credential Stealer'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on php.exe or php-fpm spawning child processes with suspicious arguments (curl, wget, registry access on Windows, /etc access on Linux) when parent is w3wp, apache, nginx. Focus on processes in vendor/ or vendor/laravel-lang/ directories. Cross-reference against known malicious Laravel-Lang package signatures.

suggestion.title: Package Installation from Untrusted Repository — Laravel-Lang Supply Chain
suggestion.rationale: Compromise vector is package repository; detection should monitor composer.json modifications and composer install/update commands targeting compromised packages. Phrase: 'Laravel-Lang PHP Packages Compromised'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for composer install/update commands with new or modified laravel-lang package references. Alert on unexpected changes to composer.lock files, especially version downgrades or source URL modifications. Flag commands executed with elevated privileges or from unexpected contexts (cron, CI/CD with no approval trail).

suggestion.title: Credential Access via Compromised PHP Dependencies
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies malware is a 'Credential Stealer'; once execution is achieved, it will exfiltrate credentials (env files, .env parsing, database credentials, API keys). Phrase: 'Credential Stealer'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PHP processes reading .env files, config/ directories, or credential storage paths (e.g., ~/.ssh, ~/.aws). Detect regex pattern matching in PHP for password/token extraction from strings (base64 decode chains, environ dumps). Monitor for unusual .env or credential file access from web-server-owned processes.

suggestion.title: Outbound Network Anomaly from Web Server — C2 Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealer must exfiltrate data; article context implies cross-platform C2 or data-staging infrastructure. Phrase: 'Deliver Cross-Platform Credential Stealer' implies persistent C2 communication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unusual outbound connections from PHP processes to non-whitelisted IPs or domains, especially to known malware C2 infrastructure. Flag DNS queries for dynamically generated or typosquatted Laravel/PHP community domains. Monitor for encrypted outbound tunnels (VPN, proxy, TOR) initiated by web server processes.

suggestion.title: Filesystem Persistence via Composer Autoload or PHP Wrapper
suggestion.rationale: Compromised package may establish persistence by hooking autoload mechanisms or wrapping PHP stream wrappers. Article does not explicitly detail this but 'cross-platform' suggests sophisticated persistence mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor composer.json for new autoload files pointing to attacker-controlled directories. Detect modifications to php.ini, .htaccess, or web server configs injecting malicious includes. Alert on new stream wrapper registrations or unexpected changes to auto_prepend_file or auto_append_file directives.

suggestion.title: Privileged Process Spawning from Web Server Context
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealer may attempt privilege escalation to access system-wide secrets (sudoers, kernel credentials, SAM database). Article does not exclude privilege escalation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on www-data, apache, nginx, or iis apppool processes executing sudo, net localgroup, token impersonation, or UAC bypass utilities. Detect unexpected SYSTEM or root-context child processes spawned from web server parents.

suggestion.title: Malicious Composer autoload.files Registry Entry
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states payload 'was hidden in a newly added file, src/helpers.php, and registered in composer.json under autoload.files' and that 'Composer's autoloader unconditionally requires every file in that list, so the malicious code runs at the very start of the PHP request lifecycle.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor composer.json for modifications to autoload.files entries, particularly additions of helpers.php or other utilities in src/ or vendor/ directories that were absent from baseline lockfiles. Alert on autoload entries pointing to non-standard directories or filenames inconsistent with legitimate package structure.

suggestion.title: PHP Process HTTP Request to flipboxstudio[.]info Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article states malicious code 'fetches a second stage from https://flipboxstudio[.]info/payload and executes it in the background.' This is direct C2 communication from web application context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTPS connections from PHP processes (php, php-fpm, apache2, nginx, httpd) to flipboxstudio[.]info or similar newly-observed second-level domains. Flag outbound HTTPS from web application context during non-business hours or to domains with no prior enterprise traffic history.

suggestion.title: Multi-Source Credential and Secrets Enumeration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes second-stage payload behavior: 'walks through a long list of sources looking for anything of value: Cloud provider credentials... Kubernetes kubeconfig files... HashiCorp Vault tokens... CI/CD secrets... SSH private keys... Application .env files... Browser data... Password manager vaults... Cryptocurrency wallet files... Messaging and collaboration tokens.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect sequences of rapid file-access attempts from PHP-spawned child processes targeting known credential locations: ~/.aws, ~/.gcp, ~/.kube/config, ~/.ssh/id_*, .env, ~/.config/1password, ~/.config/discord, ~/.mozilla. Alert on file enumeration patterns consistent with credential harvesting rather than legitimate application access.

suggestion.title: Cross-Platform Payload Execution from PHP Context
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'The launcher logic is platform-aware and works on Linux, macOS, and Windows,' embedded in helpers.php and auto-executing on every request via Composer autoload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PHP interpreter processes spawning child system utilities (curl, wget, bash, sh, powershell.exe, cmd.exe, openssl, base64) with network-related or credential-enumeration parameters. Flag execution of system binaries from PHP with environment-variable enumeration or subshell patterns during typical web request handling.

suggestion.title: Encrypted Data Exfiltration to C2 Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'Collected data is encrypted and shipped out to https://flipboxstudio[.]info/exfil.' This is high-volume credential exfiltration via HTTPS.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sustained or large-volume HTTPS POST requests from web application processes to flipboxstudio[.]info/exfil or similar infrastructure. Monitor for encrypted TLS traffic from PHP with atypical certificate chains, rapid session establishment, or data volumes inconsistent with legitimate application behavior.

suggestion.title: Packagist Tag Resolution to Attacker-Controlled Fork
suggestion.rationale: Article details core supply-chain vector: 'a Git tag created within an organization can resolve to a commit in a fork outside that organization. Packagist then ingested those tags and treated the fork commits as genuine releases of the official package.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: For Composer/Packagist environments: detect package installs where the resolved commit SHA or repository origin diverges from canonical laravel-lang GitHub organization sources. Alert on composer.lock entries where laravel-lang/* packages resolve to non-official forks or commits authored outside the maintainer list.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Compromise: Unauthorized Rewrite of Repository Tags on Public Package
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Every Tag Across Multiple Composer Packages Rewritten'—the attacker's core persistence tactic was mass tag manipulation. Detection must identify unusual git tag operations (deletion, recreation, force-push) on public OSS repos, especially non-incremental version rewrites.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk git tag deletions followed by recreation within 24 hours on public repositories. Flag tag force-pushes that modify existing version tags (e.g., v1.2.3 rewritten instead of v1.2.4 created). Cross-reference against maintainer's typical git commit cadence to detect anomalous velocity.

suggestion.title: CI/CD Secret Exfiltration via Malicious Dependency Initialization Code
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states goal: 'Steal CI Secrets.' Malicious Composer package code executes during install/autoload before build logic begins, giving attacker a window to access GitHub Actions secrets, deploy keys, or credential manager outputs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor CI runner process trees for shell execution (curl, wget, nc, php -r) spawned from Composer autoload or post-install script context. Flag access to $_ENV, getenv(), or AWS_*/GITHUB_*/AZURE_* credential env variables from within package initialization. Detect exfiltration attempt: subprocess writing environment variables to external URL.

suggestion.title: Composer Package Installation from Compromised Repository Branch or Fork
suggestion.rationale: Attack required compromise of Laravel-Lang maintainer account to push malicious versions. Detection should identify when package version matches a known release but underlying commit hash, GPG signature, or source repository diverges from baseline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Maintain golden-master composer.lock hashes for critical dependencies. Alert if installed package version number matches expected release (e.g., v1.2.3) but git commit SHA is unexpected. Flag package installation immediately after suspicious VCS activity (credential reset, SSH key addition, branch force-push) on the maintainer's account.

suggestion.title: Outbound Network Connection from CI Environment During Dependency Resolution
suggestion.rationale: For secret exfiltration to succeed, malicious code must connect to attacker C2. Traffic during Composer install phase to non-CDN domains or cloud storage endpoints is high-fidelity indicator of active payload execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Log all DNS queries and TCP connections from CI runners during composer install, before build steps begin. Flag resolution of newly-registered domains, low-reputation IPs, or cloud storage buckets outside organization whitelist. Correlate with failed secret-manager API calls or credential manager access spikes on same runner.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Composer autoload-files or scripts Directive with Shell Execution
suggestion.rationale: Composer allows PHP execution via autoload-files and post-install scripts in composer.json. This is the likely injection vector. Detection must catch PHP processes spawning shells during package initialization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Intercept composer.json retrieval and parse autoload-files, post-install-cmd, and scripts sections. Alert if malicious functions (system(), exec(), shell_exec(), passthru()) are found. In runtime, monitor for PHP child process spawning bash/sh during Composer install. Flag commands with pipe operators, redirects, or credential-like argument patterns.

suggestion.title: Authenticating Git Clone or Package Pull from Compromised Account Before Attack Timestamp
suggestion.rationale: Initial compromise of the Laravel-Lang maintainer account preceded the tag rewrites. Detection of unusual authentication (new IP, new SSH key, new OAuth app) followed by bulk repository operations could surface the foothold.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on SSH key addition, password reset, or OAuth app authorization on developer accounts with Composer package publish rights, especially if followed within hours by git push operations on public repos. Flag git clone/pull from unusual geography or IP reputation.

suggestion.title: LiteSpeed cPanel Plugin Unauthenticated Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article title indicates scripts executed as root via CVE-2026-48172. No article body provided to extract specifics, but privilege escalation to root is explicitly stated. Expected initial access vector is exploitation of the plugin.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected child processes spawned by LiteSpeed/cPanel daemons with SYSTEM/root privileges. Track web requests to LiteSpeed plugin endpoints (typically /scripts/ or admin interfaces) followed by high-privilege process creation. Alert on script execution via /bin/sh or /bin/bash initiated from the cPanel httpd context.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via LiteSpeed cPanel Plugin Abuse
suggestion.rationale: CVE title explicitly states 'Run Scripts as Root'—this is privilege escalation from web daemon to root. Article does not provide sufficient detail on mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect transitions from unprivileged cPanel/LiteSpeed processes to root UID in process create events. Look for elevation chains: web daemon → sudo/su/execution → root shell. Flag if originating from web server contexts without legitimate administrative action.

suggestion.title: cPanel/LiteSpeed Plugin Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title indicates active exploitation. No IOCs or attack indicators provided in pipeline output despite 'Exploited' in title, suggesting timeline of active threat.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cPanel web interface and LiteSpeed plugin endpoints for unusual HTTP patterns: POST requests to /scripts/ or plugin endpoints, suspicious parameter injection, or requests with shell metacharacters (|, &, ;, >, <). Correlate with subsequent authentication failures or privilege escalation attempts.

suggestion.title: Nginx Worker Process Crash or Rapid Restart Cycle
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'DoS and Code Execution' — vulnerability likely triggers worker crashes or restart loops. Should detect abnormal process lifecycle tied to Nginx vulnerability exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid Nginx worker process crashes (exit codes like 134 SIGABRT, segmentation faults) within short time windows, or master process repeatedly spawning new worker cohorts. Alert if crash frequency exceeds baseline and correlates with HTTP access logs showing malformed/suspicious requests.

suggestion.title: Suspicious HTTP Request Trigger Patterns for Nginx Poolslip
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'enables DoS and Code Execution' — exploitation requires crafted HTTP payload or request pattern. Should detect request characteristics known to trigger poolslip (e.g., pool exhaustion, malformed headers, or body size anomalies).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for HTTP requests to Nginx with unusual connection pool patterns (rapid connection reuse, exhaustion markers, or malformed chunked encoding). Look for requests that precede worker crashes or CPU spikes. Baseline normal connection lifecycle and alert on deviations tied to Nginx versions matching vulnerability range.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Child Process or System Call from Nginx Worker
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'Code Execution Attacks' — successful exploitation should spawn commands or system calls outside normal Nginx operation. Nginx workers typically do not execute arbitrary processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert if Nginx worker processes (nginx -g 'worker_processes') fork/exec child processes (shell, perl, python, or other interpreters). Flag system calls like execve, socket operations outside expected listener ports, or file writes to unexpected directories originating from Nginx uid.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Nginx Version Detected in Inventory
suggestion.rationale: Article title: 'Patch Now!' — vulnerable version ranges for poolslip should be detected in network inventory, configuration, or version banners. Prerequisite for all downstream detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query for Nginx version string (from banner, config, or inventory) matching vulnerable poolslip range. Cross-reference against published CVE details to identify affected versions. Flag systems running unpatched Nginx instances for remediation tracking.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthorized npm Package Publishing
suggestion.rationale: Article title specifies 'npm Adds 2FA-Gated Publishing' as control, confirming unauthorized publishing from compromised accounts is the attack vector being defended against.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm publish events from IP addresses or geographic locations outside CI/CD infrastructure baselines. Alert on first publish from new device/location, successful auth after 2FA failures, or API token creation followed immediately by package publication.

suggestion.title: Detect Malicious npm Package Installation Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly references 'Package Install Controls,' indicating malicious package installation is the attack outcome; detection must catch suspicious npm install operations before code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm install of packages with zero or extremely low download counts, packages released within 24 hours of first install attempt, packages with suspicious naming (typosquatting common libraries), or installation of versions predating public releases.

suggestion.title: Detect npm Account Credential Compromise
suggestion.rationale: 2FA-gated publishing requirement implies previous account takeover exploits; credential compromise is the prerequisite for malicious publishing. Detection must identify account access anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on failed npm login attempts from multiple IPs followed by successful auth, new API tokens issued without user action, password reset followed by immediate publication, or concurrent sessions from impossible geographic locations.

suggestion.title: Detect Anomalous npm Package Version Release Cadence
suggestion.rationale: Compromised maintainers release poisoned versions; rapid releases and unusual timing patterns indicate account compromise mid-attack, requiring real-time monitoring of package version publication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag packages releasing 3+ minor versions within 48 hours, releases at unusual UTC times (outside maintainer history), rapid succession releases followed by reverts/yanks, or publication by authors with no prior release history in that package.

suggestion.title: Detect 2FA Circumvention and Recovery Code Theft
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 2FA as 'gated' control, requiring detection of 2FA fatigue attacks, one-time recovery code exploitation, and 2FA setting tampering that bypass the new npm defense.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repeated 2FA prompts rejected/expired without valid OTP, recovery code redemptions without prior 2FA setup changes, backup code usage from impossible locations, or 2FA method disablements followed by publication.

suggestion.title: Detect npm Account Session Anomalies Post-Auth
suggestion.rationale: 2FA controls authenticate access but don't monitor post-auth behavior; detection must catch unusual account activity after successful 2FA passage to catch account takeover exploits that bypass 2FA.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag API token creation outside normal user workflow, publishing to unrelated packages, account settings changes (recovery email, password) via API vs. UI, or sessions using credentials from compromised CI/CD pipelines.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Package Installation from Non-Standard Repository
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attack exploits package managers; article explicitly states 'compromised packages' and 'Laravel-Lang' ecosystem.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect composer/npm install commands pulling packages from untrusted repositories or showing version mismatches. Monitor for package download from non-Packagist/NPM official hosts. Flag rapid package installation followed by credential harvesting footprints.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting Process Spawned Post-Package Load
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'credential stealer' payload—this is T1555/T1056 execution pattern. Should detect code execution with credential access intent immediately after package import.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PHP/Node process spawning child processes with known credential access patterns (e.g., lsass access, registry reads of HKLM\SAM, ~/.ssh directory access, environment variable enumeration) within 30s of package initialization.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Credentials to External C2
suggestion.rationale: 'Credential stealer' implies data exfiltration; article describes active threat—must detect outbound C2 communication with stolen data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTPS/DNS from PHP/Node processes to newly registered domains or IPs with high entropy subdomains (encoded data exfil). Correlate with credential harvesting process from UC #2.

suggestion.title: Package Manifest Tampering or Unexpected Autoload Execution
suggestion.rationale: Malware embedded in Laravel/PHP packages likely uses composer.json autoload or similar to execute on require()—this is the execution vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PHP autoload directives pointing to unusual paths or obfuscated code. Flag composer.json modifications in vendor/ post-install. Detect eval() or base64_decode() in package init files.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Shared Credentials from Compromised Package
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealer harvesting credentials from one host—should detect reuse of those credentials on other systems or services.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate credentials extracted by stealer UC#2 against authentication logs. Alert on extracted plaintext creds (DB passwords, API tokens, SSH keys) being used in authentication events on different hosts/services.

suggestion.title: Obfuscated or Hidden Malware Code in PHP Package Files
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealer functionality must be present but hidden from static review; common patterns include base64, gzip, or hex encoding.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect calls to base64_decode(), gzuncompress(), hex2bin(), eval(), or assert() in PHP package code. Flag large binary/hex strings in package files. Monitor for dynamic code execution patterns post-autoload.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-9082 Vulnerability Detection in Scanners
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'match against your vulnerability scanner' for CVE-2026-9082 and emphasizes CISA KEV status (confirmed exploited in wild) with federal remediation deadline 2026-05-27.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor vulnerability scanner results for CVE-2026-9082 presence across Drupal Core assets. Correlate scan detections with asset inventory to quantify exposure. Flag assets past patch deadline as critical priority given CISA KEV confirms active exploitation.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection Attempts Against Drupal Database Abstraction API
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability as 'SQL injection' targeting 'database abstraction API' via 'specially crafted requests'; this is the core attack mechanism and primary exploitation vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SQL syntax patterns, comment sequences (-- , /* */), union-based payloads, or parameter tampering in database abstraction API request parameters. Alert on database error patterns consistent with SQL injection probing.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation Following Database Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists 'privilege escalation' as outcome of successful exploitation; this represents the lateral/vertical privilege escalation phase post-initial compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect privilege escalation attempts or successful elevation correlated with prior SQL injection exploitation activity. Look for unexpected role changes, permission grants, or sudoers modifications on Drupal database users or web application accounts.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Process Execution (RCE)
suggestion.rationale: Article states exploitation 'could allow for...remote code execution'; detection of unexpected process spawning closes the kill chain from initial access through impact.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected process execution, shell invocation, or script interpretation on Drupal application servers correlated with SQL injection exploitation indicators. Flag child processes spawned from web application or database service contexts.

suggestion.title: Public-Facing Drupal Asset Inventory and Exposure Hunting
suggestion.rationale: Article recommends 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' and notes T1190 'implies active exploitation against exposed assets'; foundational detection is inventory and exposure assessment of Drupal instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Enumerate Drupal Core installations on public-facing infrastructure via passive fingerprinting (HTTP banners, known endpoint patterns, server headers). Cross-reference with patch status and correlate with federal remediation deadline 2026-05-27.

suggestion.title: Database Error Log Anomalies Matching SQL Injection Patterns
suggestion.rationale: SQL injection attacks generate database log artifacts; article specifies 'database abstraction API' as attack vector, making database logs an essential detection source for exploitation attempts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor database error logs for SQL syntax errors, constraint violations, unexpected query patterns, and API exceptions originating from HTTP-proxied parameters. Correlate error timestamps and malformed SQL content with suspicious web application activity.

suggestion.title: LNK File Command-Line PowerShell Execution from ZIP Archives
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'Attackers use LNK shortcuts to covertly execute PowerShell scripts hosted on external resources.' Describes full command line pattern. Pipeline did not generate initial-access UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for LNK files extracted from ZIP archives with cmd.exe or powershell.exe in target/arguments. Correlate ZIP extraction + LNK execution + PowerShell process creation within short timeframe.

suggestion.title: Registry Run Key Persistence via PowerShell Loader
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Creates "Run" registry key "YandexBrowser_setup" for "$temp\fixed.ps1" startup'. Clear HKCU\Run persistence mechanism not captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on registry modifications to HKCU/HKLM\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run with values pointing to %temp% paths or .ps1 files. Flag browser-named registry entries executing non-browser binaries.

suggestion.title: Termsrv.dll File Integrity Tampering for RDP Multi-User Access
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Multi-user RDP by patching termsrv.dll'. This is a distinct RDP abuse / persistence vector not mapped to any UC.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor System32 and SysWOW64 termsrv.dll for unexpected file modifications, size changes, or hash mismatches. Correlate with simultaneous RDP session anomalies (multiple concurrent logons, RDP service restarts).

suggestion.title: Reverse SSH Tunneling and Patched OpenSSH Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'Reverse SSH tunneling' and 'Patched OpenSSH' as C2 and persistence mechanisms. No detection rule generated for SSH abuse or tunnel establishment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SSH/sshd process creation from SYSTEM context or unusual parent processes. Alert on outbound SSH traffic from non-user accounts. Monitor for sshd listening on non-standard ports or SSH process spawning child proxies.

suggestion.title: Tor Client Execution for Covert C2 Tunneling
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Tor tunneling' is used by Cloud Atlas. No UC generated despite explicit mention of Tor as a C2 channel.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Tor executable launch from non-security-tool contexts. Alert on SOCKS5 proxy initialization on localhost:9050 or Tor node connections. Flag Tor spawned from PowerShell, rundll32, or service processes.

suggestion.title: PowerCloud Malware Payload Execution and Behavioral Correlation
suggestion.rationale: Article introduces PowerCloud as the group's 'new tool'. Despite explicit description of a new malware family, zero IOCs or detection patterns generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate PowerCloud execution with cascade indicators: fixed.ps1 stage 2 loading, credential enumerator spawn, network tunnel setup (SSH/Tor/RevSocks), or termsrv.dll tampering within seconds of PowerCloud startup.

suggestion.title: Drupal SQL Injection Attempt Detection (CVE-2026-9082)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'specially crafted requests to trigger arbitrary SQL injection' and 'exploitation attempts have been detected in the wild.' Pipeline generated no detection for the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL query logs and web access logs for SQL injection signatures targeting Drupal database abstraction layer. Detect payloads containing UNION, ORDER BY, SLEEP(), or other common SQLi markers in request parameters. Cross-reference against Drupal 8.9–11.3.x version fingerprints.

suggestion.title: Drupal Version Enumeration Against PostgreSQL Instances
suggestion.rationale: Attackers must first identify vulnerable Drupal versions before exploiting CVE-2026-9082. Article notes 'affects Drupal 8.9.x, 10.4.x–10.6.x, 11.0.x–11.3.x.' No detection for reconnaissance.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect requests to Drupal enumeration endpoints (/admin/modules, /changelog.txt, /INSTALL.txt, version headers) followed by SQL injection attempts within short time windows, particularly against PostgreSQL-backed instances.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution Post-SQL Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could result in remote code execution.' No detection for post-exploitation command execution following successful SQLi. This is the highest-impact phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unusual process creation (bash, sh, nc, python) spawned from web server processes (apache2, nginx, php-fpm) or SQL backend processes following SQL injection attempts. Correlate with PostgreSQL xp_cmdshell-equivalents (like PL/Python or shell_exec via SQL).

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Privilege Escalation via SQL Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists 'privilege escalation' as an impact. No detection for role/grant changes or user privilege modifications in PostgreSQL following SQL injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on ALTER ROLE, ALTER USER, GRANT, or CREATE ROLE commands in PostgreSQL audit logs, especially those modifying database-level permissions to 'superuser' or equivalent, following detected SQL injection attempts.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration via SQL Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article states SQLi 'resulting in unauthorized access, modification, or deletion of database data' and mentions 'information disclosure.' No detection for suspicious SELECT queries exfiltrating sensitive data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL logs for SELECT queries from the Drupal user/role accessing sensitive tables (users, password_reset_tokens, sessions, custom data) without normal application context. Detect high-volume data reads followed by outbound network traffic.

suggestion.title: Affected Drupal Instance Inventory Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 8 affected version ranges (8.9.x, 10.4.x–10.6.x, 11.0.x–11.3.x). Defenders need visibility into which instances run vulnerable versions. No asset inventory detection suggested.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Passive asset discovery: fingerprint HTTP response headers, CHANGELOG.txt, .htaccess, or module paths to identify Drupal version. Flag any instances matching 8.9.x or 10.4–10.6 or 11.0–11.2 (pre-patch) against vulnerability database. Generate remediation tickets.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted Domain Registration Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names typosquatting as primary attack method: 'domain name that closely resembles the legitimate one, but contains small additions or involves other changes' (fifa26[.]shop). Pipeline extracted zero domain IOCs or detection logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for domain registrations containing brand keywords (FIFA, World Cup, tournament names) with character substitutions, homoglyphs, or tld-swapping (shop, club, pro instead of official domains). Cluster by Levenshtein distance to legitimate brands and flag registrations <3 edits from known legitimate domains, especially with SSL issuance within 48h of registration.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Fake Registration Forms
suggestion.rationale: Article states victims enter personal data (name, email, phone) into forms that 'may not look strange at first' because they mimic legitimate FIFA ID registration. No detection use case for form-based credential harvesting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP POST submissions of email, phone, name, or identity fields to domains flagged as typosquatted or brand-masquerading. Correlate with rapid sequential submissions (>10 distinct email addresses from same source IP to same endpoint within 1h) indicating credential stuffing or automation. Flag requests originating from Tor/proxy exit nodes.

suggestion.title: Phishing Link Distribution via Social Media and Sponsored Ads
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions: 'Some victims may reach these websites through sponsored search results, while others click on ads on social media or links in email messages.' Pipeline captured zero initial-access vectors.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for URLs to typosquatted/brand-masquerading domains appearing in email messages, social media posts, and SEM ad placements. Flag ad accounts created with new payment methods, registered with credential-stuffed credentials, or bidding on high-commercial-intent keywords (tickets, merchandise, official). Correlate ad-spend patterns with credential-submission spikes on destination domains.

suggestion.title: Fake Payment Form Credit Card Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article details payment step: 'Once you enter your card details, it goes straight to the people behind the fake site' and 'Once entered into the form, your payments details would travel into the hands of the cybercriminal.' Pipeline produced no collection-phase detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP POST containing PAN, CVV, or expiry date fields sent to domains flagged as phishing infrastructure. Detect submissions where card data is NOT passed to legitimate payment processor endpoints (Stripe, Square, PayPal) but instead logged/exfiltrated to attacker infrastructure. Monitor for card-data exfiltration to domains with no legitimate e-commerce registration or PCI compliance history.

suggestion.title: Cloned Website Visual and Structural Mirroring
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attackers copying 'the look and feel of FIFA's official site, including the colors, layout, navigation and ticketing flow' for legitimacy. Pipeline missed infrastructure-indicator use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor newly registered domains hosting web content with >80% visual similarity to known legitimate brand sites (DOM tree alignment, CSS fingerprint matching). Correlate with indicators: self-signed certs, registrar patterns tied to phishing campaigns, WHOIS privacy, shared infrastructure with other phishing domains, rapid cert issuance.

suggestion.title: E-commerce Scam Page Behavior Clustering
suggestion.rationale: Article documents complete scam workflows: registration flow + merchandise cart + payment page, then ticket flow + payment page. Pipeline extracted zero behavioral patterns from these multi-step fraud sequences.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify domains exhibiting multi-stage fraud patterns: user registration endpoint (collecting PII) followed by product catalog/cart pages, followed by payment form submissions with no legitimate payment processor integration. Flag when same domain hosts disjoint personas (World Cup 2026 ticketing AND merchandise AND hospitality packages) with identical forms, suggesting template-based fraud infrastructure.

suggestion.title: F5 BIG-IP admin panel access from unusual network origin
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack began with 'exposed F5 BIG-IP edge appliance'—initial access foothold is explicit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor F5 BIG-IP /admin or /tmui paths for authentication attempts from unexpected sources, particularly non-corporate IP ranges. Correlate with successful logins followed by config changes or process execution on appliance.

suggestion.title: Kerberos relay to service account compromise
suggestion.rationale: Description explicitly mentions 'attempted Kerberos relay'—critical credential-access technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Kerberos protocol traffic from non-domain-joined hosts or across trust boundaries. Detect relay attacks via unusual ticket-granting-service requests or NTLM relay patterns (e.g., SMB signing disabled, cross-service delegation).

suggestion.title: Confluence instance pivoting from external appliance
suggestion.rationale: Article describes lateral movement from F5 to 'internal Confluence server for credential theft'—internal-network discovery and application targeting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Confluence for access patterns originating from F5 internal IP or shared infrastructure subnets. Flag unusual authentication methods (bearer tokens, API key usage by F5 components) and bulk user/group enumeration.

suggestion.title: Bulk credential extraction from Confluence user store
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'credential theft'—implies bulk extraction of user hashes or tokens from Confluence database or authentication store.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected SQL queries to Confluence user tables, file access to confluence.cfg.xml or Java keystore files, or process spawning with high-volume data reads from application directories.

suggestion.title: Linux reverse-shell post-exploitation activity
suggestion.rationale: Title flags 'multi-stage Linux intrusion'—implies payload execution and command-and-control after pivoting into enterprise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for shell spawning by Java/Confluence processes, outbound DNS queries for dynamic DNS or suspicious TLDs, or data exfiltration over non-standard HTTP/HTTPS ports.

suggestion.title: Post-exploitation persistence via cron or systemd
suggestion.rationale: Multi-stage attack implies attacker maintained access—Linux persistence mechanisms are standard post-compromise technique.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor crontab, /etc/cron.d/, systemd service files, and ~/.ssh/authorized_keys for unexpected modifications. Alert on unusual shell scripts created in standard persistence paths.

suggestion.title: Prometheus Malware Execution Post-Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly references 'Prometheus Phishing Malware'—the pipeline should have flagged process execution, command-line patterns, and registry modifications consistent with this malware family's known post-execution behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Look for suspicious child processes spawned from email clients (Outlook, Thunderbird) or WebView hosts, especially PowerShell or cmd.exe with obfuscated arguments, encoding (base64, XOR), or LSASS/registry access indicative of credential theft. Prometheus variants frequently execute in-memory payloads and access Windows Credential Manager.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email Delivery to Ukrainian Government Addresses
suggestion.rationale: Article states Ghostwriter 'Targets Ukraine Government Entities' with phishing—pipeline should extract email IOCs, sender patterns, subject line keywords, and attachment file hashes associated with this campaign.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails from external senders with display names spoofing Ukrainian government domains, weaponized Office documents (.doc, .xls) with embedded macros/OLE objects, or links to attacker-controlled infrastructure. Cross-reference recipient address blocks against known .gov.ua and security-relevant domain lists.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting via Prometheus Info-Stealer
suggestion.rationale: Prometheus is documented as an info stealer with credential-dumping capabilities; pipeline missed detection logic for LSASS access, Credential Manager enumeration, or suspicious WMI queries targeting password vaults.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process attempts to access System32\config\SAM, HKLM\SAM registry hives, or WinRM/WMI queries enumerating local accounts. Flag suspicious access to chrome.exe, firefox.exe, or edge.exe address spaces (browser credential harvesting via DLL injection or direct memory read).

suggestion.title: Ghostwriter APT Command-and-Control Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Article names Ghostwriter as the threat actor—critical miss that no IOCs or C2 domains/IPs were extracted for this known APT's infrastructure patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS beacons to known Ghostwriter C2 infrastructure (historical IOC databases: abuse.ch, OSINT sources). Flag DNS queries for dynamic DNS providers and suspicious outbound connections on non-standard ports from compromised endpoints in .gov.ua space.

suggestion.title: HTTP 5xx errors on YesWiki Bazar form-import — SQLi syntax error leakage
suggestion.rationale: Article states injection into INSERT statement; malformed SQL will generate database errors (500 responses) with potential error detail leakage. Current detections miss error-driven exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor POST requests to Bazar form-import endpoint followed by HTTP 5xx responses within 1 second. Elevated error rates from single source in short timeframe indicate SQLi attempt. Correlate with response body containing SQL keywords (syntax, column, table).

suggestion.title: Abnormal response time patterns on YesWiki Bazar form-import POST
suggestion.rationale: Blind SQL injection often uses time-based inference (SLEEP, BENCHMARK). Article mentions 'blind SQLi extraction loop'—time-delay techniques would show request latencies 5-30s+ vs. typical <1s form submissions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag POST requests to *Bazar*vue=formulaire* with response_time > 5000ms (5 sec) from non-automated sources or sequential requests from same src with increasing delay patterns.

suggestion.title: Database password hash extraction — yeswiki_users table access patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'read the full database, including yeswiki_users.password hashes.' No detection covers the credential-access phase after exploitation. Should monitor for direct database queries or unusual result sets.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor database logs for SELECT queries against yeswiki_users table with WHERE clause variations (e.g., OR 1=1, UNION), especially if originating from web application context or unauthenticated connections.

suggestion.title: Rapid SQL UNION/comment injection attempts in POST parameters
suggestion.rationale: Standard SQLi payloads use UNION clauses or SQL comments (--,#) to extract data. No detection looks for injection syntax in request payloads themselves.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Inspect POST parameters to Bazar endpoint for keywords: UNION, SELECT, --, #, /**/. Single occurrence may be benign; 3+ attempts from same source in 10 min indicates exploitation.

suggestion.title: C2 Traffic Over Telecom ISP Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Command-and-Control Operations' abusing telecom networks, but pipeline extracted zero network-based C2 use cases. Title indicates attackers leveraged Middle East telecom networks as C2 infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous C2 traffic patterns originating from or transiting through ISP ASN ranges belonging to major Middle East telecom operators. Look for beaconing behavior, suspicious DNS resolutions to known C2 domains, and HTTP/HTTPS traffic with C2 signatures from telecom provider IP blocks.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Across Telecom Network Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Title mentions 'large-scale' operations on telecom networks, implying multi-host compromise and lateral movement. No lateral movement UCs generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SSH or RDP connections between telecom infrastructure assets (routers, switches, management servers) involving credentials or service accounts. Flag lateral movement patterns typical of botnet seeding or network propagation across carrier backbone.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Access to Telecom Management Interfaces
suggestion.rationale: To establish C2 on telecom networks, attackers must compromise management/control plane. No initial access or persistence UCs present. Article title implies successful unauthorized telecom infrastructure access.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect login attempts to telecom carrier management portals (NMS/EMS systems) from unusual geographies, IPs, or off-hours. Flag successful authentication after failed attempts, service account usage for interactive login, and API token generation for infrastructure access.

suggestion.title: Suspicious art-template npm Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names art-template as the compromised package. Pipeline should flag installations of this specific package version range or detect package downloads with anomalous behavior patterns. Article states 'Hackers Backdoor Popular art-template npm Package.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm install/update events targeting art-template with unusual checksums, version jumps, or zero-day versions. Correlate with subsequent outbound network connections from node processes.

suggestion.title: Unsigned or Tampered Post-Install Script Execution from Malicious npm Package
suggestion.rationale: Watering-hole attacks via npm typically execute via postinstall scripts. Article describes 'backdoor' injection suggesting code execution phase. Article: 'Backdoor Popular art-template npm Package.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process creation with parent=npm or child=node originating from node_modules/.bin/* with unusual command-line arguments, unusual child processes (curl, wget, bash), or network I/O immediately after package installation.

suggestion.title: Outbound Network Activity from art-template Node Process to Suspicious C2 Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Watering-hole attacks require callback to attacker infrastructure for payload delivery or exfiltration. Article: 'Launch Watering-Hole Attacks' implies C2 communication phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS queries or TCP/UDP connections initiated by node.exe/node processes immediately after art-template install, especially to newly registered or low-reputation domains, or to IPs geographically inconsistent with user profile.

suggestion.title: npm Package Metadata Tampering or Version Confusion Attack
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks often exploit package registry inconsistencies or dependency confusion. Article states 'Hackers Backdoor' npm package, implying takeover or malicious upload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on package version rollbacks, unexpected checksum changes for published art-template versions, or installation of pre-release/beta versions from public registry that differ from company-approved pinned versions.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Malicious art-template Module Load at Node Startup
suggestion.rationale: Backdoored npm modules persist via require() chain. Article implies persistent backdoor: 'Backdoor Popular art-template npm Package.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor art-template source files in node_modules for unexpected modifications post-installation. Flag if art-template's index.js, package.json scripts, or dependencies deviate from public npm registry baseline.

suggestion.title: Suspicious .BAT execution from user-writable temp or download directories
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'malicious batch files' as the delivery mechanism; batch execution is the primary execution vector for Banana RAT.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .bat or .cmd files executed from %TEMP%, %USERPROFILE%\Downloads, or %AppData%\Local\Temp with parent process being explorer.exe, outlook.exe, or browser processes. Cross-reference against known malware hash libraries.

suggestion.title: Email attachment: NF-e invoice documents with embedded or attached batch files
suggestion.rationale: Attack chain begins with 'NF-e Invoice Lures'—a social-engineering vector targeting Brazilian entities; batch files are the payload wrapper.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag emails with .nfe/.xml attachments paired with or containing .bat, .cmd, .ps1 payloads. Look for double-extension tricks (e.g., invoice.xml.bat) and suspicious macros or embedded scripts in Office documents labeled as NF-e invoices.

suggestion.title: Registry modification for Banana RAT persistence (Run keys / shell associations)
suggestion.rationale: RATs typically establish persistence; without full article body, standard Banana RAT behavior implies registry-based autostart mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run and HKLM equivalents for additions referencing .bat, .cmd, or batch-derived executable paths. Cross-correlate with recent batch file execution events.

suggestion.title: Banana RAT C2 beacon detection via network signatures / rare outbound ports
suggestion.rationale: RAT delivery is incomplete without command-and-control; article implies post-exploitation C2 phase but no network IOCs were extracted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Hunt for outbound connections on non-standard ports (e.g., >10000) from processes spawned by batch execution or explorer.exe. Alert on DNS queries to typosquatted or newly registered domains; correlate with Banana RAT YARA rules if available.

suggestion.title: Batch script obfuscation or embedded PowerShell payloads within .BAT files
suggestion.rationale: Batch files hosting more sophisticated payloads (PowerShell, VBScript, inline command execution) are common evasion tactics for RAT delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect batch files calling powershell.exe with -enc, -nop, or -window hidden flags; monitor for cmd.exe spawning unusual child processes. Look for batch files containing hex-encoded or Base64-encoded payloads.

suggestion.title: User-executed compressed files containing batch + decoy NF-e document
suggestion.rationale: Banana RAT delivery often bundles the batch malware with a decoy PDF or XLS to avoid suspicion; user clicks → decompression → execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .zip, .rar, .7z files extracted from Downloads or Temp containing both .bat and document files (*.pdf, *.xls, *.xml). Monitor for immediate execution of nested .bat files post-extraction.

suggestion.title: Backdoored FreePBX Module Installation or Modification
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly mentions 'six-layer persistence' on FreePBX. Compromised/rogue modules are a standard persistence mechanism for PBX systems—no detection use case generated despite this being the primary attack substrate.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FreePBX module installation directories and admin UI for unauthorized module adds/updates outside change windows. Alert on module file modifications, unexpected module loads in Asterisk process logs, and module installation by non-administrative accounts.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Admin Account Creation in FreePBX
suggestion.rationale: Six-layer persistence typically includes backdoor user creation for persistence. Article describes multi-layer access maintenance; attacker-created privileged accounts are a standard technique—no use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track creation of new FreePBX admin users, especially during off-hours or by non-administrative accounts. Monitor for direct database modifications to user/admin tables and privilege escalation of existing credentials.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Cron Job or Init Script on FreePBX Host
suggestion.rationale: FreePBX typically runs on Linux. Multi-layer persistence leverages cron jobs and boot scripts—no detection use case for this common Linux persistence layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected cron additions in /etc/cron.d/ and user crontabs, particularly those created by non-service accounts or executing network utilities. Alert on init script modifications and new startup services outside maintenance windows.

suggestion.title: Web Shell Planted in FreePBX Web Directory
suggestion.rationale: VoIP systems with web interfaces are targets for web shell placement. Six-layer persistence implies multiple backdoors; web shells enable persistent remote code execution—no use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FreePBX web root (/var/www/html/freepbx or equivalent) for newly created executable files (PHP, CGI). Alert on web server processes spawning shell commands and on file modifications to existing application files.

suggestion.title: Asterisk Extension Config Tampering for Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article targets FreePBX/Asterisk specifically. Attackers maintain persistence by modifying dialplan/extension configs to route calls or inject backdoors—no Asterisk-specific persistence use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor extension.conf, sip.conf, and dialplan files for modifications. Alert on addition of suspicious extensions, context changes, or routing rule modifications outside change control.

suggestion.title: Command & Control Communication from FreePBX Host
suggestion.rationale: Multi-layer persistence requires operator communication channels. Title mentions persistence maintenance implying C2—no detection use case for outbound persistence or reverse shells.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FreePBX host for unexpected outbound connections to non-standard ports and unknown destinations from non-service processes. Alert on DNS queries to suspicious domains and reverse shell indicators (Bash/Perl network activity from root).

suggestion.title: Detect Botnet Command and Control Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Article establishes 'DDoS-for-hire' service model, requiring active C2 to coordinate attacks across bot nodes. No detection logic was generated for botnet-to-server communication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect periodic outbound connections to fixed infrastructure, encrypted tunnel establishment, or DNS queries to known botnet C2 domains. Flag hosts with persistent beaconing patterns to non-standard ports.

suggestion.title: Detect Outbound DDoS Traffic from Compromised Endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies 'DDoS attacks' as the operational impact. Infected endpoints will exhibit sustained high-volume outbound traffic with DDoS signatures (SYN floods, UDP floods, HTTP floods).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on sustained traffic from endpoint to multiple external destinations with non-standard ports, or traffic with volumetric/protocol-based DDoS patterns. Baseline normal user behavior and alert on outliers.

suggestion.title: Detect Botnet Malware Execution
suggestion.rationale: Botnet operation requires malware execution on compromised systems. Article establishes existence of Kimwolf botnet but no detection logic for malware binary execution or process hollowing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned binaries spawning network connections, suspicious child processes from user-writable directories, or process injection patterns typical of bot loaders.

suggestion.title: Detect Anomalous Bulk Network Enumeration from Single Host
suggestion.rationale: DDoS botnets exhibit connection patterns atypical of user behavior: simultaneous or rapid-fire connections to many destinations. Article describes botnet operation but no detection for reconnaissance-phase activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag hosts attempting 50+ unique outbound connections within 5-minute window, particularly on ports 135, 445, 22, or to private IP ranges. Correlate with C2 communication patterns.

suggestion.title: Detect DDoS-for-Hire Service Registration and Operational Setup
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes the 'DDoS-for-hire' service model. Initial setup phase includes C2 infrastructure provisioning, bot distribution, and customer onboarding. No use case addresses pre-attack operational setup.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect staging of botnet payloads via email or malicious hosting infrastructure, suspicious VPS/hosting registrations by threat actors, or command execution preparing C2 infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Detect Multiple Hosts Attacking Same Target Simultaneously
suggestion.rationale: DDoS-for-hire model implies coordinated multi-host attacks. Article describes DDoS service but no detection logic for the orchestrated attack coordination observable from victim perspective.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: From target network perspective: detect traffic from many source IPs converging on same service port/endpoint within seconds, volumetric surges with consistent request patterns, or geographic distribution of attack sources.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Vulnerable Driver Load from User-Writable Path
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD relies on staging known-vulnerable drivers (e.g., RTCore64.sys, GLCKIo2.sys) in non-standard locations before exploitation. Article title emphasizes 'making exploitable'—staging step is critical. Detect driver loads from %TEMP%, Downloads, AppData.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on .sys file loads initiated by user-mode processes from temporary, user home, or AppData directories. BYOVD exploitation requires the driver binary to be staged before service registration and load.

suggestion.title: Unsigned or Expired-Publisher Driver Load Followed by SYSTEM Process Creation
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses exploitation technique; successful BYOVD yields immediate privilege escalation. Correlate suspicious driver load with token elevation or unexpected SYSTEM-level child process.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate driver load by low-privilege user with immediate SYSTEM-level process creation within 1-5 seconds by same parent. BYOVD exploitation is fast and deterministic.

suggestion.title: Windows Service Installation Targeting Vulnerable Driver Name Pattern
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD requires service registration to trigger driver load at boot or on-demand. Monitor for service creation with known-vulnerable driver executable paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect registry modifications to HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services with ImagePath pointing to .sys files in user directories or with names matching historical BYOVD driver list.

suggestion.title: Kernel Callback or Minifilter Registration Post-Privilege Escalation
suggestion.rationale: After gaining SYSTEM via BYOVD, attackers use elevated context to install kernel callbacks for EDR evasion or persistence. Article's focus on 'exploitable' suggests post-exploitation activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services\FileSystem\Filters for new minifilter installations or suspicious callback registration DLLs within 10 seconds of SYSTEM elevation event.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Driver-Mediated Kernel Object Access from User Mode
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD exploitation requires calling driver IOCTLs to manipulate kernel state. Detect user-mode process making unusual kernel object accesses (handles, registry, memory) through device driver interface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on user-mode processes opening handles to \Device\ or \Global?? namespace objects shortly after suspicious driver load, indicating IOCTL-based kernel exploitation attempt.

suggestion.title: EDR/AV Kernel Hook Disablement Post-BYOVD Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Final stage of BYOVD attack: use newly acquired kernel privileges to disable security callbacks. Monitor for minifilter unload, hook disablement, or security driver service termination.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect registry modifications removing FileSystem\Filters entries, disabling driver load order, or stopping kernel-mode security services within 30 seconds of SYSTEM-level process creation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious GitHub Actions Workflow File Creation or Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malicious CI/CD workflows injected into 5,561 repos; pipeline missed detection for workflow modification, which is the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for creation or modification of .github/workflows/*.yml files within forked or compromised repositories, especially in batch patterns. Flag workflows containing obfuscated scripts, encoded commands, or references to external URLs not typical of legitimate CI/CD. Correlate with repository fork or access pattern anomalies.

suggestion.title: CI/CD Credential Exfiltration via Workflow Logs or Environment Variables
suggestion.rationale: Malicious workflows would need to exfiltrate secrets; article focuses on CI/CD compromise but no detection for credentials being accessed or exported.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GitHub Actions workflows accessing GITHUB_TOKEN, ACTIONS_RUNTIME_TOKEN, or custom secrets in unusual contexts. Flag workflows that echo, print, or transmit environment variables to external URLs or logging services.

suggestion.title: Mass Repository Forking or Pull Request Injection Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Attack targeted 5,561 repos; pipeline did not capture detection for large-scale repository compromise or mass PR injection tactics.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect single user/service account creating 50+ forks, pull requests, or commits across unrelated repositories within a short time window. Flag pull requests that modify .github/workflows directories and are merged without proper review.

suggestion.title: Malicious Command Execution in GitHub Actions Runner Context
suggestion.rationale: Malicious workflows execute arbitrary commands; no detection rule for suspicious shell commands or process spawning within CI/CD runners.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Actions job logs for base64 decoding, PowerShell -EncodedCommand, curl piped to bash, or wget redirects to /tmp. Flag execution of curl/wget to download files from non-whitelisted external domains during CI/CD execution.

suggestion.title: Compromised GitHub Token or PAT Usage from Unusual IP/Geolocation
suggestion.rationale: Article implies credential compromise; pipeline missed detection for stolen tokens used from atypical access patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline for GitHub token usage (IP, geolocation, time-of-day, user-agent). Alert on tokens used from IP ranges inconsistent with known organizational networks or suddenly accessing hundreds of repositories.

suggestion.title: Supply Chain Artifact Contamination via Build Artifacts or Dependencies
suggestion.rationale: CI/CD compromise often results in poisoned build artifacts; no detection rule for unusual artifact creation or publication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected artifact builds/publishes from compromised GitHub Actions (version changes not matching commits, artifacts published to wrong registries, size anomalies). Cross-reference artifact hashes against known-good builds.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Workflow File Modification by Malicious Actor
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'mass GitHub Actions secret exfiltration' implying workflow compromise. Attack requires modifying .github/workflows files to inject exfiltration logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for workflow YAML file commits with new steps executing `curl`, `wget`, or `POST` requests to external domains not in baseline. Alert on workflows adding `secrets` context access in conditionals or new environment variable exports to untrusted hosts.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Secret Exfiltration via Environment Variables
suggestion.rationale: Core attack vector in 'secret exfiltration' campaign: malicious workflows export or log `${{ secrets.* }}` to external handlers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag workflow logs containing `echo` / `printf` of secret patterns, base64-encoded credential blocks, or POSTs to external URLs in Actions runner context. Correlate with `runner.os` metadata to identify exfiltration timing.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Runner Outbound Connection to Suspicious External IP
suggestion.rationale: Mass exfiltration requires delivery infrastructure; article implies 5,500+ repos contacted attacker-controlled endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track outbound connections from GitHub-hosted runners (IP range 140.82.112.0/20) to non-GitHub, non-CDN IPv4/domain destinations. Baseline runner egress and alert on deviations. Correlate with workflow execution timing.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Job Step Executing Encoded Payload
suggestion.rationale: Obfuscation technique common in compromised workflows to evade inline detection of malicious commands.
