suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for base64/hex decoding pipes (`base64 -d`, `xxd -r`) in workflow step shells or PowerShell `[Convert]::FromBase64String` followed by pipe to `bash`/`cmd`. Flag multi-stage command injection in single step.

suggestion.title: Dependency Injection via Compromised GitHub Action (Upstream Supply Chain)
suggestion.rationale: If attack achieved scale across 5,500+ repos, likely vector was compromised action in marketplace or popular reusable workflow.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor GitHub Action dependency version pins for unexpected changes (floating tags like `@main`, `@v*` resolving to new commits). Alert when action source repo changes authorship, visibility, or receives large code commits unrelated to patch cycles.

suggestion.title: Mass Secrets Rotation Post-Detection of Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Detection UC: after compromise identified, track organizational response—bulk secret rotation across affected repos indicates breach confirmation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate bulk secret deletions/recreations within 1-hour window across 10+ repositories. Compare to baseline org maintenance cadence. High cardinality on `secret_name` changed in short timeframe may indicate incident response.

suggestion.title: Zero-Day Exploitation Attempt via Public-Facing Application
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states '10,000+ 0-Days' as the discovery focus. Title phrase 'Uncovers 10,000+ 0-Days in Project Glasswing' establishes vulnerability exploitation as the core threat mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalous process execution, unexpected inbound connections, or privilege escalation attempts targeting known zero-day CVE vectors. Flag indicators of exploitation attempts against cloud/AI infrastructure, particularly those matching known Glasswing-related attack signatures once IOCs are recovered.

suggestion.title: Project Glasswing Campaign Identifier Tracking
suggestion.rationale: Article title contains campaign/project codename 'Project Glasswing'—a tracking identifier the pipeline should maintain across incidents. Phrase 'Project Glasswing' is a proper noun requiring observable tracking.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track all mentions, infrastructure, and threat artifacts associated with 'Project Glasswing' and 'Claude Mythos Preview' codenames. Establish baseline for campaign signatures and command-and-control patterns once article body is fully parsed.

suggestion.title: Vulnerability Research Infrastructure Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article context suggests vulnerability disclosure or research tooling ('Anthropic's Claude Mythos Preview Uncovers...'). Phrase 'Uncovers 10,000+ 0-Days' indicates systematic vulnerability scanning or exploitation framework activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for mass-scale vulnerability scanning, fuzzing, or exploitation tool execution. Flag unusual activity patterns from AI/LLM research environments, API scanning, or systematic enumeration of application attack surfaces.

suggestion.title: Malicious Laravel-Lang Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Compromised 233 Versions of Laravel-Lang Packages'—organizations using this localization dependency need runtime alerting when versions fall within poisoned ranges. Cite exact phrase for package name and version count.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor composer install/update logs and dependency lock files for Laravel-Lang versions 1.0–233 (range inferred from article). Alert on package pulls from primary repository matching timestamps of compromise window. Correlate with post-install process execution and unexpected network connections from PHP worker processes.

suggestion.title: GitHub Account Takeover – Mass Repository Commits
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Hacking 700 GitHub Repos'—suggests credential or OAuth token compromise enabling simultaneous unauthorized commits across victim repositories. Pipeline missed initial-access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on GitHub API calls committing to 10+ unrelated repositories within 1 hour from single user/PAT. Flag commits from non-whitelisted IPs or geolocations. Baseline per-maintainer repo scope and commit frequency; alert on deviations >200%. Detect missing MFA during sensitive commit windows.

suggestion.title: Supply-Chain Package Poisoning Detection
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: '233 Versions' implies systematic code injection into package build/release. Article lacks post-compromise analysis details, but poisoning is implicit. Cite: 'Compromised 233 Versions.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Ingest package source diffs or commit SHAs. Alert on unexpected file additions to Laravel-Lang repo (non-.php/.json changes, obfuscated JS). Verify package signatures/checksums against published manifests. Flag commits by non-maintainer accounts or without required code-review approvals.

suggestion.title: Downstream Laravel Application Package Update – Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Organizations running Laravel pulling auto-updates will execute compromised Laravel-Lang code. Article implies impact to dependent projects. Cite: 'Compromised 233 Versions of Laravel-Lang Packages' as the trigger for downstream detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate composer/package manager update timestamps with unexpected PHP process spawning, curl/exec system calls, or outbound network connections to C2 domains within 5 minutes. Baseline post-update process behavior per Laravel app; alert on beaconing or shell-command execution.

suggestion.title: GitHub PAT / SSH Key Compromise – Credential Reuse
suggestion.rationale: 700 repos hacked suggests stolen developer credentials (PAT, SSH key, or session token). Pipeline missed credential-access phase entirely. Cite: '700 GitHub Repos.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for GitHub API token creation from non-standard clients (curl, Invoke-WebRequest, headless scripts). Alert on SSH key additions to dormant accounts. Flag PAT usage from multiple geolocations <1 hour apart. Correlate with uncharacteristic git commit timing and targets (700-repo bulk activity).

suggestion.title: Package Metadata Tampering – Version Tag Spoofing
suggestion.rationale: 233 compromised versions suggest either release-pipeline hijacking or tag manipulation. Article doesn't detail mechanism, but version proliferation is attack hallmark. Cite: '233 Versions.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Packagist / GitHub Releases for Laravel-Lang version releases lacking corresponding source tags or signed commits. Alert on version bumps from non-maintainer accounts. Compare release artifact checksums against git commit SHAs; flag mismatches indicating post-build tampering.

suggestion.title: SSH Activity from F5 BIG-IP Management Address Space
suggestion.rationale: Article headline explicitly states attackers 'Gain SSH Access and Pivot Into Enterprise Linux Networks' using the compromised F5—establishes SSH as the lateral-movement method. Pipeline generated zero detection for this core attack step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SSH connections (TCP 22, 443, or non-standard ports) originating from F5 BIG-IP management CIDR blocks or hostnames to internal Linux assets. Correlate with F5 compromise indicators or failed exploitation attempts. Prioritize failed-then-successful auth sequences.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of F5 BIG-IP Public-Facing Interface
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'Hackers Exploit F5 BIG-IP Appliance'—this is the initial-access vector. No kill-chain reconstruction or IOCs surfaced this critical vulnerability-exploitation phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor F5 management and data-plane interfaces for anomalous HTTP requests, including malformed payloads, known exploit signatures, paths to sensitive endpoints (/admin, /console), or HTTP status sequences (404→200) indicative of successful exploitation. Alert on repeated attempts from external IPs.

suggestion.title: Command Execution on Linux Hosts via SSH from Infrastructure Appliance
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attackers 'Pivot Into Enterprise Linux Networks'—implies post-SSH execution phase entirely absent from pipeline output. This is the impact/execution step of the attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag interactive shell spawns, process launches, or command execution on Linux systems immediately following successful SSH authentication from untrusted sources (especially network appliances). Look for privilege-escalation attempts (sudo, su) or credential-dumping tools post-login.

suggestion.title: Outbound Callback to flipboxstudio.info C2 Domain
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'The injected code acted as a dropper that downloaded a second payload from the attacker's command and control server at flipboxstudio[.]info.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any DNS queries or HTTP/HTTPS connections to flipboxstudio[.]info and variants. Prioritize connections from PHP processes, Composer environments, or development machines. Correlate with package install/update timestamps.

suggestion.title: Malicious Composer Package Autoload Execution (src/helpers.php)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes: 'The malicious releases introduced a malicious file named src/helpers.php, which was automatically loaded by Composer' via the autoload section of composer.json.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PHP execution of helpers.php from vendor directories. Alert on unexpected presence or modification of helpers.php in laravel-lang package installations. Track file creation in vendor/laravel-lang/* with suspicious autoload patterns.

suggestion.title: Rapid Supply-Chain Tag Rewriting Across Package Repos
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'the attacker rewrote every existing git tag in each repository to point at a new malicious commit' across four Laravel Lang repos 'The rewrites started at 22:32 UTC against laravel-lang/lang...and finished by 00:00 UTC against laravel-lang/actions.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk tag rewrites or force-pushes targeting multiple repos in short timeframes, especially from single compromised credential. Monitor for tag references changing to point to fork commits or non-standard ref paths. Flag org-wide push access used to rewrite existing version tags.

suggestion.title: DebugElevator Windows Infostealer Staging from Temp Directory
suggestion.rationale: Article documents: 'the PHP payload also extracts a base64-encoded executable embedded within the file, which is written to the %TEMP% folder as a random .exe filename, and then launched' named 'DebugElevator' targeting Chrome, Brave, Edge.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on arbitrary .exe execution from %TEMP% folder preceded by PHP runtime activity. Monitor for random-named executables in TEMP with recent write timestamps. Correlate with Composer installation events or package update operations.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting from Environment Variables and Cloud Config Files
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'harvests cloud credentials, Kubernetes secrets, Vault tokens, Git credentials, CI/CD secrets, SSH keys...local `.env` configuration files' and contains 'regular expression patterns used to extract AWS keys, GitHub tokens, Slack tokens, Stripe secrets, database credentials, JWTs, SSH private keys.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on single process reading from ~/.ssh, ~/.aws, ~/.env, and cloud credential stores in rapid sequence. Monitor for file handle opens to Kubernetes config paths (/var/run/secrets/kubernetes.io). Correlate suspicious regex compilation or string matching operations with credential file access.

suggestion.title: App-Bound Encryption Key Extraction from Chrome Credential Storage
suggestion.rationale: Article describes DebugElevator is 'designed to target Chrome, Brave, and Edge, and extract App-Bound Encryption keys needed to decrypt stored browser credentials.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on non-browser process accessing Chrome/Brave/Edge registry hives (HKCU\Software\Google\Chrome, HKCU\Software\BraveSoftware\Brave, HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Edge). Monitor for DebugElevator process attempting registry queries for Local State or Encrypted Key Storage. Flag unexpected credential API calls from non-browser parents.

suggestion.title: Suspicious PHP Package Installation from Composer
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malicious Laravel-Lang packages delivered via supply chain. No detection for package manager activity despite this being the initial access vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor composer install/update commands for execution context, version mismatches, and elevated privileges. Alert on unexpected package sources or pre/post-install script execution in non-development environments.

suggestion.title: Credential Collection via Injected PHP Code
suggestion.rationale: Article states stealer is 'cross-platform credential stealer' but no detection for credential access behavior post-compromise. Missing detection for memory dumps, password store access, or keylogging patterns initiated from PHP runtime.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PHP/Apache processes accessing credential stores (SAM, LSASS, Keychain), spawning LSASS threads, or invoking credential dumping utilities like mimikatz or rundll32 secretsdump variants.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Outbound HTTPS from PHP Application Runtime
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealer implies exfiltration. Article does not identify C2 domains/IPs but pipeline failed to recommend detection for data exfiltration phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of legitimate outbound HTTPS from web application servers. Flag new destinations, especially to non-CDN/non-service provider IP ranges. Monitor for high-volume POST/PUT requests encoding exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Vendor Directory Modifications Post-Package Update
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromise implies malicious code injection into vendor/laravel-lang/. Pipeline missed filesystem detection opportunity for unauthorized code changes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor vendor/laravel-lang/ directory for file creation/modification outside of expected package manager windows. Alert on code injection patterns, new function definitions, or obfuscated code in autoload files.

suggestion.title: PHP Process Spawning Suspicious Child Processes
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealer functionality would require child process execution (credential dumping, exfil tools). Pipeline produced no execution-phase detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on web server PHP processes (apache2, php-fpm) spawning cmd.exe, powershell, bash, or curl/wget outside normal request handling. Track parent-child relationships and process creation frequency anomalies.

suggestion.title: Laravel Application Error Log Exfiltration Patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article describes malicious package delivery but no detection for post-infection visibility (logs, errors as side-channel for data exfil). Missing application-layer detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Laravel error logs and application logs for unusual volumes of sensitive data patterns (API keys, passwords, tokens, session IDs). Alert on log manipulation, clearing, or redirection to external services.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Autoload Files Execution via Composer
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The payload was hidden in a newly added file, src/helpers.php, and registered in composer.json under autoload.files. Composer's autoloader unconditionally requires every file in that list, so the malicious code runs at the very start of the PHP request lifecycle'—clear execution vector through package configuration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor composer.json for suspicious additions to autoload.files sections, especially newly-added helper or bootstrap files (helpers.php pattern). Alert on PHP process execution immediately following composer install or update with corresponding autoload.files entries. Baseline legitimate package autoload patterns by organizational standard.

suggestion.title: C2 Communication to flipboxstudio[.]info
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'fetches a second stage from https://flipboxstudio[.]info/payload and executes it in the background' and 'Collected data is encrypted and shipped out to https://flipboxstudio[.]info/exfil'—dual-purpose C2 infrastructure for command delivery and data exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag all DNS queries and HTTPS connections to flipboxstudio[.]info. Inspect proxy logs for outbound traffic to this domain. Correlate network indicators with PHP process lifecycle and timing of helpers.php execution. Monitor for POST/PUT operations to /payload or /exfil paths.

suggestion.title: Bulk Credential Harvesting from Local System
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'The second stage is a credential and secrets stealer... it walks through a long list of sources looking for anything of value: Cloud provider credentials... Kubernetes kubeconfig files, HashiCorp Vault tokens, and CI/CD secrets... SSH private keys... Application .env files... Browser data... Password manager vaults... Cryptocurrency wallet files and keystores'—comprehensive credential scraping.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PHP or child processes for sequential/bulk file access to credential storage paths: ~/.aws, ~/.kube, ~/.ssh, .env files, browser profile directories, password manager vaults (1Password, LastPass databases), crypto wallet locations. Alert on anomalous access patterns across multiple credential sources within short time windows.

suggestion.title: Infection Marker File Creation in Temporary Directories
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'It writes an infection marker to a per-host temporary directory so the host is only infected once'—infection persistence indicator that runs once per compromised host.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PHP process writes to system temp directories (/tmp, /var/tmp, %TEMP%) immediately following composer package installation. Flag small binary or marker files written shortly after helpers.php execution. Correlate with presence of src/helpers.php in package directories.

suggestion.title: Malicious Git Tag Resolution via Packagist Fork Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'the attacker leveraged a quirk of the GitHub-to-Packagist publishing flow: a Git tag created within an organization can resolve to a commit in a fork outside that organization. Packagist then ingested those tags and treated the fork commits as genuine releases'—supply chain repository manipulation at tag level.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Implement git tag provenance validation: flag tags created in official repos that resolve to commits outside the upstream organization. Monitor Packagist ingestion logs for discrepancies between tag origin and commit author/repository. Alert on bulk tag creation (700+ versions in days) across multiple packages in same namespace.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration Post-Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Collected data is encrypted and shipped out to https://flipboxstudio[.]info/exfil. After exfiltration, the stealer attempts to delete its dropped files'—final exfiltration phase with post-exploitation cleanup.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate credential access patterns (bulk reads from ~/.aws, ~/.ssh, .env) with outbound encrypted traffic to flipboxstudio[.]info within same time window. Monitor for large encrypted POST requests from PHP processes. Track file deletion activity following network exfiltration events (stealer cleanup behavior).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Laravel-Lang Composer Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Every Tag Across Multiple Composer Packages Rewritten' with malicious code. Pipeline did not generate detection for compromised package manager dependencies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on composer install/update of Laravel-Lang packages followed by unexpected child process spawning (curl, wget, PHP runtime in non-standard context) within 5 seconds. Cross-reference installed files against Packagist checksum integrity baseline.

suggestion.title: CI Environment Variable Enumeration and Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states attack 'designed to steal CI secrets.' Pipeline missed credential access phase where environment variables containing AWS keys, tokens, database passwords are extracted and transmitted.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PHP/composer processes spawning shell interpreters that invoke printenv, env, or grep against CI variable names (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, GITHUB_TOKEN, DB_PASSWORD, DOCKER_USERNAME). Alert on subsequent HTTP POST/PUT requests to non-whitelisted external IPs from same process.

suggestion.title: Repository Tag History Anomaly — Mass Rewrite Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'Every Tag Across Multiple Composer Packages Rewritten.' This is a repository integrity violation indicating package source tampering, detectable via Git audit logs or Packagist webhooks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect multiple tag deletions and recreations within narrow timeframe on Laravel-Lang repositories (query Packagist API or GitHub GraphQL for tag timeline anomalies). Alert on commits that modify package auto-load files or composer.json without corresponding CI/CD validation logs.

suggestion.title: Malicious PHP Code Injection in Vendor Directory
suggestion.rationale: Attack payload delivered via rewritten package tags as executable PHP. Pipeline should detect obfuscated initialization code injected into package bootstrap files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-composer-install, scan vendor/autoload.php and Laravel-Lang package source files for base64_decode, eval(), or proc_open calls. Flag unusual PHP startup files containing HTTP requests or environment variable collection logic.

suggestion.title: Outbound Exfiltration Traffic from CI Runner
suggestion.rationale: Stolen CI secrets must be transmitted to attacker infrastructure. Pipeline should detect unauthorized network egress from CI pipeline environments during package execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline of approved egress destinations for CI pipelines (GitHub, Docker Hub, package registries). Alert on any outbound connection to non-whitelisted IPs initiated by PHP/composer process, especially POST requests to non-standard ports with >5KB payloads (credential exfil signature).

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Secret Store Access Following Package Install
suggestion.rationale: With stolen CI credentials, attacker could access secret vaults (AWS Secrets Manager, Vault, GitHub Secrets API). Pipeline should detect credential store queries from unexpected sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on SecretsManager/Vault API calls (GetSecretValue, DescribeSecret, List) originating from non-standard source IPs or initiated by processes outside expected CI service accounts, especially clustered temporally with package installation events.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48172 cPanel Plugin Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states CVE-2026-48172 is being exploited. Pipeline extracted zero IOCs and zero use cases. Article describes 'Exploited to Run Scripts as Root' but no detection hypothesis was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cPanel endpoints (typically port 2083/2087) for HTTP POST requests targeting known LiteSpeed plugin paths with suspicious parameters. Correlate access patterns with subsequent root-privilege process spawning. Baseline cPanel API call frequency and flag anomalous plugin invocation rates.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation: Unexpected Root Process from cPanel Context
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Run Scripts as Root' explicitly. Pipeline failed to generate privilege-escalation phase or corresponding detection. This is the core attack outcome.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on child processes spawned with UID 0 (root) or GID 0 (root group) when parent process is a cPanel daemon, LiteSpeed worker, or web server context (httpd, lsws). Flag discrepancies between expected privilege and actual execution privilege for plugin-related processes.

suggestion.title: Script Upload and Execution via cPanel Plugin Handler
suggestion.rationale: CVE title mentions 'Run Scripts'—suggests arbitrary script upload/execution pathway. Pipeline generated no execution-phase detection. No use case for file-write → execute sequences originating from plugin handler.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cPanel temp directories, plugin working directories, and web-accessible paths for script file creation (*.sh, *.pl, *.php) followed immediately by execution with elevated privilege. Flag script uploads from plugin module paths that result in process execution outside normal cPanel automation workflows.

suggestion.title: LiteSpeed Web Server Unexpected Administrative Access
suggestion.rationale: cPanel integration with LiteSpeed for web server management. 'Run Scripts as Root' suggests admin-level capability abuse. No use case generated for unauthorized administrative action detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cPanel audit logs and LiteSpeed control panel access logs for privilege-escalation indicators: plugin configuration changes by non-admin users, sudo/privilege-escalation command execution from within plugin handler, unexpected systemctl/service management commands from cPanel daemon context.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation: Reverse Shell or C2 Beaconing from Compromised cPanel Host
suggestion.rationale: Script execution as root enables full system compromise. Article title indicates active exploitation. No detection hypothesis for post-compromise activity (persistence, c2, data exfiltration).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Post-root-execution, threat actor likely establishes persistence. Monitor outbound connections from cPanel/LiteSpeed processes to non-whitelisted IP:port combinations, especially DNS queries from root-context processes to dynamic DNS providers, and reverse shells spawned with dup2(socket, 0/1/2) pattern.

suggestion.title: cPanel Plugin Module Integrity Violation or Suspicious Load
suggestion.rationale: CVE exploits plugin functionality. No detection for plugin tampering, suspicious module loads, or integrity anomalies despite 'plugin' being central to the attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor LiteSpeed and cPanel plugin directories for unexpected file modifications, permission changes, or unauthorized module loads. Alert on plugins loaded from non-standard paths, signed by untrusted certificate chains, or loaded at unusual times (off-hours, outside maintenance windows).

suggestion.title: Nginx Vulnerability Exploitation Attempt (Poolslip)
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Nginx-poolslip Vulnerability Enables DoS and Code Execution Attacks' but pipeline generated zero UCs for detecting exploitation. No HTTP request inspection, no version probing baseline, no shellcode signatures.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests to Nginx services containing payloads or malformed inputs consistent with poolslip exploitation. Baseline normal request sizes/patterns; alert on anomalous request structure to Nginx worker processes or suspicious CGI/FCGI activity.

suggestion.title: Nginx Process DoS - Resource Exhaustion
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly names DoS as an attack vector ('DoS and Code Execution') but pipeline created no detection for service exhaustion. Should monitor for connection/request flooding patterns against Nginx.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect abnormal spike in requests to Nginx from single or small set of IPs over short window. Track error rates (5xx responses) and response timeouts. Correlate with CPU/memory spikes on Nginx host to confirm resource exhaustion.

suggestion.title: Nginx Worker Process Anomalous Execution
suggestion.rationale: Title indicates 'Code Execution' capability but pipeline missed detection for post-exploitation command execution. Should monitor for unexpected child processes spawned by Nginx workers (typically www-data or nginx user).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected process spawning under Nginx worker user context (uid 33/www-data/nginx user). Look for exec syscalls to /bin/sh, /bin/bash, curl, wget, or reverse shell indicators. Baseline legitimate Nginx spawned processes; flag deviations.

suggestion.title: Nginx Version Scanning / Fingerprinting
suggestion.rationale: High-severity vulnerability would trigger reconnaissance. Pipeline should detect attackers probing for vulnerable Nginx versions via Server header inspection or version-specific request patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP requests with tools/patterns associated with version scanning (nmap, nikto, metasploit User-Agents). Monitor for OPTIONS/HEAD requests or error-code fingerprinting queries. Correlate clustering of reconnaissance requests from single source.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Package Publishing Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 2FA-gated publishing as npm's defense; implies attack pattern of unauthorized package publishing via compromised credentials. Article states controls are 'against supply chain attacks'—publishing malicious packages is the core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect package publish operations from accounts with no prior publishing history, accounts from unusual geographies, or accounts bypassing or disabling 2FA. Flag packages with dependencies on typosquatted or previously-unknown upstream packages.

suggestion.title: Account Compromise Preceding Package Publish
suggestion.rationale: 2FA controls target credential compromise as the prerequisite. Article mentions 'gated publishing'—implying attackers first compromise developer credentials, then publish malicious code.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate failed login attempts or anomalous auth (impossible travel, new device, disabled 2FA) with subsequent package publishing in short time windows. Alert on successful auth followed immediately by publish without intermediate user activity.

suggestion.title: Package Install from Untrusted or Spoofed Registry
suggestion.rationale: Article mentions 'package install controls'—defense against dependency confusion or registry spoofing. Implies threat of malicious packages delivered via non-official registries or name confusion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on package.json or lock files referencing non-standard registries, or install commands from hosts not typically in developer estate. Flag installs of packages with names similar to legitimate dependencies (typosquatting).

suggestion.title: Disabled or Bypassed 2FA on Privileged Package Accounts
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes '2FA-gated publishing' as control; implies adversary motivation to disable or bypass MFA on high-privilege npm accounts to avoid detection after compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect 2FA disablement on accounts with publish permissions, especially if preceded by unusual login activity. Alert on MFA bypass attempts or re-registration of authentication factors without user confirmation.

suggestion.title: Package Metadata or Content Tamper During Upload
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'controls against supply chain attacks'; malicious package publishing often includes obfuscated code, hidden dependencies, or metadata inconsistencies to evade detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Scan published packages for obfuscated or minified code in unusual contexts, mismatched version numbers, suspicious dependency additions not reflected in source control, or packages that differ from their git source.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Laravel-Lang Package Installation from Non-Canonical Source
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Targets Laravel-Lang Packages'—direct signal for malicious package compromise. Pipeline generated zero detections for supply-chain initial access despite title containing the attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor composer install/update operations for Laravel-Lang package resolution. Alert on package installations from alternative registries, mismatched cryptographic signatures, or version integers that deviate from public release history. Correlate with file write timestamps in vendor/laravel-lang/ directories.

suggestion.title: Credential Stealer Process Execution from Package Cache
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 'Credential Stealer' payload but pipeline produced zero post-installation execution detections. Credential harvesters typically execute on import or via autoload mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect child processes (PowerShell, cmd.exe, Python, bash) spawned with working directory or command-line parent path referencing vendor/laravel-lang/ or composer cache directories. Alert on credential dumping tools (mimikatz, secretsdump, Get-Credential) or registry/browser-credential enumeration (T1555) in context of recent package installation.

suggestion.title: Outbound C2 or Credential Exfiltration from Compromised Application
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealer implies attacker infrastructure to collect stolen credentials. Pipeline surfaced zero network-based or DNS indicators for C2 communication despite this being the immediate post-theft action.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network traffic from PHP/Laravel application processes for unusual HTTPS or HTTP POST/PUT requests to external domains (likely attacker-controlled C2). Alert on DNS resolution patterns for domains registered recently or with high entropy. Correlate with execution timestamp of credential stealer component.

suggestion.title: Package Manifest Tampering or Version Pinning Bypass
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks often require attackers to inject versions into composer.lock or composer.json without user detection. Pipeline missed detection logic for dependency-integrity anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor modifications to composer.lock and composer.json files outside of legitimate composer CLI invocations. Alert on version increments that skip intermediate releases or timestamps inconsistent with official package repository metadata. Hash baseline clean dependencies and flag writes that don't match expected content.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Post-Credential Theft
suggestion.rationale: Stolen credentials (from malicious Laravel package) will be used for post-compromise lateral movement or privilege escalation. Pipeline generated zero downstream attack detection use cases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In the hours/days after Laravel-Lang package installation, correlate failed/successful logon events (4624, 4625) and authentication anomalies (RDP, SSH, application API calls) originating from the compromised host using credentials harvested by the stealer. Flag account enumeration or privilege queries (whoami, gpinfo, net user, Get-ADUser) in post-compromise timeframe.

suggestion.title: Persistence Mechanism via Package Autoload or Composer Scripts
suggestion.rationale: Laravel packages can define autoload handlers and Composer post-install scripts; malicious packages may use these for persistent execution. Pipeline missed persistence-phase detection despite Laravel ecosystem documentation being public.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor composer.json and autoload.php configuration files for post-install scripts or classmap entries pointing to suspicious file paths. Alert on script:run directives executing commands outside expected application directories. Audit PHP include/require logs for unexpected sourcing of vendor-directory files at application startup.

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-9082 Vulnerability Detection in Drupal Scanners
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'CVE-2026-9082 — match against your vulnerability scanner' and references 'Standard asset-exposure hunt' template, establishing baseline detection requirement for actively exploited vulnerability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when vulnerability scanners detect CVE-2026-9082 on systems running Drupal Core. Prioritize internet-facing instances. Cross-check systems claiming patches against actual scan results; patch lag is noted as 'the silent killer' in the article.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection Payload Detection in Drupal Database Abstraction API
suggestion.rationale: Article describes exploitation vector as 'SQL injection vulnerability...via specially crafted requests sent with the database abstraction API', establishing requirement to detect malformed API calls and SQL syntax in parameters.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to Drupal database abstraction endpoints for SQL keywords (SELECT, UNION, INSERT, DROP, --) in parameters. High-fidelity signals: SQL metacharacters in normally alphanumeric fields, escaped quotes followed by SQL syntax, or requests from non-standard Drupal UI paths.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation Post-Drupal Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'could allow for privilege escalation', establishing requirement to detect privilege elevation following successful SQL injection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unauthorized user privilege changes in Drupal following exploitation. Look for: new admin accounts created via direct database manipulation, privilege upgrades for normal users within minutes of failed API requests, or user table modifications outside normal deployment windows.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution Indicators Post-SQL Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could allow for...remote code execution', establishing requirement to detect code execution on compromised Drupal instances.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected code execution on Drupal servers post-exploitation. Alert on: shell process spawning from web server processes (www-data, httpd), direct eval() or system() calls in Drupal context, or unexpected PHP execution outside configured web root.

suggestion.title: Patch Compliance Verification for CVE-2026-9082 (Federal Deadline 2026-05-27)
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes 'patch lag is the silent killer' and establishes federal agency remediation deadline of 2026-05-27, indicating need to detect systems that remain vulnerable post-deadline or where patch records conflict with scan results.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Cross-reference patch records against vulnerability scans. Flag systems with CVE-2026-9082 detected post-2026-05-27 as compliance failures. Investigate discrepancies where patch timestamps predate vulnerability scan detections as potential audit evasion.

suggestion.title: LNK file downloads and executes remote PowerShell
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly: 'Attackers use LNK shortcuts to covertly execute PowerShell scripts hosted on external resources' initiating malware chain via phishing-delivered ZIP archives.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for LNK file creation in %TEMP% or email attachment directories followed by process execution launching PowerShell. Alert on explorer.exe or cmd.exe spawning powershell.exe with command-line download indicators (IEX, DownloadString, WebClient).

suggestion.title: PowerShell registry persistence masquerading as legitimate software
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'Creates "Run" registry key "YandexBrowser_setup" for "$temp\fixed.ps1" startup' to ensure execution independent of C2, using browser name spoofing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on registry modifications to Run keys (HKCU/HKLM CurrentVersion\Run) where value name mimics browser or utility software but execution path points to temporary directories or suspicious scripts. Flag discrepancies between expected software names and actual target executables.

suggestion.title: termsrv.dll patching for multi-user RDP access
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'Multi-user RDP by patching termsrv.dll' enabling concurrent sessions and lateral movement without licensing restrictions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for modifications to System32\termsrv.dll (file write/replacement), hex/binary modifications to RDP registry configs, or RDP service restarts following suspicious file operations. Alert on unexpected concurrent RDP sessions on non-RDS infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Reverse SSH tunnel for persistent command and control
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Reverse SSH tunneling' and 'Patched OpenSSH' as independent C2 channel distinct from Tor/Socks infrastructure, indicating long-lived backdoor connectivity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on SSH process spawning with listening ports or inbound SSH traffic. Monitor for persistent bi-directional TCP flows on port 22 (or non-standard) with stable data transfer patterns. Detect OpenSSH binary replacements via file integrity or code signing checks.

suggestion.title: PowerCloud malware execution for browser credential extraction
suggestion.rationale: Article introduces 'PowerCloud Browser checker' as new tool for credential and browser data harvesting, representing unknown-family reconnaissance requiring behavioral detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution named PowerCloud or known hash signatures. Alert on unusual file system access to browser credential stores (AppData\Local\Chromium, .mozilla), LSASS process access by non-system processes, or memory dump utilities (procdump, minidump).

suggestion.title: Multi-stage VBCloud dropper and PowerShower payload chain
suggestion.rationale: Article details payload architecture: 'Fixed.ps1 (loader) → Payload (VBCloud dropper) → Payload (PowerShower) → credential grabber' requiring detection at each execution stage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerShell script execution followed by VBScript spawning (cscript.exe, wscript.exe) with temporary directory parents. Monitor for PowerShower process execution. Alert on multi-stage child process chains where parent-child relationships deviate from normal software behavior patterns.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection via Drupal Database Abstraction API
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'allows specially crafted requests to trigger arbitrary SQL injection on sites using PostgreSQL.' Exploitation vector is explicit and requires immediate detection coverage.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Drupal application logs and PostgreSQL query logs for SQL syntax anomalies in database abstraction layer calls. Look for union-based, stacked, or time-based injection patterns targeting parameterized query handlers. Alert on requests containing SQL keywords (UNION, SELECT, DROP, INSERT) in unexpected input fields to Drupal endpoints.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution Post-SQL Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'could result in remote code execution, privilege escalation, and information disclosure.' RCE is a direct stated impact but requires correlation detection between SQL injection success and subsequent code execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate successful SQL injection attempts against Drupal with anomalous process spawning or command execution within seconds. Look for shell commands (bash, sh, cmd.exe) spawned by web server processes (php-fpm, apache) preceded by crafted SQL queries in logs.

suggestion.title: Unauthenticated Database Enumeration and Access
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'exploitable without authentication and could result in... information disclosure.' Unauthenticated access is critical; should detect database querying without valid session tokens.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL logs for queries executed without corresponding valid Drupal session authentication. Cross-reference database query logs with web server access logs—flag SELECT statements against system tables or user/credential tables from IP addresses with no prior successful login.

suggestion.title: Version-Specific Drupal Exploitation Targeting
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies exact vulnerable version ranges: 'Drupal 10.4.x before 10.4.10, 10.5.x before 10.5.10, 10.6.x before 10.6.9, 11.x variants.' Attackers will target these versions specifically and skip patched ones.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify Drupal version via response headers or source code comments. Flag exploitation attempts (SQL injection payloads) against known-vulnerable version banners. Alert when unpatched versions (8.9.x, 10.4.x–10.4.9, 10.5.x–10.5.9, 10.6.x–10.6.8, etc.) receive database abstraction API requests with SQL syntax.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation via SQL Injection Database Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'could result in... privilege escalation.' SQL injection allows direct database modification; attackers can elevate Drupal user roles or admin privileges by modifying user_roles tables.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PostgreSQL transaction logs for UPDATE/INSERT statements targeting user role or permission tables (users_roles, roles, role_permissions) preceded by or concurrent with SQL injection indicators. Alert on role elevation from non-admin to admin user IDs without corresponding admin UI interactions.

suggestion.title: PostgreSQL Syntax Anomalies in Drupal Requests
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'trigger arbitrary SQL injection on sites using PostgreSQL' — PostgreSQL-specific payloads differ from MySQL. Should detect Drupal+PostgreSQL installations receiving PostgreSQL dialect syntax in web requests.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Filter web application logs for PostgreSQL-specific SQL keywords (pg_sleep, pg_query, dollar-quoted strings, ::type casts, COPY TO/FROM) in Drupal request parameters. Correlate with PostgreSQL slow query logs or verbose logging showing these patterns in parsed query text.

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing Through Identified VPN Service
suggestion.rationale: Article describes VPN infrastructure used by 25 ransomware groups for C2. No use case detects outbound connections to the dismantled VPN service endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on connections to known C2 VPN infrastructure identified in takedown. Monitor for persistence of beaconing patterns post-sinkhole. Correlate with ransomware execution indicators.

suggestion.title: Bulk VPN Account Access and Lateral Movement
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes VPN used by ransomware operators for anonymization and movement. No detection for suspicious authentication patterns or multi-system VPN logins from single account.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag VPN authentication attempts with shared credentials across multiple source IPs or unusual geographic patterns. Detect if account credentials associated with takedown appear in compromise databases.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Payload Delivery via C2 Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates VPN infrastructure used for payload delivery by ransomware groups. No detection for binary transfer or execution following VPN communication.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate suspicious process execution or child process spawning immediately following connections to known C2 VPN endpoints. Alert on unsigned binaries written post-VPN session.

suggestion.title: Infrastructure Takedown Indicator – VPN Account Disabled
suggestion.rationale: Article describes law enforcement dismantling VPN. Pipeline should trigger use case for detecting shutdown signals: failed authentication spikes, service unavailability, dead-letter indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for sudden auth failure spikes from IP blocks previously associated with ransomware. Track DNS resolution failures for known VPN domains post-takedown. Alert on re-pivoting attempts by actors.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Group Infrastructure Mapping
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names 25 ransomware groups using the VPN. No use case maps these groups to observables or creates detection for their known TTPs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Build IOC feeds from the 25 named groups and their previously published C2, phishing domains, and hosting infrastructure. Cross-reference login attempts and file uploads with group-specific malware signatures.

suggestion.title: Typosquatted Domain Detection via Edit Distance Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies typosquatting as core attack vector: 'many sites...rely on a common trick known as typosquatting, which involves on a domain name that closely resembles the legitimate one, but contains small additions or involves other changes.' fifa26.shop is concrete example.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor newly registered domains for Levenshtein distance <3 from brand IOCs (FIFA, worldcup, etc.). Cross-reference with hosting providers and WHOIS privacy status. Alert on domains registered days before major sporting events with PII-harvesting infrastructure patterns.

suggestion.title: Fake Registration Form Credential Harvesting Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article demonstrates credential harvesting: 'fake registration form may not look strange at first. It also asks for the usual things such as your name, email address, and phone number. Nothing about that feels unusual if you believe you are on FIFA's official website.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests to non-whitelisted domains submitting PII forms (name, email, phone, address fields). Flag high-volume PII collection from single typosquatted domain. Correlate with missing OAuth/legitimate FIFA identity provider integration.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Payment Processing on Fake Merchant Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article describes payment theft mechanism: 'Once you enter your card details, it goes straight to the people behind the fake site — and there's no jersey coming from FIFA, of course.' Fake checkout pages capture card data.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor credit card form submissions on non-PCI-DSS-certified domains. Flag payment forms submitting to attacker-controlled backends instead of legitimate payment processors. Detect missing security headers (HSTS, CSP) on payment pages served from typosquatted domains.

suggestion.title: Social Media Sponsored Ad Phishing Campaign Distribution
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies social vector: 'Some victims may reach these websites through sponsored search results, while others click on ads on social media.' Attackers use paid ads to amplify phishing reach.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor social platforms for sponsored ads/links referencing FIFA, World Cup, ticket sales on newly registered or typosquatted domains. Track referrer patterns from social ad networks to suspicious ticketing/merchandise sites. Alert on throwaway ad accounts with high impressions to phishing landing pages.

suggestion.title: Email-Based Phishing Link Distribution with Event Context
suggestion.rationale: Article describes email vector: 'links in email messages forwarded by someone who didn't check the address properly.' Attackers exploit World Cup urgency in email campaigns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect emails linking to typosquatted FIFA/World Cup domains with urgency language (limited time, selling out, final chance). Flag emails claiming to forward official FIFA links but containing domain spoofing. Monitor for emails forwarded without sender verification.

suggestion.title: Website Content and Visual Cloning Detection via Favicon/CSS Hash Analysis
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights visual spoofing: 'The site also copies the look and feel of FIFA's official site, including the colors, layout, navigation and ticketing flow, all in order to make the victim feel that the experience is legitimate.' This increases trust significantly.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect newly registered domains serving identical or near-identical CSS/favicon/imagery to legitimate FIFA.com. Flag typosquatted domains with TLS certificates not issued to FIFA Inc. Monitor for copy-paste HTML structure matching official ticketing/merchandise flows.

suggestion.title: F5 BIG-IP EOL/Unpatched Appliance Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker exploited F5 BIG-IP version 15.1.201000, which reached EOL on December 31, 2024—core attack vector ignored by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag inventory records for F5 BIG-IP instances running versions 15.x with EOL status or missing patch dates after Dec 2024. Correlate against known exploit traffic patterns (SSH brute force, HTTP requests to unpatched endpoints).

suggestion.title: Suspicious FTP Server Setup via Python ftplib

suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python ftplib or pyftpdlib execution followed by listening on FTP port (21, 2121). Correlate with unusual file transfer patterns from reconnaissance/scanning tools to internal hosts.

suggestion.title: Confluence Configuration Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article states attacker 'harvested credentials from configuration files, including server.xml and confluence.cfg.xml'—post-exploitation credential access on internet-facing app.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Confluence server processes (java.exe) for unusual access to server.xml and confluence.cfg.xml. Flag reads of these files outside normal startup windows. Correlate with web shell or RCE exploitation indicators.

suggestion.title: Kerberos Relay Attack Post-Confluence Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attacker 'turned those credentials against Windows infrastructure' and 'Kerberos relay attacks'—attack escalates from Linux edge appliance to AD.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for multiple Kerberos pre-auth failures (4771) followed by successful auth from Linux source IPs. Flag duplicate Kerberos tickets (high GSS-API activity) from compromised Confluence host to Windows endpoints.

suggestion.title: CVE-2025-33073 Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article references 'exploitation of CVE-2025-33073'—specific Windows vulnerability exploited post-AD compromise, missing from all pipeline outputs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for process execution patterns consistent with CVE-2025-33073 exploit (kernel-level privilege escalation). Flag unusual LOLBin usage (Fodhelper.exe, etc.) from compromised domain accounts originating from Confluence host.

suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'unpatched vulnerabilities' on Confluence server used for 'code execution remotely'—no detection suggested despite internet-facing app being pivot point.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Confluence Java process spawning shell interpreters (/bin/bash, /bin/sh) or unusual child processes (wget, curl). Flag HTTP requests to Confluence with known RCE template injection payloads or suspicious Velocity Template Language syntax.

suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'Prometheus Phishing Malware' and describes targeting Ukraine government—no phishing detection use case was generated despite this being the primary attack vector.

suggestion.title: Prometheus Malware Execution Post-Phishing
suggestion.rationale: Prometheus is named as the payload malware; no execution/behavioral detection use case was generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Prometheus (or unknown downloader/info-stealer) execution with parent process tied to Office/macro execution or script interpretation. Track command-line arguments and C2 beacon patterns.

suggestion.title: Ghostwriter APT Targeting Government Networks
suggestion.rationale: Actor name 'Ghostwriter' is in the title but no actor-specific TTPs or infrastructure patterns were extracted.

suggestion.title: FileBrowser Quantum PATCH path traversal—successful exploitation (200 status + .. escape)
suggestion.rationale: Article states traversal allows 'move/copy/rename operates on a path outside the shared directory' but UC_21_1 only detects attempts. Successful 200 responses with .. in fromPath/toPath body indicate confirmed exploitation, not probing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: PATCH requests to /public/api/resources* with status=200 and request_body containing fromPath or toPath with .. sequences indicate successful path traversal escapes. Correlate with file system logs to confirm out-of-share modifications.

suggestion.title: Post-exploitation file access outside FileBrowser Quantum share root
suggestion.rationale: After successful exploitation via PATCH, attacker has access to files outside the shared directory. Article describes 'file ops outside shared directory'—detect unusual file access by the FileBrowser process or user outside declared share boundaries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect file opens/reads by FileBrowser service or associated web user for paths outside the shared directory root (e.g., /etc, /var, parent directories). Baseline legitimate share paths first to minimize false positives.

suggestion.title: FileBrowser Quantum public share PATCH fuzzing—error pattern analysis
suggestion.rationale: UC_21_2 detects volume but misses attackers who fuzz with persistent targeting. Article describes 'sanitizer never sees traversal'—track 400/403 error spikes on PATCH /public/api/resources which indicate active fuzzing of the sanitization logic.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: PATCH requests to /public/api/resources* returning 400 or 403 status with high request rate (≥5 errors/minute for same src/hash) or repeated distinct query parameter values indicate fuzzing of path traversal validation.

suggestion.title: FileBrowser Quantum share exfiltration via path traversal—sensitive file read
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation, attacker may read sensitive files via copy operations to a readable location. Article shows 'copy' is one operation allowed—detect PATCH with fromPath targeting /etc, /home, /root and toPath within share.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: PATCH requests where fromPath contains paths like /etc/*, /root/*, /home/*/.ssh, /var/www (outside declared share) and toPath resolves within the share directory, combined with subsequent read access to toPath.

Flag hybrid HTTP+P2P patterns consistent with Phorpiex and other botnet C2 architectures. Cross-reference ASN geolocation against telecom provider databases.

suggestion.title: Eagle Werewolf Phishing Campaign - Starlink/Drone Registration Themes
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies: 'Eagle Werewolf Espionage Campaign: Deployed multiple remote access tools (EchoGather RAT, AquilaRAT, SoullessRAT) via phishing lures impersonating Starlink registration and drone training themes on Regxa (Iraq) infrastructure.' Flag downloads of .exe or script files from phishing links. Detect EchoGather, AquilaRAT, SoullessRAT process execution post-email delivery. suggestion.title: Phorpiex Botnet Hybrid P2P/HTTP C2 Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article documents: 'Phorpiex (Twizt) Botnet: Operating on Syrian Telecom infrastructure using hybrid HTTP and P2P C2 architecture to distribute XMRig cryptocurrency miners and LockBit Black ransomware.' Monitor for XMRig process spawning post-infection. Correlate outbound connections to 94.252.245.193 and other Syrian Telecom ASN ranges with XMRig registry modifications or pool configuration files.

suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'DYNOWIPER: Destructive wiper malware attributed to ENERGETIC BEAR, hosted on CLODO CLOUD SERVICE (UAE).' This is explicitly attributed destructive malware with clear actor. Pipeline missed destructive malware and named APT actor completely.

ENERGETIC BEAR historical TTP correlation for similarity to Industroyer/CrashOverride patterns.

suggestion.title: Multi-Family Remote Access Tool Deployment - EchoGather, AquilaRAT, SoullessRAT, AsyncRAT

suggestion.title: Malicious NPM Package Installation

suggestion.title: Suspicious Postinstall Script Execution
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attacks via npm typically execute malicious code in postinstall hooks. Article describes 'backdoor' injection but pipeline did not flag postinstall as execution vector: 'Hackers Backdoor... npm Package to Launch...'

Monitor for encoded/obfuscated scripts in package.json postinstall fields. Alert on file writes to sensitive locations from npm process context.

suggestion.title: Watering-Hole Command & Control from NPM Context
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack goal is to 'Launch Watering-Hole Attacks' via backdoored package, implying C2 callbacks or data exfiltration. Pipeline generated zero C2 detection logic despite explicit attack pattern.

suggestion.title: NPM Package Dependency Injection Detection
suggestion.rationale: Watering-hole attacks via npm often inject malicious child dependencies or replace legitimate ones. Article's 'backdoor' mechanism not detailed but pipeline should flag dependency tampering patterns.

Correlate to network connections from cron processes (PID parent=1) to external IPs; flag any connection to 45.95.147.178, 45.234.176.202. Alert on cron job payloads containing base64 or ROT13 encoded strings.

Alert on profile files modified outside change windows. Correlate with login events (wtmp, failed logins) and process spawns originating from shell initialization.

suggestion.title: Multi-Path WebShell Deployment Across FreePBX with Immutable Attributes
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'plants webshell copies across more than twelve paths in the FreePBX web tree, many locked immutable' with identified files k.php and wr.php (hashes 100259af, d40180f7)

suggestion.title: Unsigned or Revoked Kernel Driver Load
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD attacks exploit 'vulnerable drivers' as the core vector. Article title establishes driver exploitation as the attack premise; requires detection of non-vendor-signed or revoked driver installations.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Driver Installation via Administrative Tooling
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD requires loading a known-vulnerable driver (often legitimately signed but functionally exploitable). Article phrase implies attacker brings their own driver; detect installation attempts matching Common Vulnerability Scoring patterns for kernel drivers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on PnP driver installation or .inf/.sys file writes matching VDL entries, or on execution of driver installation utilities (devcon.exe, DIM) with suspicious parent processes or source paths not aligned to OEM updates.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Kernel Access Pattern (Memory/Registry Tampering)
suggestion.rationale: Article promises drivers become 'exploitable without hardware'—implies kernel-mode arbitrary read/write post-load. Attackers then modify security tools, ETW, or kernel structures. Article's core mechanic is enabling kernel-level post-ex after initial driver load.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect registry deletes/modifications targeting security tools (Defender, 3rd-party EDRs) from unusual processes, or ETW provider disables from user-mode contexts with kernel callback origins. Flag memory access APIs (ReadProcessMemory, SetProcessMemory) targeting protected processes from driver-spawned threads.

suggestion.title: Scattered Spider / LockBit BYOVD Campaign Indicators
suggestion.rationale: Article title mentions BYOVD 'perspective'—this technique is attributed to Scattered Spider, LockBit, and BlackByte groups. Without article body, cannot confirm but should surface known BYOVD-using actor IOCs and tactics once article content is recovered.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate driver exploitation detections with known actor TTPs (e.g., Scattered Spider phishing, LockBit lateral movement patterns) and staging paths. Flag compromises from threat groups known to weaponize BYOVD.

suggestion.title: Driver Exploitation Loading Sequence / Primitive Abuse
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD requires multi-step: driver installation → exploitation primitive invocation → kernel access. Article title promises an analysis of 'making vulnerable'—should detect the exploitation call sequence (ioctl, CreateFile to driver, kernel call patterns).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect processes issuing IOCTL calls to recently-loaded drivers in VDL, especially from low-integrity contexts escalating to SYSTEM. Monitor for CreateFile→DeviceIoControl→kernel operation sequences targeting driver device objects.

suggestion.title: EDR / Security Tool Unload / Tampering Post-Driver Exploit
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD attacks typically follow privilege escalation with immediate EDR/AV disabling. Article 'making exploitable without hardware' implies full kernel control post-load; use cases must capture rapid post-exploitation defense evasion.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate driver load events with subsequent attempts to kill/disable EDR services (WinDefend service stop, 3rd-party sensor process termination, ETW provider unregister) within seconds. Alert on service account process spawning from kernel execution context.

suggestion.title: Dormant Workflow Backdoor via workflow_dispatch

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of GitHub OIDC Tokens and Secrets to External C2

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Workflow Secret Exfiltration via Curl/Wget
suggestion.rationale: Article describes mass exfiltration of secrets across 5,500+ repositories. Detect workflows that invoke curl, wget, or other HTTP methods to send environment variables or GitHub secrets to external domains: 'secrets being...exfiltrated'

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Pull Request Modifications to GitHub Actions Workflows

suggestion.title: GitHub Secrets Reference in Action Outputs or Logs
suggestion.rationale: Exfiltration attack likely exposed secrets by echoing or logging them. Article describes secrets being extracted; detect workflows that reference ${{ secrets.* }} in echo, print, or output-setting commands.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify workflow steps that print or export secrets context variables, or set GitHub Action outputs using secret values. Flag runs that read GITHUB_TOKEN or custom secrets and pipe them to external commands or URLs.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Network Connections from GitHub Actions Runners

suggestion.rationale: Attack exploited 'Git tag created within an organization can resolve to a commit in a fork outside that organization.' Packagist ingested fork commits as official releases. No detection for this supply-chain tag manipulation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Packagist ingestion for tags that resolve to commits outside the official package organization. Alert on any laravel-lang/* tag pointing to fork SHA or non-standard author. Cross-reference Packagist release commit SHAs against official laravel-lang GitHub repositories; flag mismatches.

suggestion.title: C2 Callback to flipboxstudio[.]info Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names two callback domains: 'fetches a second stage from https://flipboxstudio[.]info/payload' and 'Collected data is encrypted and shipped out to https://flipboxstudio[.]info/exfil.' No network-based detection rules created.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on DNS resolution or network connections to flipboxstudio.info (all subdomains/paths). Monitor for HTTP/HTTPS requests from PHP processes or package-manager child processes to flipboxstudio[.]info/payload or flipboxstudio[.]info/exfil. Flag encrypted POST requests to these endpoints.

suggestion.title: Post-Compromise Forensic Evasion: Malware Self-Deletion
suggestion.rationale: Payload 'attempts to delete its dropped files to slow down forensic recovery' after exfiltration. No detection for this post-compromise cleanup behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rapid bulk deletion of recently-created files in temporary directories or package vendor paths by PHP/web-server processes immediately following network exfiltration. Flag patterns where file creation → exfil → immediate unlink within <30 seconds.

suggestion.title: Composer-Based Package Version Rollback or Forced Update from Malicious Tag
suggestion.rationale: Attacker 'republished hundreds of malicious versions under historical release tags,' causing any 'new Composer install that resolved one of the affected versions pulled down the fork's code.' No detection for package managers installing known-malicious historical versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Composer install/update of laravel-lang/lang, laravel-lang/http-statuses, laravel-lang/attributes, or laravel-lang/actions any version >= 0.0.0 from 2026-05-22 onwards. Detect installation of older/historical versions that do not match semver progression. Flag presence of src/helpers.php in vendor/laravel-lang/* directories.

suggestion.title: Detect Unauthorized Mass Repository Tag Rewrites
suggestion.rationale: Article headline: 'Every Tag Across Multiple Composer Packages Rewritten' — systematic tag/ref manipulation is signature supply-chain compromise indicator requiring repository audit log monitoring.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk tag creation, deletion, or force-push operations across multiple repositories within short time window, especially from service accounts or new IP ranges. Correlate commits with CI configuration changes or script injections.

suggestion.title: Detect Exfiltration of CI/CD Secrets via Injected Code
suggestion.rationale: Article states attack goal is to 'Steal CI Secrets' — must detect code patterns that read/transmit environment variables injected into CI pipelines during package install or build phases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag composer/build scripts spawning curl/wget/nc sending environment variable contents (especially GITHUB_TOKEN, AWS_*, DB_* patterns) to external domains. Look for base64 encoding, output redirection to /dev/tcp, or SMTP exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Detect Malicious Code Execution During Composer Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain compromise inherently requires code execution during dependency resolution. Article implies injected payloads within package downloads or install hooks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor composer install/update operations for unexpected child processes (bash, sh, curl, wget) spawned outside normal plugin directories. Alert on composer scripts executing with escalated privileges or network I/O.

suggestion.title: Detect Repository Maintainer Account Compromise via Anomalous Authentication
suggestion.rationale: Mass tag rewriting requires authenticated access. Attacker must first compromise package maintainer accounts, detectable via login anomalies and API token abuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on new SSH keys or PAT tokens created for repository accounts, logins from new geographies, or MFA changes. Flag subsequent git operations (push/tag) from previously-unseen IPs.

suggestion.title: Detect Suspicious composer.lock or Package Manifest Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Compromised packages imply git history tampering. Detect repository state modifications that bypass normal CI approval gates.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on commits modifying composer.lock, composer.json, or install.php without PR review, bypassing branch protection rules, or signed by unexpected actors. Flag autoload or require changes pointing to new code paths.

suggestion.title: Detect Downstream Lateral Movement Using Stolen CI Credentials
suggestion.rationale: Exfiltrated CI secrets enable attacker to authenticate against repositories, cloud infrastructure, and internal systems. Detect secondary abuse of stolen credentials.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when CI tokens used during composer install phase are subsequently observed authenticating against unexpected services, cloud accounts, or repositories outside the CI pipeline's normal scope of access.

suggestion.title: LiteSpeed cPanel Plugin Privilege Escalation via Script Injection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Exploited to Run Scripts as Root.' Plugin-based code execution leading to root-level script execution is a clear attack chain the pipeline should flag. No UCs were generated despite this being the core attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for script execution (bash, sh, python, perl) with parent process litespeed, lshttpd, or cPanel-related processes where UID=0 (root). Flag executions initiated via HTTP requests to cPanel plugin directories. Correlate with suspicious cPanel API calls or plugin file writes.

suggestion.title: Exploitation of CVE-2026-48172 via cPanel HTTP Requests
suggestion.rationale: Title references 'CVE-2026-48172' directly as being exploited. The pipeline must extract this CVE identifier and map exploitation patterns. No IOC for the CVE itself was surfaced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Search cPanel and LiteSpeed HTTP access logs for requests to known vulnerable plugin paths (typically /usr/local/cpanel/base/frontend/plugin/ or /opt/litespeed/). Flag requests with injected script payloads, unusual query parameters, or POST bodies containing code. Correlate with subsequent root-level process creation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious LiteSpeed Plugin File Write and Execution
suggestion.rationale: Plugin exploitation requires either file write or dynamic loading. Article describes 'plugin' exploitation but pipeline generated no detection for malicious plugin code. File creation/modification events in plugin directories are a critical precursor.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file create/modify/write events under LiteSpeed plugin directories by non-admin processes or HTTP service accounts. Flag new .php, .so, .conf files in /usr/local/cpanel/base/frontend/plugin/ or plugin cache directories. Combine with suspicious LiteSpeed child process spawning.

suggestion.title: Root-Level Command Execution via cPanel/LiteSpeed Child Process
suggestion.rationale: Core attack outcome is 'run scripts as root.' Detection must specifically capture elevation from service account to UID 0. No UC addresses this privilege escalation boundary crossing.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor ProcessCreation events where PPID is litespeed/lshttpd service account, but UID/GID transitions to 0 (root). Flag creation of /bin/bash, /bin/sh, or other interpreters with UID 0 parent chaining back to cPanel or HTTP service processes. Exclude legitimate cron/systemd privileged tasks.

suggestion.title: Suspicious cPanel Module/Plugin Loading Without Authorization
suggestion.rationale: cPanel plugins are installed/loaded via administrative interface. Exploitation likely bypasses normal plugin mgmt. Pipeline missed detection for unauthorized plugin registration or dynamic loading.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor cPanel configuration files and plugin registry for unauthorized modifications outside cPanel's plugin mgmt interface. Flag new entries in plugin autoload directives, .htaccess files containing code execution, or symlinks pointing outside expected plugin paths.

suggestion.title: Nginx Poolslip Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly states vulnerability 'Enables...Code Execution Attacks.' Pipeline produced zero detection use cases. Should detect HTTP requests matching published exploit PoCs for the poolslip flaw against vulnerable Nginx versions.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Nginx access logs and network traffic for HTTP requests containing poolslip exploit signatures or targeting known-vulnerable endpoints. Correlate with process-level signals (socket binds, unusual worker behavior) and asset inventory version checks to confirm vulnerable deployment.

suggestion.title: Code Execution from Nginx Worker Process
suggestion.rationale: Title states 'Code Execution Attacks' via poolslip. Pipeline failed to generate detection for post-exploitation process spawning—critical for impact detection and containment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect shell or binary execution spawned as child process of Nginx master, worker, or the nginx binary itself, especially following an observed poolslip exploitation attempt. Flag unexpected interpreters (bash, sh, powershell, cmd.exe) or privilege escalation attempts in this context.

suggestion.title: Nginx Service Denial of Service via Poolslip
suggestion.rationale: Title explicitly calls out 'DoS' attacks enabled by the vulnerability. Pipeline missed detection for availability impact. Article phrase: 'DoS and Code Execution Attacks.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate sudden spikes in Nginx error rates, 502/503 responses, worker process memory exhaustion, or connection queue saturation with timestamps of poolslip exploitation attempts. Monitor for service unavailability or client-side connection timeouts immediately post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: npm Account Takeover via Credential Compromise
suggestion.rationale: Article emphasizes '2FA-Gated Publishing' as the primary defense. The inverse—failed 2FA attempts, logins from new geolocations, or successful publishes despite 2FA requirement—indicates account compromise driving package tampering. Title explicitly names 2FA as control but pipeline ignored account credential anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on multiple failed 2FA challenges within 1 hour, successful logins from new countries on accounts with publish scope, or 2FA method disabled followed by rapid package releases. Baseline account access patterns and escalate out-of-policy locations.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Package Publish Bypassing 2FA Requirement
suggestion.rationale: Article states npm now gates publishes behind 2FA. Publishes succeeding without 2FA proof or from non-browser channels (e.g., leaked automation tokens) signal account compromise at the OS or CI layer. Pipeline should detect publishes claiming 2FA but lacking authentication headers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag publish operations from accounts requiring 2FA where the request origin is a CI/CD environment, non-standard npm client, or lacks 2FA session identifier. Correlate publish IP with account's CI/CD infrastructure allowlist.

suggestion.title: Package Installation from Non-Official Registry or with Install Controls Bypassed
suggestion.rationale: Article introduces 'Package Install Controls' to restrict installation sources. Attacks bypass this by pointing npm at mirrors, offline caches, or alternate registries. Title names install controls as mitigation but pipeline ignored detection of bypass techniques.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for npm install commands with --registry pointing outside official npmjs.com, .npmrc modifications disabling package-lock verification, or installation from file:// URLs. Alert on install commands using --no-save or --force flags that suppress validation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Package Version Sequence Indicating Malicious Replacement
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks exploit version resolution logic by publishing high versions or backfilling old major versions with malicious code. Article's install controls imply version spoofing is a known threat vector, but pipeline failed to generate version-anomaly detections.
