suggestion.rationale: Article explains attack vector: 'a Git tag created within an organization can resolve to a commit in a fork outside that organization. Packagist then ingested those tags and treated the fork commits as genuine releases.' Monitor for this tag manipulation in build pipelines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: In package CI/CD logs, detect git tag operations where the commit target resolves to a repository outside the official org (e.g., laravel-lang tag pointing to attacker-controlled fork). Flag any package publish triggered by such tag-based builds.

suggestion.title: Infection Marker Persistence in System Temp
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'It writes an infection marker to a per-host temporary directory so the host is only infected once.' Marker indicates persistent compromise on that host.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor creation of sentinel files in /tmp, /var/tmp, %TEMP%, or %APPDATA% with patterns consistent with malware infection tracking (hashes, dotfiles, lock files). Correlate creation with recent Laravel-Lang Composer install and PHP request activity.

suggestion.title: Composer Package Tag Rewrite Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article core attack: 'Every Tag Across Multiple Composer Packages Rewritten.' No use case captures detection of unexpected Git tag modifications or version history anomalies in package repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for concurrent tag rewrites across Composer packages targeting identical timeframe. Alert on tags modified post-release, tag deletion followed by re-creation at same version, or commits added to existing tags that bypass CI/CD workflows.

suggestion.title: CI Secrets Exfiltration via Compromised Dependency Code
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly targets 'to Steal CI Secrets' but pipeline missed execution-phase detection for environment variable access within CI/CD runners triggered by package imports.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect code execution (node, php, python) within CI/CD environment (GitHub Actions runner, GitLab Runner logs) accessing env vars matching secret patterns (GITHUB_TOKEN, CI_*_TOKEN, *_KEY, *_SECRET) followed by HTTP POST to external domain.

suggestion.title: Malicious HTTP Exfiltration from Package Installation
suggestion.rationale: Stolen secrets must be transmitted; article describes theft objective but no detection addresses network egress patterns during 'composer install' phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag HTTP/HTTPS POST requests initiated by PHP/Composer process during dependency installation to domains absent from declared package metadata. Correlate with base64/URL-encoded payload patterns or JSON bodies containing env var names.

suggestion.title: Package Lock File Hash Mismatch vs. Installed Code
suggestion.rationale: Tag rewriting allows injected code to masquerade as pinned versions. Detection should identify when locked dependency version resolves to unexpected commit or code hash.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Compare SHA hash of installed package against composer.lock recorded hash. Alert on mismatch. Cross-reference resolved commit hash against known-good upstream mirror. Flag installations using git-based package sources (git:// or dev branches).

suggestion.title: Credential Materials in Process Environment at Package Load Time
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks target CI secrets available as environment variables. Detection missing for code paths that enumerate or dump environment state during package initialization.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for child process spawning (env, printenv, Get-ChildItem env:, etc.) initiated by PHP, Node, or Python processes during Composer/pip/npm install. Detect attempts to read GITHUB_ENV or CI-specific state files (.github/workflows configs).

suggestion.title: CVE-2026-48172 LiteSpeed cPanel Plugin Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Exploited to Run Scripts as Root'—pipeline failed to generate detection for initial exploitation vector. No UC created despite CVE reference providing clear attack surface.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP requests to LiteSpeed cPanel plugin endpoints for payloads with shell metacharacters, command substitution syntax, or script interpreter invocation patterns. Correlate timing with subsequent suspicious process spawning or file creation in temporary directories.

suggestion.title: Root-Privilege Process Execution via cPanel/LiteSpeed Daemon
suggestion.rationale: Core impact statement is 'Run Scripts as Root'—pipeline extracted zero privilege escalation detection. This is the defining threat characteristic and requires dedicated alerting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process creation where ParentImage contains 'lsws', 'httpd', or 'cPanel' process but User context is 'root' or 'SYSTEM', especially for shell interpreters (bash, sh, python, perl). Flag anomalous parent-child process relationships where non-root daemon spawns elevated children.

suggestion.title: Script Injection and Execution via LiteSpeed Plugin
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly covers 'Run Scripts'—pipeline omitted execution-phase detection. No UC maps T1059 despite clear command/script execution capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid creation and execution of temporary shell scripts (*.sh, *.py) in /tmp or /var/tmp from cPanel/LiteSpeed context. Monitor for base64-encoded payloads in process command lines or environment variables spawned from web daemon processes.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation C2 and Persistence from Root Shell
suggestion.rationale: Root-level compromise enables persistence and exfiltration; pipeline generated zero command-control or persistence detections despite impact severity permitting such activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for outbound network connections initiated by cPanel/LiteSpeed daemons to non-whitelisted external IPs. Flag DNS queries for suspicious domains from these processes. Detect modification of cron jobs, sudoers, or SSH authorized_keys from cPanel process context as persistence indicator.

suggestion.title: Nginx Poolslip Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states vulnerability 'Enables...Attacks.' Pipeline generated zero initial-access detections despite this being the primary attack vector for compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Nginx access logs for HTTP requests with poolslip exploitation signatures—likely connection pool header manipulation (Connection keep-alive abuse, upgrade requests, malformed chunked encoding). Flag request patterns anomalous to normal pool behavior such as unusual frequency of connection resets or incomplete transactions.

suggestion.title: Arbitrary Code Execution from Nginx Worker Process
suggestion.rationale: Title specifies 'Code Execution Attacks' as attack outcome. Pipeline entirely missed execution phase despite this being the critical post-exploitation capability.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child processes spawned by Nginx workers (parent: nginx or worker PID). Flag shells, interpreters, and system utilities. Nginx baseline should show zero child process creation. Correlate process spawning events with suspicious HTTP requests in preceding 30 seconds.

suggestion.title: Outbound DoS Attack Pattern from Compromised Nginx
suggestion.rationale: Title identifies 'DoS...Attacks' capability. Compromised instances could be weaponized for outbound volumetric attacks. Pipeline ignored impact/weaponization phase entirely.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish baseline Nginx egress traffic by destination IP, port, and request volume. Alert on sudden spikes to previously-unseen external IPs, systematic scanning patterns (sequential ports/subnets), or identical high-frequency requests to third parties. Correlate timing with exploitation attempts 10-60 minutes prior.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Package Metadata or Manifest Tampering
suggestion.rationale: Article discusses 'package install controls'—any feature that gates package delivery presumes detection gaps for sideloaded or tampered manifests. Pipeline should surface detection for manifest inspection, integrity checks, or version anomalies regardless of whether the article provides specifics.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for package installations that bypass checksum validation or originate from non-official registries. Flag install attempts with modified package.json manifests or version downgrades when newer signed versions exist. Detect installations of packages with names similar to popular libraries (typosquatting).

suggestion.title: Unauthorized npm Publish/Token Usage
suggestion.rationale: Title mentions '2FA-gated publishing'—this implies past or concurrent risk of unauthorized publishing. Pipeline should map to T1078 (valid accounts) and T1199 (trusted relationship) techniques used in supply-chain publishing attacks.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on publish operations lacking 2FA verification or performed from unusual geographies/IP ranges. Detect rapid package version increments from single maintainer account, or publishing from CI/CD contexts with weak token rotation.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Composer Package Installation from Affected Laravel-Lang Versions
suggestion.rationale: Article states '700+ malicious versions' of laravel-lang packages were published with embedded credential stealer. Pipeline should detect composer installations of versions between May 22-23, 2026 for affected packages (laravel-lang/lang, laravel-lang/http-statuses, laravel-lang/attributes, laravel-lang/actions).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect composer.lock or package-lock.json modifications installing Laravel-Lang packages with timestamps between May 22-23, 2026, or detect PHP process execution with composer autoloader loading from vendor/laravel-lang directories. Cross-reference against official Laravel-Lang release timeline for false-positive mitigation.

suggestion.title: C2 Callback to flipboxstudio[.]info from PHP Process
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies 'C2 domain flipboxstudio[.]info' as exfiltration endpoint for stolen credentials. Pipeline should detect DNS queries and HTTP/HTTPS connections to this domain originating from PHP processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for DNS queries or network connections from PHP processes (php.exe, php-cgi.exe, or php CLI variants) to flipboxstudio[.]info or similar obfuscated variants. Given C2 is 'hidden inside an integer array decoded at runtime,' also monitor for suspicious base64/hex encoding patterns in PHP memory or process command-line arguments.

suggestion.title: Credential Stealer Module Execution - CI/CD Token Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes '15 specialist collector modules' that 'scrape CI/CD tokens.' Should detect unauthorized read access to CI/CD credential stores (GitHub Actions secrets, GitLab CI variables, Jenkins credentials, Azure DevOps PATs) from PHP processes.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PHP processes attempting to read .env files, environment variables containing CI tokens (GITHUB_TOKEN, GITLAB_TOKEN, AZURE_DEVOPS_PAT), or accessing credential management files. Monitor for recursive directory scanning of common CI secret locations (~/.aws, ~/.azure, ~/.ssh, ~/.docker, .github/workflows).

suggestion.title: SSH Key and Cloud Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article states malware 'scrapes cloud keys, Kubernetes and Vault secrets, SSH material, environment files, browser data, password manager vaults.' Should detect PHP process access to ~/.ssh, ~/.aws/credentials, kubeconfig, or Vault-related files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for PHP processes reading from sensitive credential directories: ~/.ssh/*, ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.config/Vault, ~/.kube/config, USERPROFILE\.ssh on Windows, or accessing password manager local databases (1password, LastPass, Bitwarden vaults). Flag process execution with combined read access to multiple credential types.

suggestion.title: Laravel-Lang Git Tag Rewrite Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attack vector as 'GitHub allows version tags to point to commits from a fork...attacker exploited this to create tags pointed to commits in a malicious fork they controlled.' Should detect unusual git tag creation patterns pointing to external/forked repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor git tag creation/update operations (git tag, git push) where the tag reference resolves to a different repository fork than the canonical upstream. Flag rapid sequential tag creation (article notes 'seconds apart') across multiple package versions. Require human review when non-maintainer accounts create tags.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Autoloader Execution Loading Non-Standard Laravel-Lang Code
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'malicious code loads automatically via composer's autoloader feature.' Should detect PHP autoloader (vendor/autoload.php) execution paths that reference modified or unexpected Laravel-Lang module paths.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor PHP execution with vendor/autoload.php in call stack where included files reference laravel-lang/* paths but have unexpected file hashes, modification times post-May 22 2026, or file content containing encoded strings (integer array mentioned in C2 obfuscation). Correlate with process parent being composer or package manager.

suggestion.title: Drupal CVE-2026-9082 Vulnerable Instance Discovery
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly directs to asset-exposure hunt templates and states 'CVE-2026-9082 — match against your vulnerability scanner'. Vulnerability is in CISA KEV (actively exploited) with federal patch due 2026-05-27.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on any vulnerability scanner result for CVE-2026-9082 against Drupal Core installations. Prioritize exposed internet-facing instances and cross-reference with deployment inventory to identify assets requiring emergency patching before federal deadline.

suggestion.title: Drupal Database Abstraction API SQL Injection Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies vulnerability manifests as 'SQL injection vulnerability... via specially crafted requests sent with the database abstraction API'.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Drupal application and web server logs for requests with SQL metacharacters (UNION, SELECT, CAST, etc.) targeting database abstraction endpoints. Flag anomalous database error patterns or injection-signature matches in request parameters.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Privilege Escalation Activity
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states vulnerability 'could allow for privilege escalation and remote code execution', requiring detection of account or permission elevation post-compromise.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect unexpected privilege escalation within the Drupal database or web-server process context. Monitor for rapid changes in database user permissions, sudo additions, or permission bitmap modifications correlated with web-request timing.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution Detection - Process Spawning
suggestion.rationale: Article documents that SQL injection can achieve 'remote code execution via specially crafted requests', requiring process-level detection of code execution spawned by the exploit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected child process spawning from Drupal web-server process (apache/nginx/php-fpm). Flag shell interpreter invocation, script execution, or utility binary execution from web-server contexts that normally only run application logic.

suggestion.title: Drupal Database Query Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: Exploit specifically targets 'the database abstraction API' requiring direct observation of query patterns diverging from baseline application behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline normal Drupal database query patterns and alert on anomalies: complex nested queries, UNION operations, INTO OUTFILE writes, or schema introspection queries from the abstraction layer that deviate from application baseline.

suggestion.title: Malicious LNK Execution from Email Attachment
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'attackers emailed a ZIP archive containing an LNK file as an attachment... Attackers use LNK shortcuts to covertly execute PowerShell scripts hosted on external resources.' Primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect LNK file extraction from email attachments or ZIP archives triggering PowerShell process execution with external script URLs. Flag suspicious command lines in LNK shortcuts and correlate with subsequent network requests.

suggestion.title: PowerShell Persistence via Run Registry Key with Software Masquerade
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Creates "Run" registry key "YandexBrowser_setup" for "$temp\fixed.ps1" startup.' Persistence achieves autorun on logon by spoofing legitimate application names.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HKCU/HKLM Run registry writes pointing to temp or unusual paths, especially when value names mimic legitimate software but target PowerShell or script interpreters.

suggestion.title: Reverse SSH Tunnel Establishment for Command & Control
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'Reverse SSH tunneling... Patched OpenSSH... these utilities gain a foothold in infected systems and create additional backup control channels.' Named as active Cloud Atlas C2 mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SSH client execution from suspicious parents, SSH service binaries spawned outside normal context, and SSH connection establishment with unusual remote ports or geolocation. Correlate with Tor/RevSocks deployment.

suggestion.title: RevSocks Proxy Utility Deployment
suggestion.rationale: Article lists RevSocks as third-party utility: 'third-party public utilities (Tor/SSH/RevSocks) to gain a foothold in infected systems and create additional backup control channels.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Identify RevSocks binary presence via file hash or name patterns. Monitor for process creation with arguments consistent with reverse proxy setup (listening ports, forwarding rules).

suggestion.title: Termsrv.dll Patching for Unauthorized Multi-User RDP Access
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'Multi-user RDP by patching termsrv.dll' as defense evasion and persistence technique to circumvent single-session limit.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on file modifications to %windir%\System32\termsrv.dll from non-Windows Update processes. Correlate with multiple concurrent RDP sessions from single source.

suggestion.title: PowerCloud Credential Stealing Tool Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article: 'new tools used by this group... its new tool, PowerCloud' described as browser checker. Appears designed for credential/browser data extraction.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect PowerCloud binary via known hashes or filenames. Monitor for process execution patterns accessing browser data stores, certificate stores, or making unusual browser API calls.

suggestion.title: SQL Injection Exploitation Attempt Against Drupal Database Abstraction API
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states: 'allows specially crafted requests to trigger arbitrary SQL injection on sites using PostgreSQL' and 'exploitable without authentication.' The pipeline must detect malicious request patterns targeting Drupal's vulnerable API.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor HTTP request logs for Drupal-bound requests containing SQL injection signatures (UNION SELECT, DROP, OR 1=1, --, etc.) targeting database abstraction layer endpoints. Flag requests from sources not previously observed against target. Correlate with version signatures of vulnerable Drupal branches (8.9.x, 10.4.x–11.3.x). Alert on rapid request sequences from single source IP.

suggestion.title: Abnormal Database Query Execution from Web Application Process
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'trigger arbitrary SQL injection' enabling 'unauthorized access, modification, or deletion of database data.' Must detect deviation from normal application-layer database queries.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on database queries executed by the Drupal application user that access system/metadata tables (information_schema, pg_catalog), issue DDL operations not typical for application layer (CREATE, DROP, ALTER), use UNION-based data extraction patterns, or show privilege-escalation queries. Establish baseline of legitimate queries and flag statistical anomalies in query volume or complexity.

suggestion.title: Privilege Escalation Following SQL Injection Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly lists 'privilege escalation' as a consequence: 'could result in remote code execution, privilege escalation, and information disclosure.' Post-compromise privilege elevation must be detected as distinct attack phase.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for database permission changes, role elevation, or new privileged account creation originating from application-layer queries following SQLi detection. Flag elevation of Drupal application database user to DBA/superuser role, creation of admin accounts via SQL, or modification of role_permission tables outside normal administrative patterns.

suggestion.title: Remote Code Execution via SQL Injection in PostgreSQL
suggestion.rationale: Article states vulnerability 'could result in remote code execution.' PostgreSQL SQL injection can spawn OS processes via certain functions or configurations; must detect RCE indicators.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect process spawning (cmd.exe, /bin/bash, /bin/sh) originating from web server processes (php-fpm, apache2, nginx) following SQL injection detection. Flag execution of scripting interpreters (python, perl, node) or reverse-shell utilities (nc, curl, wget) from web application context. Correlate with database logs showing SQL procedure execution or file operation queries.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration Following SQL Injection Information Disclosure
suggestion.rationale: Article lists 'information disclosure' as impact. Pipeline must detect attacker extracting sensitive data post-exploitation: 'unauthorized access...to database data.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for large HTTP response payloads from Drupal application following SQLi exploitation, outbound connections to non-whitelisted external IPs, file-transfer protocols (SFTP, SCP, FTP), or DNS queries with encoded data. Flag responses with database dumps, compressed archives of data, or abnormal egress data volume from affected web server.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Database User Provisioning via SQL Injection Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Article notes privilege escalation capability. Attacker may create backdoor database accounts for persistence: 'unauthorized...modification of database data' includes user/role tables.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for CREATE USER or CREATE ROLE operations executed through the application layer (not from admin tools). Flag creation of database accounts with non-standard names, accounts with superuser/dbo privileges from app context, or password changes on system accounts initiated by application user. Baseline legitimate account provisioning and alert on deviations.

suggestion.title: VPN Service C2 Communication Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly frames VPN dismantlement related to ransomware group usage; title states '25 Ransomware Groups' relied on this service, establishing VPN-as-C2 pattern. Pipeline generated zero UCs despite this being primary attack infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect encrypted tunnel traffic (VPN protocols: OpenVPN, WireGuard, custom VPN) with command-and-control signatures. Alert on VPN endpoint addresses appearing in threat feeds or linked to known ransomware C2 infrastructure. Flag VPN traffic volumes / timing patterns consistent with staging or exfil.

suggestion.title: Shared VPN Infrastructure Across Threat Actors
suggestion.rationale: Title states '25 Ransomware Groups' used single VPN service, establishing shared infrastructure pattern. Pipeline failed to recognize this as signature threat behavior warranting detection of cross-actor tool reuse.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate VPN client process execution or network callbacks across multiple endpoints with different ransomware malware signatures or lateral movement TTPs. Alert when VPN service credentials or configurations appear in recovered payloads from unrelated intrusions.

suggestion.title: VPN Authentication Abuse by Ransomware Operators
suggestion.rationale: Takedown implies enforcement action against shared credentials / accounts controlled by ransomware operators. Article should detail authentication patterns; pipeline generated no UC for compromised or shared VPN account detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect impossible travel to VPN endpoints (geolocation delta). Alert on VPN login failures followed by success from anomalous geolocations. Track VPN account reuse across distinct malware families or threat actor infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration Volume Anomaly via VPN Service
suggestion.rationale: Ransomware attack lifecycle involves data exfil; title + context implies VPN was abuse vector for staging/exfiltration. Zero UCs address data movement detection through identified VPN infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline data transfer rates through identified VPN endpoints. Alert on sustained high-volume outbound traffic (>100GB/day) to VPN infrastructure from hosts showing ransomware execution behavior. Correlate with known ransom group exfil patterns.

suggestion.title: Ransomware Payload Delivery via Compromised VPN
suggestion.rationale: Article title and context (25 groups using single VPN) implies service was delivery/staging platform. Pipeline generated no detection for initial payload handoff or staging via VPN endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect executable delivery/execution immediately following VPN client initialization. Alert on child processes spawning from VPN service contexts (OpenVPN, custom VPN tunnels). Monitor for malware staging directories or payloads downloaded from VPN exit IPs.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement Across VPN Segment Isolation Breach
suggestion.rationale: VPN infrastructure typically used for pivoting internal networks. Title + ransomware context implies lateral movement through VPN tunnel; pipeline missed detection for post-compromise movement.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on SMB/RDP/SSH connections from VPN tunnel IPs to internal hosts. Detect credential forwarding or cached credential usage across VPN boundaries. Flag scanning activity (port enumeration, service enumeration) originating from VPN exit points.

suggestion.title: Detect Typosquatted FIFA/World Cup Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes typosquatting as primary attack vector: 'many sites set up in the run-up to major events will rely on a common trick known as typosquatting, which involves a domain name that closely resembles the legitimate one, but contains small additions or involves other changes in the domain name.' Concrete example: fifa26[.]shop.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor domain registrations and DNS queries for domains similar to 'fifa.com' with typosquatting patterns (.shop, .xyz, .store TLDs) particularly during event buildup windows. Alert on DNS resolution of typosquatted domains and correlate with user click events.

suggestion.title: Detect Phishing Delivery via Sponsored Search and Social Media
suggestion.rationale: Article states victims reach fraudulent sites 'through sponsored search results, while others click on ads on social media or links in email messages forwarded by someone who didn't check the address properly.' Multiple T1566.002/T1598.003 delivery vectors explicitly described.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor email, sponsored search results, and social media traffic for links to typosquatted FIFA domains or non-official infrastructure. Establish baseline: legitimate FIFA communications should originate from official channels and resolve to legitimate FIFA domains only.

suggestion.title: Detect Fake Registration Form Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article describes fake registration requiring 'name, email address, and phone number' before payment, mimicking legitimate flow: 'If you expect to create a FIFA ID before buying tickets, a fake registration form may not look strange at first.' This is T1589.001/T1589.002 credential harvesting via web form.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect POST requests to typosquatted domains with form fields matching legitimate registration (name, email, phone). Cross-correlate users submitting registration data to both official FIFA site and typosquatted domains within 12-hour windows.

suggestion.title: Detect Payment Card Capture on Non-PCI Domains
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes payment theft: 'Once you enter your card details, it goes straight to the people behind the fake site' with visual evidence of fake payment pages requesting credit card details. Clear T1056.004 credential exfiltration.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for credit card number patterns (16-digit sequences via regex) submitted via HTTP POST to non-PCI compliant, typosquatted, or uncertified payment processing domains. Alert on unencrypted (HTTP) card transmission and cross-reference domain registration details.

suggestion.title: Detect Multi-Step Shopping Funnel on Phishing Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article describes complete commerce sequence on fake site: 'select any product and add it to the shopping cart' followed by checkout and payment pages. This multi-step funnel behavior on phishing domain is distinct from legitimate traffic patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate session sequences on typosquatted domains: product catalog browse → add to cart → proceed to checkout → payment page submission. Legitimate FIFA commerce shows low abandonment and order fulfillment; phishing sites show high cart-to-payment conversion with zero fulfillment/shipping activity.

suggestion.title: Detect Event-Driven Bulk Domain Typosquatting Campaigns
suggestion.rationale: Article notes scams 'set up in the run-up to major events' when 'anticipation is building toward fever pitch.' Temporal clustering of newly-registered typosquatted domains before major events is a reliable campaign signal.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor domain registration feeds for bulk registrations of typosquatted domains 3-6 weeks prior to major sporting/entertainment events. Alert on domain age <30 days with significant DNS query or HTTP traffic volume. Correlate event keywords with legitimate brand names in registrant data.

suggestion.title: F5 BIG-IP Remote Code Execution Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes attack via 'exposed F5 BIG-IP edge appliance' as entry point. Pipeline extracted no IOCs and zero initial-access detection logic despite this being the attack origin.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor F5 BIG-IP systems for exploitation indicators: HTTP POST/PUT requests to known vulnerable endpoints (e.g., tmui, config, tmsh), unusual process spawning from F5 tmsh/httpd contexts, and evidence of outbound command execution. Alert on successful authentication followed by admin-privilege process creation.

suggestion.title: Kerberos Relay Attack—Lateral Movement via Credential Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'Kerberos relay and lateral movement' as core attack technique. Pipeline's kill chain is empty; this is MITRE ATT&CK T1550.003 and represents a distinct detection need.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Kerberos relay via anomalous TGT requests from non-standard hosts, especially edge appliances (F5) or internal servers (Confluence) attempting to obtain service tickets for sensitive targets. Alert on NTLM signing/sealing bypasses and cross-host Kerberos delegation where source is not a trusted domain controller.

suggestion.title: Confluence Server Pivoting and Credential Harvesting
suggestion.rationale: Article describes pivot 'to an internal Confluence server for credential theft.' Pipeline has no use case for Confluence-specific exploitation or post-compromise credential exfiltration from collaboration platforms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Confluence for unusual authentication attempts, bulk user enumeration, or credential management API calls from edge appliance sources. Detect suspicious exports of user databases, SSO token abuse, or process spawning from Confluence Java/Tomcat runtime that indicates command execution or memory dumping for credential extraction.

suggestion.title: Linux Post-Compromise Process and Network Behavior
suggestion.rationale: Attack targets 'Linux devices'; article involves multi-stage payload delivery and command execution on Linux systems post-F5 compromise. Pipeline generated no Linux-specific behavioral detections.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Linux processes spawned by edge appliance or Confluence service accounts (httpd, www-data, confluence user, etc.) with command-line indicators: shell invocation (sh -c, bash -i), curl/wget with suspicious URLs, or unexpected outbound connections to C2 infrastructure. Monitor for living-off-the-land techniques via perl, python, or awk used for reverse shells.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Edge Appliance to Internal Servers
suggestion.rationale: Article's core narrative is traversal from F5 edge device to internal Confluence server. Pipeline has no cross-network pivoting detection, authentication chain analysis, or east-west traffic anomaly use case.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect lateral movement via anomalous authentication sequences: authentication success on edge appliance (F5) followed within minutes by authentication to internal sensitive assets (Confluence, file servers, domain controllers) using credentials harvested from the appliance. Alert on unexpected source IPs for internal service logins originating from known edge segments.

suggestion.title: F5 BIG-IP Credential or Session Token Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Multi-stage attack implies credential theft from F5 itself to enable downstream pivots. Pipeline has no specific detection for credential material being read or exported from F5 configuration or runtime.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor F5 for unauthorized reads of credential storage (config files, tmsh secrets, token caches), unusual process memory access (via /proc or ptrace), and exports of user/admin databases. Alert on tmsh commands that dump credentials, config exports, or SSL key material being written to /tmp or accessed by non-privileged processes.

suggestion.title: Phishing Email with Prometheus Payload Delivery
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly names 'Prometheus Phishing Malware' as delivery mechanism; pipeline generated zero initial-access detections despite this being primary attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect spear-phishing emails targeting Ukraine government addresses with suspicious attachments (Office files with macros, executables, archives). Flag senders using lookalike domains or external email masquerading government entity addresses with Prometheus-associated payload signatures.

suggestion.title: Prometheus Malware Execution from Office Process
suggestion.rationale: Phishing delivery implies Office macro execution or attachment opening; no execution-phase detection generated despite clear user interaction required to detonate payload.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor child processes spawned from Excel, Word, or Outlook processes: cmd.exe, PowerShell, rundll32, regsvcs with suspicious arguments. Track file creation in AppData/Temp/Downloads immediately post-Office execution during business hours in government networks.

suggestion.title: Prometheus Command & Control Beaconing
suggestion.rationale: Prometheus is malware implying persistent C2 communication; zero network-based detections generated despite this being required for full infection lifecycle.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTP/HTTPS traffic to low-reputation domains from compromised government workstations. Monitor for DNS queries to Ghostwriter-attributed C2 infrastructure. Detect unusual outbound connection patterns (high-frequency beacon traffic, consistent timing, small data transfer volumes).

suggestion.title: Credential Theft by Prometheus Information Stealer
suggestion.rationale: Ghostwriter campaigns typically harvest credentials post-phishing; no credential-access detection use cases generated despite this being core objective for government targeting.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for LSASS memory injection attempts or SAM/LSA Secrets registry reads by unsigned processes. Track browser profile access (Chrome/Firefox credential databases, cookies). Alert on clipboard monitoring or keystroke logging driver installation.

suggestion.title: Prometheus Persistence Installation via Registry/Startup
suggestion.rationale: Phishing malware requires persistence mechanisms; no persistence-phase detections generated despite Ghostwriter campaigns typically deploying scheduled tasks or run-key modifications.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unsigned executables modifying HKCU/HKLM Run/RunOnce keys or Startup folders. Detect scheduled task creation by Prometheus-infected processes with system privileges. Flag registry modifications to shell launch sequences in government network context.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement from Prometheus-Compromised Government Workstation
suggestion.rationale: Ukraine government entity compromise implies follow-on lateral movement to shared resources/domain infrastructure; zero lateral-movement use cases generated despite this being primary damage vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SMB/RDP connections from newly-infected workstations to file servers, domain controllers, or administrative systems. Alert on logon attempts using compromised credentials to access government network shares. Track remote execution attempts (PsExec, WinRM) originating from phishing entry points.

suggestion.title: YesWiki FormManager SQL response timing anomalies — blind SQLi inference
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 'blind SQLi extraction loop' requiring time-based inference. Pipeline missed detection for unusual response-time deltas on repeated requests to the same form endpoint, which is the primary signal for blind extraction attacks when error-based channels are unavailable.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on POST requests to /BazaR/*vue=formulaire* endpoint where median response time for requests from a single source within a 5m window exceeds baseline by >2σ, or where response times are bimodal (fast vs. slow) suggesting conditional SQL logic evaluation.

suggestion.title: YesWiki Bazar form parameter injection patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article states sink is 'FormManager::create()' and injection occurs in an INSERT statement. Pipeline did not generate detection for suspicious SQL metacharacter payloads ('UNION', 'OR 1=1', '--', '/*', ';') in form parameters sent to the vulnerable endpoint.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on POST requests to /BazaR/*vue=formulaire* containing form-parameter values with SQL metacharacters or UNION-based payloads (case-insensitive regex: union|select|insert|delete|or \d+=\d+). Threshold: any occurrence on this endpoint is suspicious.

suggestion.title: YesWiki yeswiki_users table access via derived credentials
suggestion.rationale: Article highlights impact: 'read the full database, including yeswiki_users.password hashes'. Pipeline missed post-exploitation detection for database query patterns or exported data containing user credential tables.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on SELECT queries against yeswiki_users table or exports of files containing password-hash-like content (bcrypt/MD5 signatures). If database query logging is unavailable, flag unusual outbound traffic (DNS exfiltration, HTTP POST with encoded data) from the compromised YesWiki host to attacker-controlled domains post-exploitation.

suggestion.title: FileBrowser Quantum: Directory enumeration before traversal exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names T1083 (File and Directory Discovery) but provided hunts detect only exploitation phase, not reconnaissance. Missing: GET requests to enumerate `/public/api/resources/<hash>` tree structure before PATCH attempts. Phrase: 'File and Directory Discovery' technique listed but not detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect rapid sequential GET requests to `/public/api/resources` endpoint from same source across multiple hash parameters or with deep recursion (`?recurse=true` or repeated `/` patterns), followed within minutes by PATCH requests with traversal payloads. This distinguishes probing from normal browsing.

suggestion.title: FileBrowser Quantum: Successful path traversal indicators via response size and file access patterns
suggestion.rationale: Article describes impact as 'move/copy/rename operates on a path outside the shared directory' but hunts don't detect success indicators. What does a successful exploitation response look like? Article: 'The sanitizer in resourcePatchHandler never sees the traversal and the move/copy/rename operates...'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: PATCH requests to `/public/api/resources` returning HTTP 200-201 with response body size exceeding typical metadata responses (>10KB), or file-system events showing FileBrowser process modifying files outside registered share mount points, especially in `/etc/`, `/var/log/`, or `/home/` directories.

suggestion.title: FileBrowser Quantum: Obfuscated traversal attempts (URL encoding, double-encoding)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes mechanism: 'filepath.Join collapses .. segments during the join, the sanitizer never sees the traversal.' Implies attackers may attempt encodings (%2e%2e, %252e%252e, null bytes) to evade detection. Pipeline queries only look for literal '..' string.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: PATCH requests to `/public/api/resources` where fromPath or toPath contains URL-encoded directory traversal sequences (%2e%2e, %252e%252e, ..%00, %3b../) or unusual encoding patterns in JSON body. Check for percent-encoding of dots or slashes in path parameters.

suggestion.title: FileBrowser Quantum: Sequential same-source exploits across multiple share hashes
suggestion.rationale: Article describes vulnerability affects 'public share PATCH' — attackers could target multiple shares. Detection should flag systematic exploitation: 'multiple requests modifying/copying files across different share paths' suggests lateral enumeration and exploitation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Same source IP issuing 5+ PATCH requests to `/public/api/resources` with distinct share hash values (different `hash=` query parameters) within a 15-minute window, each traversal attempt following a discovered enumeration query, indicating systematic targeting of multiple shared directories.

suggestion.title: FileBrowser Quantum: File operation targets indicating sensitive data interest
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability enables moving/copying/renaming files. Successful exploitation would target sensitive paths outside share dir. Article states 'file ops outside shared directory' but doesn't specify sensitive targets like configs, keys, or system files.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: FileBrowser service account accessing, reading, or modifying files in `/etc/passwd*`, `*.key`, `*.pem`, `.ssh/`, `shadow`, or application config paths that fall outside the configured share mount points. Alert on first successful access to out-of-bounds sensitive paths.

suggestion.title: C2 Beaconing from Telecom Network Ranges
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'large-scale command-and-control operations' targeting telecom networks; no detection for persistent C2 communications. Expected to detect outbound connections from compromised telecom ASNs/CIDR to known malicious IPs or high-entropy domains.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for repeated connections from telecom infrastructure (identify target ASNs from article context) to rare external IPs or newly-registered domains. Baseline outbound port/protocol combinations for targeted telecom provider and alert on anomalies indicating C2 protocol tunneling.

suggestion.title: Credential Harvesting Targeting Telecom Personnel
suggestion.rationale: Telecom C2 operations require employee account compromise; article implies operators infiltrated networks, likely through phishing or credential theft. No detection proposed for credential exfiltration or authentication anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect impossible-travel logins for telecom staff (geographic velocity), bulk password guesses against telecom AD accounts, or credential spray from single source. Correlate failed logins followed by success within short window.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement via Telecom Network Services (SSH/RDP)
suggestion.rationale: Article describes large-scale operations implying compromise depth; typical telecom lateral movement relies on SSH (routers, Linux servers) and RDP to administrative hosts. No use case proposed for detecting multi-hop propagation.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag chains of SSH logins across router ASNs or inter-VLAN RDP sessions originating from non-standard administrative accounts. Detect lateral movement by correlation: compromised user → admin host → network device.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Network Device Backdoors
suggestion.rationale: Sustaining large-scale C2 in telecom requires durable persistence; article mentions operations not credentials alone. Missing detection for webshell installation, firmware modification, or rogue administrator accounts on network equipment.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unexpected file modifications on router/switch configuration directories. Alert on new administrative accounts added to network devices. Detect unusual process execution on network equipment (e.g., web server spawning shells, cron jobs executing atypical binaries).

suggestion.title: Reconnaissance of Telecom Network Topology
suggestion.rationale: Operators must enumerate target infrastructure before escalating attacks; article implies knowledge of 'middle east telecom networks' (plural), suggesting active scanning/enumeration. No detection for network mapping or system discovery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect scanning patterns: single source probing multiple IPs on reserved telecom infrastructure ranges within short time windows. Alert on sequential SSH/RDP connection attempts to non-existent accounts, or unexpected traceroute/ping bursts from internal segment to external peers.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration over Obfuscated/Alternate Channels
suggestion.rationale: Large-scale telecom C2 operations are motivated by theft (customer data, routing tables, call records); article infers this but pipeline generates no exfiltration detection. Attackers typically tunnel data over DNS, HTTP, or encrypted channels.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect anomalous DNS query volume or TXT-record queries from internal telecom hosts (data exfil over DNS). Monitor for large outbound data transfers on atypical ports (443, 53, 8080) correlated with malware process execution. Alert on TLS/SSL connections to newly-registered C2 domains.

suggestion.title: Suspicious npm Package Installation from Registry
suggestion.rationale: Article headline establishes 'Hackers Backdoor Popular art-template npm Package'—supply chain compromise via registry is the attack vector. No installation-time detection rule generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor npm install commands and package.json modifications for unexpected package additions or version pins to unusual registries. Flag installations of 'art-template' versions from dates matching compromise window. Correlate with network egress to known C2 infrastructure during installation.

suggestion.title: Code Execution from Node Modules with Suspicious Network Egress
suggestion.rationale: Backdoored package will execute code during import/require. Article states 'Watering-Hole Attacks'—requires C2 callbacks. Pipeline produced no execution or C2 detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on process execution with parent=node or command-line containing 'node_modules'. Correlate with outbound network connections to non-CDN/non-trusted IPs, especially on unusual ports or to newly-registered domains.

suggestion.title: Package.json or package-lock.json Tampering Detection
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain compromise requires either direct registry manipulation or lock-file injection. Article structure ('Backdoor...Package') implies package metadata was altered. No file integrity rules present.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for unsigned or out-of-sequence modifications to package-lock.json (especially hash mismatches vs. remote registry). Flag package.json entries pointing to git+ssh://, file://, or HTTP URLs instead of standard npmjs.com versions.

suggestion.title: Anomalous Process Tree: Node Child Processes with External Network
suggestion.rationale: Backdoored npm module will spawn child processes for watering-hole payload delivery. Article title specifies this attack type. No process-relationship or lateral-movement detection exists.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect node.exe spawning cmd.exe, PowerShell, or curl/wget processes with command-line arguments containing URLs or C2 indicators. Alert on unexpected network connections from these child processes, especially to IP ranges not matching expected staging/CDN infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Registry Authentication Anomalies and Package Version Downgrades
suggestion.rationale: Compromised package likely injected as version bump or forced downgrade via lock-file manipulation. 'Watering-hole' suggests targeted deployment. No registry-level detection of version anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on unexpected package.json version constraints (e.g., pinned to known-malicious version range). Cross-reference npm registry publish timestamps with article disclosure date. Flag discrepancies between installed version hash and registry manifest.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Web Shell Upload to FreePBX
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly references persistence mechanisms on FreePBX; web shells are a standard persistence layer for VoIP appliances. No IOCs or UCs generated despite this being a core attack vector.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor FreePBX web directories (/var/www/html, admin modules) for executable uploads with suspicious extensions (.php, .phtml, .phar) or modified timestamps concurrent with admin login anomalies.

suggestion.title: FreePBX Scheduled Task / Cron-Based Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Multi-layer persistence often includes cron jobs or scheduled tasks; article mentions 'six-layer' architecture but pipeline captured no persistence mechanisms.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag creation or modification of cron entries in /etc/cron.d, /etc/crontab, or asterisk-specific cron files; correlate with unusual bash/curl/wget invocations in cron context.

suggestion.title: Compromised FreePBX Admin Account Abuse
suggestion.rationale: VoIP systems commonly targeted via valid account compromise for long-term persistence; no credential access or account manipulation detections generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on admin panel logins from new geolocations, off-hours access patterns, or IP addresses lacking prior FreePBX touchpoints. Correlate failed to successful login sequences.

suggestion.title: FreePBX Kernel Module / Loadable Kernel Object Persistence
suggestion.rationale: Advanced persistence on Linux telephony systems may involve LKM rootkits; 'six-layer' suggests rootkit-level techniques not captured by pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor insmod, modprobe, rmmod commands and /sys/module directory modifications; flag kernel module loads from non-standard paths or with timestomping.

suggestion.title: DDoS-for-Hire Command Infrastructure Communication
suggestion.rationale: Article describes DDoS-for-hire botnet operations; should detect C2 beaconing patterns or command distribution to distributed bot nodes for botnet coordination
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for anomalous outbound traffic patterns to known DDoS botnet C2 infrastructure. Detect coordination traffic between bot nodes using DNS fast-flux or IP rotation. Look for traffic to multiple victim IPs in short time windows from the same source, indicative of DDoS orchestration.

suggestion.title: DDoS Attack Execution and Impact Pattern
suggestion.rationale: Core attack mechanism: article states 'DDoS attacks' as primary tool; should detect volumetric or application-layer attack traffic signatures
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Baseline legitimate traffic to targets and alert on sudden spikes in connection counts, bytes/second, or request rates. For application-layer attacks, detect HTTP floods (GET/POST spike), DNS amplification replies, or SYN floods with unusual source diversity.

suggestion.title: Botnet Distribution and Bot Installation
suggestion.rationale: Operating a DDoS botnet requires bot recruitment/infection; article likely discusses payload distribution or bot-node compromise mechanisms
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect suspicious process execution chains (script interpreters spawning encoded payloads, download cradles). Monitor for obfuscated command-line activity. Alert on execution from temp directories or AppData. Cross-reference with known malware hash databases.

suggestion.title: Botnet Monetization / DDoS-for-Hire Service Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly covers 'DDoS-for-hire' service model; should detect payment/order channels and customer transaction logs if available
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for advertising or solicitation of DDoS services on dark web marketplaces, Discord, Telegram, or underground forums. Detect payment transactions to known DDoS-as-a-service operators. Alert on customer emails requesting DDoS attack services.

suggestion.title: Operator Digital Identity / Underground Market Presence
suggestion.rationale: Arrest implies law enforcement correlated digital identity (handles, email, crypto wallets); should surface actor OSINT signals for infrastructure/marketplace account detection
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate operator handles/email addresses (if disclosed) with command infrastructure registrations, hosting account creation times, and cryptocurrency transactions. Alert if known compromised operator infrastructure is accessed or reactivated.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Vulnerable Driver Loading
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD attacks fundamentally involve loading known-vulnerable drivers for privilege escalation. Article title establishes this as the core technique; pipeline extracted no detection use cases around driver loading behavior.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for loading of known-vulnerable drivers (rtcore64.sys, gdrv.sys, DBDriver.sys, Capcom.sys, etc.) from non-standard paths or by low-integrity processes. Alert on unsigned driver loads or those matching CVE databases of privilege-escalation-vulnerable drivers.

suggestion.title: Exploit Kit / KDU Activity Detection
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD tooling (KDU, KDMapper, Cheat Engine) is commonly used to load and exploit vulnerable drivers. Title mentions 'exploitable without hardware' implying automated exploitation. Pipeline found no detection around known BYOVD tools.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect execution or download of known BYOVD tools (KDU variants, KDMapper, Cheat Engine) via process names, code signing certificates, parent-child relationships, or C2 callbacks. Monitor for tool-specific command-line patterns and registry modifications.

suggestion.title: Kernel-Mode Privilege Elevation via Vulnerable Driver
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD chains to privilege escalation. Article topic 'making vulnerable drivers exploitable' directly indicates escalation from user-mode to kernel-mode. No escalation technique signals detected.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for processes spawning child processes with elevated privileges immediately after suspicious driver load. Look for SYSTEM-context processes launched from user-mode tools, or token duplication/impersonation patterns tied to driver interactions.

suggestion.title: Vulnerable Driver Exploitation Registry Artifacts
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD attacks often abuse driver-specific registry keys for exploitation. Title implies direct driver manipulation to bypass protections; no registry-based detection coverage generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for suspicious modifications to driver-related registry paths (e.g., HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Services, device driver parameters) from user-mode processes or scripts, especially those paired with kernel object creation.

suggestion.title: Defense Evasion via Kernel Integrity Bypass
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD purpose is to bypass security controls without hardware interaction. Article subtitle 'without hardware' emphasizes evasion of kernel protections (CFG, CIG, HVCI). No defense-evasion use cases present.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect manipulation of kernel-mode code integrity protections, Control Flow Guard (CFG) bypass, or HVCI/VBS evasion techniques typically associated with vulnerable driver exploitation. Monitor for code writes to protected memory regions or disabling of integrity policies.

suggestion.title: Post-Exploitation Persistence via Vulnerable Driver
suggestion.rationale: BYOVD can establish persistence via kernel-mode hooks or rootkit installation through vulnerable drivers. Article's 'exploitable' framing suggests sustained access is the goal, but no persistence UC generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for rootkit or kernel hook installation following vulnerable driver loading. Detect anomalous kernel callbacks, system call table modifications, or persistence mechanisms tied to driver execution contexts.

suggestion.title: Malicious GitHub Actions Workflow File Creation or Modification
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'malicious CI/CD workflows' as the attack vector. Pipeline generated zero UCs to detect workflow file changes (.github/workflows/*.yml) in affected repositories.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on commits to .github/workflows/ directory with suspicious content: shell commands exporting secrets, outbound curl/wget to attacker-controlled domains, base64-encoded payloads, or environment-variable exfiltration patterns. Correlate with repos outside normal deployment patterns.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Secret Exfiltration via Workflow Execution
suggestion.rationale: Malicious workflows inherently access repository secrets (${{ secrets.* }}) for exfiltration. Article states workflows are malicious but pipeline missed detection for credential access within Actions jobs.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Actions job logs for secret variable access followed by piping to external commands, network utilities, or unknown service account calls. Flag workflows that export secrets to environment or encode them for transmission.

suggestion.title: Mass Workflow Injection Across Repository Set
suggestion.rationale: Article indicates '5,561 repos' compromised—implying coordinated injection. Pipeline should detect when single actor or service account injects identical or near-identical workflow payloads across 50+ repos in a short window.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Establish per-repo workflow modification baseline. Alert when N>50 repos receive workflow file commits with >90% content similarity within 1 hour, sourced from single user or automation token. Cross-reference with repository ownership scope and org privilege levels.

suggestion.title: GitHub Actions Runner Outbound Data Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: CI/CD workflows execute in runner environments and must exfiltrate stolen data. Article describes malicious workflows but pipeline generated zero UC for detecting runner egress to attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound HTTP/HTTPS and DNS from GitHub Actions runner IP ranges for: newly registered domains, IPs with low reputation, domains not whitelisted in org firewall policy, or bulk data transfer patterns during workflow execution.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Personal Access Token (PAT) Generation and Misuse
suggestion.rationale: Attackers likely generated or stole PATs to commit malicious workflows to 5,561 repos. Article mentions widespread compromise but pipeline missed detection for token lifecycle anomalies.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on creation of new PATs or SSH keys immediately preceding or during suspicious workflow commit activity. Flag tokens used across unusual repo sets or orgs. Monitor for tokens written to workflow logs or forwarded to external systems.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized GitHub Actions Workflow Trigger via Repository Dispatch or Manual Invocation
suggestion.rationale: Malicious workflows must be triggered. Pipeline missed UC for detecting abnormal workflow invocation patterns from untrusted sources (e.g., external webhooks, repository_dispatch events).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on repository_dispatch or workflow_run events triggered from sources outside normal CI/CD orchestration (Jenkins, GitLab, internal automation). Monitor for workflow manual triggers by newly-created or external accounts. Correlate with workflow executions containing data-exfiltration commands.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Secrets Access in GitHub Actions Workflow
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'mass GitHub Actions secret exfiltration.' Pipeline generated zero detections for credential theft. Detection required for non-baseline access to ${{ secrets.* }} environment variables.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert when GitHub Actions workflows access secrets that have not been referenced in previous commits for the same workflow, or when secrets are exported to external environment variables (run: export SECRET=${{ secrets.X }}). Baseline per-workflow secrets usage and flag anomalies.

suggestion.title: Malicious GitHub Workflow File Injection into Public Repositories
suggestion.rationale: 5,500+ public repositories compromised. Title indicates workflow-based attack vector. Should detect unauthorized or suspicious .github/workflows/*.yml modifications across repository population.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag creation or modification of .github/workflows/* files by untrusted or new committers. Escalate if workflow introduces suspicious commands (curl/wget to external IPs, base64-encoded payloads, env var exfiltration). Cross-reference against known malicious action registries.

suggestion.title: Data Exfiltration from GitHub-Hosted Runner to External Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Core attack: secret 'exfiltration.' Pipeline should surface network-based detection for credential data leaving GitHub Actions environment to attacker infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor outbound connections from GitHub-hosted runner IP ranges to non-whitelisted external domains. Alert on POST/PUT requests to suspicious endpoints containing JSON, base64, or patterns consistent with API keys, tokens, or credential material.

suggestion.title: Mass Unauthorized GitHub API Calls for Workflow Modification
suggestion.rationale: Systematic injection into 5,500+ repositories implies compromised GitHub tokens or authenticated account abuse. API-level detection required.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect bulk repository push operations, workflow file modifications, or action updates from single IP/user agent across unrelated repositories in short time window. Flag API calls from geographically anomalous locations or off-hours patterns.

suggestion.title: Suspicious or Typosquatted GitHub Actions in Workflow Dependencies
suggestion.rationale: If malicious workflows invoke unknown or compromised third-party actions, should detect supply-chain injection vector. No UC for action-level threats produced.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Extract all 'uses:' directives from workflow files; alert on newly-created actions, actions from obscure/untrusted namespaces, or actions matching known typosquats of popular tools (e.g., 'actions-checkout' vs 'actions/checkout').

suggestion.title: Block Outbound Traffic to Stark Industries / WorkTitans Infrastructure
suggestion.rationale: Article identifies Stark Industries and successor company WorkTitans B.V. (brand THE.Hosting) as sanctioned infrastructure enabling cyberattacks; organization should block known ASN/IP ranges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Create firewall rules and alert signatures to block outbound connections to known IP ranges and ASNs historically associated with Stark Industries and WorkTitans infrastructure. Cross-reference WHOIS and government seizure filings to identify confirmed CIDRs.

suggestion.title: Detect DDoS Attack Traffic from NoName057(16)
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states 'pro-Russian hacktivist group NoName057(16), which has previously targeted key organizations with distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks' used this infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for volumetric and protocol-level DDoS signatures consistent with NoName057(16) attack patterns—botnet traffic, amplification floods, layer-3/4 attacks. Alert on traffic originating from or transiting compromised hosting providers toward known targets of pro-Russian hacktivist groups.

suggestion.title: Detect Sanctioned Entity Infrastructure Substitution
suggestion.rationale: Article describes defense evasion: 'following this restriction, the web hosting infrastructure was transferred to a newly created Dutch company that investigators believe acted as a front'—rapid entity creation to hide sanctioned infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on newly registered hosting provider ASNs or company entities with infrastructure footprints, server counts, or BGP announcement patterns matching recently sanctioned providers. Correlate WHOIS registration metadata for rapid business entity creation using similar ownership or overlapping upstream connectivity.

suggestion.title: Detect Malicious Colocation and Transit Provider Abuse
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies 'Mirhosting...operated physical servers, provided colocation, and supplied high-capacity connectivity to major internet exchanges in Amsterdam and Frankfurt'—this infrastructure enabled attacks; detection should flag known bad transit providers.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for BGP route leaks or anomalous traffic transiting through compromised internet exchanges and colocation facilities. Alert on high-capacity traffic flows between hosting infrastructure and known victim networks, suggesting command relay or data exfiltration.

suggestion.title: Alert on Disinformation and Information-Warfare Campaign Hosting
suggestion.rationale: Article states infrastructure 'enabled cyberattacks, interference operations, and disinformation campaigns'—mass web content delivery and coordinated social media account activity originating from provider ranges.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor web proxy logs for bulk requests to content delivery networks, social media platforms, and news aggregators from known malicious hosting provider ASNs. Alert on patterns consistent with coordinated account registration, bot-net amplification, or bulk fake-content seeding campaigns.

suggestion.title: Detect Infrastructure Indicator Metadata (Organization, ASN, Dates)
suggestion.rationale: Article provides organization names (Stark Industries founded 'February 10, 2022, shortly before Russia's invasion'), EU sanctions date ('May 20'), raid locations (Dronten, Schiphol-Rijk, Almere)—these are infrastructure indicators searchable in threat databases.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Index known hosting provider names, founding dates, and geographic seize coordinates into threat intel repository. Cross-reference against internal network logs for any historical connectivity to these providers, enabling forensic timeline correlation.

suggestion.title: Nezha CVE-2026-46716 exploit: POST /api/v1/cron with empty servers array and CronCoverAll flag
suggestion.rationale: Article states 'RoleMember user can create a scheduled cron task' via POST /api/v1/cron with 'per-server permission check on cron creation has a vacuous-true bypass.' Detection should hunt requests with empty servers array and cover=1 flag triggering all-server execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: POST /api/v1/cron requests from authenticated users returning HTTP 200–299 where request body JSON contains `servers: []` and `cover: 1`, indicating intent to schedule cron on all infrastructure.

suggestion.title: Nezha-agent spawning credential-access subprocesses on Linux
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states post-RCE attacker 'can then execute credential dumping' via '/etc/passwd and /etc/shadow.' Detection correlates child processes (cat, grep, sed, awk) spawned by nezha-agent parent with credential-access path patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Parent process nezha-agent (or shell child of nezha-agent) spawning credential-dumping utilities where process commandline contains /etc/shadow, /etc/passwd, or references to iam/security-credentials, metadata.google.internal, metadata.azure.com.

suggestion.title: Nezha-agent initiating IMDS/cloud-metadata connections
suggestion.rationale: Article describes access to 'cloud instance metadata API' post-RCE. Detection correlates outbound connections to 169.254.169.254 (AWS IMDS) and GCP/Azure metadata endpoints with process chains containing nezha-agent.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Outbound TCP/IP to 169.254.169.254, metadata.google.internal, or metadata.azure.com from process InitiatingProcessParentFileName or InitiatingProcessCommandLine matching *nezha-agent*, indicating credential enumeration.

suggestion.title: RoleMember (role=1) accessing /api/v1/cron administrative endpoint
suggestion.rationale: Article root cause: 'cron routes POST /api/v1/cron and PATCH /api/v1/cron/:id are wired through commonHandler (any authenticated user) rather than adminHandler.' Detection should flag role=1 (RoleMember) accounts successfully calling admin-only endpoints.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: POST/PATCH requests to /api/v1/cron* endpoints where authenticated user role field = 1 (RoleMember) returns HTTP 2xx and response contains cron creation confirmation, indicating privilege-boundary bypass.

suggestion.title: File-system modification of /etc/shadow or /etc/passwd by Nezha-managed agents
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly names '/etc/passwd and /etc/shadow' as T1003.008 targets. Detection flags file creation or modification on these paths where initiating process traces back to shell/Nezha context.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: FileCreated or FileModified events on /etc/shadow or /etc/passwd where InitiatingProcessName is shell (sh, bash, dash) or CommandLine contains credential-dumping utilities (cat, head, awk, grep) and parent process is nezha-agent or Nezha-spawned cron.

suggestion.title: Suspicious Git Commits to Popular Language Packages
suggestion.rationale: Attack required initial repository compromise; 'Hacking 700 GitHub Repos' precedes package poisoning. Detection must catch the compromise phase before malicious packages reach users.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on commits to Laravel-Lang repositories from new/anomalous IP addresses, commits lacking PR review, commits modifying dependency versions or package manifests, and commits outside normal maintenance windows. Flag commits that add unexpected external dependencies.

suggestion.title: Installation of Compromised Laravel-Lang Package Versions
suggestion.rationale: Article specifies '233 Versions of Laravel-Lang Packages' compromised; detection must trigger when developers install affected versions. This is the primary execution vector for the supply-chain attack.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for composer require / npm install / pip install of laravel-lang packages, correlate installed version against known-compromised range, and alert on unexpected code execution from vendor/laravel-lang/ directories within seconds of install. Track hash mismatches between composer.lock and installed artifact.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Code Execution from Laravel Locale Package
suggestion.rationale: Compromised Laravel-Lang packages would execute attacker-controlled code in production; 'Compromised 233 Versions' implies active payload delivery on dependency load.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag process spawning (bash, powershell, curl, wget, nc) originating from PHP-FPM, Apache, or Nginx processes after laravel-lang namespace code execution. Monitor for unexpected DNS queries or outbound connections (port 80/443/53/5353) from web application processes post-package-load.

suggestion.title: Package Installation from Untrusted or Attacker-Controlled Repository
suggestion.rationale: Supply-chain attack requires malicious packages reach package managers; 'Hacking 700 GitHub Repos' likely involved pushing malicious versions to official repositories or intercepting downloads. Must detect installation from non-canonical sources.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package manager (composer, npm, pip) connection logs for Laravel-Lang installs from non-packagist.org (Composer) sources. Alert on hash/signature mismatches. Detect environment variable overrides (COMPOSER_HOME, npm registry redirects) that could redirect package installs to attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: GitHub Account Takeover - Bulk Commits to Multiple Repositories
suggestion.rationale: Initial access required compromising GitHub accounts controlling Laravel-Lang and related repos; '700 GitHub Repos' hacked indicates coordinated account compromise or SSH key theft. Early-stage detection must catch unusual GitHub activity.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk commit activity from single IP/session to multiple popular repositories within short timeframe. Detect SSH key additions from new geographic locations or unusual IP ranges. Monitor for disabling of branch protection rules or forcing of commits to main/master branches by service accounts.

suggestion.title: F5 BIG-IP Exploitation Attempt Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article title explicitly states 'Hackers Exploit F5 BIG-IP Appliance'—this is the initial access vector and should trigger detection for anomalous requests to F5 management/API interfaces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP POST/GET requests to F5 BIG-IP default management ports (443, 8443) with suspicious URI patterns (e.g., /tmui, /mgmt/tm/), especially from external sources or unusual source IPs. Correlate with failed authentication attempts and privilege escalation logs.

suggestion.title: SSH Credential Access from F5 BIG-IP
suggestion.rationale: Article describes attackers gaining 'SSH Access'—the pipeline should detect extraction or generation of SSH credentials on the BIG-IP appliance, a classic post-exploitation step.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on SSH key generation, export, or retrieval operations on F5 BIG-IP systems. Monitor /root/.ssh, authorized_keys modifications, and SSH-keygen invocations. Flag extraction of credentials from /etc/passwd or /etc/shadow equivalents on appliance.

suggestion.title: Lateral Movement: BIG-IP to Enterprise Linux Systems
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly states pivoting 'Into Enterprise Linux Networks'—this is the lateral movement phase where BIG-IP (a trusted network appliance) is used as a pivot point to compromise downstream Linux infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect SSH connections originating from F5 BIG-IP management network to internal enterprise Linux servers. Flag SSH brute-force attempts, mass parallel SSH connections, or use of extracted SSH keys from unusual source appliances. Correlate BIG-IP compromise timeline with downstream Linux authentication logs.

suggestion.title: Network Segmentation Bypass: Appliance-to-Enterprise Pivot
suggestion.rationale: The attack leverages a network appliance (BIG-IP) as an entry point to bypass perimeter controls and reach enterprise systems—detection should focus on abnormal egress from trusted infrastructure.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for SSH, RDP, or WinRM traffic from F5 BIG-IP internal segments to enterprise server subnets. Establish baseline of legitimate BIG-IP-to-server communications and alert on deviations: new destination IPs, mass parallel connections, off-hours activity, or connections to systems normally not accessed by BIG-IP.

suggestion.title: SSH Public Key Injection / SSH Key Installation to Persist Access
suggestion.rationale: Post-exploitation persistence via SSH typically involves injecting attacker-controlled public keys into authorized_keys on compromised systems—a technique implied by the pivot narrative but not explicitly detected by the pipeline.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on modifications to /root/.ssh/authorized_keys, /home/*/.ssh/authorized_keys, and SSH daemon configuration files on enterprise Linux systems. Monitor for injection of new public keys alongside lateral movement from BIG-IP. Correlate file changes with SSH login attempts using newly added key fingerprints.

suggestion.title: Suspicious helpers.php Addition to Composer Autoload
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'the malicious releases introduced a malicious file named src/helpers.php, which was automatically loaded by Composer'. This is the initial payload delivery mechanism after tag rewrite. No detection generated for this critical indicator.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor composer.json modifications or version installations that introduce unexpected entries in the autoload sections, particularly 'src/helpers.php'. Alert when legitimate package versions suddenly gain new autoload declarations not present in public repository commits.

suggestion.title: PHP Process Callbacks to flipboxstudio[.]info C2
suggestion.rationale: Article states: 'dropper that downloaded a second payload from the attacker's command and control server at flipboxstudio[.]info'. Explicit C2 domain mentioned but not extracted as IOC or detection rule.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect outbound HTTP/S connections initiated by PHP interpreter processes (php.exe, php-cgi.exe, or php-fpm) to domain flipboxstudio[.]info or IP resolution thereof. Flag as high-risk if source process is loading from vendor/laravel-lang/ directory.

suggestion.title: Multi-Format Credential Harvesting Regex Patterns
