suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Nginx worker process (nginx: worker) creation rates and lifespans. Alert if a single Nginx master spawns >3 worker restarts in 60 seconds, or if worker median uptime drops below 10 seconds. Correlate with error log entries containing 'Segmentation fault,' 'memory error,' or 'signal' to validate exploitation.

suggestion.title: Nginx Connection Pool Exhaustion via Malformed Requests
suggestion.rationale: Title cites 'poolslip' vulnerability specifically—connotes pool state machine corruption. Article does not describe detection for exhaustion of connection pools, which is the primary DoS vector. This is a named vulnerability aspect with no corresponding detection.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Track Nginx 'active connections' and 'waiting' connection counts from status page or netstat. Alert on sustained connection queuing (waiting > 500) without corresponding request completions, or spike in 'Too many open files' errors in error log. Correlate with requests containing malformed HTTP headers or pool-state triggering patterns.

suggestion.title: Nginx Heap Memory Corruption Signatures
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'Code Execution Attacks'—requires memory safety violation (buffer overflow, UAF, or pool metadata corruption). No use case exists for detecting memory corruption patterns or heap spray behavior in Nginx logs or system memory access traces.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag Nginx error logs containing 'double free,' 'use-after-free,' 'stack-smashing detected,' or Address Sanitizer (ASAN) messages. Monitor for core dumps generated by nginx process. Correlate with preceding request logs containing repeated pattern injections (long headers, repeated chunks) indicative of heap grooming.

suggestion.title: Nginx HTTP Request Smuggling / Pool State Desynchronization
suggestion.rationale: Vulnerability name 'poolslip' suggests connection pooling state desync between proxy and backend. No detection rules cover request smuggling signatures or misaligned Content-Length/Transfer-Encoding patterns that would trigger pool corruption.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor for HTTP requests with conflicting Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding headers, or requests missing Content-Length on proxy reuse. Alert on sequences where a single request to upstream leaves connection in inconsistent state (e.g., partial reads, orphaned frames). Track Nginx upstream connection reuse counters for abrupt resets.

suggestion.title: Nginx Module or Upstream Panic / Segfault Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Article title 'Code Execution' but mechanism unknown—could be module-level overflow, upstream protocol handler flaw, or pool metadata corruption. Title establishes RCE as outcome but pipeline generated zero technical detection for pre-RCE signals (malformed module input, upstream protocol violations, or segfault precursors).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on Nginx error log entries containing 'SIGSEGV,' 'SIGABRT,' or panic strings. Track requests immediately preceding crashes. If ASLR/PIE bypass or ROP gadget use suspected, correlate request content with known pool-corruption patterns (oversized buffers, recursive headers, malformed upstream frames) and unusually large response latencies (indicative of heap massage time).

suggestion.title: Nginx CVE Patch Compliance Monitoring
suggestion.rationale: Article is a critical vulnerability alert but pipeline extracted zero IOCs (CVE ID, affected versions, patch version). Absence of version-based or signature-based compliance detection use case—should flag unpatched Nginx deployments vulnerable to poolslip by version range.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Query web server banner/Server header for Nginx version string. Alert if Nginx version falls within known-vulnerable range for this CVE (to be confirmed from article body—currently unavailable due to malformed input). Cross-reference asset inventory against patched version baseline. Flag any service running Nginx version without corresponding patch timestamp in deployment logs.

suggestion.title: npm Account Takeover via Stolen Credentials - Pre-2FA Bypass Attempts
suggestion.rationale: Article describes 2FA-gated publishing as a defense against account compromise leading to malicious package publication. Pipeline missed the account takeover precursor: attackers must first gain unauthorized access to npm accounts. Detection should monitor for failed authentication patterns, credential reuse, and geographic anomalies before publication events.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect npm account login failures followed by successful login from unusual geolocations or IP ranges, especially within 24h of failed 2FA challenges. Monitor for credential spray patterns and impossible travel (rapid login location changes).

suggestion.title: Malicious Package Publication Post-Compromise
suggestion.rationale: The article's 2FA-gated publishing control directly addresses unauthorized package uploads. The threat model is: compromised npm account → malicious version published → downstream users install compromised code. Detection should monitor for abnormal package publication patterns (new maintainer uploads, dependency injection, version anomalies).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on package version publishes from accounts with no prior publishing history, unusual publish velocity spikes, or publication attempts blocked by 2FA enforcement. Correlate with account compromise signals (password resets, API key regeneration, email forwarding rules added).

suggestion.title: Suspicious Package Installation - Supply Chain Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly mentions 'package install controls' as a mitigation. The downstream risk is users installing compromised packages. Detection should flag installs of packages with known malicious signatures, typosquatted names, or versions mismatched from expectations.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect installs of packages matching known malicious hashes (supply-chain IOCs), versions with abnormal file counts/sizes, packages with unexpected privilege escalation code, or installs diverging from locked dependency versions in CI/CD pipelines.

suggestion.title: npm API Token Misuse and Unauthorized Publishing
suggestion.rationale: The 2FA control applies to *interactive* publishing; automated CI/CD systems use API tokens that may not have the same restrictions. Attackers compromising build systems could use tokens to bypass 2FA. Detection should monitor for API token usage patterns inconsistent with legitimate deployment pipelines.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on npm API token usage from unexpected IP ranges, token reactivation after disuse periods, or tokens making publish calls outside scheduled CI/CD windows. Correlate token usage patterns with code commits to detect compromised build credentials.

suggestion.title: Typosquatting and Lookalike Package Uploads
suggestion.rationale: Gating publishing with 2FA doesn't prevent legitimate accounts from uploading lookalike packages. The install control mentioned in the article suggests npm is addressing downstream risk. Detection should identify packages with names similar to popular projects (typosquatting).
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect newly published packages with names differing by one character, common typos, or homoglyphs from established popular packages (e.g., 'lodash' vs 'lodsh'). Flag if install patterns show users attempting to install popular package names but resolving to newly uploaded versions.

suggestion.title: Dependency Confusion Attacks via Version Precedence Exploitation
suggestion.rationale: Install controls mentioned in the article may include version pinning or registry precedence rules. Attackers bypass this by publishing higher version numbers of private/internal packages to public npm. Detection should monitor for version anomalies and registry conflicts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect installation resolution conflicts where a lower-priority registry (public npm) is chosen over pinned private registries, or where version numbers for internal packages appear suddenly on public npm registries with suspiciously high version numbers.

suggestion.title: Malicious Laravel-Lang Package Installation via Composer
suggestion.rationale: Article title specifies Laravel-Lang packages as attack vector; no UC generated for detecting abnormal composer install/update behavior or version anomalies. Article phrase: 'Supply Chain Attack Targets Laravel-Lang Packages'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor composer install, update, require commands targeting laravel-lang/* packages. Flag unexpected version selections, constraint violations, or installs from alternate repositories. Correlate with CVE release timelines.

suggestion.title: Credential Stealer Payload Execution - Hooking and Dumping
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly identifies credential stealer malware; no UC for API hooking, credential manager access, or LSASS process interaction. Article phrase: 'credential stealer'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect LoadLibrary calls to dpapi.dll, wlanapi.dll, or credential-related DLLs from PHP/Apache processes. Monitor handle creation to lsass.exe or registry access to HKLM\SAM, HKU\*\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\RunMRU from non-standard parents.

suggestion.title: Exfiltration of Harvested Credentials to C2
suggestion.rationale: Credential stealer malware must transmit stolen data; no UC for detecting outbound C2 communication with credential payloads. Implicit in 'credential stealer' functionality.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on HTTPS/TLS POST requests from php-cgi.exe, apache2, or nginx processes to non-ASN whitelisted IPs. Look for base64-encoded, gzip-compressed, or suspicious binary payloads in request bodies correlating with credential access events.

suggestion.title: Code Execution from Malicious Autoloader or Composer Script
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks execute via package autoload or post-install scripts; no UC for detecting command-line interpreter spawning from package vendor directory. Article implies execution mechanism via 'credential stealer' payload delivery.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect powershell.exe, cmd.exe, or Python spawned as children of php.exe/apache2/nginx or from /<app>/vendor/ directory paths. Flag execution of credential dumping utilities (Get-Credential, mimikatz, credssp) in non-administrative contexts.

suggestion.title: Persistence via Malicious Composer Configuration
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks establish persistence through package lifecycle hooks; no UC for detecting suspicious composer.json modifications or script binding. Article's attack vector (package compromise) implies configuration-based persistence.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor file write events to composer.json 'scripts' or 'autoload' sections. Flag new post-install-cmd, post-update-cmd, or unknown PSR-4 handlers. Detect execution of arbitrary executables bound to composer lifecycle events.

suggestion.title: Development Environment Compromise Detection
suggestion.rationale: Laravel-Lang targets PHP developers; no UC for detecting compromised dev machine indicators (unusual parent processes, unexpected privilege elevation, lateral movement from dev to infrastructure). Dev environments are initial access points.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect lateral movement from PHP dev machines (composer install origins) to database servers, CI/CD runners, or production infrastructure. Monitor for service account credential usage originating from developer workstations post-package-installation.

suggestion.title: Compromised Package Installation Detection
suggestion.rationale: Article states '34 Packages' were compromised across npm, PyPI, Crates — pipeline must detect when these named packages are installed or imported in environments. No detection use cases suggest the pipeline missed the core delivery mechanism.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package manager invocations (pip install, npm install, cargo add) for known-malicious package names extracted from threat feeds. Alert on installation of packages matching compromise indicators or unexpected package versions that deviate from public repository metadata.

suggestion.title: Package Manifest & Dependency Anomaly Detection
suggestion.rationale: Supply chain attacks typically inject unexpected dependencies or code changes into packages. Article title 'trapdoor malware' indicates malicious code injection, yet no use case addresses abnormal package manifest changes or unexpected child processes spawned during package import.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Correlate package installation (pip/npm/cargo logs) with unexpected process execution (child processes spawned from package root or temp directories). Alert on network connections or file modifications initiated from package installation directories that do not match package documentation or expected behavior.

suggestion.title: Package Registry API Anomalous Access
suggestion.rationale: Compromised packages indicate attacker access to package registry accounts or CI/CD pipelines. Article context suggests registration/publication anomalies, but no detection covers unusual registry API activity or authentication patterns.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor package registry logs (PyPI, npm, Crates.io audit logs) for unusual publish events: new maintainers added without approval workflow, version bumps from unfamiliar IPs, rapid consecutive package uploads, or publish API tokens used from geographies inconsistent with maintainer baseline.

suggestion.title: Post-Installation Code Execution from Package Directories
suggestion.rationale: Malicious packages may execute code during install (setup.py scripts, npm install hooks, build.rs). Article alludes to 'trapdoor' functionality but pipeline did not generate detection for setup-phase execution.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect Python setup.py / npm postinstall / Cargo build scripts invoking shell commands (bash, cmd, powershell) that reach external IPs, write to sensitive directories, or execute binaries with unusual privilege levels. Cross-reference spawned processes with package installation events within 5-second window.

suggestion.title: Unexpected Network Egress from Package Processes
suggestion.rationale: Compromised packages may beacon to attacker infrastructure during/after installation. Article describes 'trapdoor' backdoor behavior, implying C2 callbacks or data exfiltration, but no detection covers suspicious network patterns from package execution contexts.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor network connections initiated by Python interpreter, Node.js, or Cargo processes spawned during package installation. Alert on connections to non-whitelisted IP ranges, suspicious domains, or IPs with low reputation; correlate with package installation timeline.

suggestion.title: Bulk Package Version Downgrades or Rollbacks
suggestion.rationale: Organizations responding to 34-package compromise will initiate rapid rollback campaigns. No detection addresses organizational response patterns or bulk version management activity that suggests incident awareness.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect mass package downgrades or pins to specific versions across multiple systems in short time window (< 1 hour). Alert on bulk changes to lock files (package-lock.json, requirements.txt, Cargo.lock) or centralized dependency management systems, indicating coordinated remediation activity.

suggestion.title: Ghost CMS SQL Injection Exploitation Attempt
suggestion.rationale: Article states attackers 'begin by exploiting CVE-2026-26980 to steal the admin API keys'—core initial access vector, no detection use case generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost CMS API endpoints for SQL injection payloads in POST/GET parameters. Detect unusual query structures in Ghost v3.24.0–6.19.0 targeting database read operations. Flag requests with SQL metacharacters (UNION, SELECT, WHERE) in article or post management endpoints.

suggestion.title: Unauthorized Admin API Key Access and Exfiltration
suggestion.rationale: Article describes stealing 'admin API keys' that grant 'management access to users, articles, and themes'—credential theft not captured in detection layer.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on bulk enumeration or export of Ghost database records via unauthenticated API calls. Flag rapid successive /admin/api/ calls from single source. Monitor for API key usage from anomalous geolocations or IPs.

suggestion.title: Malicious JavaScript Injection into Article Content
suggestion.rationale: Pipeline missed core persistence mechanism: 'use the elevated rights to inject malicious JavaScript into articles' and 'JavaScript code is a lightweight loader that fetches second-stage code from the attacker's infrastructure.'
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Monitor Ghost article/post database for injected <script> tags pointing to external domains. Detect article POST/PUT operations that introduce src= attributes not in baseline. Correlate injected script domains against known C2/attacker infrastructure.

suggestion.title: ClickFix Social Engineering Lure Delivery via Fake Cloudflare Prompt
suggestion.rationale: Article explicitly describes 'fake Cloudflare prompt loaded via an iframe on top of the article page' as delivery vector—social engineering attack step with no detection generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Flag iframes injected into article content. Detect HTTP requests to known ClickFix/fake-CAPTCHA hosting infrastructure. Alert on user-agent mismatch between article host and iframe resource domain. Monitor for visual similarity signatures of fake Cloudflare pages.

suggestion.title: Windows Command Prompt Payload Execution from Browser Context
suggestion.rationale: Attack chain states 'Visitors passing the verification are served a fake Cloudflare prompt...which drops a payload on their systems' via 'pasting a provided command on their Windows command prompt'—command execution not captured.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Detect cmd.exe/powershell.exe spawned with parents being browser processes or clipboard-derived content. Alert on suspicious command patterns: certutil, bitsadmin, curl with -o flags typical of malware staging. Monitor clipboard capture/paste events from iframed content.

suggestion.title: UtilifySetup.exe and DLL Loader Execution
suggestion.rationale: Article names specific malware samples—'UtilifySetup.exe' (Electron-based), 'DLL loaders, JavaScript droppers'—yet no file-based or execution detection use cases generated.
suggestion.detection_hypothesis: Alert on UtilifySetup.exe execution, Electron process spawning shells (child: cmd.exe/powershell.exe). Monitor for DLL injection into legitimate processes. Correlate file hashes against known samples from XLab IOC feed. Block Electron-based installers from untrusted sources.
